articles.title: Asymmetric Dual-Atom Ruthenium–Tungsten on CeO2 Enabled Highly Active and Selective NH3 Oxidation
articles.abstract: Ru single-atom catalysts are promising for NH3 oxidation but still suffer from poor activity and N2 selectivity, mainly owing to the poisoning of the isolated Ru active sites by the over-strong NH3 adsorption. Herein, we fabricated an asymmetric Ru-W atomic pair anchored on CeO2 (Ru1–W1/Ce) exhibiting considerable low-temperature activity (∼90% at 200 °C), high N2 selectivity (∼85% at 350 °C), and notable stability (∼500 h at 200 °C), surpassing most of the previously reported catalysts for NH3 oxidation. Systematic experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrated that a strong d-f orbital interaction between Ru and W atoms was revealed, inducing the smooth electron transfer from W to Ru atoms. The electron-rich Ru single atom not only weakened NH3 adsorption strength to alleviate NH3 poisoning but also reduced the energy barrier of the rate-determining step of NH3 activation. Besides, isolated W atoms coordinated with active Ru species, leading to a decrease in Ru–O–Ce coordination number. This could suppress the activation of O2 and thereby the deep oxidation of NH3. Accordingly, the reaction mechanism over this asymmetric Ru–W catalyst changed from the initial i-SCR to an imide-like pathway, accounting for its considerable catalytic performance. This work provided a paradigm for advanced Ru-based catalysts enabling both high activity and high N2 selectivity in NH3 oxidation.

articles.title: Physicochemical Reaction Control Enables Molar-Mass-Selective Macromolecular Electrolysis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Tailoring molar-mass distributions postsynthetically remains a long-standing challenge in polymer chemistry that conventionally requires the synthesis of dedicated polymer libraries. Here, we show that heterogeneous macromolecular electrolysis can edit polymer-molar-mass distributions on demand from a single prepolymer sample, tuning number-average molar mass (Mn) from 60 to 902 kg mol–1 and dispersity (Đ) from 1.3 to 7. This capability arises from a previously unrecognized mode of selectivity where heterogeneous electroreduction mediates polymer substrate reactivity through physicochemical reaction control. In this electrolytic transformation, molar-mass-dependent transport physically affects the rate of redox activation with an approximately linear dependence on the diffusion coefficient of these macromolecules. This leads to preferential activation of lower-molar-mass polymers, which is a consequence of more rapidly diffusing species having preferential access to the electrode interface. Moreover, we show that during this macromolecular electrolysis, every redox-active unit on a single polymer chain is activated prior to polymer desorption from the working electrode, which is a distinct manifestation of physicochemical control. This stands in contrast to conventional postpolymerization transformations that are inherently stochastic in nature, where target units on individual polymer chains statistically react and reactions on large polymers are more likely to occur. Electrode identity controls polymer–electrode interactions. Strong radical adsorption to graphite drives complete activation of individual chains before desorption. On reticulated vitreous carbon, adsorption is weaker and reactivity reverts to stochastic activation, which causes the molar-mass distribution to shift gradually over the course of electrolysis. We leveraged these differences to arbitrarily tune molar-mass distributions postsynthetically by selectively deconstructing prototypical N-(methacryloxy)phthalimide methacrylate copolymers. These findings establish interfacial electrochemical environments as a platform for molar-mass-selective macromolecular transformations and introduce a new axis of selectivity in synthetic polymer chemistry.

Bioinformatic-Guided Discovery of O -Dealkylation Activity in Cytochrome P450 Monooxygenases
articles.abstract: The O-dealkylation of alkyl ethers—or the removal of small alkyl protecting groups (PGs)—remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. While traditional chemical methods require harsh reaction conditions and lack sufficient selectivity, biocatalytic approaches represent valuable alternatives. However, enzymes facilitating the desired O-dealkylation reactions are scarce. In this work, we applied a sequence similarity network (SSN)-guided approach to identify cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYPs) with O-dealkylation activity within the growing sequence diversity found in public databases. We investigated six CYPs, three of which exhibited significant activity toward structurally diverse ethers bearing methyl, ethyl, propyl, or allyl groups. While P450ThcB and P450Terp enabled the deprotection of aromatic and aliphatic primary and secondary ethers, P450Sca2-mut complemented the substrate scope by effectively deprotecting sterically demanding tertiary ethers. In particular, P450ThcB and P450Terp exhibited high regioselectivity, preferentially cleaving phenolic over benzylic ethers. Furthermore, P450ThcB enabled the regioselective deprotection of veratryl alcohol. Preparative scale reactions of three substrates yielded up to 74% of the isolated and (regioselectively) cleaved alcohol product. Together, these findings substantially expand the enzymatic toolbox for the selective removal of alkyl PGs and highlight the suitability of SSN-guided database mining approaches for the identification of biocatalysts with the desired function.

articles.title: Durable Equilibrium-Level Dry Reforming of Methane over Strain Regulated Oligo-Ni/Y2O3
articles.abstract: Precise control of catalytic active centers and their interfacial strain is central to accelerating heterogeneous reactions, yet systematic regulation of strain at subnanometer metal–oxide interfaces remains challenging. Here, we report a class of 3d metal/heavy rare-earth metal oxide oligoatomic catalysts, in which finite metal ensembles are anchored on oxide surfaces to form nuclearity-dependent, strain-coupled metal–oxide interfaces. By varying the metal species, oxide support, and, most critically, the average number of metal atoms in each ensemble, we show that interfacial strain can be systematically tuned across diverse 3d metal/oxide combinations. In the Ni/Y2O3 system, an optimal nuclearity range of approximately 4–6 Ni atoms maximizes both compressive Ni–Ni strain and tensile Y–O distortion, creating a strained Ni–O–Y interface that balances CH4 oxidation and CO2 reduction during dry reforming of CH4. The resulting catalyst sustains near-equilibrium CH4 and CO2 conversion for over 1200 h without coke accumulation or detectable active-site collapse and remains stable under natural-gas reforming conditions. Theory and in situ spectroscopy reveal that nuclearity-regulated interfacial strain redirects carbon-containing intermediates away from deep dehydrogenation and toward continuous oxidation, thereby establishing a dynamic carbon balance. These findings position oligoatomic catalysts within the structural regime situated between single-/dual-atom and nanoparticle catalysts and highlight ensemble nuclearity as a tunable parameter for modulating interfacial strain in demanding catalytic reactions.

articles.title: Dynamic Zn-Based Ensembles Govern CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol on Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 Catalyst
articles.abstract: The active site of the classical Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 (CZA) catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation remains elusive as its surface structures undergo dynamic change under reaction conditions. Here, we combine neural network interatomic potential molecular dynamics simulations and grand-canonical density functional theory calculations to investigate the evolution of the representative CuZn alloy and inverse ZnO/Cu surface phases, and we consistently observe drastic restructuring under hydrogenation conditions, forming fragmented Zn-based ensembles at Cu support. Among the pathways examined, CO2 hydrogenation on these ensembles preferentially proceeds through the HCOO pathway, with different ensemble compositions being thermodynamically favored for the intermediates formed at different reaction stages. Importantly, these Zn-based ensembles are highly dynamic on Cu, allowing the inert HCOO within the ensembles to access highly active Cu/Zn interfacial sites, thereby making its hydrogenation kinetically accessible. The formation of ensembles and their dynamic behavior may be related to a suitable Cu–Zn interaction, which stabilizes Zn on Cu while preserving its mobility. Overall, these findings identify dynamic Zn-based ensembles as potential operando active sites in the Cu–Zn component of CZA and show that catalyst restructuring not only changes surface morphology but also couples directly to the reaction mechanism.

articles.title: Unraveling Regio- and Stereoselectivity in Cyclopropane Fatty Acid Synthase (CFAS) Enzymes across Native and Non-native Lipid Substrates
articles.abstract: Cyclopropane fatty acid synthase (CFAS) enzymes catalyze the formation of cyclopropane rings within bacterial membrane lipids, a transformation implicated in membrane homeostasis, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial resistance. Despite decades of biochemical investigation, the molecular determinants governing CFAS regioselectivity, stereoselectivity, chain specificity, and substrate scope remain poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigate how enzyme orthology, lipid structure, and membrane environment shape CFAS selectivity. Comparative analysis of CFAS orthologues from Escherichia coli, Lactobacillus acidophilus, and Streptococcus thermophilus reveals that the extent of mono- versus di-cyclopropanation, regioselectivity, and stereochemical outcome are not conserved properties but diverge substantially across the enzyme family. A simple two-carbon variation in phospholipid acyl chain length (C16 versus C18) reverses the absolute configuration of the cyclopropane product, revealing an unrecognized structural determinant of stereochemical outcome. Furthermore, we demonstrate that CFAS catalysis extends beyond native phospholipids to synthetic pseudo-phospholipids bearing non-phosphate anionic headgroups and to fatty acids embedded within lipid vesicles, substantially expanding the substrate scope of this enzyme family. Together, these findings provide insight into the molecular basis of CFAS selectivity, advance the understanding of bacterial lipid cyclopropanation, and broaden the synthetic potential of these enzymes for the stereoselective preparation of non-natural cyclopropyl lipids.

articles.title: Gas Retention in Porous Cathodes Governs Bicarbonate Electrolysis Performance
articles.abstract: Bicarbonate electrolysis offers a direct route for converting captured CO2 into high-value chemicals without energy-intensive CO2 regeneration and compression. However, multiphase transport within liquid-fed porous cathodes remains poorly understood. We found carbon paper and carbon cloth yielded drastically different performance, and further analysis revealed gas retention, i.e., localized and temporary entrapment of internally generated gas within the pore network, as an important transport limitation. Flow pulse and recovery experiments under galvanostatic operations showed largely reversible performance losses, while operando X-ray imaging directly visualized gas retention. Gas retention intensifies with denser electrodes, lower catholyte flow rates, and higher current densities. Guided by these observations, an interdigitated flow field was employed to enhance through-plane convection and gas removal, increasing the maximum formate partial current density to 304 mA cm–2 and enabling 120 h of stable operation. These findings establish gas management as a critical design criterion for bicarbonate electrolyzers.

articles.title: An Inflammation-Responsive Hydrogel with Targeted Microglial Delivery of Eupatilin-Loaded Liposomes Orchestrates Immunomodulation for Spinal Cord Injury Repair
articles.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) creates an inhibitory microenvironment that impedes neural regeneration. To overcome delivery barriers and achieve specific targeting of key inflammatory cells, we engineered an inflammation-responsive platform termed FlipE@GelMA/HAPBA (FGH), which integrates FTY720-functionalized eupatilin-loaded liposomes (FlipE) within a 3D-bioprinted fiber hydrogel composed of gelatin methacryloyl and phenylboronic acid-modified hyaluronic acid (GelMA/HAPBA). Under the acidic pH and elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) conditions present at the SCI site, the hydrogel undergoes boronic ester cleavage, leading to controlled FlipE release. The surface-anchored FTY720 then guides FlipE to target microglia via TREM2 receptor targeting, facilitating eupatilin delivery to reprogram microglia from a pro-inflammatory M1 to an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotypes. In vitro, FGH exhibited inflammation-triggered release and preferential uptake by microglia. Conditioned media from FGH significantly downregulated M1 markers but upregulated M2 markers in microglial cultures, ultimately promoting neural stem cell proliferation and neuronal differentiation. In a rat T9 spinal cord complete transection model, FGH implantation enhanced M2 polarization at the lesion over 2–12 weeks, reduced scar formation, and stimulated axonal growth. Consequently, FGH-treated rats exhibited superior functional recovery.

articles.title: Atmospheric Ozone Aging of Diesel Exhaust Nanoparticles Exacerbates Macrophage Pyroptosis via Protein Corona Remodeling and Intrinsic Toxicity Amplification
articles.abstract: Traffic-derived diesel exhaust nanoparticles pose a severe threat to pulmonary health, yet the toxicological consequences of their atmospheric aging remain largely unresolved. This study demonstrates that ozone aging significantly alters the physicochemical properties of these nanoparticles and exacerbates their cytotoxicity toward alveolar macrophages. Spectroscopic analyses reveal that ozone aging oxidizes the particle surface and increases the density of environmentally persistent free radicals. Upon deposition in simulated lung fluids, this oxidized surface selectively enriches complement proteins, fibrinogen, and transferrin to form a distinct bronchoalveolar lavage fluid protein corona. This remodeled bio–nano interface significantly enhances macrophage internalization predominantly through increased phagocytosis and clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Coupled with this enhanced uptake, the aging process simultaneously amplifies the intrinsic material toxicity of the particles themselves. Following accumulation in lysosomes, the combined action of released zinc and iron ions and the radical-rich carbonaceous cores promotes a substantial increase in intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS)-associated oxidative stress and severe lysosomal membrane permeabilization. The subsequent cytoplasmic leakage of cathepsin B triggers NLRP3 inflammasome activation, ultimately hyperactivating macrophage pyroptosis via the caspase-1-GSDMD pathway. By linking atmospheric chemical evolution with a coupled mechanism, these findings highlight both the remodeled protein corona and altered material identity as crucial co-mediators of particulate toxicity, providing a critical theoretical framework for evaluating the real-world respiratory health risks of traffic-derived aerosol pollution.

articles.title: Bandgap and Interface Engineering of Ag–Au–S Quantum Dots toward Bright Near-Infrared Emission and Deep-Tissue Bioimaging
articles.abstract: Low-toxicity colloidal quantum dots (QDs) with tunable near-infrared (NIR) emission are promising for bioimaging because biological tissues exhibit relatively low light scattering and absorption in the 700–1700 nm optical window. However, it remains challenging to achieve high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs), aqueous stability, and tunable emission simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate efficient NIR emission from Ag–Au–S QDs by combining composition control with heterointerface engineering. Varying the Ag/Au ratio tuned the bandgap from 1.39 to 1.88 eV and shifted the PL peak from 1130 to 745 nm. QDs prepared with an Ag/(Ag+Au) precursor ratio of 0.75 had an average diameter of 2.5 nm and consisted of a polycrystalline Ag3AuS2 core surrounded by an amorphous Ag–S-rich surface layer. These QDs exhibited a PL peak at 800 nm with a PLQY of 3.4%. In–S shell coating increased the PLQY to 33.6%. Subsequent ZnS treatment produced Janus-like Ag–Au–S@In–Zn–S QDs exhibiting a PL peak at 840 nm with a PLQY of 38.9%, consistent with suppression of nonradiative recombination through surface passivation. After ligand exchange with 3-mercaptopropionic acid, the QDs were readily dispersed in water while retaining a PLQY of 27.0% and exhibited excellent PL stability in biologically relevant media. The QDs enabled in vivo deep-tissue imaging, with NIR PL detected from tissues at depths of up to 15 mm. These findings demonstrate that Ag–Au–S-based QDs are promising low-toxicity NIR probes for biomedical imaging.

articles.title: Disassembly of Extracellular Matrix and Intercellular Adhesion Enables Noninvasive Bladder Cancer Disaggregation
articles.abstract: Bladder cancer is a type of prevalent malignant tumor of the urinary system, for which transurethral endoscopic resection serves as the first-line clinical treatment, followed by adjuvant intravesical chemotherapy or BCG immunotherapy. Current clinical regimens suffer largely from surgical trauma, procedural risks, long treatment cycles, severe systemic side effects, and high recurrence rates; conventional tumor cell-killing modalities relying on highly toxic chemotherapeutics and vaccines will inevitably damage normal tissues and induce less-tolerable adverse reactions in patients. By overturning this conventional therapeutic philosophy, we previously proposed a globally pioneering bladder cancer disaggregation therapy: calcium chelation disrupts intercellular cadherin-mediated adhesion, triggering exfoliation and detachment of tumor cells, which are subsequently excreted from the body via urine. Taking advantage of the unique anatomical and physiological characteristics of the bladder, this strategy achieves noninvasive tumor elimination through spontaneous urinary expulsion. To further enhance the disaggregation efficiency, the present work advances this concept by incorporating collagenase to realize the dual disruption of both cadherin and collagen proteins. To this end, we constructed a layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanoplatform coloaded with collagenase and EDTA. The nanosystem efficiently degrades key extracellular matrix components, thereby relieving steric hindrance and exposing cellular surfaces, which significantly promotes the subsequent disruption of intercellular junctions via enhanced EDTA accessibility for calcium deprivation from E-cadherin. This work establishes an efficient, noncell-killing modality for the physical clearance of bladder tumors, offering a promising alternative clinical strategy to suppress tumor recurrence and reduce systemic toxic side effects.

articles.title: Dynamics of Null and Electrostatic Blind Spots for Quantitative Piezoresponse Force Microscopy
articles.abstract: Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) is a cornerstone technique for probing nanoscale electromechanical phenomena, yet quantitative─and in some cases qualitative─interpretation remains hindered by parasitic electrostatic forces coupled through cantilever dynamics. Recent approaches aim to suppress these artifacts by operating at resonance-defined null spots (NS) or electrostatic blind spots (ESBS), but their quantitative separation and evolution under realistic measurement conditions remain insufficiently characterized. Here, combining analytical beam models, geometrically faithful finite-element simulations, and automated interferometric measurements, we show that NS and ESBS are fundamentally different operating conditions. The NS is a modal zero at contact resonance where sensitivity to the selected mode vanishes for both excitation pathways, whereas the ESBS is a quasistatic position where only the distributed electrostatic response is suppressed. Automated measurements reveal that both conditions evolve with the tip–sample boundary condition yet remain spatially separated under realistic experimental conditions. While beam models capture the dominant cantilever mechanics, finite-element simulations and experiments show that quantitative prediction of near-tip behavior requires realistic three-dimensional probe electrostatics and mechanics. These findings identify NS and ESBS as condition-dependent sensing locations and provide a practical framework for advancing interferometric PFM toward truly quantitative electromechanical metrology.

articles.title: Ferroelectric AlScN Four-Mode Reconfigurable Transistors Enabling Unified Logic, Memory, and Neuromorphic Computing
articles.abstract: The increasing demand for data-centric and artificial intelligence workloads has intensified the need for device platforms that integrate logic, memory, and adaptive computing beyond conventional von Neumann architectures. Here, an aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN)-based nonvolatile four-mode reconfigurable field-effect transistor is demonstrated as a multifunctional device platform. By combining the large remanent polarization of AlScN with the ambipolar transport of the MoTe2 channel, the same transistor can be persistently programmed into logic nFET, logic pFET, memory-on, and memory-off states. These modes arise from polarization-controlled modulation of carrier injection and channel electrostatics, enabling a single device to function as a polarity-reconfigurable logic element, nonvolatile memory cell, and analog synaptic element. Programming is performed through voltage pulses applied to the source, drain, and back gate, while top-gate readout is decoupled from AlScN programming, enabling stable nonvolatile operation. Based on this device, a single-transistor ternary content-addressable memory cell concept and two-input reconfigurable multifunctional logic gates are demonstrated. The wide polarization-tunable memory window further supports multilevel cell memory and nearly linear long-term potentiation and depression for neuromorphic synaptic operation. These results establish ferroelectric AlScN as a robust platform for integrating reconfigurable logic, nonvolatile memory, associative search, and neuromorphic computing within a common device framework.

articles.title: Flexible Organic Crystals toward Functional Devices: From Serendipitous Discovery to Rational Design
articles.abstract: Organic small-molecule single crystals, owing to their long-range ordered packing structures and anisotropic physical properties, have long been regarded as important material platforms for the construction of high-performance optoelectronic devices. However, because of the densely packed molecular arrangements and the relatively fragile networks of noncovalent interactions, these rigid lattices are prone to local stress concentrations under external mechanical perturbations, which can further lead to macroscopic fracture. Over the past decade, the continuous emergence of flexible organic crystals has expanded the current understanding of the mechanical behaviors of organic crystals and contributed to the development of “crystal adaptronics”, an emerging research direction centered on mechanically adaptive molecular crystals and their functional applications. Under appropriate molecular conformations and lattice symmetry conditions, some organic crystals can accommodate pronounced deformation, including bending, through reversible and cooperative lattice expansion-contraction or through interlayer slippage, thereby dissipating stress while preserving structural integrity and intrinsic optoelectronic functionality. In this review, we move beyond a simple categorization of recent works to critically summarize the mechanical mechanisms of flexible organic crystals, the corresponding molecular design strategies, and recent advances in their applications in functional devices, and further discuss the major challenges and future directions in this field.

articles.title: Lipid Tail Chemistry Regulates Selective Membrane Interactions with Model DNA Nanoprobes and DNA-Based Coacervates
articles.abstract: Biological membranes actively regulate their composition to fine-tune their packing, fluidity, phase, and surface charge, key properties that influence biomolecular interactions driving essential cellular pathways. While membrane surface charge is often attributed to specific lipid headgroups, the role of acyl-chain chemistry in modulating the interplay between these biophysical membrane properties remains unexplored. Here, we systematically investigate how the acyl-chain length and saturation modulate lipid packing, fluidity, and membrane surface charge in zwitterionic lipid membranes. Using amphiphilic DNA nanoprobes as model charged biomolecules, we describe the interplay between packing, fluidity, phase, and charge, identifying a packing-dependent guiding principle for membrane interactions that persists in the presence of anionic lipids. We also demonstrate that the identity and hydrophobicity of membrane anchors in nanoprobes significantly influence their binding to the membranes. By integrating acyl-chain chemistry and membrane biophysical properties into design criteria for biomolecular attachment, our findings provide a mechanistic framework for engineering membrane interactions with both DNA nanoprobes and DNA-based coacervates. Beyond direct application to biomimetic platforms and synthetic cell engineering, these insights are relevant to lipid-based vaccine nanotechnologies and a fundamental understanding of membrane–biomolecule interactions in living cells.

articles.title: Membrane-Context Screening Identifies a Functionally Active Peptide for Targeted Nanodelivery in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
articles.abstract: Ligand binding identified during screening does not necessarily translate into improved nanocarrier delivery. Here, we report a membrane-context screening strategy that uses BT-549 cell membrane-functionalized silica microspheres to identify peptide ligands with preserved nanodelivery activity. From a 7-mer combinatorial library, P1 (KFYVSGT) was selected as a membrane-enriched peptide candidate based on its preferential retention by the membrane-functionalized stationary phase relative to bare silica. After conjugation to PEG–PCL micelles, P1 preserved the nanocarrier’s size, charge, morphology, stability, and drug-loading capacity, yet markedly enhanced biological performance. P1-functionalized micelles increased BT-549 cellular uptake by approximately 5-fold and tumor accumulation by about 3-fold in a BT-549 xenograft model. When loaded with doxorubicin, P1 micelles restrained tumor expansion to 1.96-fold of the initial volume, compared with 4.83-fold for nontargeted micelles, with favorable preliminary systemic tolerance. Competitive uptake, energy depletion, peptide-affinity capture, inhibition, colocalization, and docking analyses suggest that P1 activity is associated with a Galectin-1-related membrane environment. This work establishes membrane-context screening as a practical route to function-preserving peptide ligands for targeted nanodelivery.

articles.title: Millisecond Blebs Precede Nanometer Pores in Disrupting Microbial Membranes
articles.abstract: Pore formation is a fundamental process for all forms of life. In the wake of antimicrobial resistance, drug-induced poration in microbial membranes attracts increasing interest. It is postulated that antimicrobial molecules bind to the membranes and insert into them, forming nanometer pores causing membrane disruption. Existing evidence indicates that pore formation completes within minutes but is energetically unfavorable, suggesting that there should be a transition state preceding it. Herein, we reveal such a state. Exemplified in a cecropin family of antimicrobial peptides we demonstrate that membrane blebbing occurs within milliseconds of introducing antimicrobials into membranes and manifests in the formation and rupture of elongated membrane blebs – causing membrane disruption under the first second of treatment.

articles.title: Nanozyme-Mediated Inflammatory Regulation Based on Redox and Non-Redox Strategies for Precision and Adaptive Intervention
articles.abstract: Inflammation is a host defense mechanism. If the host cannot prevent severe inflammation, patients would experience persistent damage and chronic inflammation that can cause many diseases. The regulation of the inflammatory process includes complex mechanisms such as oxidative stress control, intracellular and genetic signaling, antibacterial defense, tissue repair, and related processes. Nanozymes, defined as nanomaterials with intrinsic enzyme-mimetic catalytic activities, have been considered as versatile tools for inflammation control on account of their programmable catalytic process, structural and surface tunability. By integrating exogenous stimulus response, endogenous microenvironment sensing, biological carrier coupling and intelligent design strategies, nanozymes have been increasingly employed for precise, multiscale, and multistage intervention. Herein, nanozyme-mediated inflammatory regulation is organized according to the predominant mode of intervention into reactive oxygen species (ROS)-based and primarily non-ROS-based strategies, including redox homeostasis restoration, antimicrobial defense, healing, gasotransmitter signaling, and probiotic-assisted processes. From a multimechanistic perspective, interaction logic and integration principles under different regulation modalities are revealed, and some suggestions for the rational development of next generation nanozyme systems are also discussed to contribute to smart and personalized inflammation therapy.

articles.title: Structure-Engineered Lipid–Mineral Nanoparticles for Ligand-Free Myeloid RNAi Delivery in Alzheimer’s Disease
articles.abstract: Peripheral myeloid cells are key regulators of systemic inflammation and promising targets for immune intervention in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, selective in vivo small interfering RNA (siRNA) delivery to these cells remains challenging because conventional lipid nanoparticles often exhibit predominant hepatic accumulation and usually require ligand or antibody modification for immune-cell targeting. Here, we report a structure-engineered lipid–mineral nanoparticle platform, termed MCP, for ligand-free myeloid RNA interference (RNAi) delivery. MCP integrates a calcium phosphate mineral phase with a phosphatidic acid-enriched lipid interface, enabling efficient siRNA incorporation. The Ca2+–lipid cooperative architecture promoted macropinocytosis-dependent uptake and preferential siRNA delivery to peripheral myeloid cells in vivo, particularly Ly6Chigh monocytes and macrophages, with enhanced delivery under AD-associated inflammatory conditions. Systemic delivery of MCP carrying siRNA against triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 1 (TREM1) attenuated neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative pathology in an AD mouse model, supporting peripheral myeloid reprogramming as a route to modulate central nervous system (CNS) disease progression. Notably, MCP also achieved efficient TREM1 silencing in AD patient-derived peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and restored TREM1 expression toward healthy-control levels. This work establishes a structure-driven, ligand-free lipid–mineral RNAi platform for peripheral immune intervention in AD.

articles.title: Supramolecular Engineering of Polymeric Semiconductor Nanomotors with Phototactic Motion and Antimicrobial Function
articles.abstract: The development of high-performance photocatalysts is essential for advancing light-driven micro/nanomotors. However, the limited morphological tunability and inefficient charge transport of most polymeric semiconductors significantly restrict their photocatalytic activity and propulsion performance. Herein, dendritic mesoporous m-aminophenol-formaldehyde (MAPF) resin semiconductors with tunable pore structures and particle sizes are synthesized via a micelle-mediated self-assembly strategy. By integrating metal–phenolic supramolecular coordination networks with MAPF nanospheres, followed by asymmetric Au deposition, a hybrid nanomotor system is constructed. The metal–phenolic network facilitates interfacial charge transfer and optimizes charge-carrier dynamics between the photoactive MAPF core and the Au layer, thereby enhancing propulsion performance. The resulting nanomotors exhibit multiwavelength-controllable motion and phototactic collective behaviors. Meanwhile, the metal–phenolic components endow the system with intrinsic antibacterial activity and pH-responsive degradability, enabling controllable antimicrobial effects. As a proof of concept, the nanomotors demonstrate synergistic photodynamic and chemical antimicrobial activities against Escherichia coli and Karenia mikimotoi. This work presents the demonstration of supramolecular interfacial engineering for enhancing the performance of polymeric semiconductor-based micro/nanomotors, highlighting its potential for constructing multifunctional, high-performance light-driven micro/nanomotor systems.

articles.title: Hierarchical toughening of Fe-Al bimetallic heterostructures through coupled intermetallic lattice chemistry, grain-boundary state and interfacial architecture
Engineering Energy‐Storage Interfaces With Atomic and Molecular Layer Deposition: From Surface Chemistry to Process Design
articles.abstract: The performance and lifetime of energy‐storage devices are determined at the interfaces between electrodes, electrolytes, and separators, where ion and charge transfer, parasitic reactions, and mechanical degradation originate within nanometers of the surface. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) and molecular layer deposition (MLD) enable precise engineering of these interfaces through self‐limiting surface reactions that produce conformal coatings with controlled thickness and composition, even on porous electrodes. Although ALD surface chemistry is well established on ideal oxide surfaces, energy‐storage materials present chemically and structurally complex surfaces, on which reaction mechanisms, growth per cycle, and coating function can differ. This Review develops a chemistry–process–structure–function framework that connects surface chemistry, precursor reaction pathways, and nucleation behavior with film structure, ionic transport, charge‐transfer kinetics, redox stability, and mechanical response. We examine growth on oxide, sulfide, metal, polymer, and carbon substrates and relate the films to their functions at cathodes, anodes, solid electrolytes, and separators in Li‐based and beyond‐Li batteries. We further assess process scalability in terms of precursor utilization, throughput, and energy consumption, and discuss in situ monitoring, post‐deposition characterization, and full‐cell test conditions needed to validate coating performance. These relationships are summarized as six design rules presented as a decision flow.

articles.title: Fast Dynamic Re‐Equilibration of Chloroaluminate Speciation Enables a Stable Electrode‐Electrolyte Interface in Aluminum Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: The sluggish dynamic equilibration of ions in ionic liquid electrolytes, particularly under high viscosity conditions, originates from strong interionic interactions and inefficient utilization of charge carrier species. Here, we present a strategic electrolyte design that reconfigures the interionic interaction network and accelerates the dynamic equilibration of charge carriers in AlCl3/EMIC ionic liquid electrolyte. By incorporating an optimized moderator with low polarity and small molecular size, the dynamic redistribution and re-equilibration of charge carriers during cycling are significantly accelerated, while the continuous depletion of effective charge carriers is suppressed. Guided by this principle, the dichloroethane-enabled electrolyte exhibits rapid chloroaluminate equilibration and improved electrode-electrolyte stability. In situ Raman spectroscopy confirms that the moderator promotes reversible AlCl4 − /Al2Cl7 − conversion. As a result, the reorganized AlCl3/EMIC electrolyte suppresses dendrite growth and achieves unprecedented Al anode stability in symmetric cells. Matched with flake graphite cathodes, the full battery capacity increased by 120.7% from 92 to 203 mAh g−1 at 200 mA g−1 after 7000 cycles. This work establishes a dynamic speciation regulation principle for designing ionic liquid electrolytes with fast ion equilibration and provides a pathway toward long-life aluminum-ion batteries.

articles.title: Non‐Stoichiometric Molybdenum Oxides Enable Phase‐Stable Proton Storage
articles.abstract: Aqueous proton batteries are promising alternatives to lithium‐ion batteries owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and fast proton transport. However, the small size, high charge density, and strong protonating ability of H+ often perturb host frameworks during repeated insertion/extraction, causing phase transformations, lattice strain, and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we synthesis we report a non‐stoichiometric tunnel‐structured molybdenum oxide, Mo5O14, as a highly reversible proton‐storage electrode. The interconnected tunnel framework enables direct and reversible H3O+ intercalation without phase transition, pronounced structural distortion, or significant volume variation, thereby ensuring excellent structural stability and rapid ion transport. As a result, Mo5O14 delivers a high capacity of 271 mAh g−1 at 1.5 A g−1 (∼5C) and retains 142.2 mAh g−1 even at 300 A g−1 (∼1000C) and sustains stable operation for over 310 000 cycles. When paired with a VHCF cathode, the full cell achieves 73.3 Wh kg−1 and maximum power density of 43.4 kW kg−1, and over 60 000 stable cycles. Furthermore, a flexible interdigital proton micro‐cell array demonstrates rapid‐charge capability, powering a red light‐emitting diode for over 5 min after only 10 s of high‐rate charging.

articles.title: Synergistic Fluoride and Polymer‑Regulated Interfacial Engineering of NiFe‑LDH Anodes for Ampere‑Scale Natural Seawater Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Alkaline seawater electrolysis is a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its practical implementation is severely constrained by chloride‐induced corrosion and limited anode durability during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here, we develop synergistic fluoride‐management, defect‐engineering, and polymer‐interfacial‐protection strategy for NiFe‐LDH anodes, enabling kilo‐hour‐scale operation at ampere‐level current densities in natural seawater. A custom‐designed microwave‐assisted method produces fluoride‐protected NiFe layered double hydroxide on nickel foam (F‑NiFe‑LDHMW/NF). The electrode is subsequently tailored through controlled Zn depletion to generate an evolving cation‐deficient environment, followed by electropolymerization of calmagite to construct a multifunctional poly(calmagite) (poly(CM)) interfacial layer. The optimized F‑NiFeZnvac‑LDHMW@CM/NF anode delivered exceptional stable operation for 1000 h in simulated seawater and 1650 h in natural seawater at a commercial‐scale current density of 1000 mA cm−2. Mechanistic analyses combining stage‐resolved characterization, electrolyte analysis, and DFT reveal complementary intrinsic and extrinsic stabilization mechanisms: F− regulation and the evolving cation‐defect environment modify the structural and electronic state of NiFe‐LDH, while poly(CM) suppresses Cl− access and adsorption and delays interfacial corrosion. During prolonged electrolysis, F− undergoes dynamic redistribution and gradual leaching, accompanied by controlled catalyst reconstruction rather than catastrophic structural degradation. This multilevel stabilization strategy can be a step forward toward practical seawater electrolysis.

articles.title: A Bioinspired Photon‐Gated Phase‐Change Textile for Two‐Stage Heat‐Flux Regulation of Building Envelopes
articles.abstract: Passive cooling textiles for buildings must do more than reflect sunlight; they must also buffer transient heat under real outdoor conditions. Here we report a continuous coaxial wet‐spinning strategy for fabricating a microencapsulated phase‐change material (mPCM)‐integrated radiative‐cooling meta‐fabric (MFRP), consisting of a thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU)/hexagonal boron nitride (h‐BN)/barium sulfate (BaSO4) photon‐regulating sheath and a TPU/mPCM latent‐heat core. The spatially separated architecture integrates broadband solar reflection, atmospheric‐window emission, and phase‐change thermal buffering within one fiber platform. The optimized meta‐fabric shows high solar reflectance (95.44%), strong atmospheric‐window emissivity (96.21%), and a melting enthalpy of 102.28 J/g. In a representative sunny‐day test, MFRP reduced the chamber temperature by up to 10.36°C relative to the blank control; three‐day cement‐panel measurements further yielded an average peak‐temperature reduction of 7.51°C ± 2.17°C relative to bare cement. Energy‐balance analysis and climate‐scale modelling further indicate promising cooling‐energy and carbon‐reduction potential in hot and cooling‐dominated regions. These results establish wet‐spun radiative cooling/phase‐change material meta‐fabrics as continuously processable exterior textile candidates for passive building thermal management.

articles.title: Analog‐Tunable Nonvolatile Memristors with Self‐Compliance Behavior via a MoSx‐Interlayer Strategy for Neuromorphic Recognition and Zero‐Trust Image Encryption
articles.abstract: The von Neumann memory wall severely restricts the performance of traditional computing systems, and memristors have emerged as premier candidates for neuromorphic computing by virtue of their ability to integrate storage and computation functions. However, conventional HfOx memristors suffer from abrupt resistive switching and lack of intrinsic self‐protection, limiting their synaptic emulation performance. Herein, a novel nonvolatile HfOx/MoSx/HfOx trilayer heterostructure memristor with intrinsic self‐compliance and analog conductance modulation was constructed. The optimized device exhibits stable cycling endurance, multilevel retention stability and fast response speed, and achieves linear and symmetric conductance potentiation and depression. Furthermore, the proposed memristor successfully emulates diverse biological synaptic plasticities, including EPSC, IPSC, PPF, and PPD. A constructed neural network based on this device achieves a high handwritten digit recognition accuracy of 93.84% on the MNIST dataset, with excellent noise immunity and device variation robustness. Furthermore, the memristor acts as an irreplaceable physical entropy source for zero‐trust XOR‐based image encryption, generating ciphertext images with near‐optimal information entropy reaching 7.978 bits. This work presents a feasible MoSx interlayer modification strategy to optimize high‐performance artificial synapses on oxide memristors, enabling co‐integration of neuromorphic computing and hardware security.

articles.title: Architected Bio‐Based Iontronic Skin With Dual‐Mode Pressure and Strain Sensing
articles.abstract: Human skin encodes pressure and stretch through the motion of ions, a principle soft iontronics reproduce but rarely on sustainable terms. Additive manufacturing has lifted ionogels from cast slabs into architected sensors, yet this progress rests on fossil‐derived acrylates, because plant‐based networks expel the polar ionic liquids that carry charge. Here we print an ionogel whose matrix exceeds 80% bio‐based carbon while stably hosting a hydrophobic imidazolium ionic liquid, resolving a long‐standing compatibility barrier. A single monomer ratio tunes stiffness 30 fold (9 to 0.3 MPa) and nearly doubles ionic conductivity to 0.53 mS cm−1. Printed as gyroid lattices, the material senses pressure capacitively and strain resistively through separable channels: near‐incompressibility pins the gauge factor near 2 irrespective of geometry, whereas the lattice amplifies low‐pressure sensitivity eightfold and accelerates the strain response 4.6‐fold. On the body, both modes track joint motion with complementary signatures. Chemistry and printed architecture thus act as independent levers for renewable iontronic skin.

articles.title: Building‐Block Design of Nonflammable Quasi‐Solid Electrolytes for Ampere‐Hour‐Scale Sodium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a competitive technology for large‐scale energy storage; however, their commercial viability remains severely hindered by the inherent flammability and high volatility of liquid electrolytes (LEs). Herein, we propose a modular assembly strategy inspired by the building‐block principle to architect a quasi‐solid electrolyte (QSE). By synergistically integrating vinylene carbonate (VC) and 2,2,3,4,4,4‐hexafluorobutyl acrylate (HFBA) monomers, we modulate the electron density distribution within the polymer matrix. The resulting PVH QSE lowers the Na+ desolvation barrier and provides continuous ion migration pathways, thereby achieving exceptional ionic conductivity of 5.60 mS cm−1 and a sodium‐ion transference number of 0.58. Furthermore, the spatially locked polymer architecture drives the formation of ion‐solvent aggregates and a robust NaF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase, synergistically suppressing solvent decomposition and eradicating sodium dendrite growth. Consequently, the Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells exhibit an outstanding capacity retention of 94.9% after 3000 cycles alongside superior temperature adaptability. To demonstrate practical feasibility, the hard carbon||NaNi0.33Fe0.33Mn0.33O2 pouch cells maintain stable cycling over 200 cycles. Crucially, nail penetration and accelerating rate calorimetry (ARC) tests verify the exceptional safety of the pouch cells. By linking molecular microenvironment regulation to macroscopic battery safety, this work illuminates a viable pathway toward the commercialization of intrinsically safe SIBs.

articles.title: Conformational Restriction Unlocks Record Birefringence in Sulfonate Ultraviolet NLO Crystals
articles.abstract: Optimizing second–harmonic generation (SHG), birefringence, and bandgap simultaneously within a single material remains a formidable challenge due to their intrinsic mutual trade‐offs. Herein, we propose a conformational restriction strategy that replaces a flexible monocyclic cation with a rigid polycyclic analogue, which affords two organic ionic sulfonate crystals, [C5H6NO][SO3(C7H5O3)]·2H2O (HPSA) and [C12H9N2][SO3(C7H5O3)] (OPSA). HPSA adopts a highly ordered centrosymmetric (CS) crystal structure, Pbca, stabilized by strong and directional hydrogen bonds. Whereas OPSA crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric (NCS) space group P21 arising from steric hindrance and weak, asymmetric supramolecular interactions, thereby endowing OPSA with a stable SHG response (1.1 × KDP), with no observable intensity degradation upon heating up to 533 K. Both compounds possess wide bandgaps and pronounced optical anisotropy, notably OPSA with record‐high birefringence (Δn = 0.93@546 nm) among all known NLO crystals containing π‐conjugated groups with bandgap exceeding 3.1 eV. Moreover, OPSA achieves single‐phase white light with an ultrabroad dual‐band spectrum spanning 400–800 nm, enabling a prototype white‐light‐emitting diode with a color rendering index of 87, CIE chromaticity coordinates of (0.31, 0.32), and correlated color temperature of 7185 K. This work expands the structural diversity of sulfonate‐based materials and establishes a rational design strategy for multifunctional optical crystals.

articles.title: Core–Shell Solvation Structure Engineering Enables Practical Lithium Metal Batteries With 475 Wh Kg−1
articles.abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) offer extremely high theoretical energy densities, but face significant challenges in terms of electrolyte compatibility and interface stability. Existing low‐concentration electrolytes struggle to form a robust solid‐electrolyte interface to maintain stable cycling. Here, we designed a low‐concentration electrolyte based on a functionally partitioned core–shell solvation strategy. Methyl sulfone, possessing a relatively high donor number, dominates the primary Li+ coordination domain, while fluoroethylene carbonate, with a low donor number and low viscosity, primarily regulates the outer solvation environment and interfacial chemistry. This design facilitates rapid desolvation, high ionic conductivity (4.42 mS cm−1), and an exceptionally high Li+ transference number (0.74). The core–shell structure induces a gradient SEI, promoting uniform lithium deposition. Consequently, the LiFePO4 (LFP)||Li cell achieved capacity retention of 85.9% after 5000 cycles at 1 C, along with cycling stability from −10°C to 50°C. Practical application was further confirmed by stable cycling of NCM811||Li pouch cells (200 cycles, 95.7%) and NCM811||graphite pouch cells (650 cycles, 88.5%). Furthermore, a 2.2 Ah NCM811||Li pouch cell achieves a gravimetric energy density of 475 Wh kg−1. This work presents a scalable approach to engineering solvation chemistries for high‐voltage and high‐energy‐density LMBs.

articles.title: Electrolyte‐Enabled Suppression of Static Corrosion for Long‐Cycle Calendar Life in Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: The calendar life of lithium (Li) metal batteries is commonly evaluated through cycling performance, implicitly assuming that storage-induced degradation follows the same interfacial processes. However, this work reveals that Li metal undergoes continuous non-Faradaic interfacial corrosion under open-circuit conditions, defining a distinct degradation pathway governing calendar aging, distinct from cycling-induced failure. To quantify this process, we introduce a kinetically defined descriptor based on the degradation rate constant (λ), enabling direct evaluation of time-dependent capacity loss during storage. This framework treats calendar aging as a corrosion-driven kinetic process rather than an extrapolation of cycling behavior. We further show that static corrosion can be actively regulated via electrolyte design. Based on the degradation rate constants derived from capacity decay fitting, the LiNO3-15C5-CsBr electrolyte projects a 2.7-fold extension in storage lifetime at 100% SOC and a 3.4-fold extension at 0% SOC versus the baseline electrolyte. Mechanistically, Cs+-mediated electrostatic shielding, Br−-induced interfacial polishing, and NO3 −-derived inorganic passivation cooperatively stabilize the Li interface, suppress corrosion kinetics, and reduce irreversible Li loss, leading to a marked decrease in λ. These findings establish static corrosion as a distinct degradation mode in Li metal batteries and provide a quantitative framework for evaluating and regulating calendar aging beyond cycling metrics.

articles.title: First‐Principles Insights Into Fe2O3/In2S3 Heterojunction and Its Application in Dispersion‐Managed Fiber Lasers
articles.abstract: Heterostructure materials have garnered substantial interest across optics, medicine, optoelectronics, and electromagnetics due to their ability to combine advantageous characteristics from multiple constituent phases. Notably, Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunctions have demonstrated enhancement mechanisms for both photogenerated charge carrier separation and nonlinear optical response. However, their optoelectronic properties from a theoretical perspective and their potential in ultrafast photonics have not been extensively explored. Herein, robust S─O covalent‐bonded Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunctions were successfully synthesized via heat treatment technology. First‐principles calculations were conducted to examine thermal stability, electronic band structures, density of states distributions, electron localization functions, and dielectric responses, thereby establishing a fundamental understanding of intrinsic material properties while informing future optoelectronic implementations. By employing the Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunction in a fiber cavity with negative dispersion, passive mode‐locking operation was realized, delivering a pulse width of 300 fs. Moreover, the incorporation of the Fe2O3/In2S3 heterojunction into a net positive dispersion fiber cavity resulted in the achievement of mode‐locked operation with a pulse duration of 123 fs. Compared with previous studies, these lasers show improved performance. This work advances the understanding of Fe2O3/In2S3 structure‐property relationships from a theoretical perspective and highlights their potential as promising nonlinear optical materials for advanced optoelectronic devices from an experimental standpoint.

articles.title: Lanthanide‐Doped Hybrid Metal Halide Glasses with Multidimensional Luminescence for X‐Ray Imaging and Photonic Authentication
articles.abstract: Hybrid metal‐halide glasses combine optical homogeneity and processability for scintillators, yet most reported systems rely on a single emissive center and conventional radiation‐to‐light conversion. Here, we report lanthanide (Ln)‐doped BTP2MnCl4 (BTP+ = Butyltriphenylphosphonium) hybrid glasses prepared by one‐step melt‐quenching, demonstrating expanded emission channels while preserving optical transparency and the amorphous state. Eu3+ is selected as a secondary emitter for its spectroscopic complementarity with Mn2+. The glasses integrate broadband green Mn2+ emission with narrow red Eu3+ lines, whose relative contributions are regulated by Eu3+ content and excitation wavelength. Distinct thermal responses provide additional temperature modulation, while spectroscopic and time‐resolved measurements support Mn2+→Eu3+ energy transfer. As scintillators, the glasses achieve a light yield of 18 843 photons MeV−1, a detection limit of 26.7 nGyair s−1, and an imaging resolution of 28.5 lp mm−1, with stable radioluminescence under repeated and prolonged irradiation. Beyond conventional imaging, the composition‐, excitation‐, and temperature‐dependent spectral responses enable photonic barcodes for sequential multilevel authentication. Furthermore, the successful preparation of Ln‐ and Sb‐based glasses further demonstrates the generalizability of this glass‐forming strategy. These results extend hybrid metal‐halide glasses beyond conventional scintillation media toward spectrally addressable multifunctional materials, providing a route to integrate x‐ray imaging with multidimensional optical information processing.

articles.title: Low‐Melting‐Point Alloys for Printable Rear Electrodes in Perovskite and Organic Solar Cells: A Review
articles.abstract: Noble‐metal rear electrodes deposited by high‐vacuum thermal evaporation impose a major bottleneck for the development of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) and organic solar cells (OSCs), owing to high material costs, unstable interfaces, and poor manufacturability. Low‑melting‑point alloys (LMPAs) represent a versatile alternative rear‑electrode candidate that supports direct patterning under low‑temperature, vacuum‑free conditions. Upon ambient air exposure, LMPAs spontaneously develop an in‑situ surface oxide layer, which can mitigate Schottky‑barrier effects to facilitate efficient charge extraction and suppress ion/atom migration to improve device stability. In addition, the intrinsic mechanical compliance and self‑healing capacity of LMPAs render them particularly promising for flexible and stretchable photovoltaic devices. This timely review first introduces fundamental properties of LMPAs and their unique merits for photovoltaic applications. Recent advances in LMPA rear electrodes for OSCs and PSCs are reviewed, with focused emphasis on fabrication strategies for finely patterned LMPA electrodes. We thoroughly discuss the critical functions of the in‑situ oxide layer, alongside the mechanical advantages of LMPAs for bendable and stretchable devices. Design principles and performance trade‑offs are then summarized. Finally, remaining challenges and future research opportunities for LMPA‐electrode‐based solar cells are highlighted.

articles.title: One‐Component Carbon Dot Photoinitiator Enables High‐Fidelity Digital Light Processing 3D Printing With Improved Mechanical Resistance
articles.abstract: Developing efficient photoinitiators (PIs) from biomass for high-fidelity, robust, and bio-safe digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a unique one-component carbon dot-based PI (CD-PO), capable of high-fidelity DLP printing, is developed by grafting photocleavable diphenylacylphosphine oxide moieties onto the surface of CDs derived from renewable furfural. The nanostructured CD-PO effectively generates radicals to initiate the photopolymerization of acrylate monomers during DLP printing. Compared to conventional diphenyl(2,4,6-trimethylbenzoyl)phosphine oxide (TPO) used in DLP printing, CD-PO achieves three breakthroughs: 1) CD-PO enables micron-scale printing precision by optimizing the photocuring depth; 2) CD-PO enhances mechanical resistance, as approved by the increased storage modulus at T g, with the resulting polymer network exhibiting a nano-composition reinforcement effect that leads to a toughness approximately 4.6 times that of the network photocured with petroleum-based TPO; 3) The reduced migration of CD-PO components improves biological safety. The combined effectiveness of CD-PO in initiating photopolymerization, controlling curing depth, and reinforcing mechanical toughness ultimately enables high-fidelity DLP 3D-printing of diverse photoresins with structural complexity. In addition, CD-PO maintains high photoreactivity under aerobic conditions at low UV-LED intensity. This study demonstrates a robust strategy for designing one-component PIs incorporating biomass-derived components, further highlighting the versatility of biomass in photopolymerization-driven applications.

articles.title: Optimized Small Polaron Hopping Enhances the Conductivity Barrier of Polyanionic Frameworks
articles.abstract: The low intrinsic electronic conductivity of polyanionic cathodes, caused by electronic localization of isolated anionic groups, restricts the fast‐charging performance of sodium‐ion batteries. To address this challenge, we strategically introduce low‐valence Cs+ into Na4Fe3(PO4)2(P2O7) (NFPP) to enhance small polaron hopping and electronic conductivity. The Cs+ triggers a charge‐compensation effect that pre‐stabilizes Fe3+ species and establishes an Fe3+ reservoir in NFPP. This configuration creates a built‐in electric field that introduces electron‐relaying states above the valence‐band maximum, significantly lowering the small‐polaron hopping barrier between Fe2+/Fe3+ couples. Crucially, Hall‐effect measurements directly validate this mechanism, revealing enhanced carrier mobility and concentration that overcompensate for conventional doping strategies with reduced carrier mobility trade‐off due to carrier scattering from doped foreign ions. Consequently, the optimized NFPP‐Cs cathode overcomes carrier transport bottlenecks and hence enhances charge storage kinetics, achieving an 80% state‐of‐charge in just 7.9 min at 5 C and achieving full charge in 58 s at 50 C with a high specific capacity of 81.0 mAh g−1. Distribution of relaxation times analysis further substantiates that this charge‐compensation‐driven small polaron hopping constitutes the core mechanism for the enhanced electrochemical reaction kinetics. This work provides a compelling paradigm for designing polyanionic frameworks with enhanced reaction kinetics.

articles.title: Oxygen‐Rich Carbon Quantum Dots Enable Multiscale Synergistic Regulation for Ultralong‐Life Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: The practical application of aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) is now threatened by irreversible parasitic processes at the Zn anode. Here we report a molecular‐scale interfacial engineering strategy using oxygen‐rich carbon quantum dots (o‐CQDs, 38.83 wt% oxygen) that spontaneously self‐assemble into a 2D ion‐transport network in ZnSO4 electrolyte. This architecture enables multiscale synergistic regulation. First, o‐CQDs induce reconstitution of the primary solvation sheath into a stable [Zn(H2O)4(o‐CQDs)]2+ complex, reducing the desolvation barrier from 23.6 to 17.8 kJ mol−1. Furthermore, the continuous 2D network elevates the Zn2+ transference number from 0.51 to 0.85 and ionic conductivity enhanced from 40 to 93 mS cm−1. At the electrode interface, a protective electric double layer promotes preferential Zn(002) deposition while effectively excluding reactive water species. Thus, the Zn//Zn symmetric cells achieve a long cycling life (>10 000 h) and high average Coulombic efficiency (99.6%). Full cells employing the commercial activated carbon as cathode retain >96.1% capacity after 100 000 cycles. More importantly, it can work in a wide temperature range from −10°C to 60°C, with obvious self‐healing capability. This work establishes a synergistic regulation method by using a functional carbonic additive to optimize interfacial engineering to achieve durable zinc‐based energy storage devices.

articles.title: Precursor Size Governs Thermally Activated Solid State Conversion Into the Redox Active Framework Formation in Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7
articles.abstract: Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 is an attractive Fe‐based polyanionic cathode for low‐cost sodium‐ion batteries, but scalable synthesis remains constrained by the trade‐off between precursor homogeneity and process compatibility. Soluble Fe salts enable intimate mixing, whereas Fe (II)‐phosphate precursors avoid nitrate/oxalate burdens but react as insoluble domains. Here we identify precursor defined solid state reaction length as the key variable governing NFPP formation from Fe3(PO4)2. Reaction–diffusion simulations predict that oversized Fe3(PO4)2 domains retain under converted interiors, while low submicrometre domains enter a conversion‐saturated regime. Experiments using size‐controlled precursors confirm that this length scale regulates competing NaFePO4 and Na2FeP2O7 formation, Fe2+/Fe3+ local chemistry and Na+ transport kinetics. A CV precursor captures most of the kinetic and electrochemical benefit of stronger refinement, delivering 104.1 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C and 61.8 mAh g−1 at 20 C, together with stable long‐term and full‐cell operation. These findings establish reaction length scale control as a practical design rule for phosphate compatible NFPP synthesis.

articles.title: Rational Design of Vis‐to‐NIR Light Driven Photocatalytic System With Bidirectional Transfer of Charge and Energy for Enhanced Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: The rational design of photocatalytic systems capable of utilizing the full solar spectrum while maintaining efficient charge separation remains a persistent challenge in sustainable hydrogen production. Herein, we combine up‐conversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) with near‐infrared absorbing ability and visible‐light driven covalent organic framework (COF) photocatalyst together to construct a hybrid heterostructure for Vis‐to‐NIR light driven hydrogen production. In this system, UCNPs convert NIR light into ultraviolet and visible light for the utilization of TpPa‐1‐COF, while an effective heterojunction formed between UCNPs and TpPa‐1‐COF benefiting the separation of photogenerated charge carriers. As a result, PNGF(15%)@TpPa‐1‐COF composites achieve an exceptional high hydrogen evolution rate of 126.9 mmol g−1 h−1, which is 28 times enhancement over pristine TpPa‐1‐COF. The contribution of UCNPs in facilitating the separation of charge carriers of TpPa‐1‐COF was confirmed by measurements of femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy (fs‐TAS) and various characterizations. The results of control experiments demonstrate that energy band matching between COFs and UCNPs is crucial for the formation of the bidirectional transfer of photogenerated electrons and energy within the photocatalytic system. This provides an innovative strategy for developing an efficient photocatalytic heterojunction system to broaden the utilization of solar light and achieve effective separation of photogenerated charge carriers.

articles.title: Snake‐Scale‐Inspired Serrated Structures With Frictional Anisotropy for Tunable Bidirectional Shear‐Force Sensing
articles.abstract: Flexible tactile sensors are essential components of intelligent robotics, wearable healthcare systems, and human‐machine interfaces. However, most existing tactile sensors have limited capability to discriminate the direction of tangential forces, restricting multidimensional tactile perception under complex loading conditions. Herein, inspired by the serrated unidirectional compliant architecture of snake ventral scales, we develop a bioinspired serrated anisotropic tactile sensor (BSATS) for normal‐pressure sensing and bidirectional shear‐force discrimination. Moreover, modulation of the serration angle enables effective tuning of the sensing sensitivity and detection range, establishing a direct structure‐property relationship for adaptable tactile sensing. Finite element analysis elucidates the direction‐dependent deformation and contact‐area evolution of the serrated friction‐anisotropic structure under normal and bidirectional shear loading, revealing the underlying angle‐dependent anisotropic sensing mechanism. The optimized BSATS exhibits a high pressure sensitivity of 1.832 kPa−1, a rapid response time of 50 ms, and robust durability over 2000 loading‐unloading cycles, while reliably distinguishing oppositely directed shear forces. The BSATS further demonstrates versatile functionality in wearable physiological monitoring, human‐motion tracking, surface‐texture recognition, and real‐time robotic grasp‐state perception. This work establishes bioinspired friction anisotropy as an effective structural strategy for tunable multidimensional tactile sensing in wearable healthcare and intelligent robotics.

articles.title: Superior Capacitive Energy Storage in Lead‐Free Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3‐based Relaxors via High‐Entropy Design
articles.abstract: Dielectric capacitors are attractive for the high/pulsed power electronic systems owing to their ultrafast charging/discharging capability. Yet, the simultaneous achievement of high recoverable energy density (W rec) and efficiency (η) in lead-free relaxor ferroelectric (RFE) ceramics still remains a major challenge. Here, a high-entropy engineering in Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3-based RFE ceramics was proposed to construct heterogenous local structures, demonstrating an ultrahigh W rec of 13.7 J cm−3 and a high η of 86% under 780 kV cm−1. Atomic-scale microstructure, along with the three-dimensional polar structure derived from neutron total scattering, revealed that the diversified A-site atoms increase the local chemical heterogeneity and lattice distortion of AO12 cages, facilitating the formation of strong local clusters distributed in the matrix with weak polarity, thereby yielding enhanced relaxor behavior, reduced polarization hysteresis, and retained high polarization after applying an electric field. Moreover, the promoted insulating performance and significant reduced grain size result in a high endurance for external electric field. This work elucidates the roles of A-site atoms in the high-entropy effect, local lattice distortion, atomic polar displacement and energy storage properties, offering insights for the design of complex ferroelectrics with high-performance.

articles.title: Universal Water‐Based Hydrophilization of Non‐Wettable Surfaces
articles.abstract: Despite water's central role as a universal solvent, many technologically and biologically relevant surfaces, including natural substrates, polymers, and electronic materials, present low‐energy interfaces that resist aqueous wetting. We introduce here a universal, all‐aqueous hydrophilization strategy based on regenerated silk fibroin (SF) pretreatment that renders diverse natural, living, and artificial substrates compatible with aqueous processing. Brief immersion or spraying with ultra‐dilute (0.001−0.1 w/v%) SF solutions rapidly (5 s−5 min) induces surface wetting while preserving native morphology and function. This approach enables conformal coating and direct micro‐patterning of a large library of water‐dispersible materials across two‐ and three‐dimensional hierarchically structured surfaces. The versatility of the method is demonstrated through aqueous coating of hydrophobic surfaces, including plants, vegetables, skin, feathers, hair, and synthetic substrates, as well as through direct patterning of deformable and wireless sensors on living systems. Leveraging the inherently benign properties of SF, including its edibility, biocompatibility, and aqueous processability, this approach yields a simple and scalable method for sustainable surface engineering with broad relevance to manufacturing, healthcare, food technology, and bioelectronics.

articles.title: High‐Entropy Complementary d‐Band Decoupling of Redox Kinetics for Bidirectional Catalysis in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
articles.abstract: The reversible conversion of sulfur and Li2S in lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries is limited by the bidirectional redox kinetics. A single‐component catalyst is difficult to simultaneously meet the differentiated adsorption and catalytic requirements in the multi‐step conversion of polysulfides. We propose a high‐entropy complementary d‐band center model, extending the classical d‐band center theory to multi‐metal systems. The complementary d‐band centers of multiple metals align the HOMO and LUMO of sulfur species, coordinating the electron transfer balance and accelerating the redox kinetics. The multi‐metal sites collaboratively construct a “highly efficient capture → cascade conversion → rapid desorption” closed‐loop pathway, with the d‐p hybridization network regulating the adsorption energy and effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. Based on this design, the high‐entropy selenide catalyst with a customized electronic structure and strong synergy effect has achieved excellent cycle stability and rate performance in Li‐S batteries.

articles.title: Non‐Selective Suppression of Cation and Anion Crosstalk from an Anode Perspective
articles.abstract: Metal fluoride and sulfur cathodes are appealing for their abundance and high capacity but are plagued by severe electrode crosstalk. This occurs when transition metal cations or polysulfide anions dissolve and shuttle to the anode, causing corrosion and rapid capacity fade. Herein, we propose an anode‐centric mechanism utilizing a Na‐rich nanoalloy (NaxSn) anode that achieves simultaneous kinetic regulation and physical shielding, suppressing cation and anion crosstalk at both the source and destination. The ultrafast kinetics of the NaxSn alloy elevate the Damköhler number (Da), a descriptor quantifying the competition between conversion and diffusion, thereby ensuring these species are rapidly reduced at the cathode prior to outward diffusion. Concurrently, this nanoalloy induces the formation of an ultrathin, robust Na2O‐rich solid electrolyte interphase that non‐selectively blocks residual cation and anion crossovers. This mechanism enables an FeF2||NaxSn full cell to achieve a Coulombic efficiency of 99.93% over 200 cycles. Additionally, the S/C||NaxSn system supports extreme rate capabilities (630 mAh g−1 at 20C) and transitions to practical pouch cell configurations, yielding an excellent capacity retention of 91.95% after 1000 cycles at 0.5C. Ultimately, Na‐rich nanoalloy anodes offer a compelling pathway toward high‐energy, sustainable batteries by transforming electrode crosstalk into a spatiotemporally synergistic anode‐cathode coupling.

articles.title: Structure‐Encoded Magnetic Anisotropy in Super‐Tough Magnetoelastic Aramid–Silk–Magnetite Fibers
articles.abstract: Magnetic anisotropy is essential for controlling magnetic responses in soft matter, yet it is conventionally imposed using external magnetic fields. Here, we show that magnetic anisotropy can instead be intrinsically encoded and continuously tuned through hierarchical structural organization, establishing a route by which anisotropic dipolar interactions, rather than conventional shape effects, dominate the magnetic energy landscape. This mechanism is achieved by engineering composite nanofibrils in which magnetite nanoparticles are grown in situ within an aligned aramid–silk matrix, inspired by biomineralization in chiton teeth. The resulting aramid–silk–magnetite fibers combine high strength and modulus with exceptional toughness up to 820 MJ m− 3, while exhibiting tunable magnetic anisotropy spanning axial to radial easy-axis configurations through structural relaxation. Quantitative analysis reveals that collective dipolar coupling dominates magnetic anisotropy by orders of magnitude over demagnetization-field contributions, identifying nanoparticle interaction networks as the primary origin of anisotropy. This built-in anisotropy enables strain-mediated reconfiguration of magnetic properties, giving rise to magnetoelastic coupling that scales with fiber modulus and reflects the available structural mobility for magnetic reorientation. By amplifying structure-defined anisotropy under mechanical loading, we further demonstrate strain-controlled magnetic torque for actuation. These findings establish a structural design principle for programming magnetic anisotropy in mechanically robust magnetoelastic materials.

articles.title: Outside Back Cover: Sustainable Low‐Valent Iridium Active Sites in Rhenium Doped Perovskite Iridates for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction via Hybridized Reaction Pathways
articles.abstract: In a rhenium‐doped SrZrxIr1−xO3 perovskite, high‐valent Re stabilizes low‐valent iridium active sites against overoxidation during acidic oxygen evolution. Dynamic Re–Ir–O interactions open a hybrid adsorbate‐evolution/oxide‐path mechanism, delivering a 250 mV overpotential, >1,300 A gIr−1 mass activity, and 600 h durability for low‐iridium PEM water electrolysis. More in the Research Article e1466065, Jung Kyu Kim, Young‐Min Kim, Byung‐Hyun Kim, HyukSu Han, and co‐workers.

articles.title: Scope
articles.abstract: Scope taking is one of the most characteristic, distinctive, and ubiquitous phenomena in natural language. When an expression takes scope, it combines with surrounding material as its semantic argument. For instance, in Amy gave everyone a book , the semantic argument of everyone is an abstraction over the entire rest of the sentence, namely, λ x . Amy gave x a book , the property an individual has if Amy gave that individual a book. This ability to operate on surrounding context dramatically enriches (and complicates) the ways that meanings can be expressed. Although there are many formal theories of scope taking, Quantifier Raising—often thought of as a covert (silent) version of overt syntactic movement—is by far the dominant approach. There are many constraints on the availability of scope taking that depend on the identity of the scope taker as well as on its surrounding context.

articles.title: Voice Conversion, Voice Morphing, and Speech Style Modification
articles.abstract: A speech sample can be morphed from one voice to another by computing a sufficiently detailed time-frequency parameterization of the signal, optionally decomposing it into speaker-dependent and speaker-independent signal components, editing the parameterization or signal components, and then generating a speech signal based on the edited parameterization. Fine-grained control of time-frequency parameters has found applications in the scientific study of speech perception and in artistic applications such as voiceover and music. Coarse-grained control of speaker identity, emotion, and second-language accent have been applied to various tasks, including the training of speech recognizers and speaker anonymization.

articles.title: What Is Singular They and How Do We Use It? The Psycholinguistics of Singular They
articles.abstract: Singular they is valuable to psycholinguistic research because it has a long-standing usage in English that is currently undergoing changes, both in how often it is used and in what conditions. As a result, singular they is an informative testing ground for the cognitive mechanisms behind language change, which include both top-down intentional change and implicit learning and adaptation. Singular they is also an unusually socially salient function word that provides opportunities to examine how automatic psycholinguistic processes intersect with sociolinguistic issues like gender-fair language, linguistic prescriptivism, and the emerging use of they as a personal pronoun. Developments in the use of singular they are linked to broader shifts in concepts of gender. We suggest that there are two main varieties of singular they that currently differ in acceptability and processing characteristics. Psycholinguistic research shows that singular they is viewed as more acceptable and used more easily within a supportive context that helps to make the pronoun pragmatically appropriate.

articles.title: Viscosity and Phase State of Biomass-Burning Organic Aerosol
articles.abstract: Biomass-burning organic aerosol (BBOA) is a major component of atmospheric particulate matter and is expected to become increasingly important as wildfire activity increases. The viscosity and phase state of BBOA influence its climate and health impacts. This review summarizes current understanding of the viscosity and phase state of BBOA. Measurements show that the viscosity of unaged primary BBOA spans more than ten orders of magnitude, from liquid-like particles to glassy solids, depending on fuel type, combustion conditions, burn stage, and relative humidity. Aging by evaporation, OH oxidation, UV irradiation, and secondary aerosol formation can increase viscosity by several orders of magnitude. Field measurements indicate that atmospheric BBOA is often more viscous than unaged laboratory BBOA. Laboratory measurements further suggest that aged BBOA commonly exists in highly viscous or glassy states in the free troposphere and may exhibit mixing times exceeding one hour. We also highlight future research directions.
