articles.abstract: by Herni Susanti, Novitri Nurimani Asha, Penny Bee, Heni Dwi Windarwati, Budi Anna Keliat, Atik Puji Rahayu, Amy Blakemore, Afni Handayani, Mochamad Ali Sodikin, Helen Brooks

articles.title: Crafting of physical exhibits by undergraduate medical students: A mixed method study to assess the acquisition of higher-order cognitive skills and student perceptions
articles.abstract: Active learning engages students in some activity that induces them to reflect upon ideas and how they are using these ideas. It also involves the process of keeping students mentally, and often physically, active in their learning through activities that engage them in gathering information, thinking, and solving problems. This study was conducted to determine if creating physical exhibits fosters higher-order cognitive skills like problem solving and critical thinking (application and analysis, respectively). In this study, carried out in the Department of Physiology, 50 medical undergraduate students were divided into four batches of 12–13 students each. Each batch was supervised by a faculty mentor and assigned a topic for the preparation of a physical exhibit. Multiple-choice questions (MCQ) testing higher-order cognitive skills were used to assess the gain in knowledge post-intervention. The qualitative component of the study consisted of open-ended questions and a Focus Group Discussion to ascertain students’ perceptions regarding the creation of physical exhibits. The students created physical exhibits related to the sensory pathway, the light reflex & the conjunctival reflex, the micturition reflex mechanism, and the automatic bladder. Median post-test scores showed significant improvement compared to pretest scores (16 vs 12, p < 0.01). Students reported that the active learning strategy promoted deep learning, enhanced memory, and helped them apply theory to practice. Secondly, it cultivated teamwork skills. The learning experience was enjoyable and led them to score higher on the post-test exams. Students also suggested that tightening the nuts and bolts, as in prior meticulous planning, would make the experience more enjoyable.

articles.title: Ecological traits predict extinction risk of the world’s traded carnivores
articles.abstract: Wildlife trade is a major driver of biodiversity loss, yet how trade interacts with species’ ecological traits and extinction risk remains underexplored. Carnivores warrant special attention because they are disproportionately exploited and vulnerable to extinction compared to other taxa. We analyzed 171,637 international trade records spanning 50 years (1975–2024) for 129 carnivore species listed under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). We analyzed trade volumes across the globe and then used logistic regression to evaluate associations between ecological traits and extinction risk, as well as family-level differences in extinction risk. Trade volumes were dominated by exports from North America and Europe and imports concentrated in East Asia, highlighting persistent transcontinental trade. Logistic regression identified longer generation length and greater dispersal distance as positively associated with higher extinction risk, whereas broader habitat breadth was associated with lower extinction risk. Among carnivore families, only Ursidae (bears) exhibited significantly greater odds of being threatened relative to the Canidae (canids) reference family. Our findings demonstrate that ecological traits are associated with extinction risk within CITES-listed carnivores, supporting the use of trait-based approaches as a complementary tool for conservation assessment and monitoring of internationally traded species.

articles.title: Effectiveness of nurse-led hypertension interventions on retention, adherence, and blood pressure control among adults in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review
articles.abstract: Background Hypertension affects more than 1.28 billion adults globally and remains the leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, stroke, renal failure, and premature death. This burden is inconsistently distributed across Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs), where nearly three-quarters of adults live with hypertension. This gap is largely driven by poor adherence and low retention. This systematic review aims to assess the effectiveness of nurse-led interventions on retention in care, medication adherence, and blood pressure among adult patients with hypertension in primary health care settings in LMICs. Methods The protocol was registered (PROSPERO CRD420251136515) following the PRISMA guidelines. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane for articles published between 2000 and 2026. Eligibility criteria included: adults (≥18 years) with hypertension receiving care from primary care clinics; nurse-led interventions; usual care as comparator; primary outcome: retention rates; secondary outcomes: medication adherence, blood pressure (BP) control. Inclusion: experimental, quasi-experimental, and prospective cohort studies. Dual independent screening and data extraction were performed. Quality assessment was performed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2(RoB2) for randomized controlled trials and Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tools for quasi-experimental and observational studies. Due to heterogeneity in intervention duration, outcome measures, and follow-up periods, a narrative synthesis was employed. Results Eleven unique studies (n = 19,005) were identified: 63.6% RCTs, 18.2% quasi-experimental, and 18.2% observational. Seven studies were conducted in Africa and four in Asia. The mean age range was 52.0–67.4 years; 51.3%−76.0% were female. Risk-of-bias assessment revealed high or unclear risk in the missing outcomes data domain for most RCTs. Ten studies used multicomponent interventions. Retention rates varied with appointment attendance (12.6–96.5%), routine clinical retention (27.0–62.8%), and study completion of follow-up (83.8% to 97.2%). Four studies reported medication adherence with varying effects in the intervention group compared to the control or baseline. Ten studies reported systolic blood pressure (SBP) outcomes; 9 reported mean SBP after intervention; the majority reported the mean reduction of SBP was greater than 10 mmHg. Nine studies reported diastolic blood pressure (DBP) outcomes; all studies reported a reduction in DBP after the intervention, with a range of −1.8 mmHg to −20.6 mmHg. Reported SBP and DBP reductions included both within-group controlled estimates; these should not be interpreted as a pooled effect. Conclusion This systematic review included 11 studies that showed nurse-led interventions improved blood pressure control in primary health care facilities of LMICs. But retention in care showed substantial variability in nurse-led interventions in primary health care facilities of LMICs. Nurse-led interventions in LMICs are a promising strategy for improving blood pressure control. However, retention in care was substantially and variably due to heterogeneous definitions and evidence on medication adherence was limited. Future research should prioritize standardized outcome measures and robust study designs to strengthen the evidence base and inform sustainable scale-up of these models in LMICs.

articles.title: Enjoy Life LocallY (ELLY): A qualitative study of a co-designed healthy weight and wellbeing intervention in two disadvantaged Scottish communities
articles.abstract: People who are unable to achieve a healthy lifestyle are at greater risk of type II diabetes, some cancers, heart disease, stroke, mobility problems and poor outcomes from disease. For individuals living in disadvantaged areas, life circumstances such as low income, unemployment, working anti-social hours and limited local services present barriers to the challenge of living healthy lives. Working with two disadvantaged communities in Forth Valley, Scotland, we co-designed and implemented an evidence-informed, incentive-based intervention, Enjoy Life LocallY (ELLY), to support citizens with healthy weight and wellbeing. The intervention comprised free soup twice weekly (café/delivery/pickup); a loyalty card (stamped upon engagement in community assets such as local activities, groups and clubs) exchanged for a £25 shopping card when a minimum of 9 assets over 12 weeks were attended; goal setting; information resources; and self-monitoring of weight and wellbeing. ELLY was delivered by volunteers over a 12-week period, from September 2023 to November 2023, to 75 residents. Qualitative interviews were conducted at 12-weeks with 10 participants per community, to assess study feasibility and conceptualise pathways to how ELLY led to healthy weight and wellbeing outcomes. Data were analysed using framework analysis. The ELLY intervention demonstrated strong acceptability and feasibility and was positively received by participants. In-depth interview data informed the construction of a conceptual framework identifying pathways through which the intervention supports healthy weight and wellbeing, including positive changes in behaviour, strengthened social connectedness, improved dietary habits, measurable participant-reported health improvements and the acquisition of new skills and knowledge. Collectively, findings support the hypothesis that engagement in the ELLY intervention was associated with a range of important health outcomes for participants, making a valuable contribution to the evidence base on community-based interventions and highlighting the important role of co-designed community interventions in supporting underserved, disadvantaged communities in health improvement.

articles.title: Ensemble frequency ratio-maximum entropy landslide susceptibility modelling for climate‑resilient road corridors in Bocas del Toro and Chiriquí, Panama
articles.abstract: Landslides are a major rainfall-triggered hazard affecting road infrastructure across the mountainous terrain of western Panama. This study develops an ensemble Frequency Ratio (FR)-Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) modelling framework to assess landslide susceptibility, identify critical management zones, and determine key drivers of slope failure along road corridors in the mainland districts of Bocas del Toro and along the Rambala-Hornito-David route. Within a 1,000 m corridor buffer, 87 mapped landslides (63 for training and 24 for validation) and 15 environmental conditioning factors were used to develop and validate the FR and MaxEnt models. An AUC-weighted linear combination of the independently calibrated FR and MaxEnt models was used to generate the ensemble susceptibility map. The ensemble delineated 9.67% and 3.99% of the corridor as high and very high susceptibility, respectively, achieving the highest predictive performance (AUC = 0.945) and outperforming the FR (0.873) and MaxEnt (0.943) models. Sensitivity analyses based on alternative training-validation partitions (57:30 and 70:17) produced consistently good performance (prediction-rate AUC > 0.88), indicating that the principal findings were not strongly influenced by the inventory allocation. Hotspot analysis identified three major clusters of elevated susceptibility and confirmed statistically significant spatial clustering at the 95% and 99% confidence levels. More than 71 km of primary roads intersect high-susceptibility zones, with Hornito, Bajo Cedro, and Valle de Agua Arriba exhibiting the greatest exposure. Slope gradient and NDVI were identified as the most influential predictors. These findings provide a practical basis for prioritising monitoring, slope stabilisation, drainage improvement, and ecosystem-based interventions to strengthen the resilience of road infrastructure in tropical mountain environments. Future work should incorporate larger landslide inventories, event-based rainfall information, and climate-change scenarios to improve the representation of landslide dynamics and support risk-informed infrastructure planning.

articles.title: Expression of Concern: Discovery of ROCK2 inhibitors through computational screening of ZINC database: Integrating pharmacophore modeling, molecular docking, and MD simulations
Fabrication and evaluation of a sulfacetamide-loaded niosomal gel for the treatment of ocular bacterial infections
articles.abstract: Topical ocular drug delivery is often restricted by rapid precorneal clearance, which can decrease drug residence time and bioavailability at the ocular surface. The purpose of the study was to develop a sulfacetamide-loaded niosomal gel (SA-Nio-Gel) to enhance ocular drug delivery. Thin film hydration method was used for the preparation of SA niosomes, employing nonionic surfactants (Span 60 and Span 80) and cholesterol. The optimized niosomal formulation was then incorporated into a Carbopol 934 gel base to prepare the final SA-Nio-Gel formulation. The optimized niosomes exhibited encapsulation efficiency of 76% ± 1.5 and a mean particle size of 129.7 ± 2.52 nm. Rheological analysis of the SA-Nio-Gel demonstrated pseudoplastic behavior, characterized by a reduction in viscosity with increasing shear rate. Biocompatibility evaluation indicated that the formulation was non-toxic. In vitro release profiles showed a slow and sustained SA release from the developed formulation. Furthermore, microbiological assays confirmed the potent antibacterial activity of the SA-Nio-Gel against S. aureus. Compared to the SA solution and SA-Nio, the SA-Nio-Gel formulation significantly minimized precorneal drainage and improved drug penetration. These results indicate that the niosomal gel-based system could be a promising platform for the ocular delivery of SA, which provides sustained release and enhanced drug permeability.

articles.title: Gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, and patient-reported outcomes in Class III orthognathic surgery patients: An item-level analysis
articles.abstract: Objective To evaluate gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, functional and psychosocial evaluations, and treatment process perceptions among adult patients with skeletal Class III malocclusion undergoing orthodontic preparation for orthognathic surgery. Methods In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 81 adults (37 females, 44 males) with skeletal Class III malocclusion completed a 27-item investigator-developed questionnaire during pre-surgical orthodontic preparation, covering demographics, problem awareness, functional and psychosocial evaluations, motivation and expectations, treatment process, and patient engagement. Gender differences were analyzed item by item with Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, or Fisher’s exact tests. P-values for the 37 comparisons were adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure within questionnaire domains, and effect sizes with 95% confidence intervals were estimated. Because the a priori sample size calculation did not address between-gender comparisons, these were treated as exploratory. Results Seven differences met the unadjusted threshold (p < 0.05), of which three remained significant after within-domain FDR correction: females reported greater lack of self-confidence in social environments (q = 0.044), and males reported more adequate information from their orthodontist (q = 0.018) and higher pre-operative treatment satisfaction (q = 0.019), with moderate effect sizes (rank-biserial |r| = 0.30–0.35). The other four, all reported more often by females (eating difficulty, food avoidance, temporomandibular joint problems, and lack of confidence when photographed), were nominally significant only (unadjusted p = 0.013–0.043). No difference survived correction across all 37 comparisons. For the other items no significant differences were detected, but confidence intervals did not exclude small-to-moderate differences. Conclusions Gender differences in social self-confidence, perceived information adequacy, and pre-operative satisfaction were the strongest exploratory findings. Because the study was not powered for gender comparisons, non-significant results do not indicate that the genders are similar. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered multi-center, longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Harpagide alleviates neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: Association with the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway
articles.abstract: Background Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe neurological complication of sepsis, characterized by uncontrolled neuroinflammation and cognitive decline, yet no specific therapy is currently available. Harpagide, a naturally occurring iridoid glycoside, has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective activities; however, its therapeutic potential in SAE remains unexplored. This study aimed to investigate whether Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods A mouse model of SAE was established by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 18 mg/kg). Cognitive performance was assessed using behavioral assays. Brain tissue morphology and neuronal survival were evaluated through histopathological examination. Glial cell activation and the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) were measured. Network pharmacology was employed to predict potential targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to predict binding interactions with core targets. Western blotting was performed to determine the expression levels of key proteins involved in the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway. Results Treatment with Harpagide significantly improved behavioral performance, ameliorated brain pathological changes, preserved hippocampal neurons, suppressed glial activation, and reduced the levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 in SAE mice. Network pharmacology analysis predicted four core targets: GAPDH, CASP3, MMP9, and ICAM1. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested stable binding between Harpagide and MMP9. Western blot analysis further showed that Harpagide treatment was associated with reduced expression of MMP9 and phosphorylated NF-κB p65 in both hippocampal and cortical tissues. Conclusions The present study demonstrates that Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE, which are associated with mitigated neuroinflammation and reduced MMP9/NF-κB signaling, supporting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for this devastating condition.

articles.title: Integrated nutrition-sensitive interventions are associated with improvements in household food security and dietary diversity among vulnerable women in the host communities of Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh: Findings from a pre-post comparison study
articles.abstract: Introduction Nutrition-sensitive interventions aim to improve or at least safeguard the underlying causes of malnutrition, especially among the most vulnerable populations. Integrated nutrition-sensitive interventions are effective strategies for improving household food security and dietary diversity in low-income settings. In 2021, the European Union (EU) and UNICEF, in collaboration with the Government of Bangladesh and partners, implemented nutrition-sensitive interventions combining two income-generating activities (IGAs): backyard poultry rearing and tailoring with asset transfers, direct cash support, and nutrition education for vulnerable women in the host communities of Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh. We evaluated the association of these interventions with household food security and dietary diversity among vulnerable women. Materials and methods We analyzed data from two rounds (2022 and 2024) of repeated cross-sectional surveys involving 1,255 vulnerable women (638 in 2022 and 617 in 2024) across four upazilas in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh. Covariates were initially imbalanced across groups because the interventions were not randomly assigned; therefore, we employed propensity score weighting to balance the covariates between the two groups. We used modified Poisson regression and binomial regression models to estimate the association between exposure and outcomes from the pseudo-population obtained by propensity score weighting. All the inferences in this manuscript were based on a 5% significance level. Results In 2024, vulnerable women had a 53% higher likelihood of household food security (RR = 1.53, 95% CI: 1.27–1.85, p < 0.001) than in 2022. Similarly, dietary diversity of vulnerable women increased markedly, showing over two and a half-fold higher likelihood of adequate dietary diversity in 2024 (RR = 2.78, 95% CI: 2.36–3.27, p < 0.001). The E-values corresponding to the associations of food security and dietary diversity with survey year were 2.44 and 5.00, respectively, on the risk ratio scale, which shows that the findings were less sensitive to unmeasured confounders. Conclusion Household food security and dietary diversity substantially increased over time among vulnerable women in the study areas. As the study was a two-repeated cross-sectional survey, residual confounding and other time-varying contextual factors cannot be excluded, so the observed differences should not be interpreted as definitive causal effects of the intervention. Future controlled or longitudinal evaluations are needed to establish the causal effectiveness and long-term sustainability of integrated nutrition-sensitive interventions.

articles.title: Land degradation neutrality state and progress in the Central Region, Malawi
articles.abstract: Achieving Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) is vital for the long-term sustainability of human well-being and the realisation of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.3.1. We estimated the overall indicator of SDG 15.3.1, the proportion of land that is degraded over the total land area in the Central Region, Malawi, from 2001 to 2022, using the Trends.Earth tool in QGIS. The study applied the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) Good Practice Guidance methodology for SDG Indicator 15.3.1 assessment, integrating land cover, land productivity, and soil organic carbon (SOC) sub-indicators. The default datasets in the Trends.Earth plugin were adopted for all sub-indicators. The study has revealed that: (i) The proportion of degraded land increased from 26.8% in the baseline period (2001–2015) to 41.2% in the monitoring period (2016–2022). Stable land area decreased from 62.2% to 55.7%, while improved land area declined from 10.0% to 2.0%. Overall, during the entire study period (2001–2022), 27.1% of the land remained degraded, 62.4% was stable, and 9.4% improved. (ii) Land with degraded productivity significantly declined from 74.5% to 29.3%. In contrast, land with stable productivity slightly increased from 1.1% to 1.9%. (iii) SOC levels remained largely stable (>97%), although slight losses occurred in cropland, grassland, and wetland areas. (iv) Land cover remained predominantly stable (96.7%) throughout the study period. The overall SDG 15.3.1 indicator indicates continued degradation trends exceeding the rate of land recovery and restoration. This study has highlighted key spatial patterns and identified insights into the priority areas for targeted LDN interventions in the Central Region of Malawi. The findings provide critical evidence for guiding sustainable land management strategies and accelerating progress toward achieving land degradation neutrality in Malawi.

articles.title: Microclimatic regulation effects of landscape elements on university campus in a temperate monsoon climate zone: A case study during extreme summer heat
articles.abstract: Although temperate monsoon climate regions are traditionally known for their harsh winter climates, the combined effects of rapid urbanization and global climate change have significantly intensified summer urban heat island effects in these areas, making them a neglected yet increasingly severe challenge in high-latitude urban climate adaptation planning. This study takes a typical campus in Shenyang, a temperate monsoon climate region in Northeast China, as the experimental subject. It quantitatively dissects the non-linear statistical associations and regulatory mechanisms of biotic and abiotic landscape elements and their spatial configurations on microclimate parameters and human thermal comfort (Physiologically Equivalent Temperature, PET) by combining microclimate field observations with validated ENVI-met numerical simulations. Field measurement results show that the vertical structural characteristics of vegetation dominate cooling efficiency: evergreen trees and shrubs, with their dense radiation-blocking structures, exhibit optimal regulatory potential, with mean Physiological Equivalent Temperature (ΔPET) values reaching 10.6°C and 10.4°C, respectively, significantly outperforming deciduous trees (8.1°C). In contrast, abiotic elements play an auxiliary role, with dynamic water bodies and enclosed pavilions providing PET improvement values of 3.1°C and 2.9°C, respectively, while paving materials have limited direct regulatory capacity (< 2.0°C). Simulation optimization further reveals a significant “blue-green synergy” effect: the composite configuration of high-canopy evergreen trees and large-area dynamic water bodies forms the optimal spatial solution, reducing daily average PET to 48.7°C, a decrease of 7.3°C compared to the vegetation-free baseline scenario. Addressing the unique “humid-heat” challenge that distinguishes temperate monsoon climates from arid or semi-arid regions where summer thermal stress is often attributed solely to high temperatures, this study goes beyond merely documenting cooling effects to elucidate the “structural-thermal decoupling” mechanism in temperate monsoon climates. It challenges the conventional “deciduous-first” design paradigm by quantifying the superior radiative-blocking efficiency of evergreen species during extreme heatwaves, providing a physically-grounded framework for campus microclimate resilience.

articles.title: Modeling and controlling a half-car model suspension system using an ANFIS controller
articles.abstract: Passive suspension systems (PSS) use fixed spring and damping characteristics and cannot adapt to changing road disturbances and operating conditions. Active suspension systems (ASS) address this limitation by generating additional control forces, but controller design must balance ride comfort, road holding, model uncertainty, and control effort. This study develops a four-degree-of-freedom (4-DOF) longitudinal half-car model and evaluates an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) controller against PSS and PID-controlled ASS under double-bump and ISO-classified random Type A and Type C Road profiles at 10 and 20 m/s. The ANFIS controller is trained using PID-generated input-output data with two inputs, five Gaussian membership functions per input, 25 Takagi-Sugeno rules, and 150 training epochs. For the double-bump case at 10 m/s, ANFIS reduces body vertical displacement from 0.0435 to 0.0084 m (80.6%), vertical acceleration from 2.40 to 0.77 m/s2 (67.9%), and front suspension travel from 0.0652 to 0.0090 m (86.2%) relative to PSS. Compared with PID, the corresponding reductions are 53.6%, 49.3%, and 43.8%, respectively. Settling time is reduced by 38.8% for body vertical displacement and 38.6% for pitch acceleration relative to PSS. The result meets all the qualifications for riding comfort of the ISO 2631 standard. The study identifies limitations related to PID-supervised training, linear modeling, and actuator-energy assessment by employing simulation. Experimental evaluation is required to establish robustness to parameter uncertainty, sensor noise, actuator delay, and implementation energy requirements.

articles.title: PIP5K isoforms and phosphoinositide molecular species in EGF-stimulated PIP3 synthesis: A multi-method approach using enzyme genetic suppression and chemical inhibition in MCF10A cells
articles.abstract: The membrane phospholipid PI(4,5)P2 has structural functions and is a substrate for PLC and PI3K enzymes to generate Ins(1,4,5)P3, DAG and PI(3,4,5)P3 signals. PIP5Ks, that 5-phosphorylate PI4P, are the major source of PI(4,5)P2 in mammalian cells. Current thinking suggests distinct pools of PI(4,5)P2 may be differentially generated by PIP5Kα, β and γ isoforms and involved in different physiological functions. Phosphoinositides are comprised of families of acyl-chain variants but are uniquely enriched in C38:4 species. There is evidence that PIP5Ks are selective for certain acyl chain species of PI(4)P. We aimed to understand how inhibition of PIP5Ks impacts PIP3 production and whether they differentially support synthesis of a pool of PI(4,5)P2, that may be marked by a distinct profile of molecular species variants, which supply class I PI3Ks in a non-transformed human cell line (MCF10A cells). Using a combination of siRNA, Cas9/CRISPR-mediated gene knockout (k/o), recently derived selective, small-molecule inhibitors of PIP5Ks and mass-spectrometry-based lipidomic techniques, we attempted to address these questions. We found that MCF10A cells only express PIP5Kα and γ and that neither siRNA-mediated reduction nor k/o of either protein changed the levels or acyl chain profiles of any of the phosphoinositides in Epidermal Growth Factor- (EGF) stimulated MCF10A cells. We found that selective PIP5K inhibition reduced levels of PIP2 and EGF-stimulated PIP3 and increased levels of PIP, however, the acyl-chain-profiles of none of these lipids were significantly altered in MCF10A cells. We found EGF-stimulated Akt, EGF Receptor (EGFR) and MAPK phosphorylation were also reduced by PIP5K inhibitors in this cell line. To deconvolute these results, we tested the impact of a selective PI3Kα inhibitor (A66) and found it inhibited PIP3 accumulation and Akt phosphorylation and reduced MAPK phosphorylation but was without effect on total EGFR or its phosphorylation, suggesting some cross-talk between EGF-stimulated activation of class I PI3K and MAPKs in MCF10A cells.

articles.title: Perceived importance, self-rated performance satisfaction, learning stress, and practicum experiences among nursing students: A cross-sectional study with supplementary open-ended responses
articles.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined nursing students’ perceived importance and self-rated performance satisfaction regarding fundamental nursing practicum competencies, explored learning-stress scores across academic-achievement categories and psychological-counseling history, and descriptively summarized written practicum experiences. All 730 eligible third-year nursing students were invited; 28 did not participate, 702 returned signed consent forms and questionnaires, and 3 incomplete questionnaires were excluded, leaving 699 participants. Importance–performance analysis (IPA) used sample grand means (importance, 4.679; performance satisfaction, 4.503) as crosshairs. Paired importance–performance gaps and 95% confidence intervals were calculated, and 5,000 bootstrap samples assessed coordinate uncertainty and quadrant stability. Exploratory grade-group and counseling-history comparisons used analysis of variance and independent-samples t tests, respectively, with Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Exploratory adjusted linear models used heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) standard errors. The Core Competence in Fundamental Nursing Practicum Scale importance and satisfaction scores showed very high internal consistency (alpha/omega = .987/.987 and .985/.986, respectively), potentially indicating item redundancy. The nursing-process domain received high absolute ratings but fell below both sample grand means; its importance–performance gap was 0.229 (95% CI, 0.179–0.280). Communication and biomedical-science quadrant classifications were unstable across bootstrap samples, indicating sensitivity to the selected crosshairs. Exploratory analyses using the adapted learning-stress questionnaire showed higher reported stress scores among students in the lowest academic-achievement category. However, maximum-likelihood and ordinal diagonally weighted least-squares confirmatory factor analyses did not support the prespecified two-factor structure, and within-cluster dependence could not be modeled. Counseling-history comparisons were descriptive and did not evaluate counseling effectiveness. All 699 participants answered both open-ended questions; after non-substantive entries were excluded from thematic assignment, 217 non-mutually-exclusive segment-to-theme assignments remained. These findings describe students’ perceptions and exploratory associations rather than observed competence, validated stress constructs, or causal effects.

articles.title: Potential antimicrobial activity, antioxidant, and anti-wrinkle effects of Linum usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel
articles.abstract: by Ahmad M. Eid, Mohammed Hawash, Linda Issa, Areej Joma, Ansam Joma, Deema Tumeh Background Linum usitatissimum (L. usitatissimum) seeds have been reported to have several biological efficacies, such as antioxidant, anti-aging, sun protection, and antimicrobial actions. The present study aimed to develop L. usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel and evaluate its cosmeceutical and antimicrobial characteristics for use in topical applications. Method L. usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel formulations were prepared by optimizing the non-ionic surfactant (Tween® 20, Tween® 80, and Span® 80) using a self-nanoemulsifying technique, followed by the addition of Carbopol®. The droplet size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, and rheological behavior of the emulgel formulations were measured. In addition, the antioxidant activity, elastase inhibition activity, sun protection factor (SPF), and antimicrobial properties were evaluated. Results The prepared nanoemulgel had a homogenous appearance and a smooth, creamy texture and was found to have good spreadability and an acceptable adhesion to the skin. Tween® 80 gave the optimum nanoemulgel formulation, which had a droplet size of less than 200 nm. The crude L. usitatissimum seed oil was found to possess strong intrinsic antioxidant activity (IC50: 3.15 ± 0.46 µg/ml) when compared to trolox (IC50: 2.21 ± 0.23 µg/ml) and elastase inhibition activity (IC50: 17.3 ± 0.5 µg/ml) when compared with oleanolic acid (IC50: 10.2 ± 0.3 µg/ml), and a sun protection factor (SPF) of 5.87, suggesting significant potential anti-wrinkle and photoprotective properties. When incorporated into the optimized nanoemulgel formulation, the system showed considerably higher antimicrobial activity against S. aureus, MRSA, and C. albicans than the crude oil (p E. coli, E. faecium, or S. sonnei. Conclusion In conclusion, a novel L. usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel was prepared that shows promise for pharmaceutical and cosmeceutical applications.

articles.title: Retraction: An effective hotspot mitigation system for Wireless Sensor Networks using hybridized prairie dog with Genetic Algorithm
Social jetlag and DXA-derived adiposity in Korean adults: A nationwide study using the 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
articles.abstract: Background Social jetlag, the discrepancy between weekday and weekend sleep timing, is a behavioral marker of circadian timing mismatch and has been linked to obesity, mainly through conventional anthropometric measures. We examined its association with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived adiposity using the nationally representative 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES). Methods This cross-sectional study included adults aged ≥40 years reporting usual weekday and weekend bedtimes and wake times. Social jetlag, the absolute difference between weekday and weekend sleep midpoints, was categorized as <1 h, 1– < 2 h, and ≥2 h, with ≥2 h as the primary exposure. The primary outcome was DXA-derived total body fat percentage; subtotal and trunk fat percentages were key secondary outcomes. Height, weight, and waist circumference were obtained by standardized KNHANES examination. Survey-weighted linear regression was adjusted for age, sex, height, average sleep duration, income, education, smoking, alcohol use, physical activity, hypertension, and diabetes. Results Among 4,483 participants, 267 (6.0%) had social jetlag ≥2 h. In fully adjusted models, this group had higher total body fat percentage (β = 0.81 percentage points; P = 0.025), subtotal fat percentage (β = 0.86; P = 0.025), and trunk fat percentage (β = 1.01; P = 0.036), but not higher BMI or waist circumference. Associations persisted after adjustment for depressive symptoms, but were attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment for a chronotype-related proxy, and were not reproduced when social jetlag was corrected for sleep debt. Sleep duration variability showed no association. Conclusions Social jetlag ≥2 h was associated with modestly higher DXA-derived total and trunk body fat percentage, differences not captured by BMI or waist circumference. Because the associations did not persist in chronotype-adjusted or sleep-corrected analyses, conventional social jetlag may partly reflect compensatory weekend sleep. These findings are hypothesis-generating and need longitudinal confirmation.

articles.title: Study on hydration cementation and enhancement mechanism of grout-rock interface of PVA modified grouting material
articles.abstract: The weakly cemented sandstone aquifer in coal mine is prone to particle softening under mining disturbance and water-rock interaction, which induces the decrease of rock integrity and the development of water conducting channel, leading to the instability and failure of aquifer. To address the low early-age hydration activity of grouts containing a high proportion of coal gangue, discontinuous grout-rock interfacial bonding, and limited adaptability to weakly cemented sandstone, this paper uses cement and coal gangue(CG) as raw materials to prepare modified grouting materials with different polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) content. The uniaxial compression, XRD, FTIR and SEM test methods were used to systematically study the influence of PVA content on the performance of solid waste based slurry, the bearing characteristics of slurry-rock composite, the evolution of hydration products and the interface micro structure. The synergistic enhancement mechanism of PVA induced hydration cementation film coating and slurry-rock interface was revealed. The results show that: (1) High content of CG weakens the early hydration activity of cement slurry system. After PVA is added, the fluidity of slurry increases, the initial and final setting time is further prolonged, and the bleeding rate decreases, indicating that PVA can improve the flow stability and water retention performance of coal-based solid waste slurry. (2) PVA content has obvious dosage dependence on the bearing capacity of the grout rock complex. The peak stresses of the 0%, 0.3%, 0.6% and 1.0% PVA groups are 4.87 ± 0.14 MPa, 5.35 ± 0.06 MPa, 6.04 ± 0.09 MPa and 5.12 ± 0.09 MPa, respectively. The 0.6% PVA group shows relatively better mechanical properties within the test range of this paper. (3) Appropriate amount of PVA can promote the filling of C-S-H gel, AFt rod crystals and C-H flake crystals on the surface of sandstone particles and in the pores and fracture, and adsorb and coordinate through hydroxyl groups to form hydration products and flexible polymer film. The hydration products provide a rigid skeleton, and the PVA flexible film plays a buffering role in the interface bonding and deformation, and synergistically realizes the densification, continuity and toughness enhancement of the weakly cemented sandstone-grout interface. The experimental results show that 0.6% PVA content can achieve a better balance between slurry performance, water retention stability, interface hydration cementation and mechanical bearing capacity, which can provide material design basis for grouting reinforcement of weakly cemented aquifer, thickening of aquiclude and prevention and control of mining-induced water disasters.

articles.title: The impact of robot-assisted frameless brain biopsy on performance differences between junior and senior neurosurgeons
articles.abstract: Objective Frameless stereotactic brain biopsy is a standardized and routinely performed neurosurgical procedure, frequently carried out by residents under supervision in academic centers. Robot-assisted (RA) guidance has been introduced to standardize workflow and reduce operator-dependent variability. This study investigates whether RA frameless biopsy reduces experience-related performance differences between residents and attending neurosurgeons compared with a manually operated frameless system (MFS). Methods We performed a retrospective, non-randomized cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing RA frameless stereotactic brain biopsy for intracranial lesions at a tertiary academic center between 2021 and 2025. Outcomes included perioperative complications, diagnostic yield, and operative time, stratified by surgeon experience level (residents vs. attendings). Results were compared with those of a cohort operated with a MFS. Results A total of 98 procedures were analyzed (49 RA, 49 MFS). Across the entire cohort, total operative time was longer with RA than with MFS (115.6 ± 34.1 vs. 97.9 ± 27.2 minutes; p = 0.0036), primarily due to longer setup times. Diagnostic yield and complication rates were comparable between systems. Importantly, subgroup analysis demonstrated that residents using RA achieved operative times, diagnostic yield, and complication rates comparable to attending surgeons. In the MFS cohort, total operative time did not differ significantly between residents and attendings. Conclusions RA-assisted biopsy was associated with comparable diagnostic accuracy and safety relative to MFS. Robotic assistance was associated with smaller observed differences in operative efficiency between residents and attending surgeons, suggesting a potential role in bridging experience-related performance differences during neurosurgical training.

articles.title: The surgical outcome among children with congenital pseudoarthrosis of Tibia: Our 12 years of experience
articles.abstract: Background Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT) is a rare condition characterized by poorly perfused, invasive hamartomatous fibrous tissue that leads to fracture and pseudoarthrosis of the tibia. Management challenges include achieving union and preventing refractures. This study aims to evaluate surgical interventions and their outcomes in managing congenital pseudoarthrosis of the tibia in children. Materials and methods This retrospective study reviewed 70 CPT cases treated between 2010 and 2022 at Nepal’s only specialized center for children with physical disabilities. It assessed demographics, surgical procedures, and outcomes, with techniques including periosteal grafting and the Masquelet method. Union was defined radiologically, and analyses were conducted using MS Excel and SPSS. Results This study included 70 CPT patients; 40 male (57.1%) and 30 female (42.9%). The mean age at presentation was 3.84 years, with the first surgery at 5.38 years. Most cases were Boyd type 5 (71.43%) and Crawford type 4 (71.43%). Of 35 patients who underwent surgery, the union rate was 41.93% (13/31), with a refracture rate of 23.08% among unions. Periosteal grafting had a 50% union rate, while the Masquelet technique achieved 41.67%. Conclusions This study highlights the challenges in managing Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT), emphasizing the need for personalized surgical approaches based on patient age, limb length discrepancy, and classification. Effective patient counseling on risks and benefits is crucial for informed decisions.

articles.title: Unveiling Molecular Basis of Terminalia chebula in Modulating the AGE-RAGE-PRKCB Axis in Diabetic Nephropathy: Integrative Network Pharmacology and Computational Study
articles.abstract: by S. M. Riaduzzaman Niaz, Sumaia Jannat, Sheikh Abdullah Al Ashik, Md. Khairul Islam AbstractDiabetic nephropathy (DN), a progressive microvascular complication of diabetes, remains a principal cause of renal failure worldwide, yet its multifaceted molecular complexity continues to challenge effective therapeutic intervention. In this study, an integrative network pharmacology and computational modeling framework was employed to unravel the mechanistic basis of Terminalia chebula in mitigating DN pathology. A total of 357 phytoconstituents were retrieved from the IMPPAT 2.0 and PubChem databases and screened through SwissADME and pkCSM, yielding 14 bioactive, drug-like, and non-toxic compounds. Target prediction integrated data from SwissTargetPrediction, BindingDB, and CTD, while DN-related genes were compiled from GeneCards, OMIM, and transcriptomic datasets (GSE154561, GSE154881, GSE217709, and GSE30528). Overlapping targets were analyzed using STRING and Cytoscape to identify key hub proteins, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG enrichment analysis. Integration of compound- and disease-associated targets identified 173 overlapping genes. Enrichment analyses revealed significant involvement in the AGE–RAGE signaling pathway, implicating PRKCB as a key regulatory node linking hyperglycemia to oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. The Random Forest-based QSAR model (R2 = 0.91, RMSE = 0.41) denoted Luteolin and Quercetin as potent PRKCB inhibitors (predicted pIC₅₀ ≥ 6). Docking and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed stable PRKCB binding (RMSD ≤ 3.0 Å; ΔG_bind ≈ –122 kcal/mol), supported by DFT analysis indicating high chemical softness and strong charge-transfer potential. This integrative computational analysis suggests that T. chebula may exert renoprotective effects through modulation of the PRKCB-driven AGE-RAGE axis, with luteolin and quercetin emerging as promising natural inhibitors. Therefore, these computational findings provide potential molecular insight into the traditional therapeutic efficacy of T. chebula and a foundation for further experimental validation in DN.

Can artificial intelligence align with Indigenous science?
articles.abstract: As the use of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) increases, alarms are being raised about how the technology could replace human contribution, override human supervision, ignore ethical and technical guardrails, and cause increasingly irreparable harm to the environment. This creates potentially destructive outcomes for life on Earth. From a traditional Indigenous science perspective, such possibilities in themselves would be enough to immediately stop presently configured AI releases. In a Lakota context, science must ensure as little harm as possible is done to life. Therefore, AI as presently configured simply would not qualify to advance further from an ethical and scientific standpoint. Indigenous science asks something fundamentally different than what AI presently seeks to, or can, answer. But that does not mean that future forms of AI can never align with Indigenous science.

articles.title: Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression
articles.abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21 to 36% and of all county-level groupings by 9 to 58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38 to 61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of more than $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.

articles.title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago
articles.abstract: Cannabis is the world’s most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.

articles.title: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening
articles.abstract: Molecules that modulate protein-protein interactions, including through ternary complex formation, have been established as key therapeutics. Yet they can be challenging to discover, as standard screening approaches often lack throughput or fail to directly assay multibody interactions. We addressed this by combining DNA nanoswitch–based selection of nucleotide-encoded libraries with next-generation sequencing to create FIND (Functional Interaction–based Nanoswitch Discovery), which enables ultrahigh-throughput discovery of compounds that induce or increase protein-protein interactions. We demonstrate FIND by discovering nanobodies that stabilize the interaction between angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 and the receptor-binding domain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and by discovering agonists of peroxisome proliferator–activated receptor gamma from a DNA-barcoded small-molecule library. By enabling rapid discovery of molecular modulators, FIND could lead to new therapeutics across many conditions.

articles.title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat
articles.abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.

articles.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
articles.abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ . Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli–electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

articles.title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
articles.abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades—or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of “abruptness” during DO events.

articles.title: Obesity management medications: The way forward
articles.abstract: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

articles.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
articles.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)–based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

articles.title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems
articles.abstract: Hubbard systems are paradigmatic realizations of strongly correlated many-body systems. Introducing additional species breaks the SU(2) symmetry of the Hubbard model and leads to a wide variety of new exotic quantum phases. Here, we extended quantum gas microscopy to three-flavor Fermi lattice gases in the Hubbard regime. Relying on site- and flavor-resolved detection, we studied the phase diagram of the three-flavor Hubbard model and found signatures of flavor-selective localization and selective pairing at temperatures down to the tunneling energy scale. Our measurements were then compared with numerical linked-cluster expansion calculations. Further increase of phase space density may enable the observation of a distinct pair Mott phase at half filling and shows a path toward the study of color superfluidity and other aspects of quantum chromodynamics.

articles.title: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake
articles.abstract: How and when the subduction megathrust recovers its locking state after a great earthquake is important to understanding earthquake-cycle physics and future hazards. Here we report the delineation of the relocking process after the 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake with 14 years of postseismic seafloor geodetic observations. These data, combined with onshore geodetic observations, analyses of repeating earthquakes, and numerical modeling, reveal how the recovery of locking is interrupted by afterslip on the megathrust and accompanied by stress relaxation in the viscoelastic upper mantle. The results indicate that the megathrust has already arrived at a locking state today similar to that before the earthquake despite the ongoing stress relaxation. The acquired knowledge aids understanding of megathrust earthquake cycles at other subduction zones.

articles.title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
articles.abstract: Elastocaloric cooling (eC) uses shape memory alloys (SMAs) as energy-efficient, eco-friendly refrigerants. However, cost-effectively fabricating SMAs into fatigue-resistant, heat transfer–enhanced structures remains a key obstacle to commercialization of the eC technology. We introduce a “stamping and stacking” (S-S) method for producing porous, fatigue-resistant SMA structures. Honeycomb-like chips are stamped from nitinol (NiTi) thin sheets and then stacked into a layered tubular structure to increase heat exchange surface and at the same time avoid buckling and splitting failures encountered in existing SMA structures. The stacked structure endures >10 8 compression cycles and can deliver high specific cooling power of 3850 watts per kilogram. Our S-S method reduces fabrication costs by one order of magnitude compared with existing approaches, enabling mass production of eC refrigerant structures for commercial deployment.

Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
articles.abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients’ plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolven s, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

articles.title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children’s everyday speech
articles.abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child’s natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child’s ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child’s learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

articles.title: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression
articles.abstract: Cancer-associated hematopoietic abnormalities contribute to systemic immunosuppression. However, whether tumors can initiate localized extramedullary hematopoiesis to suppress antitumor immunity remains unclear. In this study, we identify a distinct form of hepatic hematopoiesis driven by liver metastasis–associated hematopoietic stem cells (LM-HSCs). Liver metastases establish ectopic periportal hematopoietic niches that recruit bone marrow HSCs through Kupffer cell–dependent C-C motif chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) signaling. Although LM-HSCs retain self-renewal and multipotency, cAMP response element–binding protein (CREB) activation skews their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, particularly annexin A1–positive (ANXA1 + ) immature neutrophils. These neutrophils produce glucocorticoids, which activate glucocorticoid receptor signaling in a paracrine manner and induce immune checkpoint receptor expression and functional anergy in CD8 + T and natural killer cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that liver metastases reprograms hepatic hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.

articles.title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease
articles.abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden therapeutic goals beyond reducing fat mass toward restoring adipogenesis, substrate turnover, thermogenic capacity, and tissue-niche function.

articles.abstract: Smart watches, health and fitness apps, and social media have fuelled an explosion in people’s access to health information about themselves and other people. Yet as these innovations serve up ever more individual data, and the reach of influencers and entrepreneurs on social media expands, so the challenges facing health workers accumulate.With social media awash with inaccurate posts about health, should doctors be wading in to offer medical advice or to correct misinformation? When influencers are pushing iron or testosterone supplementation to their followers (doi:10.1136/bmj-2026-101080 doi:10.1136/bmj-2026-101300),12 do doctors need to be more active in outlining the risks and benefits? articles.title: Mass in the liver
articles.abstract: A woman in her 30s presented with a six hour history of epigastric pain. She described a sudden onset tearing sensation which developed into a constant sharp pain of eight out of 10 severity, accompanied by pre-syncopal symptoms. She had no relevant medical history.Her blood pressure was 93/58 mm Hg. Vital signs were otherwise normal.Physical examination showed right upper quadrant tenderness and a firm mass at the inferior pole of the liver. Initially, a ruptured liver tumour or liver vascular malformation with haemorrhage was suspected.Liver function and serum tumour markers were tested and showed mildly raised levels of alkaline phosphatase (121.96 U/L; reference 35-100 U/L) and markedly raised levels of alpha fetoprotein (AFP) (2603.78 ng/mL; reference < 9 ng/mL).High levels of AFP raised suspicion of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). articles.title: Surrogate outcomes in clinical research
articles.abstract: A patient can live longer, feel better, or function better—these are direct, patient relevant clinical outcomes.1 Surrogate endpoints, in contrast, are indirect measures intended to predict such benefits. They can be used to shorten the duration of trials and make treatments available sooner, but that comes at the cost of greater uncertainty: improving a surrogate may not improve what ultimately matters to patients.A linked article by Lo and colleagues (doi:10.1136/bmj-2026-100618) presents the REASSurE framework for evaluating a single surrogate against a clinical endpoint.2 Developed through a Delphi survey, consensus meeting, piloting, and finalisation, the framework deserves credit for its transparent methods and reporting. It provides a structured checklist of mandatory or recommended items across four areas. Joint evaluation of multiple surrogates remains outside its scope.REASSurE aims to go beyond existing approaches, including the IQWiG (Institute for Quality and Efficiency in Health Care) framework,3 the Biomarker-Surrogacy Evaluation Schema,4 and the three-level...

articles.title: What doctors search for . . . and other research
articles.abstract: US Military mightAs most GPs know from bitter experience, requesting testosterone levels on healthy men creates a lot of extra worry and work, without clinical benefits. In July, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth controversially announced that US military personnel aged 30 years and older would be required to have annual testosterone screening. Researchers have estimated how many low testosterone concentration, or low T, results army medics will need to churn through, using cross sectional data from the Military Health and Nutrition Examination Study. Analysing morning testosterone levels from 479 men with a mean age of 30, they estimated that one in four active duty US Army personnel would have a morning testosterone below the American Urology Association’s cut off of 300 ng/dL (10.4 nmol/L). Scaled up to the whole US army, that’s 100 000 positive results.JAMA doi:10.1001/jama.2026.19794What doctors search forOpenEvidence is marketed as an AI copilot for doctors and claims...

articles.title: [Seminar] Eating disorders
articles.abstract: The eating and feeding disorders are serious psychiatric disorders at the mind–body interface, often with an exceptionally high burden for affected individuals, their families and supporters, and wider society. In anorexia nervosa, high acute medical risk and patients’ ambivalence about treatment can make a challenging combination that can impede engagement. First-line treatments for eating disorders are mainly psychological, with medications playing an adjunctive role. Novel biological and technology-based interventions are only slowly emerging.

articles.title: Activity and safety of first-line pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel in triple-negative breast cancer: a single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial
Co-targeting angiogenesis and immune checkpoints in breast cancer
Kenya's new cancer treatment targets test health system capacity
A consonant bias in dogs
articles.abstract: Do dogs perceive speech similarly to humans? A recent work by Morvai et al. suggests that dogs develop a focus on consonants to identify words, resembling results observed in humans. This is likely the result of massive exposure to language combined with an evolutionarily ancient ability to track regularities in the signal.

articles.title: 1D model simulations suggest biofilms can suppress cathodic H2 bubble formation
articles.abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) electrochemically generates H2 for the reduction of CO2 into acetate by acetogens. So far, the importance of a biofilm on the cathode of such systems remains under debate. Here, we investigated the role of cathodic biofilms through computational modelling. We developed MES-BIOFILM, a comprehensive one-dimensional model to simulate steady-state H2 and CO2 concentration gradients within cathodic biofilms, while accounting for the limited solubility of H2. The effects of key biofilm properties, including thickness, cell density and H2 consumption rate were analysed. Overall, our simulations indicate that cathodic biofilms play an important role in (1) minimizing H2 loss from the system through H2 consumption within the biofilm; and (2) suppressing H2 bubble formation by maintaining the H2 concentrations at the cathode surface below saturation. Our model predicts that the current density at which H2 bubbles begin to form can be increased by 5.5-fold relative to a bare electrode when biofilms exhibit a high cell density and high H2 consumption rate. This effect requires biofilms of at least 50 μm thickness, whereas CO2 diffusion limitations arise above 200 μm. These findings highlight the critical role of biofilms to increase MES performance, while requiring further experimental validation.

articles.title: A Binuclear Cluster Supports Functional Asymmetry in Dark-Operative Protochlorophyllide Reductase
articles.abstract: Many photosynthetic bacteria rely on the nitrogenase-like dark-operative protochlorophyllide oxidoreductase (DPOR) to sustain (bacterio)chlorophyll synthesis in the dark. DPOR couples ATP hydrolysis to electron transfer from a reducing component (L-protein) to a catalytic component (NB-protein) that reduces protochlorophyllide. NB-protein is an α 2 β 2 heterotetramer, and each heterodimeric half contains an active site and a [Fe 4 S 4 ] cluster. Although the two halves are identical, they react sequentially rather than in parallel. How the two halves communicate has remained unknown. Here we show, using Cu K-edge x-ray absorption spectroscopy and cryo-EM, that the NB-protein tetramer interface holds a binuclear, sulfur-bridged [Cu 2 S 2 ] cluster. Each Cu is reduced and three-coordinate, with short Cu-S and Cu-Cu distances (2.26 and 2.62 &Aring). Mutagenesis excludes the nearest cysteine as the bridging ligand, supporting inorganic sulfide as the most likely sulfur donor. To our knowledge, this is the first sulfide-bridged dicopper cluster identified in a protein. The cluster is conserved in three purple non-sulfur bacteria and connects the BchB C-terminal helices that contact opposing active sites. Loss of Cu abolishes DPOR activity and asymmetric L-protein binding without disturbing overall fold. We propose that the cluster relays substrate-binding information between active sites, suggesting a metal-mediated mechanism for cooperativity in nitrogenase-like enzymes.

articles.title: A Kernel-Spectral Index for Single-Neuron Input-Output Complexity
articles.abstract: The computational capacity of individual neurons in the brain is a central problem in computational neuroscience and an increasingly relevant link between neuroscience and AI. Recent work fitting artificial neural networks to detailed cortical pyramidal neurons showed that reproducing their millisecond-precision input-output behavior can require temporal convolutional networks with five to eight layers, suggesting that cortical neurons may function as deep computational units inside brain circuits. Yet current quantitative studies of single-neuron complexity are largely surrogate-based; consequently, the obtained results are difficult to interpret, and the process often demands massive computational resources. We introduce the Spectral Complexity Index (SCI), a white-box measure that represents presynaptic histories with an explicit kernel geometry and quantifies how many ordered spectral modes are needed to explain somatic response energy. Across 35 biophysically detailed human and mouse cortical neuron models, SCI yields a statistically significant separation of the two species, strongly agrees with the DNN-based Functional Complexity Index on these cells (Spearman correlation: {rho}=0.797), and remains stable under sampling and kernel perturbations. Additionally, compared to existing methods such as FCI, the computational cost of SCI is reduced to approximately 1/10 or less. SCI turns single-neuron complexity from a black-box surrogate property into an interpretable spectral object, enabling reproducible, fast, and efficient comparisons of neuronal computation across cells and species.

articles.title: A Staphylococcus phage recombination cassette that enables recombineering across distant bacteria
articles.abstract: Modifying bacterial genomes with phage recombinases, a process termed recombineering, has enabled precise genome editing, but its reach is limited by host specificity: each new organism generally requires its own recombinase to be identified and optimized. Using known phage recombination genes as synteny anchors, we mined Staphylococcus genomes and recovered a diverse collection of phage recombination cassettes, spanning the RAD52-like annealase superfamily (Sak, Erf) and the RAD51/RecA-like Sak4 family. Functional testing of representatives in S. aureus identified several highly efficient systems that support recombineering. We engineered the most efficient of these into a single-plasmid tool that yields markerless editing in S. aureus in four days. Notably, where other recombineering systems rely on host-specific factors for nuclease evasion and ssDNA loading, this cassette encodes both activities itself: a predicted broad-spectrum nuclease inhibitor and a dedicated single-stranded DNA-binding protein. We therefore tested the cassette across phylogenetically distant hosts, and observed recombination in Streptococcus pyogenes , Enterococcus faecium , Francisella novicida , and Escherichia coli . These results identify a self-sufficient class of phage recombination systems and provide a portable tool for

articles.title: A Urinary Metabolomic Signature Associated with Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth in Children with Short Bowel Syndrome
articles.abstract: Direct sampling of the small intestinal microbiome is challenging. Urinary metabolites may offer a noninvasive approach to studying microbial functional activity. We used clinically available gas chromatography/mass spectrometry to profile urinary organic acids in 94 children with short bowel syndrome, comparing those with clinically defined small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO; n=21) with those without SIBO (n=73). SIBO-associated metabolites included microbial fermentation products, dietary derivatives, and host metabolic intermediates. Metabolites enriched in SIBO mapped to aromatic amino acid metabolism, including tryptophan and tyrosine pathways, consistent with altered microbial fermentation. Many associations persisted after adjustment for intestinal anatomy, age, antibiotic exposure, and nutritional composition. These findings identified a urinary metabolic profile associated with clinically defined SIBO in children with short bowel syndrome and support further evaluation of urinary metabolomics as a noninvasive approach to studying small intestinal microbial function.

articles.title: A comparative transcriptomic framework across kidney organoid, assembloid, and transplantation models
articles.abstract: Human kidney organoids recapitulate key aspects of renal development and have emerged as valuable platforms for disease modeling, nephrotoxicity screening, and therapeutic development. The field now includes a wide range of emerging protocols with distinct cellular compositions and maturation states, which complicates systematic comparison and model selection. Here, we integrated single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomes from 11 studies spanning kidney organoid and assembloids, both in vitro and following transplantation, benchmarked against fetal and adult kidney references. Transcriptional maturation toward adult identity is compartment specific and does not correlate with protocol complexity. Assembloid protocols show the most adult-like podocyte and distal nephron signatures, transplantation is associated with enhanced tubular oxidative metabolic features, only protocols incorporating ureteric progenitors reliably generate collecting-duct lineages, and no protocol achieves mature adult proximal tubule identity. Annotating against either fetal or adult kidney reference alone leads to misassignment, because early fetal nephron epithelium transcriptionally resembles injury-dedifferentiated adult proximal tubule cells. Assembloid and transplantation models share elevated mechanosensing pathway expression independently of vascularization. Together, these findings provide a framework for kidney organoid model selection.

articles.title: A hawkmoth's point of view - Innate symmetry preferences are informed by floral display and foraging function in an insect pollinator
articles.abstract: Floral visual cues are key for flower recognition and feeding in many pollinators. In insects, innate preferences for characteristic floral colour and pattern cues can guide naïve foragers during their initial foraging. Symmetry is suggested to be one such foraging cue, since it is a remarkably conserved floral feature, with flowers mainly displaying radial or bilateral morphologies. Insect pollinators like honeybees, bumblebees, and hoverflies have been found to distinguish symmetry from asymmetry spontaneously or through learning. However, whether innate preferences for floral symmetry types, i.e. radial or bilateral, influence naïve flower choice, and whether such preferences are linked to functional benefits during foraging remains uncertain.We investigated innate symmetry choice and its associated foraging function in the hummingbird hawkmoth ( Macroglossum stellatarum ). Besides relying on pattern cues for flower choice, these hawkmoths feed while hovering, making symmetry a valuable visual cue for flight and proboscis control. In choice assays, the hawkmoths' innate preferences for symmetry types depended on the floral display planes, with considerable differences between the horizontal and vertical displays. Tracking the hawkmoths during foraging revealed that in both display planes, the innately preferred patterns increased foraging success by guiding approach and nectary search. While an analysis of flowers visited by hawkmoths in nature did not reveal the same link between symmetry and display plane, a majority of plant species with vertically displayed flowers showed features matching those innately preferred by the hawkmoths. In this study, we provide the first instance of display-dependent innate foraging preferences and highlight how visuomotor strategies in nectivorous insects may have coevolved with flower features.

articles.title: A protein language model for domain, functional site, and variant effect prediction
articles.abstract: Protein sequence databases are growing far faster than experimentally curated annotations, limiting functional interpretation of newly identified proteins and coding variants. We developed PALM, a protein annotation language model that jointly predicts domain and functional-site occurrence, while preserving overlapping and nested annotations through a soft-target objective. PALM integrates ESM2 with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), learned layer aggregation, and a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder.
