PALM was trained on ~15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences spanning 17,951 domain and 1,383 site classes. Across 2.3 million held-out proteins, PALM achieved domain- and site-occurrence F1 scores of 0.941 and 0.877, respectively, and retained substantial performance in proteins with <20% sequence identity to the training and validation data. PALM also substantially outperformed ESM3 annotation baseline. Without training on variant-pathogenicity labels, PALM embedding disruption distinguished 151,823 ClinVar missense variants more accurately than ESM2 embedding disruption (AUROC 0.835 versus 0.710), and combining PALM embedding disruption with the ESM2 likelihood-ratio signal reached an AUROC of 0.877. The same combined zero-shot score outperformed AlphaMissense on a benchmark dataset on 128,161 missense variants, that were derived from literature but not present in ClinVar database. At the protein level, PALM embeddings showed stronger CATH-Gene3D superfamily organization than frozen ESM2 and ESM3 embeddings, and improved prediction of experimental activation and repression effects when combined with ESM2. In a downstream case study, we demonstrated the ability to use PALM-derived embedding as proxy of deep mutational scanning (DMS), showcasing the broad application of PALM. Together, PALM converts curated residue-level knowledge into transferable and mechanistically interpretable representations that connect protein sequence, function, and variant consequence.

articles.title: ACTIVATION OF THE ARYL HYDROCARBON RECEPTOR REDUCES VISCERAL HYPERSENSITIVITY IN A MOUSE MODEL OF COLITIS IN REMISSION
articles.abstract: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is expressed on gut-projecting transient receptor potential vanilloid-1 (TRPV1)+ nociceptors, but whether it has a role in regulating abdominal pain remains to be determined. Approximately 50% of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients experience chronic abdominal pain, even when their inflammatory disease is in remission. Previous work has shown that tryptophan metabolism to indole derivatives is reduced in IBD patients. Since microbial tryptophan metabolites (indole derivatives) serve as ligands for AhR, we hypothesized that reduced AhR activation contributes to enhanced pain sensitivity. We used a post-colitis mouse model of visceral hypersensitivity to examine the role of AhR as a mediator of nociception. AhR activation using both natural and synthetic agonists reduced visceral hypersensitivity in both male and female post-colitis mice. Conversely, pharmacological inhibition of AhR blocked the antinociceptive effects of indoles. Mechanistically, AhR activation by indole-3-pyruvic acid (IPyA) increased the transcription of the inward rectifying potassium channel Kir2.2, in TRPV1+ neurons and markedly reduced neuronal activation within the dorsal horn of the spinal cord. Metagenomic analysis revealed sex differences in indole-producing bacteria, with control males exhibiting enriched abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila and Alistipes compared to post-colitis males and female controls. These findings demonstrate that oral IPyA supplementation in post-colitis mice attenuates visceral hypersensitivity in part through activation of nociceptor AhR, providing insights that support the therapeutic targeting of AhR to treat abdominal pain in IBD patients in remission.

articles.title: Age-specific pediatric templates improve EEG source-reconstructed biomarkers in children
articles.abstract: EEG source reconstruction requires an anatomical head model, ideally constructed from individual magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans. In developmental studies of children and adolescents, however, MRIs are rarely available. Researchers therefore routinely rely on adult templates, such as the FreeSurfer average (fsaverage), despite substantial anatomical changes throughout development. How much this reliance on adult models biases downstream EEG biomarkers remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether age-specific pediatric templates offer a better alternative to fsaverage for EEG-derived biomarkers in children and adolescents, using individual MRI-based reconstruction as the reference. We analyzed eyes-closed resting-state EEGs from 384 Healthy Brain Network participants aged 5.5 to 17.5 years. For each participant, we tested three anatomical models: their individual MRI, an age-specific pediatric template from a series spanning ages 6-17 at one-year intervals, and the adult fsaverage template. We compared four EEG biomarkers in childhood and adolescence: absolute power, relative power, long-range temporal correlations quantified with detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA), and functional excitation-inhibition (fE/I) ratio. Pediatric templates agreed more closely with individual MRI-based biomarkers in both developmental groups and had fewer parcels with significantly different biomarker values than the adult template, except for absolute power in older adolescents. We conclude that when individual MRI is not available, age-specific pediatric templates match individual MRI-based EEG biomarker values more closely than the adult template across all four biomarkers up to approximately 12 years of age and should be the preferred choice at least up to this age.

articles.title: An open-access neuroimaging-compatible virtual town task for assessing human spatial navigation
articles.abstract: Spatial navigation is a cognitive skill that draws on multiple processes such as learning, decision-making and memory, which are often updated on a second-by-second timescale. However, many existing virtual paradigms designed to assay spatial navigation cannot target these processes as they unfold or are not designed for integration with concurrent neurophysiological recording. Here, we present and demonstrate our open-access task for neuroimaging: NAturalistic Virtual Assessment of Navigation (NAVAN) combining high-resolution behavioural tracking and integration with electroencephalography. We report data from this task, in which fifty-three participants completed a wayfinding navigation paradigm across twenty-four trials. Navigational efficiency improved significantly following repeated exposure to the environment, although efficiency declined across trials within each block. Self-reported spatial ability (assessed by the Santa Barbara Sense of Direction) predicted performance during early environmental exposure, suggesting concurrent validity. We demonstrated the feasibility of recording electroencephalography during the task, with in-game events streamed and aligned to the neural recording. The task provides researchers with access to detailed behavioural measures and can be adapted by modifying features such as trial number and difficulty. We also provide a step-by-step implementation guide to support reuse and customisation across experimental settings.

articles.title: Asymmetric detection of relative speed during motion-based figure-ground segregation
articles.abstract: Visual motion can support figure-ground segregation when a local region moves at a different speed from its background, but whether faster- and slower-than-background targets are detected equally well, and how any asymmetry depends on background speed and motion reliability remains incompletely understood. We measured relative-speed detection thresholds in four human observers using an eight-alternative forced-choice localization task. On each trial, one of eight random-dot patches at 10-degree eccentricity moved either faster or slower than a surrounding moving background. Relative-speed detection thresholds were measured with adaptive staircases at five background speeds (2.5-30 deg/s) under 100% and 60% motion coherence. In every observer, slower targets required larger relative-speed differences for detection than faster targets. This increment-decrement asymmetry was strongest at low background speeds and diminished as speed increased. Reducing motion coherence elevated thresholds overall but disproportionately impaired detection of slower targets, amplifying the asymmetry, most strongly at the lowest measurable speeds. Under 100% coherence, increment detection showed approximately Weber-like scaling from 10 to 30 deg/s, whereas under reduced coherence both increment and decrement Weber fractions decreased with increasing background speed. Relative-speed detection therefore depends on the sign of the speed difference, background speed, and motion reliability. The faster-target advantage is consistent with faster-speed weighting reported in cortical area MT and with natural-scene statistics showing that figural regions tend to move faster than their backgrounds, suggesting that relative-speed sensitivity may contribute to motion-based figure-ground segregation. More broadly, such increment-decrement asymmetries can reveal biases in how sensory signals are represented and read out.

articles.title: BCL10 Gain-of-Function Impairs Germinal Center Participation by Naive B Cells and Cooperates with BCL6 to Drive Extrafollicular Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
articles.abstract: BCL10 gain-of-function (GoF) mutations occur in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) cases of the BN2/C1 molecular subgroup. These alterations activate CARD11-BCL10-MALT1 (CBM) signaling and drive resistance to multiple drug classes, but their role in disease pathogenesis is incompletely understood. In particular, interactions between BCL10 GoF and additional DLBCL oncogenes are undefined. Here, we show BCL10 GoF in naive B cells blocks their participation in germinal center (GC) reactions and permits transformation to DLBCL with a non-GC B-cell phenotype. Most clinical cases with BCL10 GoF also carry translocation of the BCL6 proto-oncogene, and we show that co-activation of these two lesions together promotes pronounced oncogenic synergy. Detailed single-cell analyses of underlying premalignant B-cell populations revealed expansion of extrafollicular memory B cells whose gene-expression program remains prominent in resulting lymphomas in both the mouse and corresponding human tumors. We therefore define a novel role for BCL10 activating mutations in enabling BCL6 lymphomagenesis.

articles.title: Bayesian phylogenetic inference accounting for recombination in whole bacterial genomes
articles.abstract: Recombination is a major evolutionary force in bacteria, and ignoring it distorts phylogenies and can invalidate downstream analyses such as dating. We present ClonalFrame2, a new software for Bayesian phylogenetic inference from whole bacterial genomes that accounts for recombination. It replaces both ClonalFrame and ClonalFrameML while using the same evolutionary model, in which both mutation and recombination events occur on the branches of the clonal genealogy. The locations of recombination events are integrated out of the likelihood using a hidden Markov model, so the algorithm targets only the clonal genealogy and three recombination parameters. Ancestral sequences are recomputed whenever the tree changes and are used to propose efficient topology updates. We validated the method by analysing data-free datasets, which recovered the prior, and by comparing the approximated likelihood with the exact one on simulated data. Across 100 simulated datasets of 100 genomes each, the recombination parameters were accurately recovered, and trees inferred while accounting for recombination were many times more accurate than when ignoring it. In Staphylococcus aureus ST239, we showed that accounting for recombination gave a stronger temporal signal and a more robust dated phylogeny. In Neisseria gonorrhoeae, we identified interesting patterns of clustered recombination events happening repeatedly across the branches of the tree.

articles.title: Benchmarking Statistical Methods for Differential Composition Analysis in Population-Scale Single-Cell Data
articles.abstract: Population-scale single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data capture cellular composition across cohorts ranging from several dozen to thousands of individuals, enabling the detection of cell-type composition differences between conditions. These differences reveal cellular shifts in disease pathogenesis and suggest potential targets for therapeutic intervention. However, differential composition analysis in scRNA-seq data is challenged by the unique features of cell count data, such as compositionality, prevalence of zeros, overdispersion, and confounding by technical and biological covariates. While this analysis is routinely performed, no study has yet systematically evaluated existing methods. Here, we benchmarked 12 methods for differential composition analysis using three population-scale scRNA-seq datasets with diverse and representative characteristics. Analyses of real data revealed low agreement across methods, while permutations and simulations based on the real data demonstrated excessive false discoveries for most methods. Overall, LOCOM emerged as the top-performing method that controls the false discovery rate while maintaining good statistical power, followed by ANCOM-BC and linear regression with centered-log-ratio transformation. Integrating evidence from real-data analyses and data-informed permutation and simulation experiments, we provide practical guidance tailored to common real-world challenges in differential composition analysis.

articles.title: Classifying tumors from broad category to hierarchical molecular subtype: an interpretable hierarchical framework for precision oncology
articles.abstract: Precise tumor subtype classification is important for guiding personalized treatment, characterizing tumor heterogeneity, and investigating molecular mechanisms. However, most existing multi-label classification models use flat architectures and do not fully exploit the inherent hierarchical relationships and biological constraints among tumor types, which limits their performance and interpretability in complex, fine-grained pan-cancer classification. Here, we present the cancer Hallmark-based Hierarchical Recursive Model (HHRM) for pan-cancer hierarchical multi-label classification. HHRM integrates hierarchical label structures with recursive neural networks, enabling simultaneous modeling of multi-level dependencies from broad cancer categories to specific subtypes. We trained the model on a comprehensive pan-cancer cohort of 11,476 samples spanning 26 primary cancer types and 405 subtypes across up to eight hierarchical levels. HHRM achieved an accuracy of 0.7924 for predicting hierarchical tumor subtypes and was further evaluated on a validation dataset of 887 samples. Compared with other hierarchical modeling frameworks, HHRM achieved higher accuracy in all three output modes. Ablation experiments showed that replacing the hallmark-based graph convolutional network reduced model performance. On an independent dataset of 1,608 breast cancer samples, HHRM also achieved an accuracy greater than 0.86. Finally, we combined SHAP with a network-based method to rank and analyze predictive genes at different levels of the tumor hierarchy, which identified both known and potentially novel biomarkers for cancer diagnosis. In conclusion, to our knowledge, HHRM is the first hierarchical model for multi-level tumor subtype classification. Its competitive performance, combined with post hoc biological interpretation, suggests potential value for precision cancer diagnosis.

articles.title: ClearGel: a thermoresponsive hydrogel for chronic, near-millimeter two-photon imaging through the intact skull
articles.abstract: The intact skull remains a fundamental barrier to high-resolution two-photon neuroimaging in live mice. Existing skull-clearing methods, however, cannot simultaneously provide deep cortical access, spatial selectivity, reversibility, and biological safety. Here we introduce ClearGel, a thermoresponsive hydrogel that undergoes rapid in situ gelation upon contact with the skull, confining the clearing agents to the targeted region while sustaining their release over time. ClearGel routinely enables two-photon imaging down to approximately 800 μm through the intact skull-a depth statistically equivalent to open-skull windows and substantially surpassing all prior approaches. It supports user-defined clearing patterns from focal sites to whole-skull coverage, allows repeated imaging over 14 days through a reversible optical interface, and, critically, enables awake functional imaging of both neuronal Ca2+ activity and the more elusive cAMP dynamics at single-cell resolution. ClearGel requires only simple topical application-no craniotomy or skull thinning-and provides a minimally invasive, chronic-compatible optical window for longitudinal studies of cortical function in behaving mice.

articles.title: Common attentional mechanisms, but distinct computational dynamics, across Statistical and Reward Learning
articles.abstract: Past experience guides attention through statistical learning (SL) and reward learning (RL). Yet, whether they do so through similar neural and computational mechanisms remains unclear. In a first EEG visual-search experiment, we tested whether RL establishes latent spatial representations, previously demonstrated for SL. Afterwards, we directly compared RL and SL in a double-session experiment. Using multivariate decoding, Experiment 1 showed that high-reward locations could be decoded before target onset following a task-irrelevant, spatially-unspecific visual perturbation. Experiment 2 revealed that SL and RL established comparable neural representations, and similarly facilitated target selection and evidence accumulation (drift-rate). However, combining Rescorla-Wagner and Drift Diffusion Model revealed slower learning-rate for RL than SL. Pupillometry further tracked spatially selective expectation violations during SL, but reflected increased arousal during RL. Together, our results reveal how the brain routes distinct computational algorithms (probability estimation versus value caching) into a unified attentional priority map.

articles.title: Compartment-Resolved Matrisome Shifts During Postnatal Tendon Maturation in Mice
articles.abstract: Tendons acquire their load-bearing capacity during the first month of postnatal growth, driven by the extensive remodeling of the extracellular matrix (ECM). While the role of specific individual components to this process have been well characterized, a comprehensive assessment of how the tendon matrisome changes during this critical window is lacking. This, in part, is due to the challenges associated with solubilization of mature ECM, which is underrepresented by conventical proteomic approaches. To address this, we performed compartment-resolved proteomics on murine Achilles and plantaris tendons at postnatal days 0 (P0), P14, and P28. Sequential extraction methods leveraged a CHAPS-soluble fraction, capturing cellular and soluble matrisome proteins, from the insoluble mature ECM fraction, solubilized by guanidine hydrochloride and hydroxylamine hydrochloride and separately analyzed by label-free quantitative LC-MS/MS. Analysis shows that the two compartments followed distinct trajectories during maturation. The insoluble matrix was dominated by collagenous proteins, which increased from 95% to over 99% of the identified signal intensity, and its composition was largely established by P14. Within the soluble matrisome compartment, collagens increased from 50% to over 60% by P14, accompanied by dynamic regulation of proteins implicated in collagen processing (P4HA1, PCOLCE), crosslinking (LOX, LOXL2), and regulators of collagen fibril assembly and growth (DCN, BGN, FMOD, THBS3, THBS4). Beyond these established regulators, we observed dynamic regulation of less-characterized fibril-associated proteoglycans (KERA, OGN, CHAD), matricellular (COMP, POSTN, MATN2), and angiogenic regulatorily proteins (SERPINF1, ECM1). Together, this work establishes a comprehensive protein-level reference for postnatal tendon maturating, provides new insights into the molecular regulation of functional tendon development.

articles.title: Cytomegalovirus Infection in Human Cortical Organoids Induces Unique Developmental and Viral Substates
articles.abstract: Human Cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is a ubiquitous {beta}-herpesvirus with exposure resulting in a life-long infection. Severe HCMV disease can occur in conditions of insufficient immunity, and this includes congenital infection. Infection of the developing brain can cause severe birth defects including microcephaly and sensorineural hearing loss. Also, increasing evidence suggests the contribution of HCMV infection in adult CNS diseases. Studying HCMV replication and its impact on CNS is restricted by host tropism and anatomy. In these studies, we define the impact of infection on healthy iPSC-derived cortical organoids using single cell RNA sequencing. We uncovered 16 cell type clusters in uninfected tissues using the Human Neural Organoid Cell Atlas. Following infection by HCMV expressing GFP, several clusters were altered in both GFP-positive and GFP-negative populations, including the likely transition of the Glutamatergic/GABAergic Neuron cluster into a CMV-Infected Cell cluster. Expressions of viral genes varied between cells and cell types, requiring us to introduce a TC (temporal class) indexing score to account for varying stages of infection. This analysis in conjunction with machine learning approaches revealed cells that are likely producing de novo HCMV along with several viral sub-states. Several viral sub-states had significant enrichments of genes involved in epithelial-to-mesenchymal (EMT) transition, including expression of EpCAM. We independently verified HCMV-induction of EpCAM protein expression in cortical organoids and glutamatergic neurons. In summary, our studies reveal unique features of HCMV infection of cortical organoid tissues, including varying viral sub-states and tropisms, and introduced new approaches to analyze these multi-dimensional complex data sets.

articles.title: Dated public evidence and known genes for retrospective evaluation of gene prioritization
articles.abstract: Retrospective evaluation of gene prioritization needs evidence that was public before the evaluated genes became known. Public resources are open and reproducible, but are distributed as current releases that also contain evidence produced after the genes became known. This Data Descriptor presents per-gene evidence tables for four areas (oncology, inflammatory bowel disease, metabolism and psoriasis) from public resources. Every feature carries a time axis, the date of its release in a calendar of 183 archived releases of 20 sources, and a leakage axis, a provenance class (A to E) with two risk grades that define five feature sets. Nineteen lists of known genes are dated by the first trial, study, release or classification that supports each gene. They cover targets of a kind of drug, targets of drugs tested in a disease, and genes associated with a disease. The oncology lists also carry the first day the trial registry showed the trial.

articles.title: Dendrite Control Theory: A Unifying Framework Bridging Neuronal Morphology And Dendritic Voltage Behavior
articles.abstract: Control theory and dendritic computation have revolutionized their respective fields, yet they rarely converge. Here, we use control theory as a framework to reveal how dendritic morphology and synaptic input organization constrain structural resilience and energy cost. Treating diverse dendritic trees as connected network nodes, we demonstrate that the degree of structural symmetry dictates easy- versus hard-to-access control states. Notably, control inputs restricted solely to peripheral terminal branches are mathematically sufficient to govern the voltage states of the entire dendrite and soma, granting striking resilience against input loss elsewhere. Conversely, limiting input dimensionality amplifies voltage fluctuations and metabolic costs. These findings expose fundamental biophysical trade-offs between wiring cost, functional flexibility, robustness, and energy efficiency, suggesting interneurons generally exhibit higher resilience while excitatory neurons feature superior controllability. We introduce 'Dendrite Control Theory' as a rigorous engineering framework linking neuronal morphology directly to computation and robustness, offering a new neuroscience research paradigm.

articles.title: Diversification of budding yeast polarization dynamics after compensatory experimental evolution
articles.abstract: Essential cellular processes evolve under strong selection, yet protein networks underlying conserved functions can vary substantially. To what extent evolution constrains the intracellular dynamics of proteins performing essential functions is currently largely unknown. Here, we characterize budding yeast polarization phenotypes along a previously established evolutionary recovery trajectory, compensating for the loss of near-essential polarity gene BEM1. Through quantitative live cell imaging, we show that loss of BEM1 weakens and destabilizes polarization. Surprisingly, in recovered evolved lineages, protein dynamics change significantly compared to the ancestor: most notably, presence of main regulator Cdc42-GTP is strongly decreased, while polarisome member Spa2 localizes more slowly into mobile foci. Although separate phenotypic characteristics are only weakly constrained, we find evidence of effective protein-independent localization modes, revealing signs of convergence along the evolutionary trajectory. Together, our results show that evolution can restore global cellular function without conserving microscopic organization, instead giving rise to novel molecular phenotypes.

articles.title: Dynamic allocation of MurJ coordinates bacterial growth and division
articles.abstract: Rod-shaped bacteria grow by inserting peptidoglycan into the lateral cell wall during elongation and into the septal cell wall during division. These two modes of growth are driven by distinct peptidoglycan synthesis machineries that consume the shared precursor Lipid II and must be coordinated so that cell enlargement remains matched to division. However, how cells spatially allocate this shared precursor, and whether Lipid II translocation itself contributes to this coordi-nation, remain unclear. Here we show that the spatial distribution of the essential Lipid II flippase MurJ coordinates this balance in Escherichia coli. Increasing nonseptal MurJ abundance shifted cell-wall synthesis toward elongation and reduced septal synthesis. Single-molecule tracking revealed that MurJ diffuses throughout the membrane but is transiently captured at the division site, rather than stably incorporated into the septal synthesis machinery. This recruitment requires active septal cell-wall synthesis, but not ongoing Lipid II synthesis or flipping, indicating that MurJ recruitment is coupled to the active synthesis machinery rather than to substrate availability or transport. Thus, activation of septal synthesis creates transient MurJ capture at the division site, providing a mechanism to preferentially supply Lipid II for septal growth during cytokinesis. These findings reveal a capture-and-release mechanism that dynamically enriches MurJ at active division sites and thereby coordinates elongation and division in bacterial cells.

articles.title: Earl Grey ParTEA: scalable, consistent transposable element annotation from pangenomes to deep phylogenetic scopes
articles.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) are major drivers of genomic diversity, yet understanding their mobility and functional impact requires their accurate description in genomes. TE annotation is still typically performed genome-by-genome. TEs are often shared between some members of the same or closely related species. Hence, TE annotation with a library from a single reference misses families absent from that assembly, whereas building independent per-genome libraries fails to consistently surface shared TEs, hindering comparison. Here, we present Earl Grey ParTEA, a fully automated Snakemake pipeline extending the functionality of Earl Grey for comparative TE annotation across genome panels. ParTEA builds a single non-redundant TE library from all input genomes, resolves chimeric consensus sequences, and uses this shared library to annotate every genome, enabling direct comparison of TE family diversity, abundance, shared and private content, and activity landscapes. Optional modules provide TE library saturation analysis, BUSCO-based assembly quality control, and phylogenetic ordering of outputs. We applied ParTEA to sets of genomes spanning evolutionary scales: ten Arabidopsis thaliana accessions, ten Drosophila species, and ten species spanning the fungal kingdom. The Drosophila TE library expanded from 343 to 1,852 curated families including a previously missed rolling circle element with over 6,000 copies in D. miranda. The proportion of TE families shared across all genomes was highest within A. thaliana (97.3%), 37.7% across Drosophila species and only 0.5% across the set of fungi. ParTEA is available through Bioconda and represents a computationally efficient reproducible framework for comparative TE analysis in the era of large-scale genome analyses.

articles.title: Early Increases in Hippocampal Synchrony Predict Chronic Epileptiform Burden in a Temporal Lobe Epilepsy Model
articles.abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE), the most common focal epilepsy, is often drug-resistant and arises predominantly in the hippocampus. Disease severity is conventionally assessed by seizure frequency and duration, yet epileptiform activity outside discrete seizures may also track disease progression. Whether this activity reflects hippocampal network reorganization as part of epileptogenesis, and whether such reorganization predicts chronic severity, is unknown. Here, we combined longitudinal two-photon calcium imaging of hippocampal CA1 neurons with repeated 24-hour EEG recordings that quantified epileptiform burden in the same pilocarpine treated mice over 16 weeks. CA1 firing and synchrony rose acutely, subsided during a latent period, and increased again chronically, with synchronized firing organized into brief waves that propagated in a consistent direction. Epileptiform burden followed a similar temporal trajectory and increasingly contained electrographic seizures. CA1 synchrony correlated with epileptiform burden and stratified mice into groups with distinct neuronal and electrographic outcomes. CA1 synchrony measured within three weeks of pilocarpine induction predicted chronic epileptiform burden, identifying early hippocampal synchrony as a candidate imaging biomarker and pointing to an early window for intervention in TLE.

articles.title: Evaluating State-Transition Models in Short Resting-State fMRI with Continuous-Dynamics Controls
articles.abstract: Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are widely used to describe changes in resting-state functional MRI as transitions between a finite set of inferred brain states. However, continuously varying brain activity can produce similar apparent transitions, raising questions about their biological validity. We tested whether discrete and continuous brain dynamics could be distinguished by predicting subsequent fMRI measurements, and if temporal filtering affects this distinction. We compared hidden Markov models (HMMs) with vector autoregressive (VAR) models, which predict signals from preceding measurements without assuming discrete states. Each time point contained signals from the seven Yeo functional networks. Both models used the same preceding observations to predict the next, with accuracy measured by the log probability density assigned to the observed signals. Across 864 simulated conditions, HMMs performed better in 139/144 unfiltered discrete-state cases, whereas VAR performed better in 67/72 continuous cases. Changing only the filter during testing increased the number of continuous cases favoring HMMs from 2/72 with fixed filtering to 68/72, despite unchanged underlying dynamics. We also analyzed resting-state fMRI from 270 ADNI participants (90 cognitively normal, 90 with mild cognitive impairment, and 90 with dementia). VAR outperformed HMM in 160/184 datasets with at least 180 time points and 60/86 shorter recordings. In simulations, HMMs inferred directional state transitions even from smoothly evolving activity without discrete switching. Thus, apparent fMRI state transitions do not necessarily indicate discrete underlying dynamics. Their interpretation requires comparison with continuous models and attention to temporal filtering.

articles.title: Failed allogeneic corneal lenticules show fibrosis and identity loss without dominant T cell rejection
articles.abstract: Failed allogeneic corneal stromal lenticules develop progressive opacity, but the state of the implanted tissue is unknown. Here we show that six explants from three patients occupy a fibrotic integration-failure state with scar-matrix production and loss of corneal identity without a dominant T cell rejection program. Scar-matrix, transparency and corneal-identity programs separated every patient from eight unimplanted donor controls, the last defined by independent human single-cell references. Calibrated immune programs and repertoire reconstruction distinguished the explants from canonical adaptive rejection. Exchange reduced interface reflectivity initially, followed by recurrent opacity in two patients and corneal steepening with declining uncorrected acuity in the third. In non-scarring rabbit repair, identity moved toward the uninjured state as backscatter returned toward normal despite increasing similarity to the explant-derived expression signature. Within one culture experiment, marked scar suppression accompanied opposite identity responses. Tacrolimus and rapamycin likewise suppressed canonical rejection while moving identity in opposite directions. Resveratrol combined reduced scar-associated programs and increased identity with improved graft appearance in the source study. These findings establish classic-rejection activity and tissue integration as separable axes and direct treatment of failed lenticules from escalating immunosuppression toward control of stromal remodeling and preservation of corneal identity.

articles.title: FeatureMAP enables network-guided interpretation of untargeted metabolomics
articles.abstract: Untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) metabolomics generates thousands of features, but incomplete metabolite annotation and reliance on predefined pathways limit their biological interpretation. Here we present FeatureMAP, an LC-MS feature-centric computational framework that integrates multi-evidence metabolite annotation, network-guided refinement, metabolic module discovery, and structured large language model-based functional interpretation. Across ten public datasets, FeatureMAP improved MS1-based metabolite candidate prioritization while reducing annotation redundancy. In semi-synthetic benchmarks, FeatureMAP recovered coordinated metabolic perturbations, achieving 92% recovery of a simulated perturbation, and distinguished concurrent metabolic processes. Controlled benchmarks further evaluated functional interpretation under competing metabolite-level signals. Based on FeatureMAP, we additionally developed PhenoMAP, a phenotype-aware knowledge graph comprising 12,929 dysregulated metabolic modules from 501 human metabolomics studies spanning 326 phenotypes. Module-level comparisons revealed reproducible metabolic similarities across independent studies and biologically supported relationships among phenotypes. Application to Alzheimer's disease cerebrospinal fluid and cellular datasets identified convergent membrane-lipid alterations and implicated galactose-linked glycosphingolipid remodeling. Together, FeatureMAP and PhenoMAP enable network-grounded interpretation of incompletely annotated LC-MS metabolomics data and systematic investigation of metabolic dysregulation across biological conditions.

articles.title: Feedback Valence, Prediction Error, and the Limits of Computational Attribution in Symptom-Related EEG
articles.abstract: Feedback-locked electroencephalography (EEG) responses are often interpreted using model-derived prediction errors (PEs), although signed PE can be strongly coupled to feedback valence in binary-outcome tasks. We revisited a published anxiety-related EEG association using two open probabilistic-learning datasets to examine measurement reliability, predictor separability, and participant-level recovery. In the primary dataset, greater trait anxiety was associated with a larger negative-minus-positive FCz theta response among 46 participants with elevated depressive symptoms after adjustment for depression severity. The association also differed between the sampled depression-symptom groups. The feedback contrast showed useful within-session reliability, but matched delta and P3-minus-N2 analyses did not establish theta specificity. Within participants, feedback valence and signed PE were highly correlated (r = -0.964). Exact-design simulations showed that population-level model discrimination could succeed despite poor recovery of individual neural slopes. Participant-specific learning-model refits recovered overall signed PE more consistently than the within-valence variation needed to distinguish it from feedback valence. An independent dataset reproduced the FCz feedback contrast in untreated and placebo cohorts but lacked trait-anxiety scores. Adding signed PE to valence yielded a small held-out predictive improvement under one reinforcement-learning specification, with limited support across sessions and no comparable support under the dual-rate model or in placebo. Together, these findings support a symptom-related feedback EEG association while constraining its theta-specific and participant-level computational interpretation.

articles.title: Ferroptosis of selective progenitor cell types during embryogenesis ensures proper organ morphogenesis
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis, a form of non-apoptotic cell death, is induced by lipid peroxidation resulting from an intracellular accumulation of labile iron (1). While apoptosis is involved in embryonic development (2), the role of ferroptosis in embryogenesis is unknown. Here, we report that the ferroptosis process occurs in the embryonic lung and kidney at mid- and late-gestation. In these tissues, pro-ferroptotic cells include subpopulations of the Sox9+ distal lung epithelial cells and the Flk1+ vascular progenitors in the kidney glomeruli. Lipidomic analysis reveals mixed lipid peroxidation as the driver for ferroptosis. The role of ferroptosis in the morphogenesis of these organs was confirmed by triple positivity of TfR1, 4-HNE and TUNEL, mitochondrial defects, cell membrane breakage, dead cell remnants, single-cell RNA-sequencing of a ferroptosis gene signature. Genetic manipulation of Gpx4, an endogenous inhibitor of ferroptosis. Further, genetic knockout or transgenic overexpression of Gpx4 affects lung and kidney development and results in cystic lungs and kidneys. Notably, conditional deletion Gpx4 results in hypoplasia of the lung epithelia and of the renal glomeruli, while transgenic overexpression of Gpx4 resulted in atelectasis with collapsed lung alveoli and hypertrophic glomeruli. Together, these findings show that ferroptosis regulates lung and kidney morphogenesis by acting in key progenitor cell populations during gestation. Supplementation of iron or polyunsaturated fatty acid during pregnancy has implications for organogenesis.

articles.title: Fluorescence microscopic evidence for intracellular silicon storage pools in diatoms and their partial separation
articles.abstract: Diatoms are unicellular algae that occur ubiquitously in almost every salt- and freshwater habitat on earth. Silicic acid is taken up from the environment and stored in intracellular silicon storage pools (SSPs) to form species specific silica based cell walls (frustules). During biosilica formation in the silicon deposition vesicle (SDV), the silicon is transported from SSPs into the SDV. The present contribution describes the fluorescence microscopic visualization and quantification of silica solely formed from SSPs under silicon starvation. Labeling with the fluorescence marker PDMPO demonstrates continuing cell growth and cell division without silicon uptake from the environment. The SSPs of Cyclotella nana may account for up to 1/3 of total cellular silicon and intracellular concentrations up to ca. 540 mM, significantly beyond the saturation level (2 mM). The chemical state and localization of SSPs within cells are yet unclear. Here, we report a method for subcellular fractionation of C. nana by density gradient centrifugation. Quantification of cytoplasmic silicon yields 3 to 10% of the total cellular silicon corresponding to intracellular concentrations of ca. 50 to 160 mM. Labeling with NMR active 29Si shows that this silicon occurs as condensed silica, i.e., silicic acid is converted into condensed silica after uptake. However, the detected intracellular silicon concentrations are lower than the value of ca. 540 mM predicted by the fluorescence experiments. It is thus concluded that the missing SSP silicon is either present in the form of large aggregates or compartments. Alternatively, they may also be bound to cell wall biosilica.

articles.title: Functional Assessment and Extended Culture of Human Pediatric Cardiac Tissue Slices for Preclinical Testing
articles.abstract: Background: Living human myocardial slices preserve native tissue architecture, but their application to pediatric cardiac physiology or prolonged functional testing remains limited. We adapted a passive culture method for small surgical myocardial specimens obtained from patients with congenital heart disease (CHD). Methods: Atrial and ventricular specimens were obtained from 41 cardiac surgery patients (7.7{+/-}11.1 years; 1 day-49 years). Myocardial tissue was sectioned into slices and studied acutely, or maintained under free floating, rocking cell culture conditions without electrical or mechanical stimulation. Calcium transients were recorded in response to external pacing (0.2-2 Hz) at baseline, and after isoproterenol or norepinephrine exposure. Selected preparations underwent viability, histological, and gene expression analyses. Results: Pacing evoked calcium transients were recorded from all four cardiac chambers, exhibiting expected frequency-dependent shortening. Mean interslice and intraslice coefficients of variation were 11.1% and 7.6%. Viability was 85.8 {+/-} 5.6% post-slicing and 78.8 {+/-} 5.0% after 3-5 hours. Calcium transients remained detectable through 178 days in atrial and 119 days in ventricular slices. Calcium transient durations were relatively stable during extended culture. Beta-adrenergic agonists shortened calcium transient durations (isoproterenol: 32% atrial, 25% ventricular at 0.3 Hz); responses to isoproterenol persisted to approximately 120 days in selected atrial slices and 60 days in ventricular slices. Selected histological features were preserved, although some extracellular matrix and apoptosis related transcripts changed. Conclusions: Small surgical specimens support repeated physiological measurements and pharmacological testing during extended passive culture, providing a platform for human developmental and disease-specific cardiac research.

articles.title: Genome evolution and glycosyltransferase diversification shape asperosaponin biosynthesis in Dipsacus asperoides
articles.abstract: Deciphering the genomic and enzymatic features associated with high-abundance specialized metabolism is important for understanding and engineering bioactive natural product biosynthesis. Asperosaponin Ⅵ, a hederagenin-based saponin, accumulates at exceptionally high levels in Dipsacus asperoides roots and is by far the predominant triterpenoid saponin. Here, by integrating a chromosome-level genome assembly with comparative genomics, transcriptomics, metabolite profiling, and biochemical characterization, we reconstructed a major biosynthetic route to asperosaponin Ⅵ and identified diversification of triterpenoid-associated gene families. Functional analyses revealed an ordered glycosylation sequence in which DaUGT73GZ2 preferentially accepts C-3-glycosylated substrates retaining a free C-28 carboxyl group, thereby establishing a C-3-before-C-28 glycosylation order during asperosaponin Ⅵ biosynthesis. Phylogenetic and biochemical analyses further uncovered functional differentiation among UGT85CA enzymes involved in C-3 arabinosylation, while genomic and expression analyses revealed lineage-specific patterns of pathway gene duplication and transcriptional regulation. Together, these findings identify genomic, enzymatic, and transcriptional features associated with the distinctive, high-abundance triterpenoid saponin profile of D. asperoides roots and provide a framework for understanding and engineering triterpenoid saponin biosynthesis.

articles.title: Genome-wide chromatin accessibility during early embryogenesis in a generalist cichlid fish
articles.abstract: Background Lake Malawi's haplochromine cichlids are one of the most rapid and species-rich vertebrate adaptive radiations known, generating hundreds of species within < 1 million years, yet how regulatory regions shape their embryonic development remains poorly understood. Astatotilapia calliptera, a generalist riverine lineage and proxy for the ancestral stock that seeded this radiation, offers a developmental chromatin baseline against which regulatory divergence in specialised lineages can be compared. Results We generated genome-wide ATAC-seq profiles of A. calliptera embryos across three developmental stages (3, 7 and 12 days post-fertilisation, dpf), identifying 550,876-701,889 accessible chromatin peaks per stage. Accessible chromatin was enriched at gene promoters and at both highly conserved and accelerated conserved noncoding elements at every stage. The functional repertoire of accessible-promoter genes shifted across development, from early patterning at 3 dpf to the broadest regulatory repertoire at 7 dpf, and an increasingly neural- and locomotory-behaviour-enriched repertoire by 12 dpf, coinciding with post-hatching motor maturation. Differential accessibility showed that chromatin opening, rather than closing, dominates the earliest transitions (3 vs 7 and 3 vs 12 dpf), driven mostly by general metabolic genes, whereas the smaller, later 7 vs 12 dpf transition combined targeted gains at tissue-remodelling and apoptosis genes with losses at genes governing early neural and retinal patterning; almost all of these losses (96%) were at promoters that had opened between 3 and 7 dpf, indicating transient rather than sustained opening. Transcription factor (TF) footprinting identified stage-specific regulatory activity among developmentally important TFs, while the broader TF-promoter network remained topologically stable across all three stages, built around conserved hub regulators of core neural and sensory patterning genes e.g., SOX2, FOXG1, PTF1A, SOX10. This suggests that wiring is established early and largely maintained, following the hourglass model, with developmental progression driven by changes in activity of this conserved programme. Conclusions Together, these findings establish the first embryonic epigenomic resource for A. calliptera, revealing a developmental chromatin landscape of broad early opening and progressive functional specialisation, and providing a comparative framework for understanding how regulatory evolution has shaped Lake Malawi cichlid diversification.

articles.title: Genomic architecture of the major histocompatibility complex genes in the Neotropical Midas cichlid
articles.abstract: The Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) plays a central role in vertebrate adaptive immunity, yet its genomic architecture remains poorly characterized in many evolutionary model systems, including the Neotropical Midas cichlid Amphilophus citrinellus. Here, we integrate chromosome-level functional genome annotation, transposable element (TE) profiling, transcriptomics, phylogenetics, molecular selection analyses, and protein structural modeling to characterize its MHC repertoire. We identified 298 MHC-related loci across 18 chromosomes, including 30 MHC-I genes, 15 MHC-IIA genes, and 20 MHC-IIB genes, together with antigen-processing and regulatory components. MHC-I and MHC-II genes were located on different chromosomes, consistent with the MHC non-linkage pattern characteristic of many teleosts. Gene duplication and phylogenetic patterns support birth-and-death evolution, resulting in a structurally diverse repertoire with broadly conserved protein domains. TE distribution varied across MHC genomic regions, suggesting a potential contribution to genomic diversification. Molecular selection analyses detected positive selection in MHC-I and IIB genes, whereas MHC-IIA showed more limited evidence of positive selection. Expression patterns varied across tissues, with relatively high expression of several MHC genes in the spleen and thymus, while structural models retained characteristic MHC folds. Phylogenetic analyses placed previously characterized MHC sequences with broader multilocus repertoire, suggesting that population level diversity may reflect both allelic polymorphism and variation among paralogous loci. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive chromosome-resolved characterization of the MHC repertoire in a Neotropical cichlid and establish a genomic framework for investigating immune gene diversification during the Midas cichlid radiation.

articles.title: Growth-driven mechanical buckling as a mechanism of age-related tortuosity in human cerebral arteries
articles.abstract: Human cerebral arteries become increasingly, sometimes abnormally, winding with age, but the mechanical basis of this change remains incompletely understood. To examine how arterial bends form and what sets their spacing, we modeled a cerebral artery as a slender elastic vessel supported by surrounding tissue. The distance between its ends remains constant, and the vessel can bend only in a plane tangent to the brain surface. As its natural length increases, axial compression builds until the vessel buckles. Bending partly relieves the compression, and the resulting waves grow in amplitude as elongation continues. Arterial bending stiffness and tissue support determine the wavelength, which is much larger than and proportional to vessel diameter, with comparatively weak dependence on other parameters. Numerical simulations captured a pre-buckling phase, rapid amplification of waves, and slow post-buckling growth during continued elongation. We evaluated these predictions using three-dimensional centerlines of cerebral arteries reconstructed from magnetic resonance angiography in healthy adults. Older age was associated with greater arterial length and excess-length ratio. For arterial waves oriented mostly parallel to the brain surface, wavelength increased with vessel diameter. Both this relationship and the observed wavelength-to-diameter ratio were consistent with model predictions. However, wave amplitude was not significantly associated with age. Overall, the modeling and imaging results support growth-driven buckling and post-buckling deformation under spatial constraint as a plausible mechanical explanation for age-related cerebral arterial tortuosity. This framework links vascular aging to growth-driven instability and pattern formation, with potential applications to diseased arteries beyond the brain.

articles.title: Gut Roseburia hominis-derived 10-hydroxystearic acid alleviates metabolic disorder by restoring hepatic fatty acid metabolism
articles.abstract: Metabolic disorders and health-promoting dietary interventions represent complementary contexts of metabolic impairment and improvement, providing an opportunity to identify gut microbial taxa associated with both disease status and dietary response. Here, we integrated five independent human cohorts spanning metabolic disorders and dietary interventions and identified Roseburia hominis as a gut microbial taxon that consistently decreased in metabolic disorders and increased after dietary interventions. Beyond species abundance, strain-level genetic variation in R. hominis provided additional information for distinguishing metabolic disorder status and stratifying cardiometabolic severity. Integration of phenotype-associated variants with circulating metabolomics prioritized ohyA, encoding an oleate hydratase, as a candidate functional determinant linking R. hominis genetic variation to host metabolic heterogeneity. An ohyA-based genetic burden score was associated with adverse cardiometabolic traits and changed longitudinally during dietary intervention, while circulating metabolites statistically accounted for part of the associations between ohyA variants and host phenotypes. Functional experiments demonstrated that R. hominis OhyA protein converts oleic acid to 10-hydroxystearic acid (10-HSA), whereas an OhyA carrying five prioritized missense substitutions showed markedly impaired enzymatic activity. In high-fat diet-fed mice, 10-HSA attenuated body-weight gain, improved glucose homeostasis and insulin sensitivity, and reduced dyslipidemia and hepatic steatosis. Multi-omics profiling revealed limited remodeling of the gut microbiota but pronounced hepatic transcriptional and metabolic responses, characterized by activation of PPARα-associated lipid-metabolic pathways, altered fatty-acid oxidation and desaturation, and remodeling of hepatic lipid composition. Together, these findings establish a diet-responsive R. hominis-OhyA-10-HSA axis linking microbial variation to host metabolic dysfunction and show that 10-HSA can improve metabolic health in mice.

articles.title: Harnessing catalytic knowledge to guide enzyme discovery and evolution with AlphaEnzyme
articles.abstract: Retrieving an enzyme for a target reaction provides a starting point for evolution, but predicting how to improve it remains difficult. This requires connecting evolutionary information with the structural and chemical context of catalysis. Here we present AlphaEnzyme, an enzyme foundation model built on a structure-grounded representation of an enzyme paired with its reaction, from which catalytic compatibility, kinetics and mutational response are read out together. On a time-separated benchmark, AlphaEnzyme achieves a top-1 catalyst retrieval success rate of 30.1%, against 17.2% for the strongest baseline. Michaelis constant predictions achieve the highest rank correlations among the compared methods, reaching 0.64 for enzymes sharing at most 40% identity with the kinetic training set. The model also enriches high-fitness TrpB variants at a budget of 16 candidates without target-specific fitness training. In prospective transaminase engineering, several prioritized variants exceed the parent, with the best design yielding a 30.4-fold increase in product signal in a lysate-based assay while retaining (R)-selectivity. Together, AlphaEnzyme provides a common molecular basis for selecting starting enzymes and prioritizing sequence changes for their improvement.

articles.title: HiSpoT: a novel one-tube dual-barcode PCR method for NGS spoligotyping amplicon library preparation in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis remains one of the leading infectious causes of death globally, making rapid, accurate, and affordable strain typing essential for effective outbreak tracking and epidemiological surveillance. To address the limitations and high costs of current typing methods, we developed a novel one-tube, dual-barcode PCR method for preparing targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) amplicon libraries for spoligotyping of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC), which we termed HiSpoT (High-throughput Spoligotyping by Targeted next generation sequencing). The assay targets 43 conserved spacer oligonucleotides in the CRISPR direct repeat (DR) region and is presented here together with the previously unpublished, difficult-to-design dual-barcode primer set needed to multiplex 96 samples in a single tube. HiSpoT is accurate, fast, high-throughput, and low-cost, eliminating the need for a commercial NGS library preparation kit. Because HiSpoT is PCR-based, the resulting spoligotypes remain directly comparable with the large PCR-based spoligotype databases accumulated over decades, enabling rapid outbreak tracking and biogeographic characterization of the tuberculosis burden of a country, while higher-resolution whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data are obtained. Analysis of 288 clinical MTBC isolates from Israel (2020-2022) demonstrated a broad range of genetic lineages, and comparison of 79 isolates analyzed by both HiSpoT and WGS showed 70% full concordance, with essentially all discrepancies attributable to single-spacer insertion-element disruptions of PCR primer sites. We also present two open-source Google Colab Python tools, Spoligotyping_MTBC_gcl and its condensed HiSpoT_Spoligotyping_v8_ready VIBE variant, freely available on GitHub, which automatically process Illumina paired-end fastq output from HiSpoT or WGS and report binary and octal spoligotypes, spoligo international types (SIT), and MTBC family assignments with accompanying quality-control reports.

articles.title: Hidden infections: Linking parasite ecology, fish health and stakeholder perceptions in Nile tilapia aquaculture in central Kenya
articles.abstract: Parasite infections in farmed fish may remain unrecognised when fish-health assessment relies mainly on visible signs. We investigated metazoan parasite occurrence, parasite diversity and community composition, associations between gill-parasite burden and histological alterations, and stakeholder recognition of fish-health problems in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) aquaculture in central Kenya. We examined 157 fish from 20 farms, assessed gill histology in 137 fish, measured water quality once per farm, and collected questionnaire and interview data from 48 stakeholders. Five metazoan parasite groups were recorded, with monopisthocotylans the most prevalent (36.3%). Higher monopisthocotylan burden was associated with a greater cumulative number of gill lesion types (odds ratio 1.86, 95% CI 1.43-2.42, p < 0.001), whereas copepod burden was not. Parasite diversity was higher in the larger operational pond category across all three Hill-number orders (p = 0.006-0.008), and parasite-community composition differed between categories (PERMANOVA, p = 0.034), although these comparisons were exploratory because only four farms were in the larger category and farm category overlapped with county. Single-time-point water-quality measurements showed no clear associations with parasite burden, diversity or community composition after multiple-testing correction. Farmers and fisheries or extension officers recognised signs of poor fish health but rarely identified parasites as a specific cause, and routine diagnostic confirmation was uncommon. The findings reveal a gap between laboratory detection of parasite-associated gill alterations and farm-level recognition and diagnosis.

articles.title: Higher-order metabolic interactions among oral commensals gate pathobiont expansion through succinate-driven pH modulation
articles.abstract: Despite advances in defining microbiome shifts associated with inflammatory mucosal diseases, the ecological interactions that constrain or facilitate pathobiont expansion remain poorly understood. Using a six-species synthetic oral microbial community and factorial interaction screening, we identified a higher-order interaction governing the growth of the periodontal pathobiont Porphyromonas gingivalis. The core community member Veillonella parvula was the strongest positive determinant of P. gingivalis growth, but this effect was substantially reduced by the health-associated commensal Actinomyces oris. A. oris-mediated antagonism resulted from extracellular acidification and was enhanced under anaerobic conditions. Genetic dissection of A. oris fermentation revealed that lactate dehydrogenase (ldh1) contributes to anaerobic lactate production, but ldh1 deletion only partially relieved P. gingivalis inhibition. Instead, succinate, produced through a succinate dehydrogenase/fumarate reductase pathway (sdh2), emerged as the principal driver of acidification and P. gingivalis suppression. At high cell densities, however, V. parvula consumed both lactate and succinate, reversing acidification and restoring conditions permissive for P. gingivalis growth. To assess the relevance of these interactions in vivo, we analyzed subgingival microbiome from 1,355 adults, including 555 with detectable P. gingivalis. Among these individuals, P. gingivalis abundance was negatively associated with Actinomyces abundance after adjustment for periodontitis severity, whereas this association was attenuated at high V. parvula abundance, consistent with the interaction observed in vitro. Together, these findings identify succinate as a previously unrecognized mediator of interbacterial antagonism and reveal how higher-order metabolic interactions among oral commensals regulate pathobiont expansion through pH modulation, with protective effects shaped by oxygen availability and metabolic cross-feeding.

articles.title: Hijacking Cellular S-Acylation with Molecular Assemblies Rewires Oncogenic Signaling
articles.abstract: KRAS-mutant cancers are generally treated by suppressing oncogenic signaling. Here, we investigated whether endogenous lipidation machinery could instead be used to spatially perturb that signaling. The thioester-bearing peptide precursor Stb-DPhe-DPhe-SAc (1) potently reduced PANC-1 cell viability and formed a palmitoylated product in treated cells. Synthetic palmitoylated 1 displayed increased assembly propensity, while fluorescent analogue 2 accumulated at the Golgi in a 2-bromopalmitate-sensitive manner. Compound 1 increased plasma-membrane-associated KRAS staining and ERK/AKT phosphorylation and induced pronounced LC3B and p62 remodeling. Inhibition of palmitoylation suppressed Golgi accumulation, attenuated the LC3B response, and rescued cell viability. These findings support a model in which cellular S-acylation drives organelle-localized molecular assembly that perturbs KRAS localization, oncogenic signaling, and associated stress responses. This work identifies endogenous lipidation machinery as a synthetic handle for spatial control of cancer signaling.

articles.title: Human lymphatic organoids reconstruct convergent developmental routes to functional lymphatic vessels
articles.abstract: The lymphatic vasculature maintains fluid balance, regulates immune surveillance, and supports tissue repair, yet how human lymphatic vessels arise and acquire specialized functions remains poorly understood. Here, guided by single-cell and spatial analyses of human embryos, we found that both lateral plate and paraxial mesoderm converge on venous endothelial intermediates with cardinal vein-like characteristics prior to lymphatic specification. Informed by these developmental trajectories, we generated three-dimensional lymphatic organoids from human pluripotent stem cells through two distinct mesodermal routes. The organoids formed capillary-like vascular networks with emerging button-like junctions and distinct endothelial and stromal programs. The lymphatic organoids were transcriptionally benchmarked to human fetal lymphatic endothelium. The organoids supported immune-cell interactions and antigen accumulation and, following transplantation, exhibited interstitial tracer uptake and transport. These findings establish a platform for investigating how distinct developmental origins shape human lymphatic specification, vascular organization, and function, with applications to lymphatic disease modeling and tissue repair.

articles.title: Human-caused ignitions and plant invasion drive fire-regime change in a dryland biodiversity hotspot
articles.abstract: Dryland ecosystems cover much of Earths terrestrial surface and are increasingly affected by climate warming, land-use change, and biological invasion. The Sonoran Desert of western North America, a biodiversity hotspot that historically experienced infrequent fire, exemplifies how these global-change processes are driving ecosystem transformation through the emergence of novel disturbance regimes. Using records of more than 73,000 wildland fire events, we quantified anthropogenic and environmental controls on fire ignition, size, and spread across the Sonoran Desert. Human-caused ignitions accounted for 95.5% of all recorded fires since the early 1990s and were concentrated near roads, buildings, and other areas of human activity, particularly during late spring. In contrast, lightning-caused ignitions were rare within the Sonoran Desert and occurred primarily in adjacent montane forests during late summer months. Consistent with broader trends across the western United States, fires were typically largest when they ignited far from roads, where access is limited, and fire management often relies on indirect attack strategies. Pre-fire annual and perennial herbaceous vegetation both promoted fire spread, with detectable effects at cover values as low as 5%, while bare ground reduced fuel connectivity and constrained fire growth. Rather than exhibiting a distinct threshold response, fire spread increased linearly with herbaceous cover, suggesting that even modest increases in fine fuels can alter fire behavior in this historically fuel-limited ecosystem. Together, our results illustrate that human ignitions determine where fires occur, whereas herbaceous fuels determine whether those ignitions spread, driving fire-regime transformation across an iconic North American desert. Managing and adapting to this novel fire regime will require coordinated efforts to reduce human-caused ignitions, limit invasive herbaceous fuels, maintain bare-ground interspaces, and rapidly suppress fires. More broadly, our findings identify the mechanisms controlling fire regime change in dryland ecosystems and provide a framework for anticipating ecosystem transformation under ongoing global change.

articles.title: Improving phosphoproteomic kinase activity inference by contextual refinement of Kinase Library relationships
articles.abstract: Kinase activity inference from phosphoproteomic data relies on kinase-specific substrate sets defined by kinase-substrate relationship (KSR) priors. Kinase Library (KL) expands candidate substrate coverage using experimentally derived kinase specificity profiles, but its predictions reflect sequence compatibility rather than established intracellular regulation. We benchmarked KL-expanded KSR priors using 222 perturbation phosphoproteomic samples covering 396 annotated activation or inhibition events across 78 kinases. Broad KL expansion increased the number of scoreable kinases from 108 to 391, but reduced perturbed-kinase discrimination, directional accuracy and ranking performance. Higher error rates occurred among kinases with limited curated substrate support, while broad expansion also increased redundancy among inferred activity profiles. To improve the reliability of motif-derived relationships, we constrained KL-derived KSRs using predicted protein co-localization and protein-association evidence. Protein-association filtering consistently improved inference performance, reduced activity redundancy and provided a more favorable accuracy-coverage balance than co-localization filtering. The selected protein-association-filtered prior retained activity estimates for 308 kinases with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) above 0.75 and extended inference to 200 kinases not scoreable using curated KSRs, which were significantly enriched for dark kinases. These newly scoreable kinases showed structured activity patterns across perturbation contexts and interpretable signaling associations. Our results show that protein-association evidence can refine motif-derived KSR priors while preserving broad kinome coverage, providing a practical framework for more reliable phosphoproteomic kinase activity inference.

articles.title: LCN2+ Astrocytes Mark a Pro-inflammatory Astrocyte State Associated with Secondary Brain Injury After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis
articles.abstract: Cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) is a cerebrovascular disorder with unique pathophysiological characteristics. Although the mortality rate during the acute phase has declined in recent years, the cellular mechanisms underlying secondary brain injury and long-term neurological dysfunction after CVT remain poorly understood [1,2]. In this study, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of brain tissues from a murine CVT model to systematically characterize the cellular landscape following CVT and identified a reactive astrocyte state characterized by high expression of Lcn2. This astrocyte subset was markedly enriched after CVT. Notably, despite the absence of significant changes in the overall proportion of astrocytes, this population exhibited enhanced inflammatory/cytokine response signatures, ferroptosis-related stress responses, and vascular-immune microenvironment remodeling programs, suggesting that the major alteration of astrocytes after CVT is driven primarily by state transition rather than cellular expansion. Pseudotime trajectory analysis further demonstrated that Lcn2+ astrocytes were predominantly localized at the late stage of the trajectory and displayed sustained upregulation of multiple inflammation- and stress-associated genes, supporting their characterization as a late-stage reactive astrocyte state under CVT conditions. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed extensive predicted interactions between this subset and myeloid cells, vascular-associated cells, as well as neuronal/synaptic populations, indicating its potential involvement in dynamic remodeling of the lesion microenvironment. Cross-model integration analysis further revealed the presence of Lcn2-high astrocytes in the middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model; however, their expression breadth and intensity were generally weaker than those observed in CVT, suggesting that this cellular state may represent a common reactive framework following cerebrovascular obstruction, while being particularly pronounced in CVT. Furthermore, genetic deletion of LCN2 alleviated CVT-induced brain tissue injury in vivo, providing functional evidence supporting the detrimental role of the LCN2-associated pathological state. Collectively, our study identifies a distinct Lcn2-high reactive astrocyte state after CVT that is closely associated with inflammatory amplification, ferroptosis-related stress, and microenvironmental remodeling. These findings provide new cellular insights into the mechanisms underlying secondary brain injury after CVT and highlight potential targets for therapeutic intervention. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. articles.title: Light-dependent conversion of body color change pattern during zebrafish development
articles.abstract: Zebrafish ( Danio rerio ) shows body color change in response to light: when light comes, it whitens body color. Our previous study has shown that larval zebrafish as early as 5 days post-fertilization (dpf) have this capacity fully developed whereas 2-dpf larvae exhibit light-induced darkening in sharp contrast (Shiraki et al. 2010). Here, we discovered that the conversion in body color change pattern between 2 dpf and 5 dpf is light-dependent: larvae reared in darkness exhibited light-induced darkening of body color, reminiscent of 2-dpf larvae. We also found that a 14-h light exposure on 3 or 4 dpf is sufficient to trigger this conversion, and that the conversion by light on 4 dpf still occurred after ablation of most exorh -expressing pineal photoreceptor cells. The dark-reared larvae had significantly lower transcription levels of pmch and pmchl , which encode melanin-concentrating hormone precursors, than the LD-reared larvae. However, the levels in larvae that had undergone the conversion (3-L and 4-L) were not significantly different from those in dark-reared larvae, indicating that the reduced pmch/pmchl expression alone does not account for the conversion. In conclusion, light exposure in rearing is indispensable for the maturation of body color change ability in larval zebrafish through a regulatory mechanism independent of exorh -expressing pineal photoreceptors.

articles.title: Lipidic α-synuclein fibrils catalyze the formation of pathological mature fibrils
articles.abstract: The aggregation of α-synuclein into amyloid fibrils is a hallmark of a collection of neurodegenerative diseases termed synucleinopathies, including Parkinson's disease (PD). Interactions between α-synuclein and lipid membranes modulate α-synuclein aggregation and can produce protofibril structures consisting of both protein and lipid, termed lipidic fibrils. These lipidic fibrils can mature into mature fibrils, which resemble ex vivo fibrils extracted from Lewy bodies found in post-mortem brain samples of PD patients. Here, through the combination of experiments and kinetic theory, we study the influence of lipids and lipidic fibrils on the formation of mature fibrils. We find that lipidic fibrils catalyze mature fibril formation via a heterogeneous primary nucleation mechanism, which lowers the activation energy barrier of mature fibril formation relative to lipid-independent primary nucleation. The final stage of the reaction is governed by mature fibril elongation becoming limited by the rate at which protein monomers dissociate from the metastable lipidic fibrils, confirming that fibrils form in order of stability following Ostwald's Rule of Stages. This mechanism is validated using the small molecule inhibitor ambroxol, which selectively suppresses the formation of lipidic fibrils and in this manner shifts the aggregation kinetics to the slow, lipid-independent pathway. Taken together, these findings reveal that lipidic fibrils act as on-pathway intermediates and accelerate the aggregation of mature fibrils, which could provide a quantitative framework to design novel therapeutic strategies to inhibit pathological α-synuclein aggregation.

articles.title: Live attenuated YFV-17D vaccine induces robust B and T cell immunity in vaccine-draining lymph nodes
articles.abstract: The yellow fever virus-17D (YFV-17D) vaccine is widely regarded as one of the most effective vaccines in existence, with protection linked to robust elicitation of neutralising antibodies1. The features of the germinal centre (GC) reaction driving this durable and potent antibody responses remain unclear. Here we examined immune dynamics in blood and lymph nodes (LNs) after primary YFV-17D immunisation in humans. Using fine needle biopsy (FNB), we identified robust T and B lymphocyte responses within draining LNs, underpinning maturation of antibodies targeting the viral envelope (E). Early antibody responses were largely IgM, with gradual accumulation of E-specific memory B cells and anti-viral IgG in the subsequent months. Monoclonal antibodies derived from GC B cells had specificity for E, with diversification in the LN capable of driving increases in binding and neutralising potency. While circulating vaccine-specific CD4+ T cells peaked two weeks post-vaccination, clonally related GC and IL-10+ T follicular helper populations progressively accumulated in the LN. Comparison of FNB transcriptional datasets following YFV-17D, SARS-CoV-2 mRNA/LNP, and seasonal influenza vaccination identified a conserved GC program involving similar B and T lymphocyte subpopulations. Collectively, we find that while YFV-17D induces robust GC activity, this trait is shared with other vaccine platforms and the notably durable protection against infection may reflect an incapacity of the virus to escape host immunity.

articles.title: A novel mechanism for morphological change during bacterial sporulation based on programmed peptidoglycan degradation
articles.abstract: Many bacteria form spores to endure unfavorable conditions. While Firmicutes generate endospores through cell division, sporulation in non-Firmicutes remains less understood. The Gram-negative bacterium Myxococcus xanthus undergoes sporulation through two distinct mechanisms: rapid sporulation triggered by chemical induction and slow sporulation driven by starvation, both occurring independently of cell division. Instead, these processes depend on the complete degradation of the peptidoglycan (PG) cell wall by two lytic transglycosylases (LTGs), LtgA and LtgB. Remarkably, LtgB programs the pace of PG degradation by LtgA during rapid sporulation, ensuring a controlled process that prevents abrupt PG breakdown and the formation of non-resistant pseudospores. In addition to regulation between LTGs, PG degradation is also influenced by its synthesis; cells exhibiting increased muropeptide production often circumvent sporulation. These findings not only reveal novel mechanisms of bacterial sporulation but also shed light on the regulatory network governing PG dynamics.

articles.title: Distinct neural representations of perceptual and numerical absence in the human brain
articles.abstract: The ability to represent absences is fundamental to human perception and cognition. Sensitivity to non-numerical absences depends on inferring a lack of sensory evidence, enabling the recognition of a lack of environmental resources or other objects. In turn, encoding numerical absence as a concept – in the form of the number zero – has enabled a multitude of technological and mathematical advances. Whether perceptual and conceptual absences rely on overlapping or distinct neural representations in the human brain, however, remains unknown. We employed three different tasks together with magnetoencephalography to characterise neural representations of absence evoked within perceptual and numerical domains. Using multivariate decoding and Bayes factor analyses, we replicate previous findings of shared representations of numerical absence across symbolic and non-symbolic formats. In contrast, we show that these representations of numerical absence are distinct from those evoked by non-numerical absences. This result held even after controlling for stimulus-level confounds which generate surface-level similarities between perceptual absences and non-symbolic empty sets. Our results extend a boundary between perception and cognition to the domain of absence and provide insight into the different mechanisms employed by the human brain to both perceive and conceive of absences.

articles.title: Dopaminergic neurons linking threat processing to cardiac modulation and locomotor responses
articles.abstract: Heartbeat and behavior are tightly coordinated during defensive states, yet the neuronal mechanisms linking threat processing to cardiac modulation—and the potential contribution of cardiac dynamics to behavioral output—remain poorly understood.
