articles.abstract: COVID-19 provides an unprecedented opportunity to evaluate the contribution of public health and social measures (PHSMs) to controlling transmission and inform responses to future emerging respiratory pathogens. We analysed SARS-CoV-2 transmission across 126 countries spanning multiple epidemic waves and diverse policy environments during periods when PHSMs were the primary interventions available to influence the epidemic. By explicitly representing key epidemiological drivers of transmission and measuring reductions in residual transmission scaling after incorporating OxCGRT policy time-series data, we isolated the effect of PHSMs on transmission. PHSMs frequently explained a substantial proportion of the observed variation in transmission intensity, with particularly strong effects seen in many high-income countries. In countries with strong evidence for policy effects, reductions in transmission reached 60-80% or above, although the individual policies responsible for these effects varied considerably. Harmonised analyses considering the effect of community mobility showed comparably strong effects in a similar subset of countries.

articles.title: Risk-benefit assessment of oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation using virtual clinical trials
articles.abstract: Background: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) reduces stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), and screening can enable earlier AF detection and OAC initiation. However, the population-level trade-off between stroke prevention and OAC-related major bleeding for different types of AF and OAC therapy remains uncertain, and large randomized trials to resolve this are costly and time-consuming. Methods: A state-transition Markov-like model was developed to: 1) simulate the lifetime course of AF, stroke, major bleeding, and death in different virtual populations; 2) quantify benefits (stroke reduction) and harms (major bleeding) of systematic AF screening with screening-triggered OAC across CHA2DS2-VA scores; and 3) compare rhythm-guided, time-delimited ("pill-in-pocket") OAC with continuous OAC. Results: The model synthesized information from multiple clinical sources and reproduced stroke and bleeding incidence across clinical scenarios. At CHA?DS?-VA=2, long-term continuous rhythm monitoring (LT-CRM) with OAC lowered stroke risk (HR, 0.92 [95%CI, 0.88-0.96]) but raised bleeding risk (HR, 1.17 [95%CI, 1.07-1.27]) versus no screening. Time-to-benefit was shorter than time-to-harm for CHA?DS?-VA?4, but longer for CHA?DS?-VA=0. Pill-in-pocket OAC vs continuous OAC showed no difference in stroke/mortality (HR, 1.03, 95%CI [0.91-1.16]) but lower bleeding risk (HR, 0.81, 95%CI: 0.68-0.96]) in patients with elevated bleeding risk, but not at baseline. Sensitivity analyses revealed that the risk-benefit profiles of screening or pill-in-pocket OAC strategy further depend on OAC adherence and bleeding risks. Conclusions: Our model highlights a trade-off between stroke reduction and bleeding for systematic screening-initiated OAC, with net benefit for CHA?DS?-VA?4. We provide the first virtual implementation of an ongoing rhythm-guided OAC trial, showing that pill-in-pocket OAC may lower bleeding risk compared to continuous OAC, highlighting the potential of virtual clinical trials to guide clinical trial design.

articles.title: Routine Xpert MTB/XDR for Tuberculosis Drug-Resistance Surveillance in Northern Morocco: A Four-Year Programmatic Analysis
articles.abstract: Drug-resistant tuberculosis surveillance requires diagnostic systems that can rapidly identify resistance beyond rifampicin and generate potentially actionable resistance information for routine public-health monitoring. We evaluated programmatic Xpert MTB/XDR use and characterized the molecular resistance profiles generated within a regional tuberculosis diagnostic network in northern Morocco. We retrospectively analyzed 258 Xpert MTB/XDR testing episodes performed from April 2022 to July 2026 and linked available Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra results with target-level molecular outputs. Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex was detected in 203 episodes (78.7%), of which 188 (92.6%) had an interpretable rifampicin result. Molecular rifampicin resistance was detected in 75/188 episodes (39.9%) and isoniazid resistance in 71/192 (37.0%); molecular multidrug-resistant tuberculosis was identified in 51/184 (27.7%) episodes with paired results. Among 186 episodes with interpretable rifampicin and additional resistance results, 75 (40.3%) had resistance to at least one additional drug class, including 21/112 (18.8%) rifampicin-susceptible and 54/74 (73.0%) rifampicin-resistant episodes. Among 92 resistant episodes with complete profiles, 66 (71.7%) showed resistance to two or more drug classes. rpoB3- and rpoB4-associated signals predominated among rifampicin-resistant episodes, katG-associated signals among isoniazid-resistant episodes, and gyrA targets among fluoroquinolone-resistant episodes. Mixed wild-type and mutation-associated signals occurred across rpoB and gyrA. These findings support the use of routine Xpert MTB/XDR testing as a component of regional drug-resistant tuberculosis surveillance, enabling systematic characterization of multiclass resistance and molecular resistance patterns within routine diagnostic networks. Such molecular surveillance should be integrated with phenotypic susceptibility testing and genomic sequencing to resolve discordant, atypical, or clinically consequential profiles and build a more comprehensive regional resistance-monitoring system.

articles.title: Scleral Allograft-Reinforced Cyclodialysis Combined with Phacoemulsification or Performed as a Standalone Procedure: 24-Month Outcomes from the Multicenter CREST Study
articles.abstract: Introduction: Acellular scleral allograft-reinforced cyclodialysis is a bio-interventional surgery (BIOS) to lower intraocular pressure (IOP). We report 2-year efficacy and safety outcomes when the procedure is performed in combination with phacoemulsification and as a standalone procedure in eyes with open-angle glaucoma. Methods: Analysis of the multicenter CREST real-world evidence study of eyes undergoing allograft-reinforced cyclodialysis with AlloFlo Uveo (Iantrek, Inc., White Plains, NY; NCT05506423). Eyes attending the Month-24 visit were analyzed: 176 eyes undergoing phaco-combined surgery (Cohort 1) and 32 standalone eyes (Cohort 2). Values recorded after secondary procedures censored. Cohort 1 only was stratified by low, moderate, or high baseline IOP ([≤] 15, 16-20, [≥] 21 mmHg). Results: A total of 176 eyes in Cohort 1 and 32 in Cohort 2 were analyzed. In Cohort 1, IOP decreased 3.1 mmHg at Month 24 from a baseline of 18.0 (-12.5%; p < 0.001), and medications decreased 0.5 from 1.5 (p < 0.001); medication-free eyes rose from 22.9% to 46.4% (p < 0.001). IOP changes in the low, moderate, and high baseline tiers were +0.9 (+7.8%), -3.0 (-16.3%), and -9.2 (-36.1%) mmHg; medication changes were -0.8, -0.6, and +0.1. In Cohort 2, IOP decreased 6.4 mmHg from 20.0 (-27.1%; p < 0.001), and medications decreased 1.2 from 2.8 (p = 0.004); medication-free eyes rose from 4.3% to 30.4% (p = 0.031). Secondary IOP-lowering procedures were performed in 5.1% of Cohort 1 eyes and 28.1% of Cohort 2. Kaplan-Meier freedom from reoperation was 98.9% and 84.4%. No eye developed clinically significant hypotony or choroidal effusion, and there were no allograft-related vision-threatening adverse events. Conclusion: Allograft-reinforced cyclodialysis effectively lowered IOP and medication use through 24 months.

articles.title: Similar discrimination, different behaviour under synthetic occlusion: confidence and attribution reproducibility of deep learning models for intraoral ultrasonography
articles.abstract: Objectives: To determine whether similar baseline discrimination conceals different responses to synthetic occlusion, whether loss of discrimination is accompanied by reduced confidence, and whether spatial attributions are reproducible in intraoral ultrasonography models. Methods: We analysed 477 images from 40 healthy volunteers, using acquisition position to label superior and inferior subregions. Five architectures were evaluated across five training seeds on a subject-independent test set of 97 images from eight volunteers. Images underwent constant-intensity occlusion at boundaries spanning 30-70% of image depth and an area-matched band-occlusion control. Attribution analyses assessed variation across seeds and class-activation methods and compared attribution-guided insertion with random insertion. Results: Seed-mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranged from 0.958 to 0.972, with rankings reversing across seeds. EfficientNet-B0 fell below 0.60 in 49 of 50 boundary-sweep conditions, compared with zero to two for the other architectures; the difference persisted with area-matched masking. Under 50% occlusion, its mean confidence on incorrect predictions rose to 0.989 and expected calibration error from 0.094 to 0.478. Between two inference runs, EfficientNet-B0's per-seed occluded AUCs differed by up to 0.161; seed means were 0.51-0.55 in both. Attribution patterns varied across seeds and methods.

articles.title: Single-Cell Transcriptome-Wide Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Analysis Reveals Immune Cell-Specific Mechanisms in Alzheimer's Disease
articles.abstract: Objective: To integrate single-cell expression quantitative trait locus (sc-eQTL), Alzheimer's disease (AD) genome-wide association study (GWAS), and Bayesian colocalization analyses, in order to systematically identify candidate causal genes and potential immune mechanisms that specifically regulate AD risk in peripheral immune cells. Methods: Using the cis-eQTLs of 14 peripheral blood immune cell types from the OneK1K single-cell eQTL dataset as exposure data and the AD GWAS (GCST90565439) as outcome data, a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was performed. Weak instrumental variables were removed using F-statistics, and approximately independent genetic instruments were obtained by linkage disequilibrium pruning. For significant gene-cell type associations, compareCluster functional enrichment, Bayesian colocalization, and phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) were further performed, and the 1M-scBloodNL dataset was used for replication validation. Results: The MR analysis identified 187 gene-cell type associations significantly associated with AD risk, involving 161 candidate causal genes. Among them, 141 genes showed significant associations in only a single immune cell type, suggesting that AD-related immune genetic regulation has marked cell type specificity. Functional enrichment analysis showed that the significant genes in different immune cell types were enriched in biological processes including MHC class II antigen presentation, phagocytosis, membrane invagination, and positive regulation of T cell activation. Colocalization analysis indicated a strong shared genetic signal between TNF expression in CD4+SOX4+ T cells and AD risk (PP.H4 = 0.833). In the 1M-scBloodNL replication analysis, several candidate genes showed consistent direction and nominal significance. The PheWAS results suggested that the significant phenotypic associations of the TNF instrumental variable were mainly concentrated in immune- and hematology-related traits, with no genome-wide significant neurological phenotypic associations observed. Conclusion: This study suggests that single-cell eQTL-MR combined with colocalization analysis can be used to dissect the cell type-specific genetic regulatory mechanisms of peripheral immunity in AD. The genetically predicted expression of TNF in CD4+SOX4+ T cells may represent an important immune-related signal for AD risk, but further validation in independent populations and functional experiments is still required.

articles.title: Smaller Cortical Responses to Balance Perturbations in Parkinson's Disease with Freezing of Gait
articles.abstract: Freezing of gait (FoG) is among the most disabling symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD) and is associated with balance impairment and increased falls risk, yet remains challenging to understand due to its episodic and context-dependent nature. Altered supplementary motor area (SMA) function at rest and before self-initiated movements has been implicated in FoG; however, whether this extends to functionally relevant balance behavior is unknown. A loss of balance in response to support surface translations during standing elicits a perturbation-evoked N1 potential, an error assessment signal linked to SMA activity. We therefore predicted that people with FoG would have smaller and later N1 responses than people with PD without FoG and older adults. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) during backward support-surface translations in 29 people with PD (71 {+/-} 7 years), including 13 people with a history of FoG (FoG+) and 16 people without FoG (FoG-), and 26 older adults (OA; 67 {+/-} 6 years). N1 amplitude and latency were quantified at a central midline electrode and defined as the largest negative peak 100-300 ms post-perturbation. N1 responses were similar between OA and FoG- ({Delta} = 4.0 {micro}V and 2.8 ms, respectively). In contrast, FoG+ had smaller N1 amplitudes than FoG- ({Delta} = 18.1 {micro}V, p = 0.001) and OA ({Delta} = 14.1 {micro}V, p = 0.003), and both differences persisted after adjusting for age. FoG+ also had later N1 latencies than OA ({Delta} = 26.5 ms, p = 0.029), with a similar but non-significant difference versus FoG- ({Delta} = 23.6 ms, p = 0.091); after adjusting for age, these latency differences were not retained. These findings suggest that perturbation-evoked cortical activity is altered in FoG, potentially reflecting altered SMA function, and may provide a functionally relevant marker of FoG susceptibility.

articles.title: Suvorexant Inversely Affects Phosphorylated Tau in Human Cerebrospinal Fluid and Plasma
articles.abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is characterized by amyloid-{beta} plaques and neurofibrillary tangles of tau. Suvorexant, a dual orexin receptor antagonist, was previously shown to acutely reduce the ratio of phosphorylated tau-181 to unphosphorylated tau-181 (pT181/T181) in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). However, its effects on plasma pT181/T181 and broader proteomic networks remain unknown. Here, we conducted a secondary analysis of samples from a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of 25 participants receiving placebo or suvorexant 20 mg. Paired CSF and plasma samples were collected longitudinally via indwelling intrathecal and intravenous catheters. Plasma AD biomarkers were quantified by mass spectrometry, and proteomic profiling was performed using the SomaScan 11K assay on samples from hours 0, 16, and 24. Suvorexant increased pT181/T181 in plasma while decreasing it in CSF between 08:00 to 16:00. At the pathway level, suvorexant increased the extracellular abundance of proteins associated with translation, RNA binding, cytoskeletal organization and endosomal sorting, centrally at 16 hours and peripherally at 24 hours, and decreased cytokine and receptor-ligand signaling and serine protease activity in plasma at 24 hours. As plasma biomarkers are increasingly used for clinical screening and trial enrollment, factors that influence their levels, including medications, must be identified and their effects on interpretation understood.

articles.title: Syndemic burden, menopause, and cardiovascular risk among midlife and older women with and without HIV
articles.abstract: Midlife and older women living with HIV often carry several co-occurring social and behavioral stressors, and how that accumulated burden relates to cardiovascular risk is not well described. We examined whether cumulative syndemic burden was associated with estimated 10-year risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease among women aged 45 years and older, and whether menopause stage modified it. Data came from the MACS/WIHS Combined Cohort Study, a multisite United States cohort, for visits between October 2020 and March 2025. The full sample included 1,993 women, 1,446 of them living with HIV; a secondary sample of 1,063 women virally suppressed at baseline contributed 4,009 visits. Syndemic burden was the sum of six conditions: elevated depressive symptoms, current tobacco use, hazardous alcohol use, recent stimulant use, physical inactivity, and material insecurity. Ten-year cardiovascular risk was estimated with the Pooled Cohort Equations and modeled with linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts; random forest classifiers were trained separately to predict high estimated risk (7.5 percent or greater). Median age was 56 years, 63 percent were non-Hispanic Black, and 57 percent reported two or more syndemic conditions. Each additional syndemic condition was associated with a 0.40-point higher estimated risk score (95 percent confidence interval 0.01 to 0.78; p=0.043), and postmenopausal status with a 1.3-point higher score than premenopause (0.39 to 2.3; p=0.006). The syndemic burden by menopause stage interaction was not significant overall (p=0.2), although an exploratory signal was present among virally suppressed women (0.50; p=0.079). The classifiers discriminated moderately (areas under the curve 0.727 and 0.704); serum creatinine, body mass index, syndemic burden, and postmenopausal status ranked among the most important predictors. Syndemic burden and reproductive aging were each independently and modestly associated with higher estimated cardiovascular risk, supporting joint assessment of both in risk stratification for midlife women with and without HIV.

articles.title: The Feasibility, Acceptability, and Perceived Need for Suicide Initiatives for Children in UK Primary Schools
articles.abstract: Background: Currently, there are no specific suicide prevention programmes for primary (elementary) schools within the UK. However, given the rise in suicidal thoughts and/or behaviours amongst children under 11 years, the feasibility, acceptability, and perceived need for these programmes need to be assessed. Aims: This qualitative scoping study aimed to explore whether there is a perceived need for suicide prevention programmes in primary schools and, if so, what these should look like. Sample(s) & Methods: 92 participants took part in the study. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with mental health professionals (N= 22), school staff (N= 8), and parents of children who had experienced suicidal ideation, behaviours, or been bereaved by suicide (N=7). Focus groups were conducted with secondary school students (N= 36) and primary school students (N= 19) across 5 schools. Data were analysed using thematic framework analysis. Results: Three main themes were identified: 1) the necessity of suicide prevention programmes for primary schools, 2) barriers affecting delivery and potential solutions, 3) the transition period from primary to secondary school. Conclusion: Overall, participants supported the need and acceptability of suicide prevention programmes for primary schools, particularly due to the rising concerns about suicidality among younger children and evidence that suicide-related discussions are already occurring within peer groups. However, careful consideration needs to be given to ensure it is delivered in a safe and age-appropriate way, with a focus on dispelling myths, promoting help seeking, and increasing knowledge.

articles.title: The Lived Experiences of Long-Term Users of Copper-T Intrauterine Devices: A phenomenological Qualitative Study among women at Kawempe National Referral Hospital in Uganda
articles.abstract: Background: The Copper-T intrauterine device (Cu-T IUD) is a highly effective, non-hormonal, long-acting reversible contraceptive that can protect against pregnancy for up to 12 years, with a failure rate under 1%. Despite its clinical efficacy, early discontinuation remains a substantial challenge in Uganda, where discontinuation is approximated at 29% within the first year of use. Understanding the experiences of women using the Cu-T IUD is important to predict factors associated with discontinuation and to inform practice. Methods: Between September and November 2025, we conducted twenty in-depth interviews with women of reproductive age (15-49 years) who had used a Cu-T IUD for at least two years, recruited from the family planning clinic of Kawempe National Referral Hospital, Kampala, Uganda. Data were analysed thematically, guided by the Social-Ecological Model and Lazarus and Folkman's Transactional Model of Stress and Coping. Results: Long-term Cu-T IUD users reported both positive and negative experiences shaped by individual, interpersonal, and community factors. Two themes were identified at the individual-level domain: experiences during insertion and post-insertion experiences. Negative experiences, particularly heavy menstrual bleeding, anxiety, and abdominal pain, were common and distressing. Participants employed coping strategies, including taking painkillers, using home remedies, and resting, to manage these challenges with Cu-T IUD use. Conclusions: Negative experiences of Cu-T IUD are common among long-term users; women's coping strategies such as taking painkillers lead to continued use. Client-centred pre-insertion counselling addressing both anticipated side effects and common misconceptions, alongside accessible follow-up services, may facilitate long-term Cu-T IUD use. Keywords: copper-T IUD; lived experiences; coping mechanisms; long-term use; Uganda

articles.title: The Para-ISS Dural Space Enhancement Sign: A Novel MRI Finding Independently Associated With Intracranial Atherosclerotic Burden
articles.abstract: Background: No dural enhancement sign centered on the inferior sagittal sinus (ISS) has been characterized. We observed a frequent, previously undescribed finding - para-ISS dural space enhancement (PISE) - at the free inferior margin of the falx cerebri. Objective: To define PISE, determine its detection rate in a large cross-sectional cohort, and characterize its correlates, in particular whether the pattern of association is compatible with an atherosclerosis-related dural mechanism. Methods: Consecutive contrast-enhanced intracranial vessel-wall MRI (VWI) examinations (May 2015-December 2025) were reviewed; 835 of 875 examinations were evaluable, corresponding to 811 patients. The first outcome-evaluable examination for each patient was used for all primary analyses. PISE was defined as dural enhancement strictly at the falx free margin adjacent to the ISS, exceeding the ISS vascular lumen. Forty-seven demographic, clinical-history, and imaging variables were tested univariately with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction; multivariable logistic regression with patient-grouped 5-fold cross-validation was triangulated with LASSO and random forest. Dose-response across plaque grades was assessed with the Cochran-Armitage trend test, and circulation-specific associations were compared in models adjusted for age and sex (inter-reader Cohen's kappa = 0.93). Results: PISE was detected in 609/811 patients (75.1%); detection rose from 50.0% (<40 years) to 81.7% (>70 years; trend p = 5.6 x 10^-6). The strongest univariate correlate was vulnerable intracranial plaque (OR=8.29, 95% CI 5.54-12.40). Detection increased across plaque grades 0/1/2 (38.7% -> 77.2% -> 90.3%; Z=11.09). Anterior-circulation plaque showed a stronger association than posterior-circulation plaque (OR=4.42 vs 2.76). Vulnerable plaque (OR=2.37), plaque grade (OR=2.84 per grade), age (OR=1.38 per SD), and inpatient status (OR=3.18) remained independently associated (patient-grouped cross-validated AUC=0.755). Moyamoya disease was inversely associated (OR=0.25). Findings were consistent across imputation and all-examination sensitivity analyses. Conclusions: PISE is a frequently detected novel dural enhancement sign whose independent, graded, anatomically concordant association with intracranial atherosclerotic burden supports an atherosclerosis-related dural mechanism and warrants prospective validation.

articles.title: The life course shaping of quality of life in older age: does childhood poverty associate with control, autonomy, self-realisation and pleasure? A retrospective and prospective study of HRS, ELSA, SHARE and TILDA cohorts
articles.abstract: Later-life quality of life is increasingly recognised as a life-course achievement, yet ageing research has focused more on dysfunction and decline than on positive wellbeing. This study examines whether childhood poverty shapes later-life quality of life, measured by CASP: control, autonomy, self-realisation and pleasure. METHODS: I analysed harmonised data from 59,569 adults aged over 50 in 29 countries, drawn from HRS, ELSA, SHARE and TILDA (U.S. Health and Retirement Study, English Longitudinal Study of Ageing, Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe, The Irish Longitudinal Study on Ageing). Childhood poverty was modelled as a latent class from retrospectively reported childhood material circumstances, acknowledging recall error in such reports. Country fixed-effects linear models estimated associations with CASP, first adjusting for age, sex and country, then adding education, marital status and later-life wealth. RESULTS: One in five participants grew up in poverty (22.9%). Mean CASP was 38 out of 48. Initially childhood poverty was associated with a 1.2-point lower CASP score; after complete adjustment the penalty attenuated but remained durable at 0.7 points. Education, partnership and wealth were independently associated with higher wellbeing but did not erase the penalty. Predicted age profiles showed poverty penalty in every country. They also revealed striking national differences: Nordic countries achieved markedly higher CASP levels than several Eastern European countries; Finns aged 90 had similar levels of positive wellbeing to Latvians two decades younger. CONCLUSION: Childhood poverty leaves a durable mark on later-life positive wellbeing, while welfare contexts appear to lift overall CASP levels. Reducing child poverty and strengthening social protection are therefore lifelong wellbeing policies.

articles.title: Uncovering Distinct Phenotypes of Early Onset Heart Failure in Women
articles.abstract: Background: Heart failure in younger women is understudied and may reflect heterogeneous pathways and risk not adequately captured by conventional classifications. We aimed to identify clinically distinct phenotypes of early-onset heart failure in women, assess their prognostic significance, and evaluate their transportability in an independent national cohort. Methods: We identified women aged 18-55 years with heart failure using electronic health record data from a large multi-hospital system. A variational deep embedding model incorporating 283 clinical features was used for unsupervised phenotyping. Associations with subsequent inpatient hospitalization, emergency department utilization, and mortality were evaluated using age-stratified Cox models. Phenotype transportability was assessed by both applying the institutionally trained model and by independent de novo clustering as a replication analysis in the All of Us cohort. Results: Among 1,407 young women with heart failure (median age, 45 years), four phenotypes were identified: hypertensive pregnancy (n=494), cardiorenal (n=276), autoimmune (n=394), and cardiometabolic-ischemic (n=243), with a bootstrap adjusted Rand index of 0.65 and silhouette score of 0.45. Compared with the hypertensive pregnancy phenotype, risks of inpatient hospitalization were highest for the cardiorenal (HR 2.86 [95% CI, 2.35?3.49]) and autoimmune (HR 2.25 [95% CI, 1.87?2.70]) phenotypes; mortality risks were similarly elevated (HR 4.65 [95% CI, 3.17?6.82] and HR 4.38 [95% CI, 3.03?6.31], respectively) in these two groups. In All of Us participants (n=682), transferred phenotypes retained their principal clinical characteristics and continued to stratify hospitalization risk. Independent clustering most strongly reproduced the cardiorenal phenotype (Jaccard index, 0.744). Conclusions: Early-onset heart failure in women comprises distinct cardio-obstetric, cardiorenal, autoimmune, and cardiometabolic-ischemic phenotypes with divergent clinical outcomes. These findings support a life-course approach to heart failure classification in women that complements conventional frameworks and incorporates pregnancy history and female-predominant systemic conditions.

articles.title: A Porphyrinic Metal–Organic Framework Platform for Red-Light Photoredox Catalysis
articles.abstract: Low-energy photoredox catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for promoting mild, chemoselective transformations through radical intermediates. While various red-light-absorbing photocatalysts, including molecular porphyrins, have enabled diverse synthetic transformations, these processes operate almost exclusively under homogeneous conditions in organic solvents. Here, we demonstrate that integrating a photoactive porphyrin as the organic linker in a metal–organic framework (MOF) affords an air- and aqueous-compatible, heterogeneous photoredox catalyst. Using porphyrinic zirconium MOFs such as PCN-224, we enable a range of bond-forming reactions, including Giese additions, C(sp2)–H alkylations, C(sp2)–H arylations, formal cycloadditions, and radical polymerizations under mild red-light irradiation. While preserving the intrinsic reactivity of molecular porphyrins, heterogenization provides practical advantages including efficient photocatalysis independent of catalyst solubility and reaction medium, structural tunability, high turnover number (TON), and easy catalyst recovery and reuse. Mechanistic studies indicate that radical generation occurs predominantly within the framework pores.

articles.title: Aldehyde or Carboxylic Acid: Defining the Selectivity of Electrochemical Oxidation of Aliphatic Alcohols by Tuning the Surface Phase of NiO(OH)
articles.abstract: Nickel oxyhydroxide (NiO(OH)) is the catalytically active species during electrochemical alcohol oxidation at nickel electrodes. Herein, we demonstrate that the adopted phase structure of NiO(OH) (β- and γ-NiO(OH)) can dramatically influence the catalytic properties of nickel electrodes. We show that β-NiO(OH) oxidizes aliphatic alcohols preferentially to aldehydes and that carboxylates are formed at γ-NiO(OH). By combining the effect of the NiO(OH) phase with reagent effects (electrolyte pH, alcohol concentration, and trace amounts of Fe), we achieve aldehyde formation with ∼90% selectivity or carboxylate formation with ∼85% selectivity. Furthermore, we perform an in situ Raman spectroelectrochemical study to elucidate the reaction conditions that favor the formation of β- and γ-NiO(OH) phases, respectively. Freshly deposited nickel electrodes form γ-NiO(OH) phases upon oxidation, whereas an electrochemical conditioning protocol can be employed to transform γ- to β-NiO(OH). Finally, we show that the efficiency of this transformation depends on the precise reaction conditions and the precursor used. Hence, we showcase that the exact surface structure of the phase formed in situ on top of transition metal (oxides) affects the product distribution of electrochemical reactions. Moreover, we highlight how the “history” of these catalysts affects their performance via an intricate interplay among the reaction environment, pre-treatment, and surface structure.

articles.title: Discovery of Racemization Organocatalysts and Biocatalysts for Ketoreductase-Catalyzed Dynamic Reductive Kinetic Resolution
articles.abstract: Cyclic α-halo ketones and vicinal halohydrins serve as essential synthetic intermediates or structural motifs for a variety of pharmaceuticals. Ketoreductase-catalyzed dynamic reductive kinetic resolution (DYRKR) of cyclic α-halo ketones is an attractive strategy for the synthesis of chiral cyclic vicinal halohydrins. However, we found that the spontaneous racemization of the α-halo groups of 3-bromo-chroman-4-ones and 2-bromo-1-tetralones was less efficient than the ketoreductase-catalyzed reduction of the more reactive enantiomers, resulting in a low conversion and poor (dia)stereoselectivity. To address this challenge, two classes of racemization catalysts were identified: prolinol-derived organocatalysts and racemase-based biocatalysts, both of which could accelerate the racemization of cyclic α-halo ketones. Consequently, combining these catalysts with ketoreductases improved both the conversion and product (dia)stereoselectivity of the DYRKR. Based on the discovery of racemization catalysts, this work provides an efficient strategy for biocatalytic dynamic kinetic resolution and an operationally simple route for the synthesis of chiral cyclic vicinal halohydrins.

articles.title: Covalent-Bond Engineering Stabilizes Layered Oxide Cathodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Developing practicable layered oxide cathodes remains a critical challenge for sodium-ion batteries. Here, by systematically varying Cu contents to tune TM–O covalency in Nay[CuxFe3/9Mn(6/9–x)]O2, we show that an optimal degree of covalency simultaneously boosts energy density and structural resilience. The optimized Na7/9[Cu2/9Fe3/9Mn4/9]O2 delivers 131.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and retains 80% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. Mechanistically, the enhanced Cu–O covalency converts trivalent Cu from a conventional d8 to a heavily mixed d9L configuration, delocalizing holes across the extended TM–O network, enlarging polaron size, and “flattening the ripple” of local lattice distortions. Side-by-side comparison with an ionic Ni analogue confirms the suppressed cation migration and polarization. Crucially, the covalency-driven stabilization is not unbounded–excessive covalency rigidifies the lattice, defining a covalency threshold for optimal performance. These findings establish covalency modulation within a defined threshold as a predictive design principle for durable layered oxide cathodes.

articles.title: Electrochemical Capture and Accumulation of Uranium Using a Layered Uvanite Electrode
articles.abstract: Extracting uranyl ions (UO22+) from uranium mining leachates can enhance national uranium security and mitigate the environmental impact of nuclear energy. Conventional techniques such as ion exchange and iron-based reductive precipitation have notable limitations. This study reports that the uvanite (U2V6O21) electrode, a layered uranium-vanadium oxide, enables potentiodynamic decoupling of UO22+ and proton intercalation/deintercalation, as well as proton-induced UO22+/UO3 precipitation and dissolution reactions. Building on a comprehensive understanding of charge-transfer and transport mechanisms, we found that potentiodynamic modulation enables selective capture of uranium species using a uvanite electrode. By allowing competing cations to deintercalate at lower potentials and preventing proton deintercalation, UO3 dissolution is inhibited, achieving a high UO3 recovery capacity of 515 mg/g at 10 times the competing cation concentration. The new electrochemistry of the uvanite electrode helps develop cost-effective, sustainable battery electrodes for critical ion extraction from water.

articles.title: Implications for CO2 Reduction: Methanol Formation by Reaction of Benzimidazole Hydrides with Inorganic Oxide Materials
Light-Driven Hydrogenation–Dehydrogenation of Toluene–Methylcyclohexane by Plasmonic Photocatalysis
articles.abstract: The development of an efficient and reversible hydrogen storage and transport system is crucial for a sustainable hydrogen economy. Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) offer a potential solution due to their high hydrogen storage density and ease of transport, but conventional thermal approaches for the hydrogenation and dehydrogenation of LOHCs remain heavily reliant on harsh operating conditions. Here, we demonstrate a plasmonic photocatalysis approach for toluene hydrogenation to methylcyclohexane and methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation to toluene under substantially milder conditions. We observe changes in reaction orders and substantial reductions in activation barriers by 0.34 and 1.11 eV for toluene hydrogenation and methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation, respectively, as compared to thermocatalysis due to the role of hot carriers. Both reactions exhibit high activity, stability (>70 h), and excellent selectivity (>95%), offering a sustainable pathway for on-demand hydrogen storage and release.

articles.title: When Literature Data Can Mislead Artificial Intelligence in Materials Discovery
Dislocation Arrays Hosting Topological Bound States in Epitaxial Tetragonal FeSe Films
articles.abstract: Topological defects in real space can host robust, localized quantum states for quantum information processing and sensing, yet deterministic control over their formation in crystalline materials remains challenging. Here, we show that symmetry-mismatched epitaxy of tetragonal FeSe films on SrTiO3(111) naturally generates networks of screw dislocations and tilt grain boundaries composed of periodic arrays of edge dislocations. Low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy measurements reveal localized electronic states pinned to these dislocation cores. Combined with first-principles calculations, we identify these states as topological bound states arising from the interplay between the real-space topological invariant of the defect, the Burgers vector, and the nontrivial electronic topology of FeSe. Our work demonstrates symmetry mismatch epitaxy as a scalable route toward template topological defect networks and their associated quantum states in solid-state materials.

articles.title: In Situ Nanoscale Visualization of Stripping-Induced Failure Behavior in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc batteries (AZBs) show great promise for large-scale energy storage due to their low cost, intrinsic safety, and environmental compatibility. However, their practical deployment is hindered by dendrite formation, residual zinc (Zn) accumulation, and limited cycle life. Recent studies have identified the stripping process as a critical factor governing battery longevity, yet the underlying failure mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, leveraging a fourth-generation synchrotron radiation source, we employed in situ nanoscale X-ray microscopy to visualize the morphological evolution from planar to mossy Zn during cycling at 50 mA cm–2. Combining observations of the entire cycling process with optical flow analysis of the stripping process on different substrates at 1 mA cm–2, we categorize the origins of residual Zn into four distinct pathways: (i) dendrites formed during plating; (ii) dendrites generated by crystallographically selective stripping; (iii) bulky Zn that loses electrical contact during stripping; and (iv) Zn fragments resulting from inward dissolution. Ex-situ XRD and DFT calculations further confirm the preferential dissolution of Zn(100) and Zn(101) over Zn(002). These findings highlight the critical role of the stripping process in AZB failure and demonstrate that minimizing local variations in dissolution behavior through kinetic modulation is one of the keys to achieving complete dissolution and enhancing Zn reversibility.

articles.title: Molecular Single-Photon Emitters across Chemical Space: Substrate Effects and Design Principles
articles.abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are an emerging molecular platform for single-photon emitters, but predictive design strategies across chemical space have been lacking. Here we establish two general principles governing PAH/hBN emitters. The zero-phonon-line energy is molecule-controlled and robust to the substrate environment, whereas the Huang–Rhys (HR) factor is environment-governed and exhibits two distinct regimes. Pristine hBN modestly enhances HR through soft interfacial modes. In contrast, the NB antisite defect, introduced to immobilize the molecules, produces a molecule-specific HR response that cannot be predicted from gas-phase or pristine-hBN data alone. Strikingly, the defect can either partially restore the HR factor toward its intrinsic gas-phase value or amplify it by up to 3.7×, depending on the molecule. This positions defect engineering as a tunable design knob for vibronic coupling in molecule/hBN emitters. Combining high-throughput hybrid density functional theory (DFT) screening of 662 PAHs identifies 47 gas-phase candidates with low HR factors and high radiative rates spanning the near-infrared to ultraviolet. Among five representative candidates explicitly tested on NB@hBN, two retain HR factors below unity in gas-phase, pristine hBN, and defect-bound environments. However, no PAH simultaneously exhibits favorable single-photon-emitter properties and an excited-state singlet–triplet splitting below 0.5 eV, suggesting that PAH-based spin–photon interfaces will require further molecular design. All data are released through the open MolExDB platform.

articles.title: Nanozyme-Catalyzed Lateral Flow Assay for the Simultaneous Detection of RNA and Protein Biomarkers
articles.abstract: Molecular diagnostics have advanced rapidly over the past decade, driven by the demand for accessible and scalable testing solutions. However, current assays often focus on single biomolecule types, limiting their ability to capture the multifactorial nature of disease. Integrating distinct molecular readouts─such as transcriptomic and proteomic biomarkers─could provide richer diagnostic information and improve clinical decision-making. Here, we present MOSAIC (Multiplexed Orthogonal Sensing Assay Integrated with CRISPRZyme), a unified lateral flow assay that enables simultaneous detection of RNA and protein biomarkers using a shared nanozyme-catalyzed readout. The assay combines CRISPR/Cas13a-mediated RNA detection and antibody-based protein detection, with assay components optimized through antibody conjugation tuning, blocking agent optimization, and probe loading calibration to achieve balanced and cross-talk-free performance. Using cardiovascular disease as a model, the platform successfully detects NTproBNP and LIPCAR long noncoding RNA simultaneously from the same sample. The assay was further optimized for spiked human plasma, incorporating tailored pretreatment and recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) to maintain RNA stability and performance in complex biofluids. Extending its versatility, the same assay design was adapted to detect SARS-CoV-2 biomarkers, the spike (S) protein and ORF1ab gene, in pooled human saliva. To enable standardized interpretation of multiplexed readouts, we additionally developed a machine-learning-assisted computational workflow that automates strip localization, signal extraction, and calibration curve construction. Together, these results demonstrate a modular, paper-based diagnostic platform that unites transcriptomic and proteomic analyses within one assay architecture, offering a practical step toward accessible and multiplexed molecular diagnostics across diverse disease contexts.

articles.title: Rapid-Mixing In Situ X-ray Diffraction Reveals Precursor-Reorganization Signatures in Additive-Free Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8 Nanoparticle Formation
articles.abstract: Controlling particle size and phase purity in solution-processed metal–organic frameworks requires understanding how disordered precursors evolve before they crystallize into the final framework. However, capturing this precursor-to-crystal conversion remains a key challenge. Here, we couple a central-collision-type microreactor with time-resolved in situ X-ray diffraction to track the additive-free formation of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) in water–methanol cosolvents, achieving 5 s temporal resolution after submillisecond micromixing. The setup directly captures crystal appearance, apparent crystallization kinetics, and subsequent lattice relaxation. Crystallization is fastest at 40–50 vol % methanol, where Bragg reflections appear earliest and grow most rapidly. Water-rich media approach a competing phase boundary between ZIF-8 and layered zeolitic imidazolate framework-L (ZIF-L) and yield a predominantly amorphous product at the water-rich extreme, whereas methanol-rich media form pure ZIF-8 more slowly. After crystallinity emerges, the apparent lattice constant contracts, indicating that the earliest Bragg-detectable domains undergo lattice relaxation as growth proceeds. Strikingly, raising the total reactant concentration at a fixed metal-to-linker ratio delays crystal appearance and yields larger particles, contrary to the behavior typically expected in a nucleation-dominated system. We propose that concentration-dependent precursor accumulation, coarsening, and interconnection, coupled to metal–ligand network reorganization, link these contrasting trends.

articles.title: Single-Atom Nanoisland with Dual-Nanoconfinement Effects for Cascade Self-Amplified Synergistic Antitumor Therapy via Redox/Metabolism Disruption
articles.abstract: Enzyodynamic therapy (EDT) represents a promising cancer therapeutic modality; however, its efficacy is constrained by the catalytic activity of nanozymes and intrinsic tumor-adaptive defense mechanisms. Leveraging the atomic–nano structure and nanoconfined effect of single-atom nanoislands (SANIs), a SANI-based nanozyme (CPH) is elaborately constructed through vapor filling and spatially confined reduction/growth of metal species, featuring ultrasmall Pt nanoislands with embedded Ce single atoms confined within the channels of hollow carbon spheres. CPH exhibits multienzymatic activities resembling those of oxidase, catalase, peroxidase, glucose oxidase, glutathione peroxidase, and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide oxidase, sustaining a self-reinforcing catalytic cascade that disrupts redox homeostasis and blocks energy metabolism. This process facilitates H2O2 self-supplementation while alleviating hypoxia and elicits reactive oxygen species storm and lipid peroxidation, thereby establishing an apoptosis/ferroptosis dual-pathway therapeutic strategy. Mechanism investigation reveals that the enhanced catalytic properties can be ascribed to the favorable shift of the d-band center and synergistic effects among multiactive centers after Ce single-atom embedding. Concurrently, the nanoconfined photothermal effect facilitates heat concentration while minimizing thermal dissipation, further augmenting the catalytic efficiency and enabling synergistic mild-photothermal therapy (mild-PTT)/EDT synergistic therapy. This study provides a proof of concept of SANI-based nanozymes as efficient therapeutic tools toward tumor ablation.

articles.title: Universal In-Plane Confined Growth of Mesoporous Metal–Organic Framework Crystalline Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Constructing mesoporous MOF heterostructures on conductive two-dimensional hosts remains challenging because interfacial contact and pore accessibility are rarely optimized simultaneously. Herein, we report a universal in-plane confined growth strategy for mesoporous UiO-66-NH2/MXene heterostructures featuring continuous interfacial contact and vertically accessible mesochannels. In contrast to conventional particle-on-sheet hybrids, the resulting architecture enables improved electrolyte penetration, shortened Zn2+ transport pathways, and efficient interfacial electron transfer. By regulating micellar assembly at the interface, an optimal mesostructural regime is identified in which ion accessibility and structural confinement are best balanced. Consequently, the optimized heterostructure delivers a high energy density of 163.9 Wh kg–1, excellent rate capability (∼68% retention over a 50-fold current increase), and ∼100% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles. Kinetic analyses and ex situ studies further show that the interfacial mesoporous architecture suppresses diffusion limitations and preserves structural integrity during Zn2+ storage. Moreover, the assembly concept shows transferability across substrates of different dimensionalities, highlighting its broader utility for constructing mesoporous crystalline heterostructures. This work provides an effective route to mesoporous MOF heterostructures and a generalizable design principle for hybrid crystalline electrodes.

articles.title: 3D Observations of Grain Growth in Textured and Untextured Undoped Alumina
Energetic Role of Adaptive Mg Sublattice in Size-Mismatched Mg2(Si, Sn) Thermoelectric Meta-phases
Pencil glide, crystal rotation, and non-Schmid slip behavior in MoReW single crystals during tensile deformation
Decoupling Oxygen Reduction From Hydrogen Oxidation on Platinum via Phosphorus Coordination for Reversal‐Tolerant and Durable PEM Fuel Cells
articles.abstract: During the start‐up/shut‐down (SU/SD) processes of proton‐exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), anode reversal generates an excessively high voltage that accelerates corrosion of the cathode Pt/C catalyst. Conventional approaches focus on blocking the delivery of oxygen or electrons to the anode, but fail to address the intrinsic activity coupling of Pt/C for both hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Here, we report a strategy that can selectively tailor the catalytic function of Pt nanoparticles. We used phosphorus to modulate the electronic structure of low‐loading Pt clusters on a carbon support, forming a Pt/P‐BP catalyst. The P‐coordination downshifts the d‐band center of Pt cluster, as evidenced by in situ ATR‑FTIR spectroscopy and DFT calculations, thereby widening the activity gap between HOR and ORR. Specifically, compared to Pt/C, Pt/P‐BP enhances HOR mass activity by fivefold while substantially suppressing ORR, transforming Pt from a bifunctional catalyst into a highly selective HOR catalyst. Consequently, Pt/P‐BP achieves a 10.8‐fold higher HOR/ORR selectivity than Pt/C. In SU/SD experiments, the Pt/P‐BP anode significantly reduces carbon corrosion of the cathode catalyst layer, maintaining the fuel cell performance better than Pt/C. This work paves a new avenue toward durable PEMFCs and inspires the selectivity design for electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Relay Catalysis on Phase‐Separated Janus–CuCo Alloys for Efficient Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction at Industrial Low Concentration
articles.abstract: Earth-abundant Cu and Co are attractive electrocatalysts for nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO3 −RR); however, conventional solid-solution alloys with single-phase active sites lack effective intermediate spillover, impeding the hydrogenation of multiple reaction intermediates and limiting NH3 selectivity under dilute nitrate conditions. Here we report phase-separated yet electronically coupled Janus–CuCo alloys synthesized via a time–charge regulated electrochemical reduction strategy, forming metallic Cu/Co domains with a well-defined interphase electronic structure. This Janus architecture enables relay catalysis, in which Cu domains activate NO3 −, intermediates migrate to Cu−Co interfaces for hydrogenation, and adjacent Co domains promote subsequent NH3 formation. In situ characterizations reveal pronounced Cu–Co synergy, where Co sites regulate *H-mediated hydrogenation while the balanced surface coverage of *H and *NO3 − optimizes NH3 selectivity and yield. Consequently, the optimized Janus Cu−Co catalyst, Janus–Cu70Co30/NOMC, achieves a peak NH3 Faradaic efficiency (FENH3) of 95.5% at −500 mA cm−2 and delivers a FENH3 of 93.1% with an NH3 yield rate of 4.2 mg h−1 mgcat −1 at −0.4 V vs RHE in an MEA flow cell under low nitrate concentrations. These findings establish phase separation with electronic coupling, enabled by electrochemical time–charge control, as an effective design principle for efficient multistep NO3 −RR electrocatalysis.

articles.title: A Self‐Reinforcing Hydrogel Orchestrates Dynamic Microenvironment Reprogramming for High‐Quality Diabetic Skin Regeneration
articles.abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, bacterial infection, oxidative stress, hypoxia, impaired angiogenesis, and pathological fibrosis. Herein, a self‐reinforcing hydrogel dressing (RNPP) is developed by integrating copper peroxide (CuO2)/manganese dioxide (MnO2) hybrid nanozymes and ginsenoside Rg1 (Rg1) into a sodium polyacrylate/polymetformin matrix for wound microenvironment regulation and high‐quality diabetic wound healing. RNPP rapidly promotes hemostasis, absorbs exudate, and maintains a moist protective interface. CuO2/MnO2 nanozymes provide non‐antibiotic antibacterial activity through Cu2+ release while scavenging excessive reactive oxygen species and converting endogenous H2O2 into oxygen, thereby alleviating oxidative stress and hypoxia, promoting pro‐regenerative macrophage polarization, angiogenesis, and re‐epithelialization. Meanwhile, released Cu2+ dynamically coordinates with polymetformin, reducing free Cu2+ toxicity while reinforcing the hydrogel network. Sustained Rg1 release further modulates the transforming growth factor‐β1 (TGF‐β1)/α‐smooth muscle actin (α‐SMA) axis and suppresses myofibroblast overactivation, thereby attenuating fibrotic signaling and promoting organized collagen remodeling. These effects suggest a favorable microenvironment for improved tissue remodeling. Consequently, RNPP accelerates tissue repair in diabetic and MRSA‐infected wounds while favoring regenerative tissue remodeling, providing a multifunctional material strategy for chronic wound management.

articles.title: Activating Selenium for Atomic‐Level Defect Passivation and Band Engineering Enables High‐Efficiency Bulk Heterojunction CuInS2 Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Copper indium sulfide (CuInS2) stands out as a promising candidate for next‐generation photovoltaics due to its exceptional stability, high absorption coefficient, and eco‐friendly composition. However, realizing high‐quality CuInS2 absorbers typically demands high‐temperature processing, which not only limits substrate compatibility but also invites interfacial degradation from elemental interdiffusion. Here, we overcome this challenge by introducing a low‐temperature selenium ion activation (LTSA) strategy that enables near‑surface atomic‑level defect passivation and band‑structure modulation in solution‐processed CuInS2 absorbers. Beyond conventional passivation, LTSA orchestrates three synergistic effects: (i) selenium ion diffusion tailors a favorable band alignment; (ii) atomic substitution effectively passivates critical deep‐level defects (such as InCu and VS) through robust chemical bonding; and (iii) interfacial charge transport is markedly enhanced while carrier recombination is suppressed. These combined benefits yield CuInS2 solar cells on transparent conducting oxide substrates with a record‐competitive power conversion efficiency of 11.43% and the highest fill factor of 66.88% reported to date. By establishing LTSA as a low‐temperature route for near‑surface atomic‐level defect passivation and structural reconstruction, this work unlocks new pathways toward high‐performance, cost‐effective inorganic photovoltaics.

articles.title: Bioinspired Microcone‐Array‐Based Eutectogel Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Self‐Powered Dual‐Modal Sensing and Human‐Machine Interfaces
articles.abstract: Flexible wearable sensors currently face challenges in terms of self‐powering and human‐machine interaction (HMI) capabilities. In order to cope with these challenges, through the utilization of poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):lignosulfonate (PEDOT:LS) as a dynamic physical crosslinker, N‐acryloylsemicarbazide‐acrylic acid/PEDOT:LS (NAP) eutectogel is developed via multiple‐crosslinking and direct deep eutectic solvent (DES) solvation strategies. A stable composite network is constructed within the eutectogel, which endows the gel with excellent stretchability (1559%), self‐adhesiveness (244.8 kPa), self‐healing, anti‐freezing, and anti‐drying capabilities. Therefore, the reliable monitoring of human motions and electrophysiological signals is ensured. Furthermore, a microcone‐array‐based single‐electrode triboelectric nanogenerator (M‐TENG) mimicking the setal structures of ant legs is designed, utilizing the NAP eutectogel as the back electrode. Favorable electrical outputs (196 V, 16.3 µA, and 452.2 mW/m2) are delivered by the M‐TENG, through which self‐powered and dual‐modal motion monitoring can be achieved. Finally, through the integration of the M‐TENG onto a flexible fabric substrate, a wearable human‐machine interface touch panel is constructed. Through this interactive system equipped with a password authentication mechanism, the secure remote control of a hexapod robot model is successfully achieved, demonstrating the potential of the system in unmanned search and rescue scenarios.

articles.title: Carbon‐Shell‐Confined Functional Silica Xerogels for Concurrent Lithium Dual‐Mode Optical Detection and Seawater Recovery
articles.abstract: Rational material designs for lithium extraction from unconventional dilute resources have attracted attention to meet the rising demand. Here, a new multifunctional composite is developed that not only extracts lithium but also enables its concurrent optical detection. The material design integrates silica xerogel confined within hollow carbon spheres as a high‐surface‐area matrix, heteroatom‐doped CDs as a fluorescence tag, and a covalently attached benzophenone‐derived ligand as the lithium‐binding site. This design also demonstrates an alternative detection paradigm in which a non‐fluorogenic receptor coupled with matrix‐confined CDs is used for optical signal transduction. In the presence of major seawater ions (Na+, Mg2+, Ca2+, K+), the composite demonstrates selective dual‐mode detection: naked‐eye colorimetric and turn‐on red luminescence with ultra‐high sensitivity (LOD: 1.5 nM). The turn‐on emission arises from disruption of the photoinduced electron transfer (PET) process upon Li+ binding, which restores the intrinsic emission of the CDs. The flexible benzophenone‐derived ligand enhances Li+ binding stability, as supported by density functional theory (DFT) investigations. The adsorbent exhibits high lithium uptake (110 mg g−1), fast adsorption kinetics, and good recyclability, meeting key requirements for direct lithium extraction (DLE). Real seawater‐system testing for lithium quantification and extraction highlights its potential for advancing integrated lithium detection‐extraction technologies.

articles.title: C‐H Arylation‐Constructed Non‐Fully‐Fused Dimeric Acceptors for o‐Xylene Processed Organic Solar Cells With 20.17% Efficiency
articles.abstract: Although organic solar cells (OSCs) have made significant progress in photovoltaic performance, their practical applications still face challenges, such as the complex material synthesis and involvement of Stille coupling reaction with organotin reagents of fused‐ring electron acceptors, and using halogenated toxic solvents in device fabrication. Here, we develop two non‐fully‐fused dimeric acceptors (named dNA‐C6 and dNA‐C12) with varying alkyl linker lengths using organotin‐free C‐H activation approach, which present the advantages of environmental friendliness and easy synthesis. When introducing dNA‐C6 and dNA‐C12 into PM6:BTP‐eC9 system, these OSCs achieve higher power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 19.07% and 18.74%, respectively, compared to their parental monomer based device (18.44%), while the dNA‐C6 based OSC obtains both superior PCE and device stability. Moreover, dNA‐C6 is also introduced into D18:BTP‐eC9 host to verify its universality in boosting photovoltaic performance, and the relevant device processed with halogen‐free o‐xylene offers a further improved PCE of 20.17%, ranking among the highest values in the reported non‐fully‐conjugated dimeric acceptors and halogen‐free solvent processed OSCs. This work develops organotin‐free synthesized non‐fully‐fused dimeric acceptors by integrating eco‐friendly chemistry for preparing green solvent processed OSCs with high PCE and device stability.

articles.title: Digitally Printed Eco‐Friendly Electronic Devices
articles.abstract: The sustainable life cycle of electronics is one of the major challenges of modern society. Moreover, the manufacturing of conventional electronics significantly impacts the environment due to the extensive consumption of raw materials, energy, and the release of harmful byproducts. In this regard, manufacturing of electronics using eco‐friendly materials through digital printing routes represents a promising and sustainable solution. This review discusses the state‐of‐the‐art research in this field, exploring various digital printing techniques such as inkjet, electro–hydro–dynamic jet, aerosol‐jet, and extrusion printing techniques, focusing on resource efficient manufacturing with minimal material wastage and their environmental impacts. Various eco‐friendly ink formulation strategies are discussed together with their practical application. Additionally, the review addresses various end‐of‐life management strategies such as repair, recycling, and biodegradation. Finally, major challenges associated with digital printing of eco‐friendly electronics to compete with conventional electronics are explored and future perspectives in this emerging area are outlined.

articles.title: Dual‐Alloy Exsolution in Fe‐Based Perovskite Anodes for High‐Performance Direct Ammonia Solid Oxide Fuel Cells
articles.abstract: Direct ammonia solid oxide fuel cells (DA‐SOFCs) offer an integrated route for carbon‐free power generation by coupling in situ ammonia decomposition with electrochemical hydrogen oxidation. However, anode catalysts must simultaneously achieve rapid NH3 decomposition, efficient electrochemical charge transfer, and long‐term resistance to nitridation and particle coarsening. Here, we report an Fe‐based perovskite multi‐doped with Co and Ni, La0.6Sr0.2Ba0.2Mn0.2Fe0.6Co0.1Ni0.1O3 (P‐LSBMFCN), as a precursor for dual‐alloy exsolved DA‐SOFC anodes. Upon H2 reduction, P‐LSBMFCN transforms into a Ruddlesden‐Popper (RP) layered oxide decorated with highly dispersed FeCo and FeNi alloy nanoparticles (R‐LSBMFCN). Co and Ni multi‐doping directs the reduction‐induced nucleation and alloying pathway, reducing the average nanoparticle size from 129.3 nm for the Fe‐only reference to 48.3 nm for R‐LSBMFCN while increasing nanoparticle density. The resulting dual‐alloy architecture provides abundant accessible active sites and electronically tuned metal surfaces, accelerating NH3 activation, NHx intermediate conversion, and N recombination/desorption. Consequently, R‐LSBMFCN exhibits the lowest apparent activation energy, nearly complete NH3 conversion at high temperature, and maximum power densities of 1.638 and 1.386 W cm−2 under H2 and NH3 at 800°C, respectively, with stable operation for 200 h under NH3. This work demonstrates multi‐doping‐induced dual‐alloy exsolution as an effective strategy for durable DA‐SOFC anodes.

articles.title: Highly Efficient and Stable Roll‐to‐Roll Coated Perovskite Solar Cells Enabled by Antisolvent Vapor‐Assisted Crystallization
articles.abstract: A key challenge in roll-to-roll (R2R) perovskite solar cell (PSC) manufacturing is translating crystallization-control methods developed for laboratory-scale spin coating to scalable processes. Liquid antisolvent baths suffer from process drift due to contamination and generate substantial solvent waste, while gas-assisted quenching induces rapid nucleation with limited control over grain growth. Here, antisolvent vapor-assisted crystallization (AVAC) is demonstrated as a scalable strategy for controlling perovskite crystallization during R2R slot-die coating under ambient conditions. By regulating antisolvent vapor partial pressure within the coating zone, AVAC controls host-solvent extraction, limits moisture exposure, and promotes grain growth. One-step R2R coating of Cs0.12FA0.88PbI3 films using AVAC produces pinhole-free, α-phase films with grain sizes exceeding 500 nm. Corresponding PSCs with evaporated gold electrodes achieve champion power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 18.3%, and 15.2% for fully R2R-processed PSCs with a carbon electrode. The latter retain 97% of their initial PCE after more than 550 h of maximum power point tracking under 1000 W m− 2 illumination in an inert atmosphere at 38°C ± 2°C and < 1% relative humidity. This performance ranks among the highest reported for R2R-processed PSCs. Technical challenges associated with antisolvent properties for AVAC are discussed and suitable candidates for R2R manufacturing are identified.

articles.title: Hydrogel‐Based Method for High‐Resolution Measurements of Contact Mechanics in Rapid Biological Adhesives: A Case Study in Cuttlefish Tentacle Strikes
articles.abstract: Cuttlefish and squid attach to various substrates in their environment remarkably well using arms and extensible tentacles lined with arrays of suckers. Each sucker has a stiff internal ring with terminal teeth and microstructured rim. Previous studies have measured attachment forces of amputated suckers; however, in vivo investigations are lacking given the short time scales of attachment (milliseconds) and complex array geometries. To address this, we present a novel framework using a cross‐linked and plasticized gelatin hydrogel mimicking the non‐linear mechanical properties of prey tissues, high‐speed videography to locate sucker contact points, and optical coherence tomography for 3D reconstruction of sucker imprints. Comparing in vivo imprints to ex vivo indentations with predefined loads allowed us to correlate imprint shape with normal, contact forces at the sucker rim. We show that cross‐linking significantly increased the relaxation time of the hydrogel, essential for long‐term imprint retention, while plasticization may have reduced self‐healing by interfering with hydrogen‐bond reformation. Such properties enabled observations of sucker attachment in vivo, which indicated that sucker arrays function probabilistically and that aiming and alignment are achieved through large numbers of high‐safety‐factor suckers. Our hydrogel provides a new approach to study biological small‐scale attachment mechanisms in vivo.

articles.title: In Situ Constructed Fluorosulfided Interface With Metallic Mo Sites for Robust Anode‐Free Sodium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Anode‑free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs) are acclaimed for their low‑cost, sustainability, and high energy density. However, achieving highly reversible Na plating/stripping on bare current collectors (CCs) and robust solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is challenging. Herein, we present a robust fluorosulfided SEI (FS‐SEI) layer with metallic Mo active sites through in situ electrochemical transformation of 2D MoS2 coating on the Cu CCs. Specifically, the ingenious 2D MoS2 holds short ion transport pathways and large contact active areas during battery operation. Furthermore, MoS2 can in situ convert into metallic Mo and Na2S, while catalyzing the dissolution of NaPF6 to generate NaF. The in situ formed FS‐SEI film possesses excellent sodiophilicity, high Na+ diffusion, and good electron‐blocking capability, which effectively guides a homogeneous distribution of Na+ flux, accelerates the electrochemical reaction kinetics, and blocks side reactions between electrolyte and electrodes. Benefiting from these advantages, the MoS2@Cu half cells achieve average Coulombic efficiency of 99.85% over 350 cycles at 10 mA cm−2 and 10 mAh cm−2. When paired with Na3V2(PO4)3 cathodes, the AFSMBs exhibit excellent rate capability and cycling stability (>97.0% retention). This work offers insights into engineering a stable in situ SEI via 2D sodiophilic architectures, paving the way for developing energy‐dense and durable AFSMBs.

articles.title: Integrated Multiband Smart Windows From UV to LWIR Based on Molecularly Engineered Thermochromic Hydrogels
articles.abstract: Smart windows offer energy-saving potential for buildings, while challenges remain in achieving multi-band design across ultraviolet-visible-near infrared-long wavelength infrared (UV–VIS-NIR-LWIR). Here we present a smart window integrating a thermochromic poly (EEEA-co-NIPAM) (PEN) hydrogel with an anti-UV layer and an indium tin oxide layer, enabling dynamic VIS-NIR solar modulation alongside UV shielding and low LWIR emissivity (ɛ LWIR). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that 2-(2-ethoxyethoxy) ethyl acrylate (EEEA) comonomer strengthens the polymer network and forms favorable hydrogen-bonding interactions with N-isopropylacrylamide (NIPAM), promoting rapid dehydration-driven chain collapse above a reduced lower critical solution temperature, and accelerating the optical response during heating. The produced window achieves a solar modulation (ΔТ sol) of 42.7%, nearly complete UV shielding (T UV = 0.1%), and low indoor-facing ɛ LWIR = 0.31, with stable performance after 100-h UV exposure and 100 thermal cycles. Outdoor tests demonstrate a 7.7°C cooling effect compared with ordinary glass, while EnergyPlus simulations demonstrate up to 62.6% savings in building heating/cooling energy in Singapore, San Francisco, and Brisbane. This work provides an effective multiband strategy for smart windows together with an in-depth understanding of thermochromic hydrogel, and is expected to inspire future efforts toward spectrally selective, energy-efficient building glazing.

articles.title: Ion Migration in Metal Halide X‐Ray Detectors: Mechanism, Impact, and Suppression
articles.abstract: In recent years, metal halides (MHs) and their derivatives have emerged as promising candidates for x‐ray detection. These materials offer distinct advantages, including high x‐ray absorption efficiency, tunable bandgaps, low costs, and facile processing. While the performance of MHs‐based devices has improved rapidly, ion migration under high operating bias voltages remains a critical bottleneck. This phenomenon leads to severe degradation issues, such as elevated dark currents, electrode corrosion, baseline drift, and reduced carrier collection efficiency. Therefore, a systematic review of ion migration in MHs‐based x‐ray detectors is of crucial importance for breaking through the bottlenecks in their performance and stability, as well as advancing their practical applications. This review starts with the microscopic mechanisms of ion migration, detailing its origins, pathways, driving forces, and electrical characterization methods. Subsequently, based on energy band analysis, we elucidate the impact of ion migration on device performance. We then categorize existing suppression strategies into four main approaches: enhancing lattice interactions, minimizing migration channels, blocking transport pathways, and designing self‐powered detectors. Finally, the review discusses current challenges and outlines future development directions for stable MHs‐based x‐ray detectors.

articles.title: Multifunctional Phase Engineering Expands the Carrier Concentration Optimization Window for High‐Performance Mg3(Bi, Sb)2 Thermoelectrics
articles.abstract: The optimization of thermoelectric materials is fundamentally limited by the narrow carrier concentration (n H) window, which limits n H as an effective degree of freedom for enhancing performance. Here, we demonstrate that the introduction of a multifunctional phase overcomes this inherent limitation in Mg3(Bi, Sb)2. Specifically, the work-function difference between NbC and the Mg3(Bi, Sb)2 matrix drives interfacial electron transfer, establishing an elevated n H regime. NbC-induced grain growth suppresses grain-boundary scattering, thereby improving carrier mobility and significantly boosting electrical conductivity beyond the conventional n H optimization window. Meanwhile, interfacial charge redistribution and magnetic interactions associated with NbC modulate energy-dependent carrier scattering, increasing the scattering factor and enabling the Seebeck coefficient to be maintained or even enhanced under high n H. Consequently, the optimized composites achieve an outstanding average power factor of 3.1 mW m−1 K−2 over 300–573 K, along with a maximum zT of ∼1.3 at 523 K and an average zT of ∼1.1. Furthermore, the fabricated single-leg device achieved a conversion efficiency of ∼5.5% under a temperature difference of 282 K. This work breaks the conventional paradigm that restricts thermoelectric performance optimizing solely within the optimal n H regime, highlighting the pivotal role of multifunctional phase engineering in unlocking new performance frontiers.

articles.title: Preiodization Unlocks an Orbital‐Regulated Cascade Redox Chemistry for High‐Capacity Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
articles.abstract: Zinc‐iodine (Zn‐I2) batteries are considered as competitive candidates for large‐scale energy storage devices due to their high safety and low cost, but slow iodine conversion kinetics and limited theoretical capacity have always hindered their commercial application. In this work, the preiodization strategy successfully activates the iodine redox conversion of VS2 catalytic electrodes (I‐VS2/I2) and achieves a cascade of I0/I− redox and Zn2+ intercalation/deintercalation reactions. Theoretical and experimental analyses indicate that preiodization optimizes the V─I orbital coupling strength and electron exchange by effectively regulating the bonding and antibonding states occupation, which promotes the iodine redox conversion and inhibits polyiodide formation. Moreover, the cascade of I0/I− redox conversion and Zn2+ intercalation/deintercalation reactions contributes to exceeding the theoretical capacity limitation of conventional Zn‐I2 batteries. Consequently, high‐capacity (372 mAh g−1 at 0.5 A g−1) and cycling‐stable (86% capacity retention after 4000 cycles) Zn‐I2 batteries were acquired. The work offers an essential inspiration for investigating in depth the orbital electronic structure‐catalytic performance relationship.

articles.title: Pre‐Calcination‐Governed Spatial Architecture Engineering of MOF‐Derived Magnetic Carbon Nanohybrids for Effective Microwave Absorption
articles.abstract: Precisely steering the spatial distribution of functional units in MOF‐derived carbon‐based hybrids remains a formidable challenge for microwave absorption. Here we reveal that pre‐calcination can govern the intermediate chemistry and final spatial architectures of an identical ZIF‐8@PBA precursor, yielding two structurally distinct nanohybrids (Fe3C−N−C and Fe3C−N−CNTs). Pre‐calcination at 200°C preserves the ZIF‐8@PBA framework to spatially confine Fe species enabling uniform Fe3C dispersion during subsequent pyrolysis, forming Fe3C−N−C; whereas pre‐calcination at 400°C decomposes the framework into Fe3O4/ZnO intermediates that convert to surface‐exposed Fe3C with localized enrichment, catalyzing carbon nanotubes (CNTs) growth to yield Fe3C−N−CNTs. The Fe3C−N−C architecture simultaneously enhances polarization relaxation, ferromagnetic resonance, and impedance matching, thus delivering a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of −73.60 dB and an ultrawide effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 9.29 GHz at 3.32 mm, superior to its pervious cournterparts. In comparison, The Fe3C−N−CNTs shifts to a dielectric‐dominated regime, yielding an RLmin of −65.71 dB, and an EAB of 7.79 GHz at 2.04 mm. These findings reveal that nanoscale spatial arrangements govern the attenuation–impedance balance in microwave absorbers. This work establishes a new mechanistic paradigm for designing high‐performance microwave absorbers and functional materials by tailoring spatial architectures.

articles.title: Printable Architected Porous Ceramic Metamaterials Enabling Electromagnetic‐Thermal Coupling
articles.abstract: The coupled demands for electromagnetic interference mitigation and thermal management in aerospace and advanced electronic systems necessitate lightweight materials that integrate broadband microwave absorption with effective thermal insulation under extreme operating conditions. Conventional electromagnetic absorbers and thermal barriers are typically monofunctional, whereas metamaterials, despite their architectural versatility, often exhibit limited thermal protection. Here we introduce a printable porous Silicon‐Boron Oxycarbide (SiBOC) ceramic metamaterial that combines structural precision, multifunctionality, and high‐temperature resilience. By dispersing hollow glass microspheres (HGMs) into a UV‐curable SiBOC pre‐ceramic polymer, we achieve a resin system that simultaneously supports high loading, porosity, and digital light processing printability. During heat treatment, HGMs act as both structural stabilizers and catalytic reservoirs, yielding a hierarchical SiBOC@Graphene@HGM architecture. This unique configuration enhances dielectric loss, promotes multi‐scattering, and suppresses heat conduction. Consequently, the porous SiBOC ceramic metamaterial achieves an ultrabroad effective absorption bandwidth of 35.58 GHz (within 2–40 GHz, at the incident angle of 50°) with a minimum reflection loss of −59.71 dB, along with low thermal conductivity (0.208 W·m−1·K−1) and light density (0.313 g cm−3). This strategy establishes a generalizable paradigm for multifunctional ceramic metamaterials, bridging electromagnetic and thermal protection for next‐generation extreme‐environment applications.

articles.title: Separator‐Mediated Pre‐Desolvation Regulation via Oxygen‐Doped Carbon Nitride for Efficient Sodium Storage in Hard Carbon
articles.abstract: Hard carbon (HC) is a highly promising anode for sodium‐ion batteries, yet its practical reversibility is still limited by uncontrolled electrolyte reduction at the HC/electrolyte interface. Herein, we developed a separator‐mediated pre‐desolvation regulation strategy via oxygen‐doped carbon nitride (CNOI) modified separator that enables concurrent interfacial passivation and rapid Na+ transport. The CNOI with abundant polar N/O sites electrostatically interacts with Na+ and preconditions its local solvation environment before interfacial charge transfer. As a result, the Na+ flux across the separator becomes more homogeneous, and the interfacial desolvation barrier is reduced, thereby promoting the in situ formation of a thin, ion‐conductive SEI. Accordingly, HC|Na half‐cells with the CNOI‐modified separator exhibit an initial Coulombic efficiency of 93.0%, sustain a capacity of 297.7 mAh g−1 after 600 cycles at 1 C, and deliver 247.3 mAh g−1 even at an elevated rate of 15 C. It also realizes remarkable low‐temperature adaptability, delivering a capacity of 163.5 mAh g−1 at 0.5 C even at −40°C. This work establishes separator‐driven pre‐desolvation regulation as a transferable interfacial engineering strategy for high‐performance HC anodes of practical sodium‐ion batteries.

articles.title: Tailoring Covalent Organic Frameworks as Functionalized Molecular Traps to Enable Sulfur Conversion and Li+ Desolvation for Durable Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
articles.abstract: Suppressing polysulfid shuttling and enhancing Li+ desolvation kinetics are crucial for high‐performance lithium–sulfur (Li─S) batteries.
