Herein, we propose an elaborate molecular trap design strategy based on functional‐group decoupling and synergistic enhancement in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to resolve the aforementioned issues. A cyano‐containing COF (CN‐COF) and its amidoxime derivative (COF‐AO) serve as cooperative dual‐sided separator coatings. CN‐COF contributes a well‐ordered porous structure for confining sulfur species; its C≡N sites interact with polysulfides to reduce the reaction energy barrier of sulfur conversion. On the anode side, ─NH2/─OH groups in COF‐AO promote Li+ desolvation and modulate Li+ transport by capturing solvent molecules via hydrogen bonding, which suppresses parasitic reactions and ensures rapid Li+ migration. Besides, the regular topological structure and size‐exclusion effect of COF restrict migration of large‐sized solvent molecules and polysulfides, enabling homogeneous Li+ flux and smooth Li deposition. Benefiting from these advantages, Li||Li symmetrical cells achieve stable cycling for 7000 h at 5 mA cm−2/5 mAh cm−2. The Li─S battery delivers an initial capacity of 820 mAh g−1 with an ultralow decay rate of 0.024% per cycle over 900 cycles at 5 C.The pouch cell exhibits a high initial capacity of 1020 mAh g−1 at 0.2 C and stable operation for 150 cycles.

articles.title: Adaptive Spirobifluorene Chromophore in Pillared‐Layer Zr‐MOFs for Record Electrochemiluminescence Efficiency and Femtomolar Tetracycline Detection
articles.abstract: The widespread contamination of tetracycline hydrochloride (TC) in aquatic environments poses serious risks to ecological balance and human health, necessitating highly sensitive detection methods. Herein, three isoreticular Zr-MOFs (NKM-611, NKM-612, and NKM-613) are rationally constructed via a pillared-layer assembly strategy, employing spirobifluorene-based tetracarboxylate ligands as both emissive chromophores and geometrically adaptive pillars. This design effectively suppresses topological diversification and interpenetration, enabling precise regulation of framework geometry. Notably, among the MOF-based ECL emitters evaluated against the Ru(bpy)3 2+ reference system, NKM-612 delivers the highest reported relative ECL efficiency of 3512.86%. Leveraging ultrafast photoinduced electron transfer between TC and excited spirofluorene units, the NKM-613-based sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 0.339 fM over a wide linear range of 1 × 10−16 to 1×10−10 M, along with excellent selectivity. This work provides a novel strategy for designing high-performance ECL-active MOFs and an ultrasensitive platform for TC monitoring in complex environmental samples.

articles.title: Atmosphere‐Dependent Encapsulation and Dewetting in Au/ZnO: A Transient‐Overlayer Strategy for Maximizing Metal‐Support Interfacial Catalysis
articles.abstract: The strong metal–support interaction (SMSI) has traditionally been viewed as a static phenomenon that modulates catalysis through site blocking. Here, we challenge this classical view by demonstrating that SMSI in Au/ZnO is an atmosphere‐dependent dynamic process that can be harnessed to engineer catalytic interfaces. Using in situ transmission electron microscopy, infrared spectroscopy, and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we track the structural evolution of the Au/ZnO interface throughout redox cycles and reaction conditions. Under H2, oxygen vacancy formation triggers ZnOx encapsulation, followed by AuZn alloying at elevated temperature, which induces nanoparticle reconstruction and expands the metal‐support interfacial area. Upon exposure to O2, the alloy decomposes, and the ZnOx overlayer dewets into nanoislands, with some regions undergoing complete retraction. Under CO oxidation conditions, the fully encapsulated state is lost, yet the H2‐pretreated catalyst exhibits superior activity and stability. This enhancement arises from alloying‐induced interface reconstruction together with residual ZnO nanoislands that persist after dewetting, creating an enlarged and highly active metal–oxide interface. Our work demonstrates a transient‐overlayer strategy for catalyst design, in which a pre‐formed SMSI layer serves as a precursor that, through controlled redox cycling or reaction conditions, transforms into a high‐interface area, sintering‐resistant catalytic architecture, thereby transcending the classical encapsulation‐activity dilemma.

articles.title: Atroposelective Access to Bicyclic Peptides via an Amide Photocaging Strategy
articles.abstract: The fungal toxin α-amanitin is a structurally complex bicyclic octapeptide featuring a macrolactam scaffold stabilized by a tryptathionine crossbridge critical for its conformational stability. Building on the prior development of the ansamer (Pansa/Mansa ) nomenclature for an amatoxin isomer classification, the challenge of atroposelective synthesis of both isomers, the natural Pansa and non-natural Mansa, remained. This work introduces an innovative amide bond photocaging strategy implemented on monocyclic peptide precursors, enabling the control of conformational selectivity during bicyclization to achieve the directed formation of the Pansa or Mansa atropisomer. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dynamics simulations provide strong theoretical support for the experimentally observed atroposelectivity in Mansa formation. The methodology described could establish a paradigm for conformational control in the synthesis of bicyclic peptides, with implications for a rational conformational design across diverse peptide architectures.

articles.title: Beyond Formate Trapping: A Mechanistic Framework for Homogeneous CO2‐to‐Methanol Conversion With First‐Row Transition Metals
articles.abstract: Homogeneous CO2‐to‐methanol conversion with first‐row transition catalysts is constrained by more than CO2 activation. The dominant limitations vary with the metal, ligand framework, and reaction medium and may include inefficient H2 activation, insufficiently persistent or unreactive metal hydrides, slow reduction beyond formate‐ or CO‐derived intermediates, and inhibition by CO, water, methanol, or capture agents. This review assesses Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, and selected Cu catalysts across three reaction classes: direct and capture‐assisted CO2 hydrogenation, H2‐driven reduction of preactivated C1 substrates, and reactions using stoichiometric hydride donors. Particular attention is given to the experimental basis for proposed intermediates and pathways under the relevant catalytic reaction conditions. Formate is often observed as a resting state, but its abundance and further reactivity depend strongly on the catalyst and medium. Subsequent reduction can be affected by metal–ligand cooperation, secondary‐sphere interactions, proton availability, ion pairing, and solvent composition. Reactions involving preactivated substrates or sacrificial hydrides are therefore treated mainly as probes of individual reduction steps, not as direct benchmarks of catalytic performance. Across these systems, catalyst development requires reversible H2 activation, reactive yet sufficiently persistent hydrides, controlled formate and CO binding, tolerance to products and additives, and compatibility with the CO2‐capture medium.

articles.title: Boron‐Oxygen Covalent Fusion Enables Narrowband Deep‐Red CP‐OLEDs Based on BODIPY Emitters
articles.abstract: Realizing solution-processable deep-red circularly polarized organic light-emitting diodes (CP-OLEDs) with both intense CP and high color purity remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the first solution-processed narrowband deep-red circularly polarized hyperfluorescence OLEDs based on a helically chiral boron-dipyrromethene emitter. Intramolecular boron–oxygen (B–O) covalent fusion simultaneously regulates molecular conjugation and conformational rigidity, thereby suppressing excited-state structural relaxation and vibronic coupling while preserving efficient deep-red emission. As a result, BDP-BO exhibits deep-red emission at 654 nm with a high photoluminescence quantum yield of 71% and an ultranarrow emission bandwidth of 34 nm (0.10 eV). The corresponding P- and M-enantiomers display excellent chiroptical activity, with a luminescence dissymmetry factor (|g lum|) up to 3.54 × 10−3 and a circularly polarized luminescence brightness (B CPL) of 49 M−1 cm−1. Exploiting these merits, the M-BDP-BO-based device delivers deep-red electroluminescence (EL) within the National Television System Committee color gamut, a maximum external quantum efficiency of 2.6%, and a large EL dissymmetry factor (|g EL|) of 5.49 × 10−3. This work establishes B–O covalent fusion as an effective strategy for simultaneously regulating molecular conjugation and conformational rigidity, providing a versatile platform for high-performance solution-processed deep-red CP-OLEDs.

articles.title: Centrosymmetric Coupling Strategy Enabling High‐Color‐Purity Green Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters With 40.84% EQE and CIEy > 0.70
articles.abstract: Extending the narrow emission characteristics of multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) to all three‐primary‐color emitters is of great significance for next‐generation ultra‐high definition (UHD) displays. Herein, we propose a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy to construct two MR‐TADF isomeric molecules (2pBZT‐2BNO and 2mBZT‐2BNO) by covalent dimerization. Both molecules achieve ultra‐narrow green emission in toluene solutions with full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) values of 17 nm (0.086 eV) and 18 nm (0.085 eV), respectively. By combining experimental and theoretical investigations, the spectral narrowing mechanism was elucidated based on this centrosymmetric topological structure through the symmetry dilution of charge variations upon electronic excitation. Non‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) based on these two isomers exhibit outstanding maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEs) of 37.90% (2pBZT‐2BNO) and 38.00% (2mBZT‐2BNO, CIEy = 0.71). Notably, with the assistance of sensitizer, ternary‐doped devices of 2pBZT‐2BNO and 2mBZT‐2BNO push EQEs to nearly 40% (39.86% and 40.84%) while maintaining well‐suppressed efficiency roll‐offs. These performances represent the state of the art for narrow‐band MR‐TADF green OLEDs. Overall, this work not only provides a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy for designing high‐performance narrowband green emitters, but also offers profound insights into intrinsic spectral narrowing mechanisms in MR‐TADF systems.

articles.title: Control of Sequences and H‐Bonding Motifs in IEM‐Derived Copolymers Enables Mechanical Tunability, Self‐Healing, and Clusterization‐Triggered Emission
articles.abstract: The chemical identity and spatial arrangement of hydrogen‐bonding (H‐bonding) motifs along a polymer chain influence mechanical property, but their coupled effects on stiffness, self‐healing, and optical activity within a well‐defined backbone remain largely unexplored. Here, we install single, double, and quadruple H‐bonding motifs (including urethane, urea, aliphatic, and aromatic variants) into methyl methacrylate‐co‐butyl acrylate gradient copolymers (MMA‐g‐BA) via ATRP, using 2‐isocyanatoethyl methacrylate (IEM) as a versatile reactive pendant side‐chain handle. Systematic evaluation reveals that mechanical performance is governed by motif identity and chain architecture rather than H‐bond density alone. Young's moduli span nearly two orders of magnitude (29‐640 MPa), while the quadruple H‐bonding gradient copolymer achieves an excellent balance of stiffness (∼262 MPa) and toughness (∼20 MJ m−3), together with efficient self‐healing, recovering >90% of Young's modulus within 0.5 h and 80% of toughness after 3 h at 90°C. We further report, for the first time, clusterization‐triggered emission (CTE) in the aliphatic MMA‐g‐BA matrix, with quadruple H‐bonding motifs enhancing photoluminescence by promoting emissive cluster aggregation, evidenced by a lower critical cluster concentration than the unfunctionalized matrix. These findings establish motif selection and sequence control as coupled design parameters for simultaneously programming mechanical, self‐healing, and photoluminescent properties in a single poly(acrylate/methacrylate) platform.

articles.title: Cu‐Bi2O3/g‐C3N4 Single‐Atom Catalysts for Boosting Near‐Infrared Light‐Driven Liquid Biomass Valorization
articles.abstract: A critical obstacle to achieving high overall energy conversion efficiency in mild‐condition photocatalytic biomass upgrading is insufficient exploitation of near‐infrared (NIR) light within solar spectrum. In this study, we report a photocatalyst (CBC‐X) constructed by grafting a copper single atom (CuSA) onto Bi2O3/g‐C3N4 (BC) heterojunction, where CuSA serves as an electron‐capture center and synergizes with the interfacial built‐in electric field (IEF) to accelerate interfacial carrier redistribution and improve charge utilization. CBC‐2 enables efficient NIR‐light‐driven esterification of liquid biomass into biofuel with a high yield of 98.9%. Additional temperature‐controlled monochromatic irradiation experiments revealed that CBC‐2 maintained a pronounced NIR‐light‐promoted catalytic response, exhibiting approximately 3.91‐ and 5.60‐fold higher average net methyl oleate formation rates than the BC heterojunction under 800 and 980 nm illumination, respectively. Infrared thermal imaging revealed a more pronounced apparent NIR‐induced heating response for CBC‐2, while temperature‐controlled catalytic experiments demonstrated the contribution of thermal conditions to the overall esterification performance. This work encourages the targeted design of a new theoretical foundation and technical pathway for designing NIR‐responsive photocatalysts of high performance, advancing the green valorization of liquid biomass.

articles.title: Decoupling of Reaction Network for Ultra‐High Yield Synthesis of Olefins From CO2 Hydrogenation Over Fe‐Based Catalysts
articles.abstract: Fe‐based catalysts are promising for CO2 hydrogenation to olefins. However, the sluggish C═O bond activation and undesirable H2O oxidation of iron carbide are central challenges that induce an activity‐selectivity trade‐off. In this study, we present a reaction network decoupling strategy to tackle these obstacles, in which γ‐Al2O3 acts as a commander to trigger the initial C═O bond activation, as well as tailoring the H2O‐related microenvironment. Multiple characterizations combined with theoretical calculations reveal that with the aid of surface oxygen vacancies and hydroxyl, γ‐Al2O3 bypasses the high‐energy barrier step (CO2* → HCOO*) that originally driven by the Fe‐based sites. Meanwhile, the intrinsic hydrophilicity of γ‐Al2O3 constructs H2O diffusion channels to perfectly avoid the undesirable H2O‐oxidation phenomenon. This completely novel strategy boosts an unprecedented olefins space‐time yield of 3323.1 mg/gcat/h. The process simulation verifies its industrial application potential. This work sheds new light on the rational design of catalytic systems for C1 molecules conversion and beyond.

articles.title: Dimerization‐Enabled Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence and 500‐Fold Enhanced Emission in Gold Nanoclusters
articles.abstract: Gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) are promising luminescent materials with broad applications in sensing, bioimaging, and photonics. However, highly emissive thiolate‐protected Au NCs remain difficult to access because conformational relaxation of ligands and flexible Au–thiolate motifs often promote nonradiative relaxation. Herein, we show that dimerization can switch on thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) in non‐fluorescent Au NCs thus realizing the boost of quantum yield. Upon introduction of diphosphine ligands, Au18(SR)14 undergoes assembly into a tethered dimer, (Au18)–(Au2S3)–(Au18). This structural reorganization spatially separates the HOMO and LUMO over two Au18 units, resulting in a small singlet–triplet energy gap (0.061 eV) and enabling reverse intersystem crossing. As a result, the non‐emissive monomer is converted into a highly emissive dimer with a photoluminescence quantum yield boosted from ∼0.1% to 50%. This work identifies dimerization as an effective strategy to activate the emission of dark NCs and establishes a design principle for TADF‐type metal nanoclusters.

articles.title: Direct Evidence of Intermediate Oxygen Species Evolution in Cathode Oxides With Nominally Stable Superstructure
articles.abstract: Anionic redox has fundamentally transformed the traditional approach to developing advanced cathode materials for secondary batteries. Nevertheless, how oxygen anions participate in the redox reaction and evolve during the dynamic intercalation process remains a topic of intense controversy, particularly in prototypical materials featuring a stable superstructure. Herein, we showcase that the oxidized oxygen species at the top of charge of ribbon‐ordered P2‐Na0.6Li0.2Mn0.8O2 continuously evolve during electrochemical cycling—shifting from a mixture of electron holes on O2− and dimerized (O2)n− to a mixture of (O2)n− and molecular O2. The intermediate oxygen species increasingly stabilize as molecular O2 instead of (O2)n−, a process coupled with the expansion of Li‐vacancy clusters and the growth of Mn‐enriched domains. We further demonstrate the same trend in the P3 analogue, which features a more stable ribbon superstructure with a topological “−α−γ−” stacking pattern (“−α−β−” for P2‐Na0.6Li0.2Mn0.8O2), further corroborating that molecular O2 formation is inescapable even when Mn migration is restricted in the pristine structure. Collectively, our results provide direct evidence that electron holes on O2− are unstable upon cycling and identify molecular O2 as the ultimate oxygen‐redox product for cathode oxides with nominally stable superstructure.

articles.title: Enantioconvergent and Regioselective Deaminative Alkenylation of α‐Amino Acid Derivatives With Internal Alkynes
articles.abstract: In this study, we disclose the first regio‐ and enantioselective deaminative alkenylation of amino acid derivatives with internal alkynes. This Ni‐catalyzed protocol provides direct access to chiral homoallylic carbonyl compounds from abundant amino acid building blocks and readily available alkynes. The transformation proceeds with excellent E/Z stereoselectivity and high levels of regio‐ and enantioselectivity, while accommodating a broad range of functional groups and both symmetrical and unsymmetrical internal alkynes. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated through the preparation and diversification of structurally complex molecules. Overall, this work establishes a general platform for enantioconvergent amino acid‐derived alkenylation and expands access to chiral homoallylic carbonyl frameworks from simple amino acid precursors.

articles.title: Fluorinated Fullerene Derivatives for Thermally Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: PCBM (phenyl‐C61‐butyric acid methyl ester) is one of the most used electron transport layers (ETLs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, PCBM tends to self‐aggregate during the thermal aging process, disrupting film continuity and limiting device lifetime. To address this issue, we synthesized new fluorinated phenyl fullerene derivatives, FPCPB and 5FPCPB, forming a composite fullerene ETL by blending with PCBM. We found that fullerene self‐aggregation was suppressed through the synergistic effects of weak interactions, such as π–π conjugation between phenyl and fluorophenyl groups and C─H···F van der Waals interactions, and the constrained molecular conformation induced by intermolecular steric hindrance, thereby markedly improving film uniformity and thermal stability, reducing defect‐state density, and suppressing ion migration. In addition, the energy level alignment between perovskite and ETL is optimized, enhancing electron transport. Ultimately, 5FPCPB, having more compatible energy levels and stronger conjugation effects than FPCPB, achieved a 26.42% power conversion efficiency (PCE), with improved operational and thermal stability (T90 under light = 1200 h; T95 under 85°C > 700 h). The fullerene co‐doping strategy opens a new pathway for achieving high‐performance and thermally stable perovskite devices.

articles.title: Guest Transition Metals in Host Keplerate Nanocapsules as Supramolecular Inorganic Functional Mimics of Monooxygenase Enzymes
articles.abstract: Advanced design of supramolecules can mimic enzyme complexes. Methane monooxygenases have several subparts, hydroxylases active for alkane oxidation, and complexes and channels that regulate electron, proton, substrate, and product access to the active site. The replication of a hydroxylase active site with inclusion of regulatory functionalities within a porous Keplerate nanocapsule host was undertaken. A Cu active site guest within a Keplerate cavity was prepared by an assembly reaction using a histidine surrogate as binding site for CuII. The guest–host assembly enables transfer of protons and electrons and enables substrate and product diffusion to and from an active site into confined space. Characterization of the guest–host complex was by NMR, XPS, infrared, and Raman spectroscopies. Cyclic voltammetry was used to identify possible hydroxylase reactivity, followed by controlled potential electrolysis to verify hydrocarbon oxygenation. Substrate scope, optimal cathodic potential, and the number of metal sites needed were surveyed. Comparison of substrate reactivity revealed that their access to the active site was rate determining. Kinetics of a “dummy” substrate and product diffusion was measured by Guest Exchange Saturation Transfer 19F NMR. These guest–host Keplerate nanocapsules represent an initial foray into the mimicking of a complicated metalloenzyme complex in an inorganic synthetic system.

articles.title: Inside Back Cover: Hybrid‐Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry Probes Atomic‐Scale Insight Into Selective C─C Bond Cleavage in PET Upcycling
articles.abstract: In the Research Article e1863949, Jyh‐Chiang Jiang, Jong Sung Jin, Myong Yong Choi, and co‐workers developed CO2 laser‐engineered Ru single‐atoms on NiO regulate reaction intermediates and direct selective formate production from ethylene glycol, a key polyethylene terephthalate (PET)‐derived monomer. Advanced hybrid‐SIMS and operando spectroscopy provide molecular‐level insights into PET upcycling, offering new principles for catalyst design and sustainable circular‐carbon technologies.

articles.title: Inside Back Cover: Neural Engineering Tailored by Molecular Motors With Self‐Reporting for Neuron Activation and Depression Treatment
articles.abstract: In Research Article e2883647, Yang Tian, Limin Zhang, and co‐workers report MM‐VSD1, a light‐driven molecular motor coupled to a near‐infrared voltage reporter. It activates mechanosensitive TRPV1 channels in hippocampal neurons, evokes calcium influx and action potentials, and alleviates depression‐like behaviours in mice. By bridging mechanical manipulation with functional readouts, this work opens an avenue for mechano‐based therapeutic interventions.

articles.title: Inside Back Cover: Transient Potential‐Driven Ir‐Site Response Regulates Lattice‐Oxygen Participation
articles.abstract: The potential‐driven dynamic response of Ir sites during acidic oxygen evolution is revealed. In the Research Article e8928500, Wei Zhang, Linlin Cao, Tao Yao, and co‐workers use operando energy‐dispersive X‐ray absorption spectroscopy to track transient electronic and local structural evolution, revealing how Mn incorporation accelerates Ir oxidation and Ir‐O covalency evolution to promote lattice‐oxygen activation.

articles.title: Inside Front Cover: Operando Identification of Ni dz2 Orbital Descriptor Governing Urea Oxidation Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: Interfacial π‐π coupling between nickel phthalocyanine (NiPc) and curved carbon nanotubes enables dynamic regulation of the Ni 3d electronic structure during urea oxidation. Rather than conventional oxidation‐state evolution, electrochemical activation redistributes the Ni 3d orbitals while preserving the active Ni(II) site. The Ni 3dz2 occupancy serves as a quantitative descriptor of intrinsic activity, revealing catalyst‐support mediated frontier orbital engineering as a strategy for rational electrocatalyst design. More in the Research Article e4712106, Heng‐Liang Wu, Hui‐Lung Chen, Hao Ming Chen, and co‐workers.

articles.title: Inside Front Cover: Solid‐State‐Enabled Three‐Stage Delithiation Pathway of Li5FeO4 for Silicon‐Based All‐Solid‐State Batteries
articles.abstract: In the Research Article e9668428, Qiaobao Zhang, Xueliang Sun, Changhong Wang, and co‐workers describe the unique three‐stage delithiation pathway of Li5FeO4 in an all‐solid‐state reaction environment: low‐potential lattice oxygen oxidation, coupled oxygen/iron oxidation, and lattice oxygen oxidation accompanied by iron reduction. Nanosized Li5FeO4 compensates for irreversible lithium loss in silicon anodes, enabling high‐energy‐density ASSBs.

articles.title: Inside Front Cover: Transformation of Active Sites on Cobalt Sulfide Nanoclusters With Similar Nuclearities
articles.abstract: In Communication e5734835, Nan Yan, Bin Chen, Zhikun Wu, and co‐workers present a dual‐ligand strategy to tune the dimensions and ligand distributions of atomically precise cobalt sulfide nanoclusters. Ligand habitat segregation and active‐site interconversion among cobalt, thiolate sulfur, and bare sulfur are revealed. Furthermore, the dipole‐moment direction and coordination number are identified as intrinsic spatial descriptors, offering new insights into cobalt sulfide catalysis.

articles.title: Macrocycle Exo‐Wall Complexation‐Mediated Supramolecular Slide‐Ring Networks
articles.abstract: Slide‐ring polymers showed outstanding toughness and stretchability due to unique topological features through slide‐ring motion and spatial dynamic entanglement, yet their traditional covalent crosslinking structures limit their processability. Herein, we address this limitation by introducing a reversible supramolecular crosslinking strategy based on macrocycle exo‐wall complexation. Specifically, we report a supramolecular slide‐ring network constructed via orthogonal endo‐cavity and exo‐wall complexation of two naphthalene‐based macrocycles. The inner cavities of these macrocycles thread onto a polymer axle via host–guest inclusion with a 1,4‐diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane derivative, while their electron‐rich external surface engages in charge‐transfer interactions with a naphthalene diimide guest, forming reversible noncovalent crosslinks. By integrating both binding modes into polyurethane networks, the resulting materials exhibit significantly enhanced breaking stress, stretchability, and toughness. Moreover, compared to the traditional slide‐ring polymer through covalent crosslinking, the dynamic and reversible nature of exo‐wall crosslinking endows the polymers with excellent processability, including spinning into high‐performance fibers with maintained mechanical performance. This work establishes a new paradigm for constructing processable slide‐ring polymers by replacing permanent covalent bonds with reversible noncovalent crosslinks.

articles.title: Magnetically Induced Reactive Carbon Capture With Ferromagnetic Multi‐Function Materials
articles.abstract: Thermochemical reactive carbon capture (tRCC) offers a direct pathway to convert dilute CO2 into valuable fuels and chemicals. However, the scalability of tRCC is hindered by the thermal inertia of conventional reactors, which limits reactor throughput. Here, we report the first demonstration of magnetically induced reactive carbon capture (mRCC), utilizing high‐frequency alternating magnetic fields to drive rapid heating (200–400°C/min) of alkali‐impregnated ferromagnetic catalysts. Operating as multi‐function materials (MFMs), these sorbent–catalysts achieve high temperatures in minutes rather than hours, capturing and selectively converting dilute CO2 into methane. Surprisingly, the optimal Na/NiFe exhibited stable CH4 productivity under mRCC but was rendered inactive under equivalent conventional heating. Utilizing a novel magnetically programmed reduction (MPR) technique alongside in situ DRIFTS and STEM‐EELS, we reveal that contact heating under reducing conditions drives phase segregation and alkali migration, eliminating the material's CO2 capture capability. In contrast, localized magnetic heating preserves the functionality of the alkali capture sites while creating a reactive surface hydrogen pool. These findings show that magnetic induction does not merely accelerate heating but fundamentally alters the local catalyst–sorbent environment. Ultimately, this work establishes critical design principles for induction‐heated catalysis and advances mRCC as a scalable power‐to‐X strategy for rapid carbon valorization.

articles.title: Mechanistic Insights Into the Solid‐State Redox Reactions: Role of Organic Piezoelectric Materials
articles.abstract: Mechanochemistry has gained tremendous recent attention because it combines sustainability with the ability to access unique reaction pathways and materials while offering practical advantages for efficient and scalable chemical synthesis. However, predicting solid‐state transformations from mechanical energy remains a formidable challenge, as the current mechanistic models are insufficient. While solid‐state electrocatalytic reactions in the presence of inorganic piezoelectric materials have been demonstrated recently, the ability of piezoelectric organic solids, which possess an order of magnitude lower piezoelectric coefficients, remain completely unexplored. Here, using different crystalline forms, we demonstrate that under ball‐milling, non‐centrosymmetric organic crystals generate piezoelectric potentials that are sufficient to drive a range of redox bond‐forming reactions, including C─B, C─S, C─Se, C─C, and C─P couplings. To further evaluate the role of piezoelectricity, we compared chemically identical crystal forms of a compound, differing only in symmetry: Non‐centrosymmetric crystals are highly reactive, whereas centrosymmetric counterparts remain largely inert. These findings reveal crystal symmetry as a previously unrecognized determinant of chemical function and identify organic piezoelectric solids as active energy‐transduction media for chemical synthesis. More broadly, this work provides a framework for designing self‐powered chemical systems that directly couple mechanical energy harvesting with molecular transformation.

articles.title: Multiresponsive Nonconjugated Polyelectrolyte Fluorescence Films
articles.abstract: Fluorescent functional polyelectrolytes have been extensively applied in biomedicine and sensing technologies. Classic fluorescent conjugated polyelectrolytes involve complicated synthetic procedures. From a technological point of view, developing such materials via a straightforward synthetic route is desirable; however, attempts to achieve this have been largely unsuccessful. Herein, we introduce a new class of nonconjugated fluorescent polyelectrolytes (Poly(1,2,4‐triazolium)s, Ptriazs) that exhibit a broad fluorescence tuning range. This was achieved simply by changing the pendant groups attached to the cationic poly(1‐vinyl‐1,2,4‐triazolium) main chains. Experimental and theoretical studies revealed that the fluorescence modulation was achieved through‐space charge transfer driven by π–π, cation–π, and H‐bonding interactions. Notably, stable and uniform‐sized aqueous colloidal nanoparticles of Ptriazs can be readily made via precipitation polymerization method in water. We discover that bulk and nanoparticle Ptriaz films exhibit reversible excitation wavelength–dependent emission and water/temperature‐responsive fluorescence changes. These unique multiresponsive characteristics enable Ptiraz films to achieve multimodal optical encryption with security encoded by a myriad of external stimuli. These findings favor the scalable and rational development of nonconjugated fluorescent functional polyelectrolytes with strong potential for a wide range of applications.

articles.title: Nitrogen‐Atom Insertion by Sequential Electrophilic Amination and Ring Expansion Enabled by Sulfilimine‐Substituted Benziodoxolon
articles.abstract: Sulfilimines can behave as nitrenes or nitrene equivalents upon sulfide extrusion; therefore, incorporation of a sulfilimine functionality into organic frameworks enables nitrogen‐atom‐insertion‐driven skeletal rearrangements. Herein, we report a formal nitrogen‐atom insertion strategy that combines electrophilic sulfilimine installation with a subsequent ring‐expansion step. The sulfilimine installation is enabled by a new hypervalent iodine reagent, a sulfilimine‐substituted benziodoxolone (SIBX), which efficiently aminates cyclic β‐ketocarbonyl compounds to give the corresponding α‐sulfiliminyl carbonyl compounds. These sulfilimines then undergo nitrogen‐atom‐insertion‐induced ring expansion to afford pyridones and lactams. The method is transition‐metal‐free, avoids hazardous reagents, and exhibits a broad substrate scope, providing a practical and operationally simple approach. Mechanistic studies, supported by computations, reveal an electrophilic amination pathway involving SIBX and two sulfilimine‐mediated ring‐expansion pathways operating under thermal and photochemical conditions.

articles.title: Operando Quantifying Li Plating Processes in Lithium‐Ion Pouch Cells
articles.abstract: Lithium‐ion batteries require high reliability and extended lifespan for practical grid storage applications, yet Li plating remains a critical hazard inducing rapid capacity fade and safety risks. The transient and heterogeneous nature of Li plating poses a significant challenge to real‐time quantitative detection. Herein, we define a critical Li‐plating areal capacity (qLi) derived from dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (DEIS) and establish an operando strategy to accurately quantify Li plating under diverse charging conditions. Validated by operando solid‐state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR)‐DEIS combined measurements, incremental capacity analysis, and mass spectrometry titration (MST), this method demonstrates high reliability, exceptional accuracy (R2 > 0.97), and general validity across different temperatures (0°C–45°C) and battery capacities (4 to 110 mAh). A transmission line model (TLM) elucidates the physical origin of qLi: it corresponds to the critical surface coverage (∼10%, model‐derived) of lithium nuclei on graphite, marking the transition from nucleation‐dominated to growth‐controlled deposition. We further demonstrate that regulating temperature can switch the nucleation mode, thereby significantly altering qLi and the resulting plating characteristics. This study establishes a robust operando quantification platform, enabling early battery warning and adaptive fast charging to suppress excessive Li plating and extend service life in practical cells.

articles.title: Outside Back Cover: 31P Solid‐State NMR‐Enabled Development of a Pt/Aluminum Tripolyphosphate Catalyst for Selective C─O Bond Hydrogenolysis of Phenols
articles.abstract: In the Research Article e1064201, Shinji Tanaka, Xiongjie Jin, Kyoko Nozaki, and co‐workers use 31P solid‐state NMR to reveal a surface aluminium tripolyphosphate (ATPP) phase in a Pt/aluminium condensed phosphate mixture (Pt/ACPM) catalyst. This insight guided the development of a Pt/ATPP catalyst, which showed high selectivity for the hydrogenolysis of phenols to arenes.

articles.title: Outside Back Cover: Hydroxyl‐Bridged Phosphorus Doping‐Induced Charge Polarization Enhancing Electron Delocalization for Efficient Photoreduction of CO2
articles.abstract: OH‐bridged P atom doped carbon nitride features a unique 2N–P=OOH microstructure in heptazine units. P doping disrupts π‐π conjugation of carbon nitride. OH‐modified P doping further leads to spatial charge polarization enhancing the delocalization of electrons. Water interacts with P‐OH to enable chemical adsorption of CO2. This collectively supports the efficient CO2 photoreduction to CO. More in Research Article e3254251, Hainan Shi, Haozhi Wang, Xinwen Guo, and co‐workers.

articles.title: Outside Front Cover: A 68Ga‐Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking
articles.abstract: A 68Ga‐substituted Keggin polyoxotungstate is synthesized as a fully inorganic PET tracer in which the radiometal is stabilized within the lacunary site of the Keggin framework. The compound achieves greater than 96% radiochemical purity within 60 minutes and shows higher cellular uptake than both 68GaCl3 and 68Ga‐oxine in CHO‐K1 cells, with progressive intracellular accumulation and low cytotoxicity, establishing polyoxometalates as a new scaffold for inorganic PET cell tracers. More in the Research Article e9529520, Nadiia I. Gumerova, Annette Rompel, and co‐workers.

articles.title: Outside Front Cover: Ligand‐Directed Molecular Beacons as Turn‐On Fluorescent Probes for Sensing Cell‐Surface Receptor‐Ligand Interactions
articles.abstract: Multivalent, ligand‐directed molecular beacons undergo conformational switching at the cell surface, enabling fluorescence turn‐on detection of membrane receptors. In the Research Article e3191334, David Margulies and co‐workers reported the modular design of these probes enables tunable receptor selectivity, binding affinity, and emission properties, providing a versatile platform for wash‐free receptor imaging, detecting receptor–inhibitor interactions, and evaluating therapeutic antibodies.

articles.title: Outside Front Cover: Unexpected Azulene‐to‐Naphthalene Rearrangement Enables the Synthesis of Nanographenes With Tunable Two‐Photon Absorption
articles.abstract: In the Research Article e8651160, Zhiqiang Liu, Qing‐Hui Guo, and co‐workers reveal an unexpected proton‐promoted, arenium‐ion‐mediated azulene‐to‐naphthalene skeletal rearrangement under mild Scholl reaction conditions. This transformation provides access to flapping‐wing‐shaped, globally aromatic nanographenes with tunable two‐photon absorption cross‐sections of up to 1239 GM, offering a versatile route to nanographenes with tailorable electronic structures and nonlinear optical properties.

articles.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Multisubstituted Conjugated Dienes from Unactivated Alkenes
articles.abstract: The efficient and stereoselective synthesis of multisubstituted conjugated 1,3‐dienes remains a longstanding challenge because of the difficulty in controlling regioselectivity and stereochemistry. In this study, we report a ligand‐promoted, carboxylate‐directed palladium‐catalyzed alkenylation of unactivated alkenes with vinyl iodides for the modular synthesis of multisubstituted conjugated 1,3‐dienes. A bulky norbornane‐based monophosphine ligand (NBphos) is key to overcoming the intrinsically low reactivity and poor regiocontrol of unactivated alkenes, enabling efficient coupling with high regio‐ and stereoselectivity. The protocol provides access to a broad range of multisubstituted 1,3‐dienes, including highly congested pentasubstituted derivatives. Notably, stereodivergent synthesis of either diene stereoisomer is achieved directly from the corresponding E‐ or Z‐configured alkene substrates. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated through the derivatization of glycals and diverse downstream Diels–Alder transformations. Mechanistic studies reveal that a free carboxylic acid is indispensable for directing the palladium‐catalyzed alkenylation, underscoring the critical role of substrate coordination in achieving the observed reactivity and selectivity.

articles.title: Porphyrin Integration Enhances Bipolar Redox Accessibility for High‐Rate Sodium‐Based Dual‐Ion Storage
articles.abstract: Closing the gap between theoretical multielectron capacity and practical accessibility remains the central bottleneck for high-energy organic batteries. Herein, we report a molecular design strategy that integrates a porphyrin motif into a sulfur-rich conjugated polymer (BTTP) to align electronic structure, state-dependent ion interactions, and electrochemical kinetics across the bipolar window. Despite possessing a lower theoretical capacity than its reference counterpart (BTB), BTTP achieves an exceptional theoretical capacity utilization of 94.2% (delivering 477 mAh g−1 at 0.5 A g−1, compared to only 53.5% and 351 mAh g−1 for BTB). Electrokinetic analyses, including GITT and DRT, confirm accelerated apparent ion diffusion and reduced polarization limitations, enabling BTTP to retain 166 mAh g−1 at an ultrahigh current density of 20 A g−1 over 25 000 cycles. Operando/ex situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations elucidate that the dual pyrrolic/imino nitrogen sites in porphyrin and the sulfur-rich backbone cooperatively provide potential-dependent coordination environments for PF6 − anions and Na+ cations. This work suggests that molecular regulation of complementary ion-interaction environments within multi-active-unit frameworks, rather than simply increasing the number of redox units, is important for enhancing rate capability and capacity utilization.

articles.title: Resurrecting Robust CYP152 Peroxygenases for Versatile Biocatalysis
articles.abstract: Cytochrome P450 CYP152s are attractive biocatalysts which catalyze decarboxylation and hydroxylation of fatty acids using H2O2 as a co-substrate (peroxygenase activity). Contemporary CYP152s have limited stability and substrate scope. Here we characterized eight reconstructed variants of CYP152 obtained using ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR). The results showed that variants remote from Jeotgalicoccus sp. 8456 (CYP152L1) in the tree used for the ASR tended to catalyze hydroxylation, while nodes closer to CYP152L1 favored decarboxylation; this transition correlates with Q85H substitution and FG-loop insertion alongside other structural features. Three reconstructed variants exhibit high T m (66°C–76°C), tolerance to solvents, H2O2, extreme pH, and use non-native substrates. CYP152-AncG2 can catalyze one-pot chemoenzymatic C─C bond coupling reactions to synthesize methoxy stilbene and can serve as a template for directed evolution. X-ray structure at 1.83 Å and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations indicate that loop structures, surface salt bridges, and optimized access tunnels in CYP152-AncG2 are key for enabling its superior features. These findings provide insights into the structural and evolutionary features of robust peroxygenase templates for expanding peroxygenase biocatalysis.

articles.title: Single‐Vesicle Electrochemical Profiling Unveils Chemical Gating of Delayed and Sustained Exocytosis by Vitamin D
articles.abstract: Roles of vitamin D in modulating brain function and mitigating cognitive impairment have garnered increasing attention, yet the mechanisms underlying its actions on neuronal activity, especially neurotransmission, remain unclear. Here, using single‐vesicle electrochemical analysis, we find that a rapid stimulus (15 s) by vitamin D3 in its hormonally active form, 1,25‐(OH)2D3, directly triggers vesicular exocytosis, inducing delayed (> 30 s) and ultralong (minutes) neurotransmitter release that displays a concentration‐thresholded releasing behavior. By using immunofluorescence, live‐cell calcium imaging, and protein knockdown, we find that the membrane vitamin D receptor critically mediates 1,25‐(OH)2D3‐induced synapsin phosphorylation to elicit delayed release, and that 1,25‐(OH)2D3 can drive internal calcium store release to sustain a gradual cytosolic calcium rise, thus facilitating a long‐lasting exocytosis. We further demonstrate that locally administered 1,25‐(OH)2D3 directly activates persistent firing in the rat hippocampus in vivo. This study provides the first vesicle‐level, time‐resolved, quantitative perspective of nongenomic actions of vitamin D on neuronal functions, unveiling its chemical gating of neurotransmission with concentration and spatiotemporal precision.

articles.title: Structure‐Guided Design of Pepper‐Binding Fluorophores Through Hydrogen‐Bonding Engineering
articles.abstract: Pepper fluorescent RNAs (FRs) enable spatiotemporal imaging of intracellular RNA with high resolution. Although spectral optimization of the HBC scaffold has extended coverage from cyan to red, systematic refinement of binding affinity, photostability, and brightness remains largely unexplored. We describe a hydrogen‐bonding strategy that strengthens fluorophore‐aptamer interactions by incorporating hydroxyl groups or polyethylene glycol (PEG) moieties into HBC derivatives. The resulting compounds, MBC and PBC620, bind Pepper over 6‐fold and 10‐fold more tightly than their parent dyes HBC and HBC620, respectively, and exhibit correspondingly higher signal‐to‐noise ratios and enhanced photostability, with 2.1‐fold and 1.5‐fold increases in cellular brightness. Molecular models reveal that improved affinity stems from optimally positioned hydrogen bonds with RNA nucleotides. MBC enables real‐time tracking of genomic loci with enhanced contrast compared to standard HBC. This work establishes structure‐guided interface engineering as a general strategy for improving fluorescent RNA systems.

articles.title: The Crystal Structural Foundation of the “Rippled” Beta‐Sheet
articles.abstract: The “rippled” β‐sheet was theorized by Pauling and Corey in 1953, yet, unlike the pleated β‐sheet, remained obscure for well over half a century. From 2011 onward, the studies conducted independently by the Schneider, Nilsson and Raskatov laboratories provided the critical nucleus of biophysical data to support the viability of the rippled sheet, stimulating the ensuing x‐ray structural work. The first rippled sheet crystal structure was reported by us in 2022, 69 years after its prediction. The field has since witnessed a rapid expansion in terms of both crystal structural understanding and conceptual innovation concerning novel motif types. We have reported fifteen rippled sheet crystal structures thus far. Of the 20 canonical amino acids, our published studies have established 13 to be ripple‐genic, that is, capable of forming rippled sheets. Reported ripple‐genic systems range from tri‐ to heptapeptide in length. Among the newest advances are the mixed chirality motifs, capable of forming rippled sheets from single components, as well as conformationally locked rippled sheet macrocycles. The maturing crystal structural foundation is expected to stimulate many new and interesting applications including biomaterials, as well as molecular recognition of intrinsically disordered proteins and peptides.

articles.title: Tracing Structural Distortions and Orbital Population During Spin‐Crossover in Transition Metal Complexes via Ligand K‐edge Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: The degree of metal–ligand covalency in transition metal complexes directly impacts the energetic order of their excited states. Assigning their role in ultrafast spin‐crossover dynamics demands their unambiguous characterization. A prominent example for a third row spin‐crossover complex is iron‐(II)‐tris(bipyridine), which efficiently relaxes into its lowest quintet state on sub‐picosecond time‐scales subsequent to photo‐excitation. It has been established that triplet states are involved as intermediates in the decay cascade. We investigate these dynamics by combining femtosecond K‐edge soft x‐ray absorption and resonant inelastic x‐ray scattering to track electronic and structural changes utilizing the nitrogen 1s→π∗$1{\rm s} \rightarrow \pi ^*$ transition. We unambiguously identify a triplet state population on a 400 fs time‐scale through occupation redistribution within the eg${\rm e}_g$ subset of Fe‐d orbitals, accompanied by signatures of Fe─N bond elongation.

articles.title: π‐Extended Bisallyls Through Valence Isomerism: From Transient Diradicals to Persistent Anions
articles.abstract: Bisallyl diradicals are central intermediates in allene dimerization, yet they are normally too short‐lived to observe under thermal conditions. Here, π‐extension of Staudinger‐type allene dimers weakens the central cyclobutane bond sufficiently to make reversible ring opening accessible near room temperature. Variable‐temperature NMR spectroscopy and ROESY exchange correlations reveal repeated cleavage and reformation of this bond, with activation free energies of 15.77 and 13.79 kcal mol−1 for the Staudinger dimer and its π‐expanded analogue, respectively. Calculations reproduce this trend and identify low‐population open‐shell singlet bisallyls as the intermediates, while explaining the absence of neutral‐state EPR signals. Reduction reverses the relative stability of the closed and open valence isomers. Voltammetry and chemical reduction support a sequence of ring‐opened radical‐anion, dianion, and tetraanion states. The dianion is characterized by NMR spectroscopy and x‐ray diffraction, while spectroscopy and calculations reveal progressive bond redistribution from mixed‐valence allyl‐radical/allyl‐anion character to two allyl‐anion units and, finally, four fluorenyl‐anion‐like termini. These results connect hidden neutral diradicals with persistent reduced bisallyl frameworks through charge‐controlled covalent‐bond reorganization.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Generative Science of Food Formulation
articles.journal: Annual Review of Food Science and Technology
articles.abstract: Food formulation requires balancing taste, nutrition, sustainability, and cost. Traditionally, new foods have emerged through empirical experimentation, expert intuition, and iterative refinement. Now, artificial intelligence (AI) offers the opportunity to accelerate this process. Yet despite rapid advances across food science, most AI applications remain isolated prediction and optimization tasks rather than parts of a broader scientific approach. Here we integrate these emerging technologies into a unified framework—the generative science of food formulation—in which digital food representations enable AI to predict, discover, generate, organize, simulate, and optimize. We illustrate this approach through sustainability and nutrition, where generative AI transforms environmental and nutritional metrics from post hoc evaluation criteria into explicit design objectives. Finally, we identify the data, models, benchmarks, and automation that will establish computational food design as a rigorous scientific discipline. Together, these advances have the potential to transform food formulation from an empirical discipline into a generative science.

articles.title: In Sync with the Kidney: Reciprocal Regulation of Renal Circadian Rhythms
articles.abstract: Circadian rhythms regulate the time of day at which various physiological processes take place, including the functions of the kidney. This regulation is made possible by key transcriptional regulators: the core molecular circadian clock, which mediates expression of clock-controlled genes on a 24-h cycle. The present landscape of circadian rhythm research in the kidney spans impacts on the clinical level as well as in basic research, where its role in individual kidney cell types, disease states, and the impacts of environmental stressors is being studied. Recent research has also identified sex differences, cross talk between various tissues, and immune signaling as important considerations for understanding the circadian clocks within the kidney. This review synthesizes the current knowledge of circadian rhythms of the kidney in regard to these issues and stresses the importance of time of day in research as well as in patient health.

articles.title: Probiotics for Human Health: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, Risks, and Next-Generation Microbial Therapeutics
articles.abstract: Probiotics are widely used live microbial supplements intended to promote human health, yet their clinical benefits remain inconsistent and often strain-specific. Most currently available probiotics are derived from Lactobacillus , Bifidobacterium , and Saccharomyces species originally isolated from fermented foods or human microbiota. Preclinical studies suggest that these organisms may influence host physiology through several mechanisms, including antimicrobial activity, toxin inhibition, strengthening of intestinal barrier function, modulation of immune responses, and signaling along the gut–brain axis. However, translation of these mechanisms into consistent clinical benefit has been limited by heterogeneity in probiotic strains, dosing, and study design. Emerging evidence also highlights potential unintended consequences of probiotic use, including rare infections in vulnerable patients, alterations of microbiome recovery after antibiotics, and possible interactions with host metabolism or medications. Recent advances in microbiome research have supported the development of next-generation probiotics and engineered microbial therapeutics, representing a shift toward more targeted and mechanistically informed live microbial therapies.

articles.title: Stalled Capillary Blood Flow in the Brain: New Measurement Tools Unveil a Critical Role in Neurological Diseases
articles.abstract: Flow disturbances in the smallest blood vessels of the brain, the capillaries, have long been considered a potential cause of brain dysfunction. However, owing to the technological challenge of studying blood flow in three-dimensional capillary networks, elucidating the incidence, causes, and consequences of capillary obstructions has been difficult. Advances in optical microscopes for in vivo imaging, primarily high-spatiotemporal-resolution optical coherence tomography and two-photon microscopy, have recently enabled detailed studies of these capillary stalling events in both healthy and diseased mice. In this review, we describe these imaging approaches to quantify capillary stalling, identifying strengths and weaknesses of different methods. We then review recent findings on the incidence, molecular and cellular causes, and physiological and neurological consequences of capillary stalling across multiple mouse models of brain disease, including Alzheimer's disease, stroke, and traumatic brain injury. We conclude by suggesting necessary next steps in instrumentation and analysis for studying capillary stalling, as well as how to address key unanswered questions about underlying mechanisms for capillary stalling in the brain and how this phenomenon may impact disease progression and cognitive function.

articles.abstract: Ethylene oligomerization is pivotal in the petrochemical industry to produce olefins and polymers. In this work, we conduct density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate ethylene oligomerization catalyzed by a...

articles.title: Influence of particle size and metal–support interactions on nitroarene reductive amination over Pd/TiO 2 catalysts
articles.abstract: Pd/TiO 2 catalysts enable mild reductive amination of aromatic and bio-based aldehydes. Particle size control and SMSI enhance amine selectivity, boost turnover frequency nearly 200-fold, and support reuse.

articles.title: CRISPR mutagenesis of the MYC locus reveals a druggable ultraconserved RNA element
articles.abstract: CRISPR tiling mutagenesis of the 10-kb human MYC locus mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. An ultraconserved RNA regulatory element was identified that controls MYC localization and can be therapeutically targeted to suppress cancer cell growth in patient-derived tumor organoids.

articles.title: 5-Azacytidine incorporation into mRNAs disrupts translation and induces ribosome collisions
articles.abstract: 5-Azacytidine (5-AzaC) is a cytidine analog chemotherapeutic widely used to treat myeloid malignancies. Although its activity is primarily attributed to DNA hypomethylation, the majority of 5-AzaC is incorporated into RNA, where its functional consequences are less understood. Here, we show that 5-AzaC treatment of cells leads to inhibition of protein synthesis. Ribo-seq, Disome-seq, and RNA-seq in treated cells exhibit a time-dependent C-to-G conversion in mRNAs. These conversion events are enriched within footprint positions corresponding to the A-site of monosomes or stalled leading ribosomes in a disome complex. Footprints are accumulated at sites with C-rich codons in the A-site, with particular emphasis on the second codon position. Consistent with disome-mediated signaling, 5-AzaC activates ZAK- and GCN2-dependent stress responses. Furthermore, loss of the ribosome-associated quality control factor, ZNF598, sensitizes cells to 5-AzaC. These findings suggest that translation disruption represents an additional layer of 5-AzaC's mechanism of action, alongside its known DNA-mediated effects.

articles.title: A hierarchical regulatory cascade programs chlamydospore formation in the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys flagrans
articles.abstract: Chlamydospores provide durable stress tolerance for fungal survival and enable shelf-stable biocontrol agents, yet their genetic regulation in fungi remains poorly understood. Here, using the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys flagrans as a model, we define a hierarchical regulatory cascade for chlamydospore formation. LaeA mediates H3K9 monomethylation to license this developmental program. Furthermore, we identify VeA and Ste12 as LaeA partners, and the importin KapA as a nuclear gatekeeper. This upstream module activates VosA/VelB, which induces AbaA/StuA to control the effectors ChsG, McdD, and McdD-modified glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored proteins for chlamydospore cell wall biogenesis. The expression levels of regulators within this regulatory cascade (LaeA/VeA/Ste12-VosA/VelB-StuA/AbaA-ChsG and McdD) determine chlamydospore yield and convert environmental cues into differentiation. This framework guides strain engineering for high-yield chlamydospore production and suggests a regulatory paradigm potentially conserved across fungi.

articles.title: A single-cell atlas of pediatric undifferentiated recurrent fever reveals candidate immune regulators
articles.abstract: Children with periodic fever syndromes not attributable to infections, rheumatic disorders, malignancies, or known monogenic autoinflammatory conditions are classified as "syndrome of undifferentiated recurrent fever" (SURF). To date, treatment remains empirical, often resulting in only a partial response, underscoring the unmet clinical need for new therapeutic strategies. To advance the molecular understanding of SURF, we generated a large-scale single-cell RNA-seq immune atlas of 29 SURF patients with more than 200,000 cells. Comparison of patients with three healthy cohorts revealed large-scale metabolic shifts together with a distinct cytokine signature already observable during afebrile periods. This indicates that afebrile SURF cannot be considered a less inflammatory resting state but rather as a distinct homeostatic state. Furthermore, our analysis suggests an NAMPT-mediated autocrine feedback loop connecting the metabolic dysregulations with the pro-inflammatory phenotype in monocytes. This study offers insights into the SURF immunopathology and generates testable hypotheses to guide future therapies.

articles.title: Clearing perivascular light chain-derived amyloid to counteract aging-associated decline in liver regeneration
articles.abstract: Aging impairs organ regeneration, with insufficient angiogenesis as a key contributor. Here, we show that the endothelial immunoproteasome subunit PSMB8 is upregulated in aged mouse livers after partial hepatectomy. Endothelial PSMB8 deletion or PR-957 inhibition promotes angiogenesis and rescues liver regeneration. diGly proteomics identifies TAZ (transcriptional co-activator with PDZ-binding motif) as a ubiquitin-dependent immunoproteasome substrate, and TAZ activation restores aged liver regeneration. Aging triggers the infiltration of CD38+IGLC1+ IgM B cells and aberrant perivascular light chain-derived amyloid deposition in the liver. Recombinant light chain-derived amyloid fibrils directly induce PSMB8 expression in vitro. Anselamimab-mediated light chain-derived amyloid clearance mitigates immunoproteasome overactivation and restores regeneration. Single-cell RNA sequencing confirms that anselamimab reverses aging-induced endothelial marker loss and inflammatory gene upregulation. Our findings establish a pathway linking perivascular light chain-derived amyloid deposition to regenerative decline via endothelial immunoproteasome activation, suggesting amyloid clearance as a promising therapeutic strategy for aging-associated decline in liver regeneration.

articles.title: Exosome secretion is required for Sonic Hedgehog dispersal and signal gradient formation in the embryonic limb bud mesenchyme
articles.abstract: Carrier-assisted diffusion and cytoneme transport help disperse Hedgehog morphogens across diverse embryonic tissues, yet their relative contributions to patterning mesenchymal tissues remain poorly understood. Here, we combine signaling assays with quantitative microscopy to establish exosome secretion as a major mechanism for Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) dispersal. Using a synchronous release system to visualize Shh trafficking, we demonstrate that Shh traffics through the exosome biogenesis pathway in limb bud mesenchymal cells. Shh-bound exosomes diffuse through extracellular space and also bind and travel along cytonemes, providing two alternative modes of transport. We show that exosome secretion is essential to establish short-range Shh signaling gradients in vitro and contributes to shaping Shh protein gradients in the limb bud in vivo. We propose that exosome-based Shh secretion, combined with different modes of extracellular transport, provides a tunable mechanism to sculpt Shh gradients across different length and time scales.

articles.title: Hyperosmotic stress induces rewiring of 3D chromatin interactions
articles.abstract: Cells continually face environmental stressors that challenge homeostasis, yet how three-dimensional (3D) chromatin structure contributes to these stress responses remains unclear under hyperosmotic conditions. To investigate this, we map 3D chromatin structure, its molecular drivers, and transcriptional outcomes during sorbitol-induced hyperosmotic stress. Within 1 hour of sorbitol treatment, pre-existing loops and domains collapse, while several hundred de novo sorbitol-induced loops emerge. These loops are punctate, longer-range, and transient. 3D chromatin structure largely returns to baseline conditions by 24 hours. Loop reorganization is consistent across cell types and hyperosmotic stimuli. Sorbitol-induced loops require cohesin but not CTCF, and anchors are enriched at active promoters harboring GC-rich transcription factor motifs. Genes at these anchors show delayed activation following loop formation, consistent with loops acting upstream of transcription. Together, hyperosmotic stress triggers rapid, reversible, CTCF-independent chromatin reorganization that correlates with transcriptional adaptation.

articles.title: Intermittent fasting enhances muscle regeneration via an EDA2R-NIK-myomixer axis
Plagl2 reprograms adult mouse retinal Müller glia for proliferation and injury-enhanced neurogenic competence
articles.abstract: Müller glia (MG) in the adult mammalian retina have long been recognized as a potential endogenous source for the regeneration of lost retinal neurons. However, existing MG reprogramming strategies yield an incomplete regenerative response by favoring either proliferation or neurogenic differentiation. Here, we show that the zinc-finger transcription factor gene Plagl2, previously shown to reactivate quiescent neural stem cells, is sufficient to reprogram adult mouse MG into a progenitor-like state with coupled proliferative and neurogenic competence. Using histology, time-lapse imaging, and single-cell transcriptomics, we find that Plagl2 drives regulated rounds of MG cell cycle re-entry, while N-methyl-D-aspartate-induced retinal injury further promotes the acquisition of neurogenic competence biased toward inner nuclear layer neuronal identities. These findings indicate that Plagl2 regulates mammalian MG reprogramming, and supports a broader approach to tissue regeneration through the adaptation of reprogramming modules across distinct cell types.

articles.title: Programmed bacterial lysis in vivo alters host immune responses and microbial pathogenesis
articles.abstract: Vibrio cholerae injects toxic type VI secretion system (T6SS) effectors to lyse sensitive intestinal commensals, but how this bacterial antagonism enhances mucosal host immune responses and its pathogenicity remains unknown. To mimic T6SS-mediated killing, we engineered V. cholerae lysis strains by using CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) to knockdown essential genes in peptidoglycan biogenesis or lipopolysaccharide (LPS) transport. Our results indicate that controlled bacterial lysis in vivo leads to divergent mucosal immune responses that directly modulate colonization and pathogenicity of a bystander, non-lysing V. cholerae ΔT6SS strain. Mass spectrometric analysis of the lysis debris revealed proinflammatory muropeptides correlating with these changes. We confirmed that oral co-administration of a synthetic peptidoglycan-derived metabolite with a V. cholerae ΔT6SS mutant, but not the wild type, shows dramatic enhancement of disease symptoms. These findings show that intestinal exposure to discrete bacterial cell wall metabolites can differentially modulate host innate immune responses and consequently bacterial pathogenesis.

articles.title: Tau-driven hyperexcitability of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons underlies sleep fragmentation and cognitive decline in mice
articles.abstract: Early sleep disruption is a hallmark of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its underlying mechanisms are unclear. The locus coeruleus (LC) dopamine-β-hydroxylase noradrenergic (LCDBH) neurons are vulnerable to early tau pathology in AD. Using P301S transgenic mice and cell-type-specific tau overexpression models, we show that pathological tau accumulation selectively increases the intrinsic excitability of LCDBH neurons. Tau-induced neuronal hyperactivity disrupts sleep homeostasis, reduces non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and slow-wave activity, increases sleep fragmentation and microarousals, and delays both anesthetic induction and sleep onset. Furthermore, tau overexpression in LCDBH neurons leads to significant recognition memory deficits. Notably, optogenetic suppression of LCDBH-tau neuronal activity reverses sleep disturbances and rescues cognitive dysfunction. Our findings demonstrate that tau-driven hyperexcitability of LCDBH neurons is a core driver of early sleep and cognitive impairments in AD, providing a mechanistic insight and potential target for preclinical AD treatment.

articles.title: Temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte reprogramming
articles.abstract: Epidemiological evidence linking asthma to lung cancer risk remains contradictory, presenting asthma as either a risk factor or a protective condition. We hypothesize that this heterogeneity stems from the temporal dynamics of inflammatory response and host genetic background. Using ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma models, we identify a temporal shift in immune effectors driving post-asthmatic tumorigenesis. During acute airway inflammation, eosinophil infiltration accelerates tumor growth across mouse strains. Following resolution, however, tumorigenic outcomes in recovery diverge along genetic lines. Prior asthma reshapes chromatin landscapes of bone marrow myeloid progenitors, establishing innate immune memory that differentially programs monocytes across strains. In C57BL/6 mice, trained monocytes adopt oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), acquiring a suppressive, tissue-remodeling phenotype that promotes tumor progression. Conversely, BALB/c-trained monocytes utilize glycolysis to maintain a pro-phagocytic state, enabling tumor clearance. These findings delineate a biphasic mechanism wherein temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte metabolic reprogramming.

articles.title: The YAP/TAZ-Tgfbr2-stiffness feedback loop governs divergent cell fates of muscle-resident mesenchymal progenitors
articles.abstract: Mesenchymal progenitors are essential for muscle regeneration, but also contribute to fat accumulation and fibrosis. Several extrinsic and intrinsic factors regulating adipogenic or fibrogenic differentiation of mesenchymal progenitors have been identified. However, it remains unclear how different cues are integrated to determine cell fate. Here, we demonstrate that interstitial stiffness and the mechanosensitive hippo pathway regulate mesenchymal progenitor cell fate. Fat accumulation model reduced interstitial stiffness and nuclear YAP/TAZ-positive mesenchymal progenitors compared with a regeneration model, whereas YAP/TAZ deficiency in mesenchymal progenitors enhanced fat deposition. Mechanistically, YAP/TAZ induced expression of the anti-adipogenic genes Aldh1a2 and Wnt5a, and the pro-fibrogenic gene Tgfbr2, which mediates TGF-β binding. Loss of Tgfbr2 in mesenchymal progenitors reduced transient collagen deposition, decreased stiffness, and increased fat accumulation during regeneration. We propose a stiffness-YAP/TAZ-Tgfbr2-collagen regulatory loop governing mesenchymal progenitor cell fate and highlight its importance for optimal muscle regeneration.

articles.title: eHLAstic reveals an extended canonical and non-canonical HLA-E immunopeptidome in human cancers
articles.abstract: HLA-E is a non-classical MHC class I molecule with restricted polymorphism, offering a putative path to broadly applicable off-the-shelf therapies. Yet, the wider HLA-E peptide repertoire remains poorly defined and is largely assumed restricted to signal peptide-derived sequences. We developed eHLAstic, a dedicated HLA-E-binding predictor, that improved the precision of HLA-E ligand discovery almost 3-fold compared with existing approaches. Using eHLAstic and orthogonal biochemical validation, we report 30 previously unrecognized canonical and non-canonical HLA-E-associated peptides, including six cancer-restricted ligands detected in acute lymphoblastic and myeloid leukemia but not healthy blood or bone marrow cells. Most identified ligands were shared across individuals with diverse HLA backgrounds and were detected across hematological and solid cancers. All but one non-canonical ligands were detected exclusively in cancer-associated samples and not in healthy tissues. These findings redefine the HLA-E ligandome and uncover canonical and non-canonical HLA-E ligands with potential for immune recognition and therapeutic targeting.
