Duality of root‐dominated net soil organic carbon gain and mycelium‐mediated carbon loss in hyper‐arid afforestation
articles.abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) pool dynamics during hyper‐arid afforestation by root pathway and mycelium pathway. Summary Afforestation regulates soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration via plant‐ and microbial‐derived carbon (C) inputs, but root‐ and mycelium‐derived C inputs differ in quantity, turnover, and stabilization mechanisms, and these differences may shift as stands develop. However, how root vs mycelium pathways drive SOC dynamics across a dryland afforestation chronosequence remains unclear. Using the ingrowth‐core method along a dryland afforestation chronosequence (young forests, middle‐aged forests, and mature forests), we quantified the contributions of root and mycelium pathways to SOC. The root pathway promoted SOC accumulation via particulate organic C and mineral‐associated organic C inputs, contributing to 77.19–85.05% of the SOC changes. By contrast, the mycelium pathway induced net SOC loss via particulate organic C depletion, contributing to 14.95–22.81% of the SOC changes. SOC concentrations peaked in middle‐aged forests, whereas relative SOC stability peaked in young forests. This study provides the first quantitative assessment of the distinct contributions of root and mycelium pathways to SOC accumulation and stabilization during dryland afforestation, advancing understanding of their roles in regulating SOC dynamics. As climate change intensifies land‐use pressure, management strategies should integrate stage‐specific root and mycelial traits to enhance SOC sequestration in arid forests.

articles.title: Engineering crop immunity: cyclic nucleotide‐gated channels as promising targets for broad‐spectrum disease resistance
OsERF27‐OsPLT4 regulatory module and ROS equilibrium control temporospatial rice crown root patterning
articles.abstract: Schematic representation of the auxin‐OsERF27‐OsPLT4‐ROS module in regulating outgrowth and emergence of the pCRP of the P0 in rice. Summary In rice (Oryza sativa), the root architecture is heavily shaped by shoot‐borne crown roots that arise from the phytomers at the stem base. Each phytomer typically generates two spatially distinct crown root populations – lower/proximal and upper/distal crown roots – that also emerge temporally, with the proximal roots forming first. The mechanisms that coordinate this temporospatial patterning, however, remain poorly understood. Here, we identify an AP2/ERF gene OsERF27 which is differentially expressed between proximal and distal crown root primordia and is specifically required for the timely development of proximal roots. We further show that OsPLT4 functions downstream of OsERF27, defining an OsERF27‐OsPLT4 regulatory module that drives the outgrowth and emergence of proximal crown roots. Interestingly, we uncover a requirement for reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis in crown root development: Loss‐of‐function mutants display disturbed ROS accumulation pattern and sensitized root formation to ROS perturbation, indicating that this module promotes root emergence by spatially maintaining optimal redox balance. Together, our findings reveal a multi‐layered regulatory network that integrates genetic elements with positional cues with redox control to pattern distinct crown root populations. Our study highlights how localized developmental programmes scale to shape root system architecture for tuning plant form and function in grasses.

articles.title: Oviposition fluid protein NlOFP1 in the brown planthopper suppresses rice plant defenses
articles.abstract: NlOFP1 is an oviposition fluid protein deposited into rice tissue during oviposition that helps eggs resist desiccation and suppresses plant defense. Summary Insect oviposition fluid plays a role in the early recognition of plants and the initiation of plant defense responses. However, the characterization of oviposition fluid proteins and their relationship with plant defenses remains poorly understood. The oviposition fluid protein NlOFP1 in the brown planthopper (Nilaparvata lugens) is synthesized in the ovarian follicular cells and can be deposited into rice tissue. Functional studies reveal that NlOFP1 helps eggs resist desiccation stress. Furthermore, it can suppress plant defenses. NlOFP1‐silencing leads to decreased honeydew secretion, fecundity, and egg hatching rate. Orthologs of NlOFP1 in other planthopper species exhibit highly conserved functions. Transgenic rice overexpressing NlOFP1 showed reduced lignin and salicylic acid, increased cellulose, and downregulated resistance genes, indicating weakened defense responses of plants. This phenotype effectively compensated for the adaptive loss caused by NlOFP1 silencing in the brown planthopper. NlOFP1 interacted with the photosynthetic electron transport chain component OsFeS. This interaction partially impaired the import of OsFeS into the chloroplasts and might lead to a decline in plant resistance. Our study reveals that NlOFP1 acts as an effector against plant defense responses and provides insights into pest reproduction and host defense evasion.

articles.title: Academic entitlement and student well-being: The mediating role of the impostor phenomenon
articles.abstract: Despite growing evidence linking academic entitlement to diminished student outcomes, the psychological mechanisms through which entitled academic expectations erode student well-being remain insufficiently understood. The present study examines the mediating role of the impostor phenomenon in the relationship between academic entitlement and well-being among university students. A cross-sectional correlational design was employed with a sample of 864 undergraduate students recruited from Al-Azhar University and Kafr El-Sheikh University in Egypt. Participants completed the Academic Entitlement Scale (AES-28), the Short Clance Impostor Phenomenon Scale (CIPS-10), and the BBC Well-Being Scale (BBC-WBS). Mediation analysis was conducted using the PROCESS macro with bootstrapping based on 5,000 resamples. Results revealed that academic entitlement significantly and positively predicted the impostor phenomenon, which in turn significantly and negatively predicted student well-being. The impostor phenomenon partially mediated the relationship between academic entitlement and well-being, accounting for approximately 23% of the total effect. These findings suggest that entitlement-driven expectations are associated with lower overall well-being (composite score), both directly and indirectly by fostering fraudulence-related self-doubt. Mediation was not tested separately for psychological, physical, and relational well-being. Universities, particularly in comparable Egyptian and collectivist contexts, may consider addressing both entitled academic attitudes and impostor-related cognitions through counseling interventions and pedagogical strategies.

articles.title: Assessment of Pleurotus ostreatus and Pleurotus citrinopileatus mushroom as bioshielding materials for neutron attenuation in medical cyclotron
articles.abstract: by Md. Jahid Hasan, Md. Nahid Hossain, Hasan Mehdi, Jannatul Ferdous, Md. Shohag Mia, Md. Akhtaruzzaman, Md. Mohi Uddin Neutron absorbance efficiency is crucial for radiation shielding and nuclear reactors, with mushrooms like Pleurotus Ostreatus (PO) and Pleurotus Citrinopleatus (PC) enhancing this property due to their nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, cadmium, and carbon content. Processed into 3 × 3 inch blocks at the National Institute of Nuclear Medicine and Allied Science (NINMAS), the mushrooms are dried at 80°C and ground to powder for analysis. Structural studies using XRD, FESEM, FTIR, and UV-vis spectroscopic reveal high carbon and oxygen levels. For the PO, the XRD investigation showed a broad diffraction peak that corresponded to an estimated crystallite size of about 1.34 nm, while PC showed a mostly amorphous structure devoid of clear crystalline diffraction peaks. The FTIR identifies various functional groups, and UV-vis spectra confirm the presence of sulfur and carbon. Neutron interaction mechanisms in mushroom-derived shielding materials involve moderation and scattering by the hydrogen-rich matrix, followed by capture at nitrogen and sulfur sites. HPGe spectroscopic confirms effective neutron interaction and attenuation via the detection of activation products such as K-40 in this study. Both samples show significant K-40 levels of 30 Bq/kg, while Th-232 and U-238 are found to be 2–3 Bq/kg and 5–6 Bq/kg, respectively. The findings demonstrate that these mushroom blocks are not neutron-transparent, but rather contribute to neutron moderation and absorption acts as a bio-shielding materials in the cyclotron facility.

articles.title: Case studies on IoT monitoring of debris flow and landslides
articles.abstract: Aiming at the critical demand for real-time monitoring of slope disasters in mountainous and urbanized regions, this study develops Internet of Things (IoT)-based real-time monitoring systems to resolve the issues of data delay and fragmentation in conventional manual monitoring. Through three engineering cases conducted by the authors, we demonstrate the adaptability of IoT technology in slope disaster monitoring under different instability mechanisms (debris flows and landslides) and geological conditions (artificial-reinforced and semi-natural slopes). Specifically, in Case 1, a novel IoT monitoring system for debris flows integrated with the structural characteristics of rigid barriers is proposed. In Cases 2 and 3, multi-type monitoring sensors and equipment are deployed, including deformation sensors, rainfall gauges and video surveillance devices, to achieve accurate early warnings of rainfall-induced landslides. The novelty of this work lies in proposing a unified IoT architecture scheme applicable to different types of slope disasters. This scheme systematically integrates physico-mechanical sensing devices, a solar-battery collaborative power supply system, video monitoring equipment, data transmission methods, early warning modes, and a cloud-based processing module. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the proposed scheme is validated via successful early warning cases, and this scheme provides an effective technical framework for slope disaster prevention and control.

articles.title: Computational modelling of acetylcholine deficiency-mediated dysfunction in the basal ganglia-thalamocortical network related to Parkinson’s disease dementia
articles.abstract: by Hao Yang Parkinson’s disease dementia (PDD) is a significant form of dementia. Its pathophysiology involves not only the dopaminergic system impairment but also the degeneration of cholinergic neurons in the pedunculopontine nucleus (PPN), which is considered a potential contributor to the cognitive decline in PDD. Therefore, this study develops a computational model of the PPN-modulated basal ganglia-thalamic-cortical network to investigate how acetylcholine deficiency affects cortical oscillations. Based on anatomical evidence, acetylcholine deficiency is modeled by modulating synaptic connections from the PPN to the thalamus and basal ganglia output nuclei. Power spectrum analysis shows that acetylcholine deficiency, whether in the PPN-thalamic nucleus pathway or in the PPN-basal ganglia output nucleus pathway, leads to a decrease in cortical power ratio between the high-frequency band and low-frequency band. These results qualitatively reproduce the characteristics of electrophysiological measurements recorded in PDD. Further dynamical analysis suggests that this reduction may be associated with weakened oscillatory activity, reflected by a shift in neuronal firing patterns from limit cycle to point attractor. Moreover, simulations of combined acetylcholine and dopamine deficiencies reveal that both neurotransmitters can reduce the cortical power ratio, with a synergistic interaction rather than a simple additive effect. These findings provide a systems-level perspective on how ACh deficiency may contribute to cortical dysfunction in PDD and may offer a potential direction for future therapeutic research.

articles.title: Correction: MicroRNA miR-328 Regulates Zonation Morphogenesis by Targeting CD44 Expression
articles.abstract: by Chia-Hui Wang, Daniel Y. Lee, Zhaoqun Deng, Zina Jeyapalan, Shao-Chen Lee, Shireen Kahai, Wei-Yang Lu, Yaou Zhang, Burton B. Yang

articles.title: Defining and predicting outcomes of a work-injuries rehabilitation program through multivariate baseline phenotypes and longitudinal modeling
articles.abstract: Objective To characterize short-term pain and health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) recovery trajectories in injured workers undergoing standardized musculoskeletal rehabilitation. We also examined whether multidimensional baseline phenotypes derived from brief self-report measures predicted these trajectories and subsequent recovery. Methods Adults with work-related musculoskeletal injuries were enrolled at entry into a community-based rehabilitation program (N = 146), of whom 134 contributed to pain and 138 to HRQoL trajectory analyses. Participants were classified into one of 4 latent profiles at intake from a prior analysis: Localized/Resilient (57.0%), Mood-Dominant (21.8%), Neurosensory-Dominant (12.7%), and Complex/Central (8.5%). Pain (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, NPRS) and HRQoL (EQ-5D-5L index) were measured at baseline, 4, and 8 weeks; self-rated global recovery, self-reported return-to-work status, and administrative discharge/ongoing-care codes were collected at 8 weeks. Growth mixture modeling defined NPRS and EQ-5D-5L trajectories. Odds ratios (ORs) quantified associations between baseline classes and “No Recovery/No Improvement” trajectories, as well as point outcomes. Results Three pain trajectories (Rapid Recovery 34.1%, Incomplete Recovery 42.2%, No Recovery 23.7%) and two QoL trajectories (Good QoL 86.2%, No Improvement 13.8%) were identified. Compared with the Localized/Resilient baseline class, odds of NPRS No Recovery were higher in the Mood-Dominant (OR 3.97, 95%CI 1.32–11.92), Neurosensory‑Dominant (OR 10.99, 3.20–37.38), and Complex, Central (OR 22.67, 4.76–107.90) classes, with similarly graded increases for EQ‑5D‑5L No Recovery (ORs 9.00, 7.50, and 150.00, respectively), although estimates for the small Complex/Central subgroup were imprecise. The Complex /Central class also had higher odds of self-reported “not fully returned to work” (OR 4.18, 1.05–16.64) and being coded as “requires ongoing care” (OR 5.74, 1.93–17.11) relative to Localized/Resilient, whereas self-rated global recovery showed no significant between-class differences. Conclusions Brief, fully self-reported, multivariate phenotypes obtained at program entry stratify acutely injured workers into likely rehabilitation outcomes in the short term. These findings support the potential value of integrating mechanism-informed phenotyping with trajectory modeling to inform stratified, risk-guided musculoskeletal rehabilitation.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of machine learning models for predicting prediabetes in China
articles.abstract: Background Diabetes imposes a growing health burden among Chinese adults, necessitating scalable tools for early identification of high-risk individuals. We aimed to develop and internally validate survival machine-learning models for prediabetes risk stratification using routinely available clinical indicators. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 77,478 Chinese adults from the Dryad repository (2010–2016). Candidate predictors were selected via LASSO regression and random survival forests (RSF). Six survival models, Cox proportional hazards (Cox-PH), CoxBoost, DeepSurv, gradient boosting machine (GBM), random survival forests (RSF), and survival tree, were developed and evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent ROC curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The best-performing model was deployed as a web-based application. Results Eight predictors were consistently selected across methods: age, BMI, fasting plasma glucose, total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL-C, LDL-C, and creatinine clearance rate. In the test set, DeepSurv and GBM achieved comparable discrimination (C-index: 0.756 vs. 0.751; adjusted P = 0.694). GBM was preferred due to better calibration and greater net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds, leading to its selection as the candidate model. Conclusion The GBM-based prediabetes risk model, built on eight inexpensive and routinely available clinical measures, showed promising internal discrimination and calibration in a large Chinese cohort. An interactive web tool was developed as a research prototype to facilitate future external validation and early risk identification. External validation in independent populations is warranted before clinical use.

articles.title: Differential and directional body coupling analysis in Parkinsonian gait
articles.abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder primarily characterized by motor impairments and altered whole-body coordination. Objective and accessible approaches for quantifying inter-limb and cross-directional coupling during gait remain limited in clinical settings. Using a prospectively collected dataset of individuals with PD and healthy controls (HC), we propose a comprehensive analytical framework based on human pose estimation to extract time-series kinematic signals from key body landmarks. Coupling strengths between body segments were quantified to characterize whole-body coordination patterns. Statistical filtering identified discriminative body coupling factors that significantly differentiated PD from HC. The identified factors demonstrated clear and consistent alterations in coordination patterns across groups. Furthermore, multiple machine learning classifiers validated their discriminative capacity, achieving robust classification performance. Correlation analyses between the top 10 pre-specified directional body coupling factors and MDS-UPDRS III scores demonstrated modest but statistically significant associations in the full PD cohort (n = 121), with 8 of 10 factors surviving FDR correction (ρ=0.27–0.31). These associations suggest that directional body coupling metrics capture clinically relevant variation in motor impairment severity beyond binary PD versus HC discrimination and may serve as potential digital biomarkers of PD-related motor dysfunction. Subtype-stratified analyses were conducted only as exploratory supplementary analyses, and larger, more balanced subtype cohorts are required before subtype-specific conclusions can be drawn. Overall, body coupling metrics provide reliable biomechanical markers of PD-related gait impairment and support the clinical potential of this non-invasive and cost-effective pipeline for early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring.

articles.title: Double gravity-assist rendezvous trajectory to Halley’s comet using deep-space low thrust
articles.abstract: The perihelion of comet 1P/Halley in 2061 is an excellent chance to revisit this object of outstanding scientific and cultural relevance. During its 1986 approach to the Sun, it was targeted by several flyby missions. Due to its retrograde, highly-inclined orbit, the relative velocities during the encounter were large, restricting the scientific return due to the short time spent inside the coma. A rendezvous trajectory would overcome this limitation, but the design is challenging due to the limitations of current propulsion technology. Given the lead times of spacecraft development and the long duration of the interplanetary transfer to the comet, it is imperative to start mission planning as soon as possible. We present a novel rendezvous strategy, combining unpowered Jupiter and Saturn gravity-assists with deep-space low-thrust arcs. It minimizes launch energy and propellant budget, constraining the arrival to occur before the onset of high activity. The double flyby strategy reduces the otherwise prohibitive cost of the plane change maneuver. Closed expressions for the optimal flyby geometry, together with an explicit low-thrust transcription technique, reduce the number of design parameter to three, improving computational efficiency. Crucially, this is the first rendezvous mission concept achievable with well-proven technology (standard radioisotope thermoelectric generators and an ion thruster) and compatible with several existing launchers. We describe the trajectory optimization strategy and perform a comprehensive exploration of the design space. Finally, we present two promising proof-of-concept trajectories in detail.

articles.title: Effects and mechanisms of exercise timing on cognitive function in older type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with mild cognitive impairment: A magnetic resonance imaging-based randomized controlled trial protocol
articles.abstract: Background Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a prevalent complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Cognitive impairment progressively impairs self-care abilities, thereby triggering a vicious cycle of poor glycemic control and further cognitive decline. Exercise has been widely recognized as an effective strategy to improve both glycemic control and cognitive function; however, an optimal time of day for exercise to mitigate this neurodegenerative trajectory has not been determined. This trial aims to determine the most effective exercise timing to maximize cognitive benefits in older T2DM patients with MCI (T2DM-MCI) and to investigate the underlying neurobiological mechanisms using multimodal magnetic resonance imaging. Methods In this randomized controlled trial, patients 60–75 years of age with T2DM‐MCI will be assigned to a morning exercise group (09:00–10:10), an evening exercise group (19:00–20:10), or a health education group. The exercise groups will complete a 12-week, home-based, remotely supervised exercise program comprising aerobic and resistance exercises. The health education group will receive a 12-week health education program. Cognitive function will be evaluated at baseline and post-intervention using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, Color-Word Stroop Test, N-back task, Trail making Test, Attention Network Test, and Digit Symbol Substitution Test. Additionally, brain structure and function based on imaging, blood biomarkers, and physical fitness will also be assessed. Discussion In this study, we aim to identify the optimal time of day for exercise to maximize cognitive benefits in patients with T2DM‐MCI and to elucidate underlying neurocognitive mechanisms. We will examine whether glycemic control mediates the relationship between exercise and cognitive function improvement. This research is expected to provide “time-specific” evidence for exercise prescription to maximize the neurocognitive benefits and mitigate dementia risk in this population. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: [http://www.chictr.org.cn], identifier [ChiCTR2300073737].

articles.title: Expression of Concern: Epidemiological studies of sleep disorder in educational community of Pakistani population, its major risk factors and associated diseases
Health visibility in electoral candidate programs: Insights from the ballot box in an Arab Gulf country
articles.abstract: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries face substantial burdens from noncommunicable diseases along with high public expectations of health services, yet little is known about whether health is visibly represented in candidates’ declared election programs in this region. This study examined publicly identifiable candidates’ programs from the Kingdom of Bahrain’s Council of Representatives 2022 elections and assessed among candidates with identifiable programs whether the presence of explicit visible health content and candidates’ characteristics are associated with positive election outcomes. A cross-sectional study was undertaken using the complete cohort of candidates in Bahrain’s 2022 elections (N = 336). Election programs were identified from publicly declared materials, and health visibility was coded as present when a program contained an explicit pledge, priority or proposal addressing health services, public health, prevention, health issues, or health related social support. Descriptive data analysis used full cohort of candidates (N = 336) where applicable, whereas analysis of health visibility was conditional on 108 candidates with identifiable programs. Of the 336 candidates, 262 (78.0%) were men and 40 (11.9%) were elected to the council. Among candidates with a publicly identifiable program (108), 88 (81.5%) candidates had visible health content in their identified programs. In Firth penalized-likelihood analysis, women had higher odds of visible health content than men (OR=3.826, 95% profile-likelihood CI 0.943–15.522, p = 0.060). Among program identified candidates (N = 108), the association between visible health content and electoral success was inconclusive (two-sided Fisher’s exact test p = 0.188). This study has systematically quantified the health content visibility in a full candidate cohort from Bahrain’s Council of Representatives 2022 elections. Although exploratory, these findings provide evidence on how health issues are represented in electoral discourse in this Arab Gulf setting and may inform future comparative studies across GCC countries.

articles.title: Identification and validation of biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics dysfunction in Parkinson’s disease based on GEO datasets
articles.abstract: Background Parkinson’s disease (PD), the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by an unclear etiology and a lack of specific early diagnostic biomarkers. This study investigated novel biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics (MD) dysfunction in PD. Methods Transcriptomic data from the Gene Expression Omnibus database (training set: GSE6613, n = 72; validation set: GSE99039, n = 438) and 23 MD-related genes (MDRGs) were integrated. Differentially expressed genes were screened using the limma package. Three machine learning algorithms (random forest, support vector machine, and generalized linear model) were employed to construct diagnostic models. Feature importance analysis identified key candidate biomarkers, which were preliminarily validated in clinical samples via reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, and compound prediction analyses were subsequently performed. Results Cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 2 (CYSLTR2) and alpha‑tocopherol transfer protein‑like gene (TTPAL) were identified as MDRG score-correlated biomarkers. In the validation set, CYSLTR2 was significantly downregulated (log2FC = −1.25, P TTPAL was significantly upregulated (log2FC = 1.52, P Escherichia coli infection pathway. Immune analysis revealed six differentially infiltrated immune cell types. Notably, TTPAL expression was positively correlated with keratinocytes (cor = 0.30, P = 0.031). Four potential therapeutic compounds were predicted. RT-qPCR suggested the downregulation of CYSLTR2 and upregulation of TTPAL in patients with PD (P < 0.0001). Conclusion This study identified CYSLTR2 and TTPAL as novel candidate biomarkers associated with MD dysfunction in PD, providing novel targets for mechanistic investigation and therapeutic exploration.

articles.title: Integrative analysis reveals shared biomarkers and pathways in osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis using machine learning and single-cell sequencing
articles.abstract: Background Osteoporosis (OP) and Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) are prevalent chronic diseases characterized by bone loss and immune dysregulation. Evidence suggests that patients with RA are at increased risk of developing OP; however, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions remain incompletely understood. Methods Publicly available bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets for OP and RA were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to identify shared gene modules associated with both diseases. Functional enrichment and protein–protein interaction analyses were performed to characterize common biological pathways. Machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), were used to identify and validate shared hub genes and to construct diagnostic models. Immune cell infiltration was evaluated using CIBERSORT, and the cellular localization of hub genes was further validated using scRNA-seq analysis. Results WGCNA identified 329 genes shared between OP- and RA-associated modules, which were significantly enriched in muscle-related processes, cytokine signaling, and immune–inflammatory pathways. RF analysis identified three shared candidate genes: ANO5, IL27RA, and CNTN3. Among these, ANO5 and IL27RA demonstrated consistent expression evidence and literature support, whereas CNTN3 emerged as a computationally nominated candidate requiring cautious interpretation and experimental validation. An SVM-based model incorporating these genes demonstrated robust predictive accuracy in both OP and RA validation cohorts. Immune infiltration analysis revealed distinct yet coordinated immune landscapes, with hub genes showing significant correlations with T cells, macrophages, B cells, and plasma cells. ScRNA-seq analysis revealed that ANO5 was predominantly expressed in macrophages and fibroblasts, IL27RA was mainly enriched in T cells, whereas CNTN3 showed minimal enrichment at the single-cell level in both OP bone and RA synovial tissues. Conclusion This integrative bioinformatics and machine learning study identifies shared molecular signatures and immune-related mechanisms underlying OP and RA. ANO5 and IL27RA emerge as robust candidate regulators linking immune dysregulation and bone remodeling, whereas CNTN3—although identified by machine learning—requires cautious interpretation and further investigation due to limited supporting evidence. These findings provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of RA-associated OP and highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for their comorbidity.

articles.title: Lifestyle and dietary changes among cancer patients receiving active treatment: A cross-sectional study at a tertiary care center in Lebanon
articles.abstract: Background Cancer diagnosis is often accompanied by changes in nutritional needs and lifestyle habits, which may ultimately be associated with patients’ quality of life (QOL). Despite the high burden of cancer in Lebanon, limited data exist on how dietary intake and lifestyle behaviors change following diagnosis. This study aimed to assess self-reported retrospective changes in dietary and lifestyle behaviors following cancer diagnosis and examine factors associated with these changes and their relationship with QOL. Methods This single-center, cross-sectional study was conducted at Al Zahraa Hospital University Medical Center in Beirut, Lebanon. Adult cancer patients receiving active treatment were assessed regarding self-reported dietary and lifestyle behaviors before and after cancer diagnosis. QOL was assessed using the validated Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy–General (FACT-G). Results This study included 145 participants, the majority of whom were Lebanese (93.79%) and female (69.7%). Most lacked health insurance (84.8%), and 91.0% reported a financial burden related to treatment. Compared with recalled pre-diagnosis behaviors, 47.6% of participants reported favorable changes in smoking behavior, while 34.5% reported decreased physical activity. The most frequently reported favorable dietary changes according to the prespecified framework were reduced sugar (60.0%), reduced red meat (49.6%), and reduced fast-food consumption (34.5%). Younger age and employment were associated with the favorable dietary-change score in bivariate analyses, while age and marital status were associated with tobacco-habit change in multivariable analysis; medical insurance was associated with physical-activity change in bivariate analysis. The mean FACT-G total score was 70.48 ± 20.79. Favorable dietary changes were associated with FACT-G scores, including changes in fruit, milk, and fast-food intake. Conclusions Self-reported retrospective changes in dietary and lifestyle behaviors were observed among patients receiving active cancer treatment, with substantial variation across behavioral domains. The favorable dietary-change score was associated with QOL; however, the cross-sectional design and retrospective assessment preclude causal or directional interpretation. These findings may inform future longitudinal and interventional studies evaluating structured, individualized nutritional and lifestyle support during cancer treatment in Lebanon.

articles.title: Metagenomic analysis of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes detects Ralstonia phage sequences in Kenyan agricultural soils
articles.abstract: Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum species complex is a major constraint in tomato production in Kenya, resulting in yield losses of up to 100% in heavily infested fields. This study used high-throughput shotgun metagenomic sequencing approach to characterize the rhizosphere microbiomes of tomato plants in three of the major production areas in Kenya (Kirinyaga, Kiambu, and Laikipia counties) focusing on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences. Soil samples were collected from the rhizosphere of bacterial wilt-infected tomato plants, and microbial DNA was extracted using a modified phenol-chloroform protocol and sequenced using Illumina NovaSeq platform. Taxonomic profiling revealed diverse microbial communities dominated by Actinobacteria and Proteobacteria. Four Ralstonia species were confirmed (R. insidiosa, R. pickettii, R. mannitolilytica and R. wenshanensis). Sequences similar to the R. solanacearum species complex were also detected but were too short for species-level confirmation. Metagenomic analysis detected sequences matching four previously described Ralstonia phages (RSL1, RSIBR3, Anchaing, and Cimandef). Functional annotation demonstrated abundant metabolic pathways, energy production systems, and stress response mechanisms, indicating highly adaptive microbial communities in the tomato rhizosphere. This study provides baseline data on rhizosphere microbiome composition in Kenyan tomato production systems and identifies Ralstonia phage sequences that could guide future isolation and host-range studies. If future work shows that these phages are active against Ralstonia, they could contribute to locally adapted biocontrol approaches that reduce reliance on chemical pesticides.

articles.title: Mothers’ experiences of caring for a child with acute lymphoblastic leukemia in the West Bank, Palestine: A qualitative study
articles.abstract: Background Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) is the most common childhood cancer globally and requires prolonged, intensive treatment that places substantial demands on families. Mothers often assume primary caregiving roles; however, their experiences in conflict-affected settings remain underexplored. Objective This study aimed to explore the experiences of Palestinian mothers caring for a child diagnosed with ALL in the West Bank. Methods A qualitative descriptive study included fifteen mothers of children diagnosed with ALL and receiving treatment at Beit Jala Governmental Hospital, who were recruited using purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, transcribed verbatim and analyzed using qualitative content analysis following the approach of Graneheim and Lundman (2004). Results The study identified five major themes and eighteen sub-themes reflecting mothers’ experiences: emotional issues (shock and disbelief, negative emotions, denial and rejection); hindrances due to political situations (limited health care access, feeling isolated due to closures); impact of the child’s illness (caregiver burden vs. protective bonding, financial strain, loss of previous life, sibling neglect, shift in the role of the mother, marital life impact, challenges in balancing home routine); resilience and endurance (leveraging social support networks, fatalism and religious faith as a framework, cultivating optimism and positive outlook); and mothers’ needs to enhance resilience (emotional and psychological support, educational and informational needs, financial needs). Conclusion Mothers caring for children with ALL in the West Bank face profound emotional, social, and structural challenges shaped by both illness-related and political contextual factors. Despite these adversities, mothers demonstrate resilience through social support networks, religious faith, and optimism. Family-centered and context-sensitive interventions that address emotional, educational, and financial needs are essential for strengthening maternal resilience and improving care outcomes.

articles.title: Nationwide trends in physical disability among rheumatoid arthritis patients in Korea (2010–2022): A retrospective cohort study based on national registry data
articles.abstract: Background Whether the burden of legally certified disability among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) has decreased in the modern treatment era is uncertain, particularly in Asia. We investigated trends in registered and physical disability among Korean patients with RA. Methods Using National Health Insurance Service data (patient-level 50% random sample), we identified patients aged ≥19 years with seropositive RA registered in the copayment assistance program for rare and intractable diseases in 2010–2022. Disability status, including physical disability (certified musculoskeletal impairment), came from the national disability registry. We estimated annual prevalence and, in newly diagnosed patients, incidence per 1,000 person-years, and compared the results with national disability statistics. Results The number of patients with seropositive RA identified in the database and included in this study was 33,992 in 2010 and 67,844 in 2022. The prevalence of registered disability declined from 20.3% to 14.6% and that of physical disability from 17.4% to 10.9% (both p for trend <0.001) in both sexes. Among 61,086 newly diagnosed patients, the incidence of registered disability did not change (5.08 per 1,000 person-years; annual change −0.9%, p = 0.24), whereas that of physical disability declined by 6.7% per year (p < 0.001). Men had a higher incidence of registered disability than women (6.73 vs. 4.58 per 1,000 person-years), but not of physical disability. Older age (odds ratio [OR] 1.035 per year, 95% CI 1.032–1.039), male sex (OR 1.295, 95% CI 1.174–1.429), and lower income were associated with incident registered disability. In 2022, physical disability remained more prevalent in RA (10.9%) than in the general population (2.3%) and in those aged ≥65 years (7.1%). Conclusions Certified physical disability among Korean patients with RA declined substantially between 2010 and 2022, whereas the incidence of any registered disability remained stable. An excess burden of physical disability compared with the general population persisted.

articles.title: Operationalizing independent oversight in large-scale public health cohorts: Monitoring protocol for the NIMHANS–NH–SKAN Stroke project
articles.abstract: Background onitoring the implementation of observational studies are rare, unlike experimental studies. This article aims to describe the development and implementation of a monitoring plan and framework for a large-scale cohort and quasi-experimental study: the NIMHANS-NH-SKAN Stroke project. Methods The monitoring framework was developed through a systematic, stepwise process involving expert consultation workshops conducted by an Independent Monitoring Team in collaboration with the study team. A logical framework approach was used to identify key processes throughout the study implementation. These processes were then disaggregated into critical activities (sub-processes) to generate an initial list of monitoring items. These items were prioritized using the Vital–Essential–Desirable (VED) strategy through consensus building. The shortlisted items were further refined using SMART criteria (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound) to finalize checklist components. Key Performance Indicators were subsequently derived from the finalized checklist items. The framework emphasized usability, feasibility, and relevance to implementation, enabling systematic monitoring of critical study processes. Results A total of 89 activities were identified and consolidated into 10 checklists, from which 16 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) were derived. The monitoring framework primarily emphasized indicator-based assessment of project outputs and outcomes while ensuring adherence to key processes and quality standards. KPIs were expressed as proportions to facilitate standardized performance assessment across sites and time periods. The checklists comprised a combination of in-person observations and record reviews. Monitoring findings were synthesized into periodic reports based on KPI proportions, enabling objective evaluation of implementation performance and identification of areas requiring corrective action. Conclusions Timely and systematic monitoring is critical to ensure rigor in large-scale projects, and the approach described in this study provides a replicable framework for the development of robust monitoring systems in similar community-based large-scale observational studies in India and similar countries.

articles.title: Opportunities and challenges for introduction of balanced energy protein supplementation through routine antenatal care
articles.abstract: Background The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends balanced energy and protein (BEP) supplementation during pregnancy in contexts where prevalence of maternal underweight, defined as body mass index (BMI) < 18.5 kg/m2, is ≥ 20%. Evidence shows that BEP supplementation in underweight pregnant women reduces the risk of low birthweight, small for gestational age, and preterm birth. Yet little is known about how to introduce BEP through routine antenatal care (ANC). This paper explores challenges, opportunities, and recommendations for successful introduction of BEP supplementation through ANC service delivery. Methods From August – December 2023, a mixed-methods landscape analysis was carried out, which comprised of a review of country antenatal care guidelines, as well as key informant interviews (KIIs) with thirteen global and country stakeholders. KIIs were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed by themes and subthemes using Dedoose qualitative software 10.0. Results Findings revealed confusion around the definition of BEP, coupled with low awareness of the WHO ANC guideline on BEP supplementation among country stakeholders. Provider capacity for BEP provision is weak. Sharing, selling, and stockouts of BEP supplies are common. Data on the feasibility and cost-effectiveness of the introduction of BEP at country level is critical to inform implementation. Conclusion Successful introduction of BEP as part of ANC service delivery requires country program implementers to consider government commitments, health provider training, demand generation, compliance, supplies and logistics, local production, and routine monitoring of BEP indicators. Globally, standardized BEP guidance, indicators, and definitions are critical to support quality country implementation. For sustainability, emerging concerns around reductions in global health funding should be addressed in future program design and implementation.

articles.abstract: We formulate a time-dependent density functional theory for the coupled dynamics of electrons and nuclei that goes beyond the Born-Oppenheimer (BO) approximation. articles.title: Rare physics demystifies Martian cloud mystery
articles.abstract: An exceptionally long, thin cloud appears for a few hours each morning during Mars’s dusty season. Models of the atmosphere couldn’t explain how it develops—until now.

articles.title: Bionic intelligent surfaces based on deformable micro/nanostructures
Water and air pollution remediation by COFs, ZIFs, MILs, and their composites: green synthesis, structure–property relationships, mechanisms, and future perspectives
A frugal automated contact angle analyser for low-cost surface wettability characterization
articles.abstract: Contact angle measurement is a fundamental technique for evaluating surface wettability in materials science, biomedical engineering and coating technologies. However, the high cost of commercial contact angle analysers limits access to surface characterization, particularly in resource-limited laboratories. This study presents a low-cost automated contact angle analyser developed using frugal engineering principles and open-source hardware. The system integrates Arduino-based control, NEMA 17 stepper-motor actuation, automated microdroplet dispensing, smartphone-based optical imaging and a 3D-printed polylactic acid (PLA) framework. A calibrated 330-step dispensing cycle generated reproducible 5 μl water droplets, with fixed optical alignment minimized operator variability. Wettability measurements were performed on polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and aluminium substrates and analysed using ImageJ. Mean contact angles were 108.5° for PTFE, 73.9° for PVC and 85.8° for aluminium, closely matching published literature values. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) demonstrated significant differences between substrates (p < 0.001), with measurement variability of ±2.3° indicated good repeatability. The total fabrication cost was £114.26, representing approximately 99% cost reduction compared with commercial instruments. The proposed platform demonstrates that automated, reproducible surface wettability characterization can be achieved using low-cost, open-source instrumentation, providing an accessible solution for research, education and engineering laboratories while broadening access to advanced materials characterization.

articles.title: Beyond sperm competition: perspectives on sperm economy from external fertilizing fishes
articles.abstract: Research on sperm economy has traditionally focused on sperm competition as a major selective pressure shaping sperm production and allocation. In this review, we broaden this perspective by considering how other reproductive and ecological pressures influence the management of a costly and finite sperm supply. We synthesize evidence showing that in externally fertilizing fishes, high mating frequency, low female fecundity, prolonged spawning, rapid sperm dilution and costly male reproductive investment can favour sperm-economy strategies even when sperm competition is weak or absent. Across fish taxa, these constraints have led to convergent behavioural and physiological adaptations, including fractionated ejaculation, temporal matching of sperm release to egg deposition and manipulation of the fertilization microenvironment, which improve fertilization efficiency while minimizing sperm expenditure. We further highlight a recurring association between these strategies and semi-cystic spermatogenesis, consistent with the possibility that optimization of sperm use extends beyond ejaculate allocation to the regulation of sperm production during spermatogenesis. By integrating evidence from behaviour to reproductive physiology, this review reframes sperm economy as a general resource-allocation problem, with sperm competition representing one of several selective pressures. Externally fertilizing fishes emerge as an exceptional model for understanding the diverse evolutionary routes by which males optimize reproductive investment.

articles.title: Decoding the dead: new combined application of strontium and lead isotope analysis to Romano-British cremations from Colchester (UK)
articles.abstract: This paper presents an innovative application of two distinct isotope systems to paired otic capsule and outer petrous bone samples from cremated remains. This dual analysis approach, applied to 22 human cremation burials from Roman Colchester (UK), demonstrates evidence for origins outside Britain for several individuals, shedding fresh light on an emerging capital city within a new province of the Roman Empire. Results have implications for understanding the population dynamics of large Roman provincial urban centres following the conquest period in the north-western provinces, when cremation is the dominant burial practice. The method also allows a detailed reconstruction of individual mobility at different ages within an individual's life.

articles.title: Design principles for natural SGLT2 modulators from multi-scale computation
articles.abstract: Human sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (hSGLT2) is a membrane-embedded renal transporter and an established therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes. Hyperoside, myricetin, cyanidin-3-O-glucoside and isoliquiritigenin were investigated as a chemically diverse panel of natural scaffolds using a multi-scale computational workflow combining redocking-validated molecular docking, reconstruction of an unresolved transporter segment, molecular dynamics (MD) in an explicit POPC bilayer, molecular mechanics/Poisson–Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, principal component and free-energy landscape analyses and density functional theory (DFT). The membrane simulations preserved the global hSGLT2 fold while revealing distinct ligand-dependent binding behaviours. Myricetin and cyanidin-3-O-glucoside exhibited limited positional deviations; hyperoside achieved persistent accommodation following an initial adjustment, whereas isoliquiritigenin underwent a marked late rearrangement. Ensemble-based energetic analysis prioritized cyanidin-3-O-glucoside, while hyperoside and myricetin formed an energetically comparable intermediate group and isoliquiritigenin displayed the least favourable profile. Electronic-structure analysis further characterized cyanidin-3-O-glucoside as the most responsive ligand within the DFT subset. Collectively, these findings indicate that glycone-assisted polar anchoring, aromatic complementarity and restricted conformational flexibility promote persistent hSGLT2 recognition. Direct hSGLT2 inhibition and hSGLT1 counter-screening assays remain necessary to establish potency and selectivity.

articles.title: Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches
articles.abstract: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a key therapeutic target for various cancers because of its central role in tumor growth and survival signaling. This study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, umbrella sampling (US), and toxicity prediction to identify potential ALK inhibitors from 307 phytochemicals of the Glycosmis genus. A previously validated CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies, leading to the selection of 26 compounds with ΔGML < −11 kcal mol−1. Molecular docking identified six top candidates with favorable binding affinities ranging from −5.856 to −9.667 kcal mol⁻¹, which subsequently underwent 200 ns MD simulations. Structural analyses confirmed the stability of all ALK–ligand complexes, while interaction studies revealed extensive hydrophobic contacts and conserved hydrogen bonds involving key ALK residues. US calculations estimated binding free energies from −8.354 to −13.272 kcal mol−1, with compound 54 exhibiting the strongest affinity (ΔGUS = −13.272 kcal mol−1). Several alkaloids, including acrifoline, heptazoline, and atalaphyllidine, also demonstrated promisingbinding properties and reported anticancer activities. Toxicity prediction indicated acceptable safety profiles, highlighting Glycosmis-derived phytochemicals as promising potential ALK inhibitor candidates and supporting the utility of ML-guided virtual screening combined with advanced molecular simulations for natural product-based anticancer drug discovery. Nevertheless, biochemical and cellular experiments are required to confirm their ALK inhibitory activity, selectivity, and therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Drivers of zoonotic spillover at human–domestic animal–wildlife interfaces: a multi-species model incorporating wildlife chronic stress
articles.abstract: Zoonotic disease emergence at the wildlife–domestic animal–human interface results from a complex interplay of ecological, physiological and anthropogenic factors. Here, we have developed a multi-environment, multi-host compartmental model to identify key drivers of spillover risk across urban, rural and natural environments. The framework incorporates heterogeneous host populations, inter-species contacts and host movement, and includes wildlife chronic stress as one factor influencing susceptibility, transmissibility and recovery. Sensitivity analyses show that domestic animal populations at agricultural interfaces strongly amplify spillover risk through their recovery dynamics and per-contact transmission probabilities, while within-wildlife transmission across environments also shapes system dynamics. Chronic stress effects can further increase spillover risk, and the model indicates that reducing wildlife stress alongside improving domestic animal health and management can markedly lower the likelihood of cross-species transmission. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining ecological conditions that reduce chronic physiological stress in wildlife populations and integrating physiological and ecological data into epidemiological modelling. Such models can inform both bottom-up interventions targeting domestic animals and top-down strategies that sustain resilient wildlife communities and, thereby, mitigate zoonotic spillover.

articles.title: First direct measurement of food transit time through the gastrointestinal tracts of plant-eating primates using isotopic tagging
articles.abstract: The time it takes for food to transit animal gastrointestinal tracts is essential information to fields from organismal evolution to ecosystem ecology. Nevertheless, current estimation methods do not measure food directly, are impractical for many species and often require unnatural conditions to administer. We overcome these limitations by adopting techniques from organic geochemistry. We trace isotopically tagged greens in lemurs, from ingestion to excretion, through isotopic analysis of higher plant biomarkers recovered in faeces. For frugivorous ruffed lemurs (Varecia rubra), omnivorous ring-tailed lemurs (Lemur catta) and frugo-folivorous sifakas (Propithecus coquereli), respectively, the biomarkers first appeared at 1.2, 4.3 and 23.4 h after ingestion and peaked at 2.9, 5.7 and 48.4 h after ingestion. These measurements generally match published estimates from pre-existing proxies. However, not all animals cleared the isotopic signal by the end of sample collection, yielding minimum gut retention times of 23.9–29.5 h for ruffed lemurs, 25.5–30.3 h for ring-tailed lemurs and 95.7 h for sifakas. We thus extend gut retention times approximately threefold from pre-existing proxies. Our interdisciplinary approach is applicable across diverse plant eaters, can help refine models of nutrient, seed and pathogen dispersal and be used to probe consequences of lifestyle and medical interventions on organismal nutrition and health.

articles.title: Generalized maximum entropy: when and why you need it
articles.abstract: The classical maximum entropy principle based on Shannon entropy is widely used to construct least-biased probability distributions from partial information. However, the Shore–Johnson axioms that single out the Shannon functional hinge on strong system independence—an assumption often violated in real-world, strongly correlated systems. When that assumption fails, enforcing the Shannon form imposes an independence the data do not support, and can systematically distort the inferred distribution. We provide a self-contained guide to when and why practitioners should abandon the Shannon form in favour of the one-parameter Uffink–Jizba–Korbel (UJK) family of generalized entropies. After reviewing the Shore–Johnson axioms from an applied perspective, we recall the most commonly used entropy functionals and locate them within the UJK family. The need for generalized entropies is illustrated with two applications, one in economics and the other in ecology. A simple mathematical model worked out in detail further shows the power of generalized maximum-entropy approaches in cases where strong system independence does not hold. We conclude with practical guidelines for choosing an entropy measure and reporting results so that analyses remain transparent and reproducible.

articles.title: Influence of soft coral density and depth on benthic communities on Fiji's Rainbow Reef
articles.abstract: Some soft corals have the potential to increase in prevalence on tropical coral reefs as the severity of anthropogenic climate change increases. While soft corals are therefore an increasingly important component of reef ecosystems, little is known about their ecological role on coral reefs and their influence on community dynamics and diversity. We used Bayesian network inference (BNI) to identify the associations among benthic taxa across sites with varying degrees of soft coral dominance on Fiji's Rainbow Reef, and then employed spatial point process analysis (SPPA) to reveal the ecological processes behind these associations. We found that depth was a dominant driver of community dynamics, and that white Nephtheidae soft corals were negatively associated with scleractinian corals and positively associated with algal proliferation—possibly owing to soft corals reducing grazing pressure. Our results show distinctions in reef benthos and ecological dynamics between scleractinian and soft coral-dominated components of the Rainbow Reef. We found that diversity levels were significantly lower on soft coral-dominated quadrats relative to scleractinian-dominated quadrats, potentially highlighting the reduction in benthic diversity when Nephtheidae soft corals dominate reef walls.

articles.title: Large language model developments
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are generative artificial intelligence (AI) models trained with vast amounts of data and context, and excel at processing, understanding and generating human language, using transformer models to learn statistical relationships between tokens. LLMs are a subset of transformer models, and hence are closely related but not interchangeable. Given the ‘explosion’ of LLM research, the challenge is tracking emerging developments and matching LLMs to applications. This paper reviews LLM developments with the aim of understanding the underlying models’ computational strengths and weaknesses, building on previous work focusing on LLM optimization (Sharkey & Treleaven 2025 Optimising large language models: taxonomy and techniques. SSRN Scholarly Paper no. 5278456. Rochester, NY: SSRN). We find that despite their power, LLMs (transformers) face several key challenges. These include: (i) computational complexity and resource requirements—training and deploying large models is extremely costly and slow, and energy consumption is a concern; (ii) understanding long sequences and dependencies—even with enhancements, models can struggle with very long-range dependencies or context lengths beyond their window (e.g. maintaining coherence in a long document), which reflects the more fundamental absence of continual learning; (iii) interpretability and bias—it remains difficult to interpret why a model produces a given output, and models can inadvertently amplify biases present in training data; and (iv) optimization challenges, including fine-tuning for specific tasks without overfitting or losing generality and ensuring efficient inference (latency, the delay before a response is completed) for real-time applications. In summary, this review focuses on architectural, optimization and interpretability developments in LLMs. It does not aim to provide a systematic benchmark comparison, exhaustive implementation details or empirical performance evaluation, which are covered extensively elsewhere. The authors are committed to updating this review aligned to constant changes in the technology; please reach out with any additions.

articles.title: Mast fruiting in a large tropical African legume tree species and the mineral nutrient limitation hypothesis
articles.abstract: The large grove-forming ectomycorrhizal tropical tree Microberlinia bisulcata displays strong mast fruiting on poor soils. Evidence is presented that masting is probably determined primarily by mineral nutrients and secondarily by radiation. To test the nutrient resource limitation hypothesis, phenological recordings were matched with climate variables and modelled using logistic time-series regression. A strong predictor was average daily rainfall in the dry season, low in the current year of masting and high in the year prior. Less strong was the increase in dry season radiation between prior and mast years. Masting events showed no relationship to annual stem increment. Masting intensity was reduced after two caterpillar attacks. Fallen-leaf phosphorus concentration increased in the inter-mast interval, and that for potassium peaked mid-interval. A drier dry season prior to masting may have increased tree carbon, while a wetter one increased nutrient uptake by roots and mycorrhizas. A rooting–fruiting trade-off in carbon is suggested. The long-term stochastic driver appears to be dry season rainfall. Synchrony across masting trees may be enhanced by equilibration of nutrients across the mycorrhizal–root network. A life-history strategy determined by mineral nutrient resource dynamics provides the best explanation and advanced model of the observed pattern of events.

articles.title: Patterns in conflict dynamics in Yemen and Syria
articles.abstract: Conflict fatalities tend to follow heavy-tailed statistical distributions. A 2005 fusion–fission theory predicts that, when armed groups operate through dynamically forming and fragmenting clusters, the number of fatalities per event should be approximated by a power-law distribution with exponent α near 2.5, with deviations reflecting the relative robustness of larger versus smaller fighter clusters. We use Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED) event-level fatality data to estimate α in recent Yemen and Syria conflict periods during 2023–2025. These conflict event datasets are small, incomplete and imperfect and only produce very crude approximations to a power law; nonetheless, the best-fit α values occupy the range 2.5<α<3.5 across most periods, which is broadly consistent with predominantly fragmented or weakly consolidated armed-group organization. Temporary reductions in α are broadly consistent with episodes in which larger coordinated clusters become more consequential. More rigorous testing will require improved datasets to become available in the future.

articles.title: People and bats in Fiji: perceptions and interactions
articles.abstract: The management of wild bat populations often presents challenges in balancing the needs of biodiversity conservation and public health risks from zoonotic diseases. In Fiji, the most important recognized zoonotic infection is Leptospira, which was recently detected in wild bat populations. Five out of six species of Fijian bats are considered threatened to critically endangered on the IUCN Red List. This study investigates the perceptions of bats by people in Fiji and aims to identify and quantify the reported frequency and types of interactions between bats and people. In this mixed-methods study, 198 Fijian people were interviewed across the three main islands of Fiji: Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and Taveuni. Bats were generally perceived positively (63%, 125/198), mostly because they are perceived to be ‘clean, healthy and tasty’ meat sources (73%, 134/184). The majority of participants consume and come into contact with bats or with their urine, faeces, blood and saliva. Older adults, men and those who recognize that bats can cause harm are more likely to contact bats in Fiji. Quantifying these interactions and identifying other risk factors for bat exposure is an important step in targeting conservation efforts, community engagement and education, as well as determining at-risk groups for possible zoonotic pathogen exposure.

articles.title: Phenological shifts of low-latitude frogs over 15 years revealed by passive acoustic monitoring
articles.abstract: Phenological responses to climate warming are well-documented, yet limited data come from low latitudes. Because phenological sensitivity may vary with latitude, studies in low-latitude regions are essential to understand global patterns. To fill this gap, we analysed acoustic recordings collected daily over 15 years on Iriomote Island, in Japan's transitional zone between subtropical and tropical biomes. We applied the BirdNET deep learning model to quantify the breeding phenology of seven frog species. Seasonal calling patterns differed among species, with peaks occurring in various seasons while one species called nearly year-round. Among six species analysed for phenological trends, a winter-breeding tree-frog (Zhangixalus owstoni) showed a statistically significant shift in median calling date (3.8 days later per decade), whereas the other species showed no significant shifts of varying magnitude and direction. Sliding time window analysis indicated late-summer temperature—which increased during the study period—best predicted median calling dates in Z. owstoni, suggesting that climate warming delayed the phenology of a winter breeder even where year-round reproduction is possible. The absence of significant phenological advancement in our dataset contrasts with spring advancement commonly reported in temperate regions. These findings reinforce the importance of examining long-term phenological shifts across more sites in low-latitude regions.

articles.title: Quantifying ‘surprise’ in capuchin monkeys ( Sapajus apella )
articles.abstract: Violation-of-expectation (VoE) events offer a fascinating lens into the intersection of cognition and emotion. Research suggests that, like humans, many animals are susceptible to VoE events in many physical domains, susceptibility typically assessed through behaviours such as visual and physical exploration of a stimulus. In humans, such susceptibility has been further documented through emotional surprise, such as delight following positive surprise and frustration following negative surprise. However, evidence in animals remains relatively limited. To address this gap, this study examined behavioural, cognitive and emotional responses of capuchin monkeys (Sapajus apella) to bait-and-switch VoE events of food items. Capuchins were chosen for this study not only for their exploratory and information-seeking behaviours, but also for known emotional responses to VoE events (e.g. frustration following inequity aversion). Contrary to prior research, this study found no evidence for violation susceptibility via behavioural, cognitive or emotional responses. Overall, such findings contribute valuable information to the VoE literature in primates regarding methodology and information salience, as well as underscore the current challenges of investigating emotional surprise in animals. Future research may benefit from establishing stronger expectations (e.g. more salient stimuli), to better investigate and quantify surprise to VoE events in animal species such as capuchin monkeys.

articles.title: Spatial and chemical heterogeneity of insect cuticular hydrocarbon layers: insights from extraction methods and acclimatization regimes
articles.abstract: Insect cuticles are covered by a complex mixture of cuticular hydrocarbons (CHCs) that are essential for desiccation resistance and chemical communication, yet the physical structure of CHC layers remains poorly understood. We extracted CHCs from five insect species (desert locusts, house crickets, American cockroaches and two ant species) using solvents of differing polarity and extraction durations, and from insects reared under different temperature regimes. Extractions with n-hexane were enriched in relatively solid CHCs (n-alkanes and terminally branched monomethylalkanes), while extractions with dichloromethane and dichloromethane–methanol yielded proportionally more fluid compounds (internally branched monomethyl and dimethylalkanes, unsaturated hydrocarbons). Solid-phase CHCs were proportionally more abundant in shorter extractions, whereas fluid-phase compounds were proportionally more abundant in prolonged or sequential extractions. These patterns are consistent with a model of cohesive solid domains surrounded by more accessible fluid regions, though this interpretation remains indirect and alternative explanations (e.g. differential solubility and diffusion kinetics) cannot be excluded. CHCs of similar phase behaviour covaried across treatments, indicating that they aggregate within shared domains. Warm acclimatization increased the proportion of solid compounds, whereas fluctuating temperatures enhanced CHCs with intermediate phase behaviour. Our results suggest spatial and chemical heterogeneity in the CHC layer, with patterns of differential extractability consistent with clustering into phase-distinct domains, though direct imaging is required to confirm spatial topology. This potential heterogeneity may facilitate CHC multi-functionality, with the phase behaviour and domain membership of each CHC depending on its biophysical properties relative to the individual's overall CHC profile.

articles.title: Spectral theory of spin relaxation
articles.abstract: A dynamical theory of spin relaxation previously formulated in terms of stochastic differential equations is extended beyond the extreme narrowed approximation to incorporate temporal correlation in the driving random magnetic fields. An analysis of spin–spin relaxation in this case is provided, which is non-perturbative in the random field and yields an exact solution to the spin dynamical equations for axial (longitudinal) field fluctuations. We provide a real-time dynamical derivation that leads to a generalized class of spin spectra that are essentially non-Lorentzian for all finite field parameters. A spectral-moment analysis and novel parameter-extraction scheme lead to distinct notions of observable relaxation timescales compared with the standard characteristic exponential. The Lorentzian case is recovered as the extreme narrowed limit.

articles.title: Sublethal insecticide exposure and inbreeding impose a developmental bottleneck but enhance crop-damaging traits in surviving Colorado potato beetles
articles.abstract: Intensive agricultural insecticide use often fails to eradicate pest populations completely, leaving small remnant populations exposed to persistent sublethal residues and potentially elevated inbreeding. How such remnant populations persist remains poorly understood. Here, we examined how inbreeding and sublethal imidacloprid exposure shape survival and post-emergence performance in the Colorado potato beetle (Leptinotarsa decemlineata), a major agricultural pest. We compared four groups differing in breeding status and insecticide exposure history, and quantified emergence rate, locomotor activity, feeding behaviour and reproductive output. We found that despite the insecticide dosage being sublethal, both chemical exposure and inbreeding imposed severe developmental costs, reducing the adult emergence rate with no significant interaction effects. However, among the adults, we observed trait-specific phenotypic plasticity. Male locomotor activity was reduced by both stressors, while female activity remained stable. Notably, herbivory significantly increased under both inbreeding and sublethal insecticide exposure. Furthermore, while inbreeding severely reduced both egg production and hatching success, sublethal exposure to the insecticide surprisingly increased hatching success in surviving pairs. These results demonstrate that sublethal insecticide exposure and inbreeding can create a strong developmental bottleneck. Yet, surviving individuals can exhibit compensatory plasticity that maintains or even enhances their capacity for crop damage.

articles.title: Triterpenoid saponins from the aerial parts of Phytolacca americana and their anti-influenza A virus activity
articles.abstract: Phytolacca americana L. (Phytolaccaceae), a perennial species native to North America, is rich in oleanane-type triterpenoid saponins. In this study, ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC–QTOF–MS) profiling of the aerial-part extract revealed characteristic fragment ions of phytolaccagenin- and phytolaccagenic acid-type saponins with diverse glycosylation. MS-guided annotation enabled targeted isolation and structural elucidation of two previously undescribed compounds, one oleanane-type triterpenoid saponin (1) and one neolignan (3). Additionally, compound 2, which had been reported only based on mass spectrometric data, was isolated, and its structure was fully elucidated for the first time, together with those of 10 known oleanane-type triterpenoid saponins (4–13). Their structures were elucidated by comprehensive one-dimensional and two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopic analyses combined with UPLC–QTOF–MS data. Although P. americana extracts have been reported to inhibit influenza A virus infection in previous studies, the bioactive constituents responsible for this antiviral activity have not been identified. The crude extract and isolated saponins were evaluated using complementary in vitro assays. In H1N1-infected A549 cells, compound 11 (3-O-trisaccharide phytolaccagenic acid) reduced viral NS1 RNA levels at 6 and 24 hpi as determined by RT–qPCR. Antiviral activity was further confirmed by plaque reduction and immunoblot analyses, with a plaque-assay IC50 of 57.98 ± 0.26 µM.

articles.title: What drives the winter behaviour and ecology of the temperate coral Astrangia poculata? An examination of thermal and nutritional cues
articles.abstract: In temperate ecosystems, accessing subtidal environments in the winter is challenging, and therefore, winter ecology and seasonal variation are understudied. For the temperate coral Astrangia poculata, winter is thought to be a period of biological ‘reset’, in which many cellular processes slow or stop, and the microbiome and symbiont community shift dramatically. The period of quiescence, when corals enter a dormant state with limited feeding or metabolic activity, is primarily driven by cold temperatures. However, other ecological drivers of quiescence remain unclear. Here, we documented quiescence in symbiotic and aposymbiotic colonies of A. poculata over a four-month winter period at two depths. First, we confirmed that quiescence is strongly associated with water temperatures under 6°C. Although we quantified a thermocline associated with depth, there was no influence of depth on quiescence. Symbiotic corals were more likely than aposymbiotic corals to enter quiescence, and higher chlorophyll α concentration was associated with lower quiescence, indicating a nutritional link to quiescence in A. poculata. Finally, we compared our results with previous quiescence observations and determined that the dormancy period is shorter in warmer winters, which has implications for the future ecology and behaviour of A. poculata in an era of global change.

articles.title: A biofilm-derived peptide as an underwater adhesive
articles.abstract: Wet adhesives that perform under water have broad applications in industrial and biomedical settings. To date, molecular designs for underwater adhesives have largely been inspired by marine animals including mussels and barnacles. Here, we propose bacterial biofilms as an alternative source of inspiration for underwater adhesives. Specifically, we demonstrate the application potential of a peptide derived from biofilms formed by the notorious pathogen Vibrio cholerae . We characterize the ability of this biofilm-derived peptide to adsorb onto various surfaces and to glue wet surfaces by using a combination of confocal microscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, atomic force microscopy, lap shear tests, and spectroscopic tools. We further show that the peptide can coaggregate with microspheres acting as an effective flocculant. Our results open new design possibilities for underwater adhesives inspired by natural biofilms.

articles.title: A disynaptic trigeminal circuit for the transformation and integration of oral chemesthesis in male mice
articles.abstract: Chemesthesis, encompassing oral sensations such as spiciness and coolness, is an important yet incompletely understood component of mammalian chemical sensing. Unlike taste or olfaction, these sensations are conveyed primarily through trigeminal pathways; however, how modality-specific peripheral signals are processed and transformed along central ascending pathways remains poorly understood. Herein, we delineate the structural and functional organization of an ascending trigeminal-brainstem-parabrachial circuit that mediates oral chemesthetic processing in male mice. Using viral tracing, in vivo calcium imaging, and chemogenetic and optogenetic manipulations, we identify a genetically defined disynaptic glutamatergic pathway (trigeminal ganglion → spinal trigeminal nucleus caudalis → lateral parabrachial nucleus) that is both necessary and sufficient for capsaicin- and menthol-evoked defensive behaviors. Although peripheral TRPV1 + and TRPM8 + neurons retain a degree of modality bias, we observe substantial convergence of spicy and cooling signals within the spinal trigeminal nucleus, followed by sustained and synchronized population activity in vglut2 + neurons of the external lateral parabrachial nucleus. This hierarchical transformation from peripheral segregation to central integration reveals the organizational principle by which distinct chemesthetic modalities are progressively integrated along a trigeminal-mediated ascending pathway, providing a circuit-level framework for understanding how chemical stimuli are processed and coordinated to drive defensive behaviors.

articles.title: A functional connectome identifies vulnerability to cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease progression
articles.abstract: Identifying the neurobiological basis of cognitive vulnerability is essential for preventing Alzheimer’s disease (AD). We derived the Alzheimer’s Resilience-Vulnerability Connectome (ARC) by contrasting SuperAgers (SA), an extreme phenotype of preserved late-life memory, with AD using resting-state fMRI.
