As a consequence, two regions with different Chern numbers acquire different chemical potentials at charge neutrality, leading to a built-in potential of topological origin across the junction. Using this built-in potential as a boundary condition, we solve the 2D Poisson equation to obtain the electric potential and charge density profiles, as well as the capacitance, of Chern semiconductor junctions. Our results inform the interplay between electronic topology and electrostatics in devices made from 2D materials.

articles.title: Emergent Incompressibility in Polariton Condensates for Scalable XY Spin Simulation
articles.abstract: Driven-dissipative polariton networks offer a powerful analog platform for simulating continuous-spin Hamiltonians. However, their practical scalability is fundamentally limited by amplitude-phase coupling and metastable trapping in highly frustrated energy landscapes. Here, we present an \textit{in situ} dual-enhancement mechanism to address these bottlenecks without requiring external site-specific fine-tuning. First, a renormalization-group analysis based on density rescaling shows that higher-order nonlinear loss drives the condensates toward an incompressible regime, intrinsically suppressing amplitude fluctuations and enforcing phase-only dynamics. For macroscopic XY networks (up to 10,000 spins), this phase-amplitude decoupling yields a more than 50-fold reduction in energy, while simultaneously shrinking the standard deviation by a factor of six. More generally, it restores the extensive scaling of the optimized XY energy with system size. Second, to navigate the rugged, nonconvex energy landscape, we introduce weak Hermitian pulses. When implemented through a multistage protocol, these pulses enable repeated escapes from local minima and drive the system to deeper energy minima. Benchmarking shows an increasing advantage with system size, with the polariton simulator outperforming the classical Monte Carlo-SQP baseline in every sampled macroscopic realization. Our work provides a physical framework for scalable polariton analog computing.

articles.title: Exact Transport-Information Correspondence for Distribution-Adaptive Discretization
articles.abstract: Discretization of continuous probability distributions is an operation on the sample space, and the structure induced by this operation cannot generally be determined solely from information geometry. In our recent work on unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), we established a non-arbitrary connection between the transport cost associated with discretization and the information-geometric indistinguishability of continuous probability distributions. Through the transport-information correspondence, the UCN quantify the information-theoretic cost due to discretization as the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence between nearby continuous distributions associated with the discretization geometry. In the original UCN construction, discretization is implemented by transporting the probability mass within each cell to its geometric centroid. The resulting transport-information correspondence, however, is derived under specific conditions involving the cell geometry, spatial coverage, and the vanishing-cell-scale limit. In this work, we introduce an alternative local-map discretization scheme in which the probability mass within each cell is transported to its own probability-weighted centroid. This change in the representative-point selection enables an exact expression for the transport cost of each cell in terms of the covariance matrix of its conditional probability distribution and the Fisher metric of the underlying continuous family. We establish an exact correspondence between the resulting transport cost and the expectation of the associated Fisher-induced quadratic form, without requiring uniform cell geometry, complete coverage of the sample space, or an infinitesimal cell-scale limit. The proposed construction thus generalizes the transport-information correspondence to finite-scale discretization using arbitrary collections of non-overlapping bounded convex sets.

articles.title: Experimental evaluation of Kolmogorov's first similarity hypothesis for shear-dependent viscosity fluids
articles.abstract: We experimentally investigate the applicability of Kolmogorov's first similarity hypothesis to shear-dependent viscosity fluids. We assess whether dissipative range statistics exhibit a self-similar behavior in nearly homogeneous and isotropic turbulence, using stereo particle image velocimetry in aqueous Carbopol solutions across two concentrations and a range of forcing conditions. We observe that, when normalized by the mean viscosity and mean dissipation rate, second- and third-order structure functions collapse across the different experimental conditions and exhibit functional forms compatible with classical Newtonian results. These observations are in general agreement with the recent numerical results of Rosti [J. Fluid Mech. 1012, R5 (2025)], who proposed that Kolmogorov's similarity hypotheses can be extended to shear-thinning fluids by considering dissipation scales based on the mean viscosity, the mean dissipation rate, and the flow index.

articles.title: Field evolution of the multi-$k$ magnetic states in NdB$_4$ revealed by neutron diffraction
articles.abstract: We investigate the magnetic states of the Shastry-Sutherland-lattice magnet NdB$_4$ using single-crystal neutron diffraction. We focus on magnetic fields applied along the tetragonal $c$ axis, which stabilise the fractional 1/5~magnetisation plateau. In the low-temperature phase below 4.9 K, the transition into the plateau state at approximately 12 kOe is marked by a change in the propagation vectors from $(1/5,0,-2/5)$ and its double $(2/5,0,1/5)$ to $(0,0,1/5)$ and $(0,0,2/5)$. At the transition from the plateau to a nominally `field-polarised' state near 33 kOe, all magnetic reflections associated with non-integer propagation vectors disappear, whereas reflections corresponding to the $\mathbf{k}=0$ component persist throughout the entire field range. We conclude that that the in-plane components survive even in the high-field phase and that the polarisation is, in fact, incomplete. The observed field dependence provides direct support for a description of NdB$_4$ in terms of two coupled magnetic instabilities: all-in-all-out order of the in-plane moments and a spin-density wave of the out-of-plane components.

articles.title: Floquet-Volkov spin polarization in spin-degenerate Antiferromagnets
articles.abstract: Periodic driving enables ultrafast control of electronic structures in solids through the formation of photon-dressed Floquet-Bloch states. However, the measured photoemission spectra are influenced not only by these states but also by their interference with Volkov-dressed outgoing photoelectrons. Here, we demonstrate that Floquet-Volkov interference can generate spin-polarized photoemission in a collinear antiferromagnetic Dirac model without spin-orbit coupling (SOC). An in-plane linearly polarized pump preserves $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry, leaving the Floquet quasienergies spin degenerate. Under near-resonant driving, photon-dressed conduction and valence bands hybridize, producing spin-dependent relative phases that are converted into unequal spin-resolved photoemission intensities through interference between pathways reaching the same Volkov-dressed final state. We analytically identify this interference mechanism and verify it using nonequilibrium Green-function calculations under periodic driving and finite pump-probe pulses. We further demonstrate that rotating the probe polarization can suppress or reverse the spin polarization without modifying the Floquet bands. Our findings establish Floquet-Volkov interference as a route to spin-selective photoemission in driven antiferromagnets without Floquet spin splitting or SOC.

articles.title: Frank Elastic Constants of Associating Rigid-Rodlike Systems
articles.abstract: Frank elastic constants of associating rigid rodlike systems are investigated using a mean field theory combined with the Straley elastic free energy formalism. The aggregation equilibrium and orientational ordering are treated self-consistently to analyze the concentration and temperature dependences of the elastic constants. Both a monomer--dimer model and a fully polydisperse rodlike aggregate model are considered. We find that aggregation selectively enhances the bend elastic constant through the long-tail structure of the aggregate-size distribution. As a result, a pronounced elastic anisotropy, $K_{33}\gg K_{11}>K_{22}$, emerges in the nematic phase. Decreasing temperature or increasing concentration promotes the formation of long rodlike aggregates and induces a rapid increase in the bend elastic constant, while the relation $K_{11}=3K_{22}$ remains unchanged. The exceptionally large bend elastic constants predicted here should be regarded as upper-bound estimates for the rigid-aggregate limit.

articles.title: Gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave source limited by thermal noise
articles.abstract: Josephson junctions are compact on-chip sources of coherent microwave and terahertz radiation, but conventional radiators couple the emission frequency, output power and dissipation through a single bias voltage. Here we demonstrate a gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave radiator based on a graphene weak link integrated with a separately gated graphene shunt resistor. The bias voltage sets the Josephson frequency, while the local gates tune the Josephson current and the total device resistance, enabling electrostatic control of emitted power at a chosen frequency. The device resolves Josephson harmonics up to fourth order, and its radiation power scales with source current and impedance as expected from a lumped-element circuit model. We further show that the emission linewidth is quantitatively described by Johnson-Nyquist noise at the electron temperature. The linewidth therefore provides an on-chip thermometer under bias, with the resistance-dependent heating captured by a minimal heat-balance model based on Wiedemann-Franz diffusion and electron-phonon coupling.

articles.title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS$_2$ Transistors
articles.abstract: The origin of the apparent metal-insulator transition in two-dimensional electron systems remains debated. Using temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on industry-relevant MoS$_2$ monolayer FETs with amorphous HfO$_2$ dielectrics, we establish classical percolation as the underlying mechanism. We report two complementary signatures of disorder-driven conduction onset: a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse as a function of absolute gate voltage and a vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density $n_{\mathrm{c}}$, identified as the percolation threshold. These findings identify dielectric-interface disorder, rather than channel quality alone, as the key parameter governing device turn-on. The extracted activation barriers reach values substantially exceeding room-temperature thermal energies, indicating that disorder-driven conduction onset remains relevant well beyond cryogenic transport.

articles.title: Hidden entropic order of emergent charges in a classical Ampère spin liquid
articles.abstract: Classical spin liquids are characterized by an extensive number of ground-state configurations. Coulomb spin liquids have, in this ground-state manifold, a divergence-free local constraint, which gives dipolar correlations and pinch points in the structure factor. Recently, models with a complementary ground-state constraint, defined by a zero-circulation constraint (Ampère's law), have been proposed. While classical Coulomb spin liquids forbid emergent charges, their Ampère counterparts leave the charges unconstrained. Here we study an Ising Ampère model on the octochlore lattice. The ground states obey a Gauss law for an antisymmetric rank-two field, i.e., three coupled two-dimensional Gauss laws, which are expected to produce pinch points in the structure factor. Nevertheless, maximal charges, vertices with all six arrows in or out, spontaneously accumulate on one of the two sublattices of the cubic lattice, with disordered signs. This order has a purely entropic origin; it washes out the pinch-point singularities at large scales, produces no magnetic Bragg peaks, and coexists with an extensive entropy. The system enters into this sublattice long-range ordered state through a continuous transition in what seems to be the three-dimensional Ising universality class. Moreover, the state has no magnetic order; it is even under time reversal: it is a hidden, entropic order within the Ampère manifold. Thus, a system whose Gauss law would predict an algebraic spin liquid becomes, through a non-magnetic ordering transition, a partially ordered short-range spin liquid. Our study is based on a combination of the constraint-vector theory, exact bounds and enumeration, and Monte Carlo, Wang-Landau, and parallel-tempering simulations.

articles.title: How Rich is the Rich-Club? Super Rich-Club Organization in Complex Networks
articles.abstract: The rich-club coefficient is used in complex networks to quantify the tendency of progressively higher-degree nodes to be more densely connected than expected by chance. However, it does not capture whether high degree nodes towards the core are actually more interconnected than the original network. Here, we jointly analyze the rich-club coefficient and an enrichment coefficient, which quantifies whether the internal average degree of progressively higher-degree subgraphs is greater than that of the original network, despite the decreasing number of nodes. We apply this framework to real and synthetic networks. Our results reveal three distinct regimes of core organization: rich-club organization without enrichment, enrichment without rich-club organization, and a combination of both, which we call Super Rich-Club organization. In the latter regime, high-degree nodes form cohesive and unusually dense cores that support efficient communication. Our results show that characterizing core organization across structural scales requires considering both relative density and internal connectivity, revealing a stronger form of core organization in real systems with implications for network structure, spectral properties that govern dynamical processes, and communicability.

articles.title: Hydrogen sublattice in LaH$_{12}$: structural stability and possible ordering motifs
articles.abstract: Lanthanum polyhydrides, synthesized under extreme pressure, exhibit near-room-temperature superconductivity. Finding a precise arrangement of the hydrogen sublattice that is critical for understanding the strong electron-phonon coupling remains experimentally unresolved due to the small X-ray scattering form factor of hydrogen atoms. In this work, we attempt to computationally reconstruct hydrogen sublattices of the LaH$_{12}$ at 100-200 GPa combining unconstrained evolutionary searches and structure generation with fixed lanthanum sublattice. By implementing a similarity metric, we screen the computationally generated configurations against experimental powder X-ray diffraction data. We specifically identify the trigonal $R\bar{3}$-LaH$_{12}$ and pseudo-hexagonal $C222_1$-La$_2$H$_{24}$ phases, which demonstrate close agreement with the experimental X-ray diffraction data. First-principles calculations confirm the metallic and superconducting nature of these hydrides. Crucially, our lattice dynamics analysis using the stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation (SSCHA) indicates that these structures are dynamically stable. We reveal the presence of molecular H$_2$ units and soft phonon modes in the trigonal LaH$_{12}$ that suppresses superconductivity ($T_c \ge 30$ K), while the hydrogen clathrate network in the $C222_1$ phase drives strong electron-phonon interactions, yielding the coupling parameters of $λ\approx 1.83$, $ω_{\log} \approx 87.5$ meV and transition temperature of $T_c\approx 150$ K at 150 GPa.

articles.title: Hyperbolic Nanocavities for Single-Molecule Vibrational Strong Coupling
articles.abstract: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in low-loss anisotropic materials such as hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) provide extreme sub-diffractional field confinement in the mid-infrared, making them attractive for enhancing the interaction of light with molecular vibrations. Collective vibrational strong coupling between molecular ensembles and HPhPs has already been demonstrated in extended slabs. Reaching this regime with a single molecule, however, remains a major challenge, and would provide a platform for investigating how vacuum electromagnetic fields influence molecular dynamics and chemical reactivity. Here, we show theoretically that single-molecule vibrational strong coupling can be reached in hBN nanocavities that laterally confine HPhPs within a finite volume. Combining full-wave electromagnetic simulations with the few-mode quantization approach, we find that these nanocavities support a rich set of asymmetric resonances that strongly enhance the local spectral density, with frequencies that follow from simple HPhP ray trajectories and can be tuned through the cavity aspect ratio. We identify resonances with quality factors of about $600$ and effective mode volumes of $|V_{\mathrm{eff}}| \sim 10^{-7}λ^{3}$, sufficient for single-molecule strong coupling with vibrational transitions with dipole moments on the order of $1\,\mathrm{D}$. These results establish hyperbolic nanocavities as a promising platform for single-molecule vibrational strong coupling and open new routes toward the local control of vibrational dynamics and molecular energy flow.

articles.title: Interplay between Spin Stripes and Pairing Crossover in the Bilayer Hubbard Model
articles.abstract: Whether $d$-wave or $s_\pm$-wave pairing prevails in the bilayer nickelate \ce{La3Ni2O7} remains unresolved, and how its observed spin order and magnetic excitations relate to the pairing mechanism is unclear. Here, we use finite-temperature determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a minimal bilayer Hubbard model to investigate pairing competition at strong interlayer coupling, where intralayer and interlayer antiferromagnetic correlations have comparable strengths. We find that spin stripes develop spontaneously with increasing hole doping, accompanied by a crossover of the dominant pairing symmetry from $d$-wave to $s_\pm$-wave. The crossover tracks the changing relative strengths of the spin correlations, with the interlayer correlations overtaking their intralayer counterparts in magnitude. Concomitantly, the dynamical spin structure factor exhibits a momentum-dependent reorganization of the magnetic excitations, consistent with fluctuating spin stripes. Our results identify the structure of spin fluctuations as a key link between spin stripes and pairing competition, offering a minimal-model perspective for understanding \ce{La3Ni2O7}.

articles.title: Kardar--Parisi--Zhang density hydrodynamics in a coherent XXZ--ASEP Lindbladian
articles.abstract: Coherent interactions can generate quantum correlations without changing a stationary density current. Whether that current still determines long-wavelength transport is a dynamical question. We study an XXZ chain with asymmetric Lindblad hopping, whose stationary current has the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) form although its populations do not evolve autonomously. The current curvature and static susceptibility fix the leading Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) length and amplitude without a fitted length or amplitude conversion factor. The density-visible Liouvillian spectrum, real-space spreading, and Fourier relaxation support KPZ scaling at the finite coherent couplings studied. Central and intermediate stationary density correlations are consistent with the Prähofer--Spohn profile at this microscopic scale, with resolved finite-time corrections. Reservoir-matched classical references quantify boundary effects, while symmetric hopping recovers diffusion and reduced asymmetry produces the expected crossover. These results connect an exact nonlinear current to the observed long-wavelength KPZ transport of the physical density in an interacting open quantum chain away from the isotropic Heisenberg point.

articles.title: Marginal Operator Deformations and Pseudocriticality in Baxter--Wu Models
articles.abstract: Weak first-order transitions can exhibit extended pseudocritical scaling regimes that mimic genuine criticality. We show that the long-debated apparent criticality of the dilute Baxter--Wu model arises from a marginally relevant renormalization-group flow, which ultimately drives the system into a first-order regime with phase coexistence. By integrating conformal perturbation theory with symmetry-resolved tensor-network level spectroscopy, we parameterize a slowly running coupling in a numerically accessible form and construct a generic flow-based diagnostic. The renormalization-group trajectories of the dilute and self-dual Baxter--Wu models under marginal operator deformations collapse onto the multicritical phase diagram of the dilute four-state Potts model, exposing the flow structure on both the marginally relevant and irrelevant sides of the Potts point.

articles.title: Mutual linearity in semi-Markov networks
articles.abstract: Despite their microscopic complexity, stochastic networks show a surprising degree of universal, parameter-independent properties. One example is mutual linearity, which has recently been characterized as a generic, pairwise-linear relation between observables of Markov processes under local perturbations, valid for both stationary dynamics and for transient dynamics in Laplace space. Here we show that mutual linearity arises if a certain global affine relation is satisfied. This allows us to demonstrate that mutual linearity also holds for a broad class of local perturbations in semi-Markov networks, which, unlike Markov networks, have memory in terms of the dwell time in the current state. However, exceptions exist, meaning that mutual linearity does not extend to all possible perturbations of semi-Markov networks. Strikingly, this restriction disappears for first-passage times. Thus, semi-Markov networks exhibit a fundamental asymmetry between occupation and first-passage statistics, different from Markov networks. Finally, we show that our results are directly applicable to stochastic resetting in semi-Markov networks, where the Laplace-space relations acquire a physical interpretation in terms of stationary occupations and the probability to reach a target before reset. This provides a natural setting in which the predicted affine relations can be probed.

articles.title: Odd Capillarity
articles.abstract: Capillarity governs interfacial relaxation and hydrodynamic motion in binary fluids through parity-even mechanical stresses. Here, we introduce \emph{odd capillarity}, a parity-breaking interfacial mechanical response, by incorporating a symmetric, nonvariational, parity-odd capillary stress into the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes (CHNS) equations. This stress generates forces along interfaces, transverse to ordinary capillary forces, and performs mechanical work that is not balanced by changes in the composition free energy. Direct numerical simulations reveal that odd capillarity arrests domain coarsening while sustaining turbulent fluid motion without a conventional inertial energy cascade, as energy injection is predominantly balanced by viscous dissipation. In asymmetric mixtures, odd capillarity driven deformation and breakup interrupt droplet growth, producing dynamically arrested emulsions with composition hyperuniformity and suppressed large-scale vorticity fluctuations. These findings establish odd capillarity as a distinct interfacial mechanism for controlling phase separation and sustaining nonequilibrium fluid motion.

articles.title: Photonic and Electronic Interaction of TMD-Hybridized ZnO Nanowire Lasers
articles.abstract: Semiconductor nanowire lasers are promising on-chip coherent light sources for photonic integrated circuits, but integration inevitably places them in contact with other materials, thereby changing their properties upon hybridization. In this study, we examine the photonic and electronic coupling between single ZnO nanowire lasers and TMDs. Using deterministic nanomanipulation, we first hybridized the same nanowire first with a WS$_2$ monolayer and then with a MoS$_2$ monolayer. The respective lasing threshold rises, the emission is strongly quenched at high pump power densities, and the mode envelope blueshifts. Upon hybridization with bilayer, trilayer, and bulk MoS$_2$, lasing is fully suppressed. Finite-Difference Eigenmode simulations show that the TMD absorbs part of the evanescent field. Because this absorption is wavelength dependent, it also removes modes from the low-energy flank of the envelope, which accounts for small difference between the two monolayers, while the blueshift itself follows the increase of the carrier density at threshold. Density functional theory calculations that include the interface dipole predict a type-I alignment at the ideal ZnO(10$\bar{1}$0)/TMD interface, which turns into type~II for a moderately reduced dipole, as expected for hydroxylated facets in air. In both cases, holes are transferred from the nanowire into the TMD and removed from the gain medium. Evanescent absorption and hole transfer thus jointly suppress lasing, and both must be accounted for when integrating nanowire lasers with 2D materials.

articles.title: Predictions of superconducting properties from chemical bonding interactions
articles.abstract: The need for rapid estimates of superconducting critical temperatures, Tc s, is becoming increasingly urgent as first-principles and artificial intelligence based methods enable the exploration of ever-larger and more chemically complex materials spaces. In this context, chemical bonding based quantities have emerged as promising descriptors for predicting superconductivity. To date, these approaches have mainly been developed for hydride superconductors, notably through the networking value, a descriptor based upon the electron localization function, whose topological properties have been found to correlate with Tc . In this perspective, we review and consolidate the method's theory, and we discuss how the estimate of the Tc is achievable within a real-space view. We conclude by proposing a framework that enables Tc prediction for the broad family of conventional superconductors from easily computable intermediate physical quantities.

articles.title: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
articles.abstract: We propose a Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. The exponential damping and oscillations when approaching thermal equilibrium can be understood as the analogs of quasi-normal mode (QNM) frequencies of black hole perturbations within the framework of holography. Holographic intuitions and some general properties of thermal Green's functions motivate the existence of such a TBA formulation, as well as lead to the imposition of a nonstandard analytical structure on the QNM TBA, while comparison with integrable form-factor expansions fixes the remaining ingredients. We conjecture the QNM TBA to be equivalent to performing an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded 2-point correlation functions. We compare the predictions with tensor network simulations of the E8 deformation of Ising CFT at nonzero temperature. We conjecture that the QNM TBA framework should also be applicable for describing out-of-equilibrium approach to Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD).

articles.title: Rotated-Frame Determinant Discovery for Ground- and Excited-State Quantum Selected Configuration Interaction
articles.abstract: Quantum Selected Configuration Interaction (QSCI) constructs a variational determinant space from measurements of a prepared electronic state, but finite-shot sampling can repeatedly observe high-probability determinants, limiting efficient discovery of configurations important for an accurate selected-CI description. We introduce rotate--sample--unrotate (RSU) determinant discovery, in which the same state is sampled in complementary orbital frames and the observed rotated determinants generate a finite set of candidates in the canonical basis. The Hamiltonian is then diagonalized in an orthonormal selected-CI space without enumerating the full determinant space. State-targeted orbital frames are constructed from an initial selected-CI wavefunction and its external residual. For excited states, we combine RSU with the generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) to prepare target-specific sampling states. Candidate GQE circuits are evaluated by classical selected-CI diagonalization in finite sampled spaces, so the quantum procedure requires only state preparation and determinant sampling. For N$_2$, exact-state controls isolate the determinant-discovery effect: at the stretched geometry, residual-natural-orbital RSU reaches chemical accuracy with 5,000 shots, compared with 20,000 shots for conventional QSCI. The improvement persists with approximate GQE-prepared states and is also observed for target excited states. These results demonstrate improved finite-shot determinant discovery in QSCI for both ground and excited states.

articles.title: Simulating a chiral gauge theory
articles.abstract: Chiral gauge theories underlie the Standard Model, yet none has been simulated nonperturbatively. Lattice constructions that evade the Nielsen-Ninomiya obstruction entail complex fermion measures or infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces. Here we provide a gauge-invariant Hamiltonian lattice regularization of 1+1-dimensional abelian chiral gauge theories built from clock-and-shift qudits with $\mathbb{Z}_N$ gauge fields, in which the global chiral symmetry and its 't Hooft anomaly survive exactly mod $N$. Anomaly cancellation on the lattice lets the Gauss laws be imposed and solved exactly, reducing the theory to an unconstrained qudit chain. Using infinite matrix product states, we simulate the canonical 1+1-dimensional chiral gauge theory, the 34-50 model, and find excellent agreement with analytic predictions, showing that a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space at $N=6$ reproduces the expected infrared physics of the continuum 34-50 model. This provides an efficient and practical solution to the problem of simulating general abelian chiral gauge theories in 1+1 dimensions, both on classical and quantum computers.

articles.title: Spatial Cost of Recovering a Fusion Qubit in a Critical Spin Chain
articles.abstract: Vanishing-error recovery of a fusion qubit from a fixed-sector ground doublet of four Kramers--Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain requires at least the shorter three-defect span of physical spins to leading order. Across arbitrary preselected spin sets and unrestricted joint decoding, this bound holds when the thermodynamic limit precedes large spacings at fixed positive ratios. An exact interval decoder attains it. Collective records of both logical axes in the complement force successful near-minimal supports to concentrate in density on a leading-order shortest interval.

articles.title: Spin Simulators based on Exciton-Polariton Waveguide Networks
articles.abstract: Many NP-hard optimization problems can be mapped onto interacting spin systems, whose ground state encodes the optimal solution. Polaritonic implementations based on gain-dissipative dynamics have recently emerged as promising analog computing platforms owing to their intrinsic parallelism and ultrafast operation. However, existing approaches are hindered by two fundamental limitations: maintaining the homogeneous amplitudes required for faithful problem encoding remains challenging in realistic physical systems, and most architectures are restricted to nearest-neighbour interactions, severely limiting the variety of optimization problems that can be efficiently addressed. We introduce a feasible polaritonic XY simulator based on a reconfigurable waveguide platform that overcomes both limitations. Our approach guarantees amplitude homogeneity while enabling the implementa- tion of arbitrary symmetric coupling matrices, thereby allowing the direct encoding of a wide variety of XY Hamiltonians. These results establish a practical architecture for programmable polaritonic spin simulators and pave the way towards scalable optical hardware for analog optimisation.

articles.title: Spin swapping mediated by spin-orbital textures in centrosymmetric multiorbital materials
articles.abstract: Spin swapping converts a primary spin current into a secondary one by interchanging its flow and spin-polarization directions, attributed to spin-orbit scattering or spin-band splitting. Here we uncover a fundamentally distinct route to spin swapping arising from the orbital degree of freedom in the spin pumping to centrosymmetric multiorbital materials \textit{without spin-band splitting}. When the dynamical proximity ferromagnet injects a longitudinal spin current flowing normal to the interface, spin-orbit-entangled orbital textures redirect the injected spins into longitudinal and transverse orbital currents. Their subsequent conversion back to the spin sector generates transverse spin currents with propagation and polarization directions swapped relative to the primary spin current. The swapping efficiency achieves $50\%$ for Ge and Si. Governed by a fourth-rank tensor constrained by crystalline symmetry and without requiring spin-orbit scattering or inversion symmetry breaking, our finding reveals spin-orbital textures as hidden intermediate channels of spin swapping with unexplored material choices and functionalities.

articles.title: Stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter
articles.abstract: In quantum many-body physics and quantum field theory, it is often assumed that gapped systems remain gapped under sufficiently weak local perturbations. However, to what extent this assumption holds is elusive, except for some special systems. In this work, we examine the stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter that is only subject to two physically natural conditions, locality and translation invariance. We first show that in any spatial dimension, there are gapped local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap, i.e., they become gapless under certain arbitrarily weak local perturbation in the thermodynamic limit. We then prove that for both spin and fermionic systems in one dimension, such Hamiltonians with an unstable gap must not only break translation invariance but also be fine-tuned. We further show that in any dimension greater than one, there are fine-tuned local translation invariant Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap. These results greatly sharpen our understanding of the fundamental problem of the stability of quantum phases of matter. We also discuss implications of our results on, for example, anyon superconductivity and higher-form symmetries.

articles.title: Statistical mechanics and hierarchy of learnability in quantum codes: From generalized symmetries to non-Abelian topological orders
articles.abstract: Local weak measurements provide noisy information about observables encoded in a quantum code. We formulate the corresponding Bayesian inference problem for a broad class of topological stabilizer codes by mapping it to classical spin models with generalized symmetries. When the wavefunction deformation and Gaussian measurement strengths coincide, the replicated model acquires an enlarged symmetry. We use this symmetry to derive exact identities among correlators averaged over measurement records that quantify the learnability of nonlocal observables associated with fractionalized excitations. Together with correlation inequalities in the associated clean ferromagnetic models, these identities establish hierarchies of learnability: if two observables remain learnable at long distances, their product must also remain learnable. We demonstrate these relations in the rank-2 toric code and the X-cube model, whose classical descriptions exhibit modulated and subsystem symmetries, respectively. We further extend the analysis to finite group quantum double models, including non-Abelian ones. We derive exact relations between learnability and correlations in the corresponding classical models, and show that the representation structure and fusion rules of anyons impose further constraints under suitable positivity conditions. These results constrain which types of nonlocal information can be learned simultaneously, providing a guide to learning phase diagrams in quantum codes under local weak measurements.

articles.title: Steady states in asymmetric exclusion processes with reactions: Fluctuations and non-mean field behaviour
articles.abstract: We study an totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) in an open geometry. We couple TASEP with simple reactions in the form of production (birth) and degradation (death) due to over crowding taking place in the bulk. We investigate the steady states, which are generically space-dependent. Phase coexistences are also possible for some choices of the model parameters. We study the system by mean-field theories (MFT) supplemented by extensive Monte-Carlo simulations (MCS). Intriguingly, unlike oridinary TASEP and other related models, configuration-dependent bulk reactions in a TASEP model can make nearest-neighbour correlations quantitatively important even in an open driven system where mean-field theory would ordinarily be expected to provide a useful description. We attribute this to the correlation effects ignored in MFT. We numerically quantify this correlation effect.

articles.title: Symmetry-Selective Shift Current in Polar Multidomain Superlattices
articles.abstract: Periodic polar multidomain superlattices can act as symmetry-selective elements for shift-current generation. We demonstrate this using a two-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with prescribed multidomain configurations. The distinct full-supercell symmetries of periodic head-to-head and head-to-tail arrangements impose different constraints on the shift-current tensor and thereby select complementary nonlinear-response channels, as confirmed by numerical calculations. A direct comparison with equal-area averages of the constituent single-domain spectra shows that an independent-domain average does not reproduce the detailed multidomain spectra. A bond-resolved contribution analysis further clarifies the real-space origin of the multidomain response. Widening each domain from one to ten primitive cells leaves the selection rules intact. On the photon-energy grid used here, the allowed head-to-tail response changes sign and grows by about an order of magnitude. These results provide a theoretical framework for the symmetry-based design of anisotropic optical rectification in polar multidomain superlattices.

articles.title: The quantized Hall effect knows which way the current flows: mirror covariance and rectification in a laterally asymmetric Hall bar
articles.abstract: The quantized Hall effect is the textbook emblem of universality: a resistance fixed by $h/e^2$, apparently indifferent to the shape of the sample, to its edges and to the direction of the current. That indifference is only half true. The plateau value is universal; the plateau is not. In a gate-defined Hall bar with one hard and one soft edge, reversing the current moves the plateau edge, and exchanging the edges reverses the move. We identify the symmetry that forces this. Because a perpendicular field breaks time reversal, the relevant operation is the in-plane $C_2$ rotation; within the self-consistent screening model it gives the covariance relation $R_α[B,V_{\mathrm{conf}}(x),I]=R_α[B,V_{\mathrm{conf}}(-x),-I]$, exact deep in the nonlinear regime and independent of linear response or microscopic reversibility. It predicts a rectification that is odd under exchange of the gate voltages and reverses with the magnetic field. The field-reversal test leaves the frozen lateral disorder untouched, so it holds for a single sample; it has not yet been performed. A further measurement, collapsing one incompressible strip, discriminates between co-directed and chiral pictures of the current. Self-consistent calculations show the soft-edge strip widening from 69 to 106\,nm on current reversal, moving the Hall resistance from 0.940 to $0.999994\,h/2e^2$ within a bounded window in magnetic field. The effect is a gate-tunable vector-product nonreciprocity, not magnetochiral anisotropy.

articles.title: Thermodynamic signatures of the period-doubling route to chemical chaos
articles.abstract: Chemical reaction networks can evolve from stable oscillations to chaos through successive period doublings. We investigate general properties of entropy-production fluctuations near the onset of chaos and within the chaotic regime in reversible, well-mixed reaction networks. Near an isolated supercritical period-doubling bifurcation, we find a one-sided divergence of the diffusion constant with exponent one. For chaotic attractors satisfying the stated conditions, the entropy variance per unit volume grows exponentially when the macroscopic limit is taken first. Its exponential growth rate is $2λ_{\max}$, where $λ_{\max}$ is the largest Lyapunov exponent, implying a divergent diffusion constant. We also discuss the volume dependence of the fluctuations and the underlying physical mechanisms.

articles.title: Variational Monte Carlo Study of Superconductivity in a Correlated System with Broken Inversion Symmetry
articles.abstract: Unconventional superconductivity in systems with broken inversion symmetry has attracted considerable interest because antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling (ASOC) can strongly affect the spin structure and stability of superconducting states. In this study, we investigate superconductivity in a correlated system with the symmetry of a honeycomb network using the variational Monte Carlo method. We consider a single-band Hubbard model including an on-site Coulomb interaction $U$ and ASOC with coupling strength $λ$, and compare several pairing states with different pairing symmetries. The trial wave functions are constructed from particle-number- and Gutzwiller-projected BCS states. To examine the energetic stability of each pairing state, we calculate the variational energy as a function of the gap amplitude, while optimizing the variational parameter $μ$ and the Gutzwiller parameter $g$ for each gap amplitude. At $U/t = 10$, the $f$-wave state has the lowest variational energy for $λ/t = 0$, whereas the chiral $p$-wave state becomes the most energetically favorable for $λ/t = 0.1$. These results indicate that ASOC strongly affects the competition among superconducting pairing states in the presence of strong electron correlations.

articles.title: All reweighted paths lead to Rome: Unification of reweighting schemes for stratified path sampling
articles.abstract: Path sampling-based stratification algorithms such as Transition Interface Sampling (TIS) enable the evaluation of kinetic rate constants and mechanisms of complex molecular rare event transitions. By sampling only short dynamical trajectories, TIS allows constructing an estimate of the unbiased dynamics by reweighting the interface path ensembles. In the past decades several methods have been developed and applied to achieve such path reweighting, based on statistically optimal use of the trajectory data. Why and how this reweighting exactly works has been underexplored up to now. Here we discuss several different schemes to compute the reweighted path ensemble (RPE), notably point-wise matching, Weighted Histogram Analysis Method (WHAM), Multistate Bennett Acceptance Ratio (MBAR), variance based reweighting (VBR) and survival analysis reweighting (SAR). We show that except for the point-wise matching the other methods are leading to the same outcome, and in fact can be seen as identical. Moreover, the SAR links to a well-established nonparametric maximum-likelihood estimator of product-limit form. This allows a synthesis of all path reweighting schemes, identifying the common underlying nature. All schemes follow from this common origin. We illustrate the reweighting with some simple examples, and show that care has to be taken when applying WHAM, if the number of interfaces and histogram bins do not match.

articles.title: Brueckner Orbitals in Local Pair Natural Orbital Coupled-Cluster Theory: DLPNO-BCCD(T) and DLPNO-BCCD(T)_Lambda2
articles.abstract: In this work, we implement closed-shell Brueckner orbitals for the efficient domain-based local pair natural orbital DLPNO-CCSD(T) and DLPNO-CCSD(T)$_Λ$ methods of the free and open-source \textsc{Psi4} package. We introduce a new algorithm that allows Brueckner orbitals to be computed within the DLPNO framework, resulting in the novel DLPNO-BCCD(T) and DLPNO-BCCD(T)$_{Λ_2}$ methods. We show that DLPNO-BCCD(T) approximates its canonical BCCD(T) counterpart with significantly lower errors relative to the errors incurred by DLPNO-CCSD(T) over CCSD(T). Through a test on the S22 set of noncovalent dimers, the peak error across the set is reduced from 0.36 kcal mol$^{-1}$ to 0.25 kcal mol$^{-1}$ using normal cutoffs, and 0.28 kcal mol$^{-1}$ to 0.13 kcal mol$^{-1}$ at tight cutoffs. In addition, we show that BCCD(T)$_{Λ_2}$, a ${Λ_2}$-only implementation of Brueckner orbitals for the asymmetric triples method, generally produces the best agreement with CCSDT, compared to the (T), (T)$_Λ$, and B(T) perturbative triples corrections. This is established through benchmarks on thermochemistry tests on the barrier heights of semibullvalene and bullvalene Cope rearrangement, while the robustness of DLPNO-BCCD(T)$_{Λ_2}$ is demonstrated along bond-breaking potential energy curves, where it matches the orbital-optimized quasi-variational asymmetric renormalized-triples OQVCCDAR(T) method closely for single-bond breaking, and approximates DLPNO-CCSDT respectably even when triple bonds are stretched, at a fraction of the computational cost.

articles.title: Colloidal 2D WS2 nanosheets exhibiting high-purity single photon emission
articles.abstract: The search for quantum emitters, delivering single photons "on demand" at cryogenic and elevated temperatures for photonic technologies is ever progressing. For example, micrometer-sized WS2 monolayers exhibit single photon emission by elaborated local defect or strain engineering. Here, we show that wet-chemically synthesised monolayered two-dimensional (2D) WS2 nano sheets (NSs) with lateral sizes of 14 (+/- 6 nm) readily emit single photons from exciton recombination without the need for substrate-induced patterning, strain/defect engineering or spectral filtering. Single particle spectroscopy of 70 individual NSs shows photoluminescence from excitons (2.02 eV), trios (1.94 eV) and defect-localized states (1.85 eV) with fast emission (t1<0.2 ns, t2=3.2 ns), allowing highly frequent excitation cycles. Pulsed at 80 MHz, colloidal WS2 NSs exhibit limited spectral diffusion, no blinking and distinct photon antibunching (g2(0)=0.07 at 5 K), thereby tackling challenges of established colloidal quantum dot systems (blinking, longer emission cycles), while retaining high single photon purity as key quality of deterministic quantum emitters.

articles.title: Effective Harmonic and Anharmonic Models for Vibronic Spectra
articles.abstract: Vibrationally resolved spectra of medium-sized molecules contain dense progressions, weak borrowed-intensity bands and large-amplitude structural motions. Their interpretation requires state-to-state assignments together with a complete spectral envelope, while a fully anharmonic treatment of every normal coordinate is usually impractical. We introduce a general workflow that builds both outputs from automatically generated nonredundant internal coordinates and a common transition-operator representation. The harmonic level combines time-independent (TI) assignments with time-dependent (TD) thermal correlations and an explicit omitted-strength bound for the positive harmonic dipole sum. A discrete-variable representation (DVR) promotes selected flexible coordinates while the remaining modes are contracted analytically. Perturbative and variational nuclear states extend the same operator treatment to separate-state modes with Duschinsky mixing or to shared modes with residual quadratic couplings. The workflow recovers approximately 99% of the harmonic intensity for strongly reorganized medium-sized examples, reproduces measured absorption and fluorescence trends for anthracene and p-terphenyl, and gives signed electronic circular dichroism (ECD) profiles for camphor. Water photoionization, a diffuse-basis two-photon response tensor for the pyrazine $n\to3s$ Rydberg band, and nonplanar 4-pyrone calculations test continuum and anharmonic extensions. The result is a unified route from molecular structure to resolved assignments and numerically converged finite-model spectra.

articles.title: Exact periodic electrostatics for latent-charge machine-learning potentials
articles.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials of the latent Ewald summation (LES) type learn atomic charges from energies and forces and evaluate their electrostatic energy in reciprocal space. I formulate this long-range term as a smeared Epstein-Hurwitz lattice sum and derive its exact periodic structure: a decomposition isolating a net-charge artefact and a local self-energy, an image theorem for cells of any shape, and the forces and virial. Full charge equilibration, LES with induced charges, constrained and unconstrained LES models and fixed-charge force fields follow as successive approximations of one variational problem, whose diagonal-hardness limit is a projection of the latent charges onto fixed total charge, which I call projected latent Ewald summation (pLES). Energies and forces determine the latent charges only up to a gauge, so fragment-level rather than atom-level charge quantization is the consistent target. The latent channel is guaranteed to be a dielectric only if charge is conserved locally; charges that are local functions of the environment and conserved only globally can screen like a conductor. pLES is implemented in the atomic cluster expansion and in LAMMPS, and the exact identities hold to machine precision, also for trained models. For charged NaCl clusters, pLES recovers the total charge that an unconstrained model misses by up to 1.8 e and reduces the test errors of a short-range model from 1.44 to 0.42 meV/atom and from 37 to 13 meV/Å. In two water datasets, constrained and unconstrained models learn the same latent charges up to sign and scale. In molecular dynamics of pLES water, fluctuating molecular charges dominate the screening at all accessible wavelengths; a crossover model excludes a conductor and gives a latent dielectric constant between 19 and 71; molecular charges are compensated over about 1 nm, beyond the training cells.

articles.title: Exploiting floating point emulation in tensor contractions in relativistic coupled cluster theory
articles.abstract: In this manuscript we outline a computational strategy to leverage a vendor-optimized implementation of the Ozaki scheme I for floating point emulation as part of an implementation of the Transpose-Transpose-GEMM-Transpose (TTGT) pattern for tensor contractions, and assess its potential to accelerate two of the most expensive tensor contractions appearing in relativistic coupled cluster theory in high-end accelerators such as the NVIDIA Blackwell B200 system in which there is a strong differential in the performance of computations for double and lower precision datatypes. Our results indicate that this emulation-based TTGT strategy can provide significant speedups compared to runs without emulation, and can be competitive with state-of-the-art, vendor-optimized tensor contraction libraries using native double precision as compute datatype. More importantly, our scheme provides a path towards easily allowing users to tune the desired accuracy in the tensor contraction steps, including cases where precision between single and double is sufficient for the application.

articles.title: Machine Learning the Complete Active-Space Wavefunction Reconstruction
articles.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials enable multireference-quality reaction dynamics but do not retain the electronic structure underlying the predicted energies and forces. Recovering this information by independently performing complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) calculations is both expensive and potentially inconsistent. We introduce the Complete Active-Space Wave Function Reconstruction (CAS-WR) model, which learns the geometry-dependent electronic structure from CASSCF data and reconstructs the CAS wave function without repeated orbital optimization. Combined with uncertainty-based active learning, CAS-WR is demonstrated for the Diels--Alder reaction and \ce{TiC+}-catalyzed C--H activation. The approach enables trajectory-resolved analysis of multiconfigurational electronic structure across reactive ensembles. Preliminary applications to excited-state proton transfer and transition-metal photocatalysis suggest that CAS-WR can provide a general route toward recovering electronic structure along complex ground- and excited-state reactive dynamics.

articles.title: Open-shell Configuration State Functions as trial states for phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: The accurate description of open-shell states in molecular systems poses challenges for approximate electronic structure methods. One emerging approach is to variationally optimize the orbitals of a single user-selected Configuration State Function (CSF), i.e., a linear combination of Slater determinants that is constructed as an eigenstate of the total spin operator. In this work we explore the use of these orbital-optimized single CSFs as trial wavefunctions in phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (ph-AFQMC), a stochastic method that recovers electron correlation by evolving an initial state in imaginary time, subject to a constraint imposed by the trial state. We investigate the symmetric stretch of H-He-H, a series of small $p$-block compounds with diradicaloid singlet states, twisted ethene conformers, and a bimetallic iron-sulfur complex. We find that accurate energetics are obtained for states dominated by open-shell character, and that for certain atoms and diatomics the accuracy can be significantly improved when the trial is made to also preserve the relevant angular momentum symmetries. Furthermore, our study reveals that the open-shell CSF trial is suboptimal when the target electronic state reflects a significant mixture of ionic and covalent character, e.g., at shorter bond lengths in H-He-H and for the superexchange-stabilized ground state of [2Fe-2S]$^{2+}$. Our findings suggest that ph-AFQMC using CSF trial states is a promising method for many (but not all) strongly correlated molecular states, especially given its relatively low computational cost, and that it provides a reasonable non-perturbative way to recover some of the dynamic correlation that is otherwise missing in the CSF.

articles.title: SO3LR Tauri: Generally Applicable Force Fields for Reactive (Bio)Molecular Simulations Covering the Periodic Table
articles.abstract: Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) aim to create a unified model that describes all major classes of (bio)molecules at quantum-mechanical accuracy. We present SO3LR Tauri, a family of MLFFs developed toward this goal, coupling a fast SO3krates network to explicit, physics-based interaction modules: pair-specific short-range repulsion, environment-dependent dispersion, and electrostatics, each improved beyond its original formulation. The models are trained on 148 million structures spanning 85 elements, drawn from several quantum-chemical datasets. Against coupled-cluster references, the models accurately reproduce nucleobase-pair and charged protein-ligand interactions, carbohydrate conformer ordering, and molecular dipoles. They also resolve the transition pathways of organic and enzymatic reactions. Dynamical simulations recover experimental densities of water and organic solvents, the hydration structure of mono- and divalent ions, the pKa values of amino-acid side chains, and the structure and dynamics of proteins, membranes, nucleic acids, glycoproteins, and metal-containing biomolecules, all without system-specific fitting. Released in three sizes, the models reach 0.7-3.2 $μ$s/atom and scale to 27-84 million atoms on a single GPU. Much work remains to be done: achieving predictive accuracy for static and dynamic liquid properties, reaction barriers, coverage of chemical and conformational space, and the sampling and inference speed needed to describe biomolecular processes.

articles.title: Subtle Energy Corrections Reshape Condensed-Phase Property Predictions from a Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential
articles.abstract: Accurate reproduction of electronic-structure labels by machine-learning interatomic potentials does not necessarily ensure reliable condensed-phase properties. We investigate the effects of basis-set superposition error (BSSE) and an explicit Axilrod-Teller-Muto (ATM) three-body dispersion contribution on molecular-liquid predictions. Starting from MACELES-OFF, we fine-tune a baseline potential at the $ω$B97M-V/def2-TZVPD level. A separate branch learns counterpoise (CP) energy and force corrections with the baseline frozen, while a D4-parametrized ATM term is added during molecular-dynamics inference. Mean atom-normalized CP and ATM contributions are 0.222 and 0.205 meV/atom, respectively, for the analyzed SPICE2 configurations from OMol25. We compare baseline, CP-only, ATM-only, and CP + ATM variants for 39 organic liquids. Relative to baseline, the mean system-wise density changes are -1.17%, -10.38%, and -11.93% for CP-only, ATM-only, and CP + ATM, respectively; the corresponding enthalpy-of-vaporization changes are -2.79%, -14.74%, and -18.32%. For the 11 liquids with experimental self-diffusion data, the mean self-diffusion changes are +17.66%, +203.02%, and +230.36%. Both corrections thus lower density and enthalpy of vaporization while increasing molecular mobility on average. ATM dominates these changes, while CP provides a smaller contribution; their combination yields the largest average shifts. These results show that corrections with sub-meV/atom mean values on the analyzed configurations can substantially reshape the predicted structural, thermodynamic, and transport properties of molecular liquids.

articles.title: Sympathetic Cooling of Ionic Fullerenes with Ultracold Atoms to Millikelvin Temperatures
articles.abstract: Cooling complex molecular ions to millikelvin temperatures remains a major challenge because their intricate internal structures prevent laser cooling. Here, we propose to use an ultracold gas of Cd atoms to efficiently cool C$_{60}^+$ ions to average kinetic energies of approximately 20 mK, following an initial precooling stage with He buffer gas. Our approach is based on full molecular dynamics simulations using accurate ion-atom interaction potentials derived from high-level electronic structure methods. Furthermore, using a Monte Carlo approach, we predict the formation of C$_{60}^+$ Coulomb crystals supported solely by collisions with the buffer gas. The probability of reaching these cold states shows a pronounced dependence on the number of trapped ions, revealing the competition between neutral-atom cooling and many-ion dynamics in radio-frequency traps.

articles.title: Synchronization transitions in ensembles of active particles with distance-dependent higher-order interactions
articles.abstract: Higher-order interactions are ubiquitous in biological systems and can be used to better describe the ensemble dynamics of self-propelled particles. To this end, this article investigates a Vicsek-Kuramoto model with distance-dependent higher-order interactions and obtains analytical results, albeit under certain assumptions, that characterize its collective dynamics. Subsequently, these are validated through simulations of the system equations, demonstrating both continuous and explosive transitions between the asynchronous and synchronous collective states. Further numerical results also reveal that short-range interactions and tightly clustered initial states can lead to deviations from the theoretical predictions, whereas the latter can be offset by increasing the common self-propulsion velocity. These results offer insights into a broad class of active matter systems with higher-order interactions, and provide a framework for designing and utilizing them for specific applications.

articles.title: Thermodynamics-Informed Learning Captures Hierarchical Hydrogen-Bond Networks in Deep Eutectic Solvents
articles.abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) offer a tunable platform for lignocellulose refining, but their solvation behavior depends on multicomponent hydrogen-bond networks rather than individual constituent properties. We develop TiNN, a thermodynamics-informed neural network that hierarchically represents HBA-HBD association and solute accommodation through a learned free-energy pathway. Trained on 938 records, TiNN achieves a test-set $R^2$ of 0.917 and generalizes to new HBA-HBD combinations and sparse conditions. Ablation identifies solute-specific stabilization as the largest contributor to prediction accuracy, while the importance of hydrogen-bond compatibility depends on the dissolution mechanism. Experimental measurements of glucose, xylan, and Kraft lignin in acidic, basic, and neutral DESs show that TiNN reduces the geometric mean solubility error from more than 23-fold with COSMO-RS to approximately 1.5-fold. Without training on fractionation data, TiNN also distinguishes DES formulations with high and low lignin and hemicellulose removal from corn stover. These results support chemically grounded solvent screening for lignocellulose fractionation.

articles.title: Unraveling Primary Energy Conversion Dynamics in Intact Cells of Gemmatimonas groenlandica
articles.abstract: Photosynthetic bacteria have evolved specialized light-harvesting structures to efficiently capture sunlight. Here, we investigate the ultrafast dynamics in intact cells of Gemmatimonas groenlandica, featuring unique double-ring LHh-LH1 photosynthetic complexes containing bacteriochlorophyll a. Two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy with lock-in detection allows us to directly observe primary energy-conversion processes, from excitation-energy transfer within the antenna system to the formation of a charge-separated state in the reaction center, taking place on 50 ps time scale. Through comparison with Rhodospirillum rubrum, which lacks the outer antenna ring, we use a combination of global analysis and nodal/center line slope analyses to resolve LHh-LH1 excitation energy transfer which occurs on a ~1-2 ps timescale in Gemmatimonas groenlandica.

articles.title: When optimized geometries are not optimal: Implications for inverted singlet-triplet gap predictions
articles.abstract: Pseudo-Jahn-Teller distortions can substantially alter singlet-triplet gaps, potentially reversing the predicted excited-state ordering in molecules proposed to exhibit inverted singlet-triplet (INVEST) gaps. In this study, we benchmark geometry optimization methods for 13 azaphenalenes against CCSD(T)-quality reference geometries, assessing their ability to reproduce symmetry lowering and its consequences for singlet-triplet gaps. Among the methods examined, $ω$B97M-D4 reliably describes the distorted geometries and corresponding gaps, whereas the commonly used methods B3LYP and MP2 retain high-symmetry structures, potentially leading to false-positive INVEST assignments. We further assess $ω$B97M-D4 geometries across 337 molecules comprising azaphenalenes, boron/nitrogen-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and non-alternant hydrocarbons. Subsequent L-CC2/aug-cc-pVDZ calculations predict negative singlet-triplet gaps for 85 molecules and identify discrepancies with previously reported INVEST assignments. These findings demonstrate that the choice of geometry optimization method is crucial for reliable INVEST screening, particularly in systems susceptible to symmetry-breaking distortions.

articles.title: An All-Atom Model of the Resorcinol-Formaldehyde Aerogel Skeleton from DFT and Molecular Dynamics: Validation and Iron Incorporation
articles.abstract: Resorcinol-formaldehyde (RF) aerogels are lightweight, ultra-porous thermal superinsulators whose complex amorphous structure has not yet been described at the all-atom level. Here, we build an all-atom model of the RF aerogel skeleton by combining density functional theory (DFT) and classical molecular dynamics (MD), validate it against experimental infrared and density measurements, and use it to study the incorporation of iron dopants. The RF base unit was optimized with Gaussian, DMol$^{3}$ and SIESTA, and its calculated infrared spectrum agreed with experiment. Comparing classical force fields with DFT for branched systems of two to four base units (140-278 atoms) led to the choice of COMPASS II. A 15,012-atom system of 54 branched RF units, not cross-linked to each other, aggregated into a single cluster in the canonical (NVT) ensemble and reached an equilibrium density of 1.296 g.cm$^{-3}$ in the isobaric-isothermal (NPT) ensemble, in agreement with the experimental skeletal density (1.3 g.cm$^{-3}$). Then, 5 wt$\%$ iron (109 atoms) was added to the equilibrated structure: during 1 ns of NPT simulation, the fraction of iron atoms embedded in the skeleton rose from 63$\%$ to 71$\%$, and the Fe-C radial distribution function peaked at 3 Å. The model thus provides an experimentally supported starting point for screening fillers and dopants in RF gels, with prospective application to their thermoelectric functionalization, which we have previously demonstrated experimentally with basalt and PANOX fibres. Future extensions could address skeleton properties relevant to thermal insulation and the pyrolysis of RF gels into carbon and metal-doped carbon aerogels.

articles.title: Anomalous thermal transport in isotope-enriched germanium carbide
articles.abstract: Advances in modern electronics demand the dissipation of heat fluxes approaching 1000 W cm$^{-2}$, which drives an urgent need for materials with thermal conductivity ($κ$) exceeding 1000 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. Here, by solving the Boltzmann transport equation considering both three- and four-phonon interactions, we observe that isotopically pure cubic germanium carbide (GeC) exhibits a remarkable $κ$ of 1018 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, which is further corroborated by state-of-the-art machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations. Two unique mechanisms underlie this anomalously high $κ$: a remarkably strong isotopic enhancement effect (289%) and a surprisingly modest suppression due to four-phonon scattering (22%)-despite the presence of a wide acoustic-optical phonon gap. Moreover, we find that GeC defies the conventional Leibfried-Schlomann formula and exhibits a non-monotonic variation of $κ$ with external hydrostatic pressure at elevated temperatures. Our findings establish isotope-enriched GeC as a material of ultrahigh $κ$ and an ideal platform for exploring exotic phonon physics.

articles.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. Spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations show that this Si layer opens new channels for phonon transport across the interface. The engineered interface raises the interfacial thermal conductance to 165 MW m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$ -- the highest value yet reported for $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC interfaces. These results offer an effective way to manage heat in $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ devices and point to a general approach for building phonon-bridging interfaces that improve heat dissipation in heterogeneous systems.

articles.title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
articles.abstract: We analyze the unusual microstructure resulting from the cubic to orthorhombic phase transformation in the shape-memory alloy ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$. This seems to represent an approximate experimental realization of a deformation having a finite number of incompatible deformation gradients, which has been known to exist only as a theoretical possibility. Because the middle eigenvalue $γ$ of the transformation strain is very close to 1, the phase transformation in this alloy takes place via nucleation of exact austenite-martensite interfaces rather than, as usual for other alloys, by classical austenite-martensite interfaces separating the austenite from a finely-twinned laminate of martensite. According to the moving mask approximation of Della Porta this leads to the question whether a microstructure can be formed from the set $H$ of the twelve matrices ${\mathbf V}_i$ on the martensite energy wells that are rank-one connected to the identity, even though these matrices are mutually incompatible. We show that when $γ=1$ and the transformation is volume preserving, such a microstructure is possible that does not deform the grain boundary. This is a consequence of $H$ forming a degenerate $T_{12}$ configuration in the sense of Kirchheim. In fact there are such microstructures supported on just 8 of the 12 matrices in $H$. However there is no deformation satisfying the same boundary condition whose gradient belongs to $H$ almost everywhere. An additional prediction, confirmed experimentally, is that the macroscopic deformation gradient equals the identity everywhere. We also analyse the approximate compatibility of the ${\mathbf V}_i$. Although mutually incompatible, they are nearly compatible, with some pairs much more nearly compatible than others, these pairs corresponding to interfaces that are more frequently observed.

articles.title: Core Reactivity in Cs-Ba-O ternary system under pressure
articles.abstract: High pressure can activate Cs $5p$ core electrons for covalent bonding. In this study, we investigate the Cs-Ba-O system at 150 and 250 GPa using first-principles structure searches. CsBa$_3$O$_8$ and CsBaO$_4$ both lie on the static-lattice convex hull at 250~GPa and exhibit mild Cs $5p$-O $2p$ bonding while retaining O$_2$ units with intermediate superoxide-peroxide character. Cs$_2$BaO$_3$ shows substantially stronger bonding but remains metastable with respect to CsO and BaO. A 1:1 Cs$_2$O-BaO$_2$ mixture provides a solid starting composition for investigating this chemistry, with core-reactive CsO among the predicted products at 250~GPa. Calculated Cs $L_3$-edge x-ray absorption near-edge spectra and powder diffraction patterns provide electronic and structural signatures to guide identification of the predicted phases in diamond anvil cell experiments.

articles.title: Evolutionary Design of Interpretable Spatial Descriptors for Structure-Property Relationship Discovery
articles.abstract: Structure property prediction is a classical task in machine learning, ranging from molecular activity and materials properties to local functional responses measured in microscopy. For image-based regression, two choices define the information available to the predictor: the size of the image neighborhood and the spatial resolution retained within it. A small neighborhood can omit relevant surrounding structure, whereas a large, finely sampled neighborhood can introduce redundant or irrelevant information. Here, we develop a framework for constructing spatial descriptors for prediction of local spectra and hysteresis loops. We benchmark regression models, use SHAP maps to examine their spatial attribution, and explore the effect of the patch size and compression to establish the relationship between predictive accuracy and descriptor dimensionality. We then use a genetic algorithm to optimize spatial partitions and the assignment of mean, minimum, and maximum pooling operations. Each retained region contributes an explicit measurement of the image, allowing the search to balance prediction error against the number of descriptor values. Cartesian and polar constructions provide complementary ways to organize this information. The resulting descriptors make it possible to examine where spatial detail is needed, where regional summaries are sufficient, and how these choices depend on the predictor and the measured response. The same approach can be used for molecules and solids once the genetic algorithm rules for these are established.

articles.title: Explicit pore pre-conditioning and inverse design of amorphous nanoporous carbon
articles.abstract: Porous carbons store energy, capture gases and purify water, and their performance depends strongly on the geometry of their pores. Atomistic models mostly simulate their synthesis by molecular dynamics, with results that depend on the interatomic potential, and return the pore network as an output rather than as a specification. Here we show that the pore network can be an input: pores drawn from a target size distribution fill a prescribed volume fraction, carbon is grown around them by stochastic ring placement, and a particle swarm recovers the construction parameters from a structural fingerprint. The search reproduces the density, surface area and pore volume of a carbon produced by quenched molecular dynamics within about 5 %, together with its pore size distribution. As a stress test, it also recovers a bimodal distribution, and the search history reveals which parameters the targets constrain and flags a failed search. A short anneal completes the network, recovering the coordination of the reference while the pore size distribution keeps its shape. Molecular dynamics still supplies the local chemistry, but the pore geometry becomes a design variable for a given application.

articles.title: Ferroelectricity and Peierls transition in MOI$_2$ (M=Ta, Nb): a first-principle analysis
articles.abstract: The van der Waals ferroelectric NbOI$_2$ hosts a polar distortion that is commonly attributed to the Peierls dimerization of its Nb chains. Here we show, using first-principles calculations and a Landau-type energy, that the polar instability is in fact a distinct order parameter that does not stem from the Peierls mode condensation and that three main distinct modes are important in the whole MOI$_2$ family. They are a polar mode $P$, an antipolar mode $\eta$, and a Peierls mode $\delta$, whose stabilities and couplings strongly depend on the nature of the $M$ metal element, as evidenced by the fact that the isostructural, TaOI$_2$ system is not polar while possessing Peirls distortions.

articles.title: First-principles study of the formation of Group-IV--vacancy color centers in diamond
articles.abstract: $XV$ ($X$ is Si, Ge, Sn, or Pb, and $V$ is the carbon vacancy) color centers are promising platforms for quantum computing and quantum information science due to their favorable optical and spin properties. They are commonly fabricated by ion implantation, which inevitably introduces vacancies and carbon self-interstitials (C$_i$) into the lattice. However, the microscopic formation mechanism remains unclear, limiting the yield and stability of $XV$ centers. Here, first-principles calculations are conducted to systematically investigate the roles of $V$ and C$_i$ in $XV$ formation. We find that $XV$ formation is energetically favorable, with large binding energies and low diffusion barriers. Nevertheless, $XV$ readily captures C$_i$ to form substitutional defect $X_s$, or captures an additional $V$ to form the complex $XV_2$. Charge transition levels show that oppositely charged reactants never meet in these reactions, and that Coulomb repulsion blocks them only when both reactants carry charges of the same sign, which for the capture of C$_i$ requires strongly n- or p-type conditions. These competing defect reactions destabilize the split-vacancy configuration and could account for the low formation yield of $XV$ centers, so that they appear at concentrations well below those expected from the implanted dose. Our results elucidate the microscopic origin of this intrinsic instability and suggest that Fermi-level control may suppress defect conversions and stabilize the split-vacancy configuration.

articles.title: Helium States in a CAS(2,2) Subspace Inspired by Quantum Photonics
articles.abstract: We present a four-mode Fock-state photonics implementation of the variational quantum deflation (VQD) algorithm to calculate the ground-state and excited-state energies for the neutral helium atom in a CAS(2,2) Subspace. Its CAS(2,2) electronic Hilbert space is encoded into a bosonic Fock-space representation and subsequently optimized using a continuous-variable quantum circuit. The circuit architecture under study is constructed of single-mode phase shifts, beam splitters, and cross-Kerr interactions. The variational circuit is initialized in the Fock state $\ket{1100}$ and its performance is benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the active-space configuration-interaction (CASCI) Hamiltonian. We also extend the method to optimize from the first to three excited states of the helium atom with the aid of the variational quantum deflation $(VQD)$ method in a CAS(2,2). We then investigate the performance of this circuit architecture as a basis for implementing the VQD method. In the ideal noiseless simulation setting, we see that the survival probability of the ground and the excited states within the target $CAS$ subspace is unity, because the total photon number and the photon number in the two spin sectors $α$ and $β$ are preserved.
