articles.title: Long-Term Impact of Vutrisiran in Patients With TTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: 1-Year Efficacy and Safety Outcomes From the HELIOS-B Open-Label Extension
articles.abstract: In HELIOS-B (A Study to Evaluate Vutrisiran in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy), vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) and recurrent cardiovascular events and slowed disease progression measures versus placebo in patients with TTR (transthyretin) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy after 33 to 36 months. We report the long-term efficacy and safety of vutrisiran from an ongoing open-label extension of HELIOS-B. Patients who completed HELIOS-B could enroll in the open-label extension, continuing with vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (continuous vutrisiran) or, if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (placebo/vutrisiran). Prespecified end points assessed in the open-label extension are the composite of ACM and cardiovascular events, ACM, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire–Overall Summary score, New York Heart Association class, and NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide) and troponin I levels. Outcomes were assessed through month 48 in this analysis. Of 654 participants in HELIOS-B (vutrisiran, n=326; placebo, n=328), 478 completed double-blind treatment and 466 (vutrisiran, n=243; placebo, n=223) entered the open-label extension. In the continuous vutrisiran group, the risk of first cardiovascular event or ACM was reduced by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.51, 0.79]; P =0.0001) and ACM by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.46, 0.84]; P =0.0023) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Through month 48, patients in the continuous vutrisiran group had preserved health status and quality of life per Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire–Overall Summary score (least squares mean difference, 9.0 [95% CI, 5.3, 12.6]; P <0.0001) and more patients had improved or stable New York Heart Association class (odds ratio, 1.6 [95% CI, 1.1, 2.2]; P =0.0084) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Benefits in the continuous vutrisiran group were maintained for NT-proBNP and troponin I levels (adjusted geometric mean fold change ratios, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.58, 0.74]; P <0.0001; and 0.71 [95% CI, 0.64, 0.79]; P <0.0001, respectively) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Similar benefits were observed in the vutrisiran monotherapy population. No new safety signals were observed. Long-term vutrisiran resulted in clinically meaningful benefits across mortality, cardiovascular events, cardiac biomarkers, functional status, and quality of life in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy through month 48. Patients initially treated with vutrisiran had better outcomes than those first receiving placebo, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT04153149.

articles.title: Targeting ALDOA Lactylation Reverses Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension by Disrupting Actin Polymerization and YAP Activation
articles.abstract: Maladaptive vascular remodeling is a hallmark of pulmonary hypertension (PH), and therapeutic strategies directly targeting the pathological activity of smooth muscle cells remain limited. Metabolic and epigenetic dysregulation are established drivers of PH, and lysine lactylation has emerged as a novel posttranslational modification implicated in diverse diseases; however, its direct contribution to PH progression remains undefined. Integrated lactylomic and proteomic profiling was performed in hypoxic human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells. The functional role of ALDOA (aldolase A) lactylation at lysine 42 (K42) was assessed using site-specific mutant virus and smooth muscle cell-specific inducible ALDOA knockout mice in 2 established PH models: SU5416+hypoxia in mice and monocrotaline in rats. We identified ALDOA as a prominent lactylation target in hypoxic pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells, with K42 lactylation consistently elevated in primary pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells derived from PH rodent models and human PH tissues. Mechanistically, AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1)-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation enhanced its binding to γ-actin, independent of glycolytic activity. This lactylation-enhanced interaction promoted F-actin polymerization and activated YAP (Yes-associated protein) signaling via LATS1 (large tumor suppressor kinase 1) inhibition, thereby driving pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell proliferation and phenotypic switching. Moreover, YAP/TEAD4 (TEA domain transcription factor 4)-mediated transcriptional upregulation of AARS1 established a positive feedback loop reinforcing ALDOA K42 lactylation under hypoxia. In vivo, ALDOA inducible knockout or reconstitution with the lactylation-deficient K42R (lysine 42 mutant to arginine) mutant attenuated experimental PH progression, with suppressed F-actin/YAP activation and reduced vascular remodeling. Furthermore, competitive inhibition of lactylation through β‑alanine reduced ALDOA K42 lactylation and ameliorated vascular remodeling in ALDOA-overexpressing rodent PH models. Translationally, pharmacological disruption of the ALDOA/γ-actin interaction by raltegravir suppressed cytoskeletal reorganization and YAP signaling, mitigating PH progression in both mouse and rat models. AARS1-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation drives pulmonary vascular remodeling through a mechanism independent of ALDOA’s catalytic activity, promoting F-actin polymerization and YAP activation. Precision targeting of this modification selectively inhibits pathological signaling while preserving metabolic homeostasis, highlighting a translational potential for precision intervention in PH.

articles.title: A critical reflection on the application of hot product frameworks to explain the target selection of wildlife products
articles.abstract: The application of hot product frameworks, such as value, inertia, visibility, and accessibility (VIVA) and concealable, removable, available, (abundance and accessibility), valuable, enjoyable, and disposable (CRAVED/CRAAVED), to illegal markets to understand the selection of wildlife products in them has gained momentum. Originally developed to study property crimes, these frameworks have been adapted for predictive analysis of wildlife product selection. However, their utility in explaining target selection and their empirical testability remain ambiguous. This study critically examined the use of the VIVA and CRA(A)VED frameworks in analyzing wildlife product selection for illegal markets. By reviewing peer‐reviewed studies and conducting a case study on Southeast Asian monitor lizards (Varanus spp.), we identified the challenges of applying these frameworks to real‐world contexts. These challenges are not merely methodological shortcomings of individual studies but reflect systematic difficulties inherent to applying these frameworks to wildlife contexts. The application of these frameworks to Southeast Asian monitor lizards confirmed that these issues transcend species groups. We also examined issues related to intraspecific variation in measures and variation between harvesters. Our analysis revealed complex interactions between attributes that influence wildlife product selection and identified key challenges to applying these frameworks, including incomplete data, inconsistent attribute measurements, and the dynamic nature of decision‐making during wildlife harvesting. A significant concern is the reliance on trade data, which are typically collected much later in the wildlife trade chain, to infer harvesting decisions. Moreover, we argued that target selection is not solely determined by product attributes. A more problem‐oriented and individualized approach that accounts for opportunity structures relevant to individual harvesters is needed to prevent aggregation fallacies. Thus, applying hot product frameworks to study the selection of target wildlife products cannot be quantitatively tested using an additive equation, and these frameworks should not be applied alone but situated within other theories of crime. Reflexión crítica de la aplicación de marcos de productos de moda para explicar la selección de objetivos de los productos de fauna Resumen Resumen. Hoy en día ha cobrado impulso la aplicación de marcos de análisis de productos de moda, como el de «valor, inercia, visibilidad y accesibilidad» (VIVA) y el de «ocultable, extraíble, disponible (abundancia y accesibilidad), valioso, agradable y desechable» (CRAVED/CRAAVED), a los mercados ilegales para comprender cómo seleccionan los productos de fauna silvestre. Desarrollados originalmente para estudiar los delitos contra la propiedad, estos marcos se han adaptado para el análisis predictivo de la selección de productos de fauna silvestre. Sin embargo, su utilidad para explicar la selección de objetivos y su capacidad de comprobación empírica todavía son ambiguas. Este estudio examinó críticamente el uso de los marcos VIVA y CRA(A)VED en el análisis de la selección de productos de fauna silvestre para los mercados ilegales. Revisamos los estudios sometidos a revisión por pares y la realización de un estudio de caso sobre los varanos del sudeste asiático (Varanus spp.) para identificar los retos que plantea la aplicación de estos marcos a contextos del mundo real. Estos retos no son meras deficiencias metodológicas de estudios individuales, sino que reflejan dificultades sistemáticas inherentes a la aplicación de estos marcos a contextos relacionados con la fauna silvestre. La aplicación de estos marcos a los lagartos monitor del sudeste asiático confirmó que estas cuestiones trascienden los grupos de especies. También examinamos cuestiones relacionadas con la variación intraespecífica en las mediciones y la variación entre los recolectores.…

articles.title: Conceptual framework for the implementation of the Species Threat Abatement and Restoration metric's threat abatement component
articles.abstract: One important goal of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) aims to halt extinction of species and reduce extinction risk 10‐fold by 2050. To help ensure that the actions taken under the targets of the KMGBF contribute to reducing species’ extinction risk, the Species Threat Abatement and Restoration (STAR) metric was designed to enable science‐based target setting for species. STAR quantifies the potential contribution of threat abatement actions or habitat restoration to reducing species’ extinction risk in an area. To support the effective implementation of STAR, we developed a framework to move from determining the threat abatement component of STAR (START) using global data to calibrating START using local data to setting targets and calculating realized START scores to measure progress. The framework outlines the specific approaches that can be implemented to calculate these different START metrics. First, estimated START scores use global data to provide an initial indication of the species and threats expected to be present within an area. Then, calibrated START scores involve confirming the local presence of species and threats, and the locally verified data allow for setting robust threat abatement targets, which can be articulated as target START scores. Calibrated START can also inform both reactive and proactive threat management. Finally, changes in threat intensity are then monitored and used to calculate realized START. Achieving realized START requires actors to not only reduce existing threats but also prevent additional threats emerging within the area. This framework provides a means for all potential actors, working across varying spatial scales, to quantify, plan, monitor, and deliver interventions to address species threats and then report the impact of the interventions using a consistent method and metric that are comparable and aggregable across actors and locations. Marco conceptual para la aplicación del componente de reducción de amenazas de la medida de Reducción de Amenazas y Restauración de Especies (STAR) Resumen Uno de los objetivos principales del Marco Global de Biodiversidad de Kunming‐Montreal (KMGBF) es detener la extinción de especies y reducir el riesgo de extinción diez veces para 2050. Con el fin de garantizar que las medidas adoptadas en el marco de los objetivos del KMGBF contribuyan a reducir el riesgo de extinción de las especies, se diseñó el indicador «Reducción de amenazas y restauración de especies» (STAR), que permite establecer objetivos basados en la ciencia para las especies. STAR cuantifica la contribución potencial de las medidas de reducción de amenazas o de restauración del hábitat a la reducción del riesgo de extinción de las especies en una zona. Para apoyar la aplicación efectiva de STAR, desarrollamos un marco que permite pasar de determinar el componente de reducción de amenazas de STAR (START) con datos globales a calibrar START utilizando datos locales, para finalmente establecer objetivos y calcular las puntuaciones START reales para medir el progreso. El marco describe los enfoques específicos que pueden aplicarse para calcular estas diferentes métricas START. Primero, las puntuaciones estimadas de START utilizan datos globales para proporcionar una indicación inicial de las especies y las amenazas que se espera que estén presentes en una zona. A continuación, las puntuaciones calibradas de START implican confirmar la presencia local de especies y amenazas y los datos verificados a nivel local permiten establecer objetivos sólidos de mitigación de amenazas que pueden articularse como puntuaciones objetivo de START. El START calibrado también puede servir de base para la gestión reactiva y proactiva de las amenazas. Por último, se supervisan los cambios en la intensidad de las amenazas y se utilizan para calcular el START realizado.…

articles.title: Reduction of Tree Water Stress by Large Herbivores in an African Savanna
articles.abstract: Large mammalian herbivores (LMH) play complex roles in shaping tree cover and composition in savannas by suppressing trees through browsing and reducing competition from neighbouring trees and understory vegetation. Where LMH are declining, release from browsing and intensification of competition has unpredictable physiological consequences. To test how LMH removal affects tree growth and water stress, we combined 16 years of growth data with measurements of leaf water potential and gas exchange from a herbivore‐exclusion experiment in Kenya. Across tree species, LMH exclusion increased growth but elevated water stress, particularly under dry conditions. Moreover, the tree species with the most acquisitive water‐use strategy was most susceptible to increased water stress and reduced carbon assimilation under exclusion. These findings indicate that although LMH limit tree growth, they also reduce water stress. Ultimately, interspecific differences in tree physiology will affect how savanna communities respond to interacting pressures from climate change and LMH declines.

articles.title: Biogeography of Argentine Stem Weevil Invasion of Southern New Zealand and Two Offshore Islands
articles.abstract: Understanding the biogeography and genetics of the invasion of oceanic islands by pest species can provide insights into how to limit such incursions. The invasive pasture pest weevil, Listronotus bonariensis (Kuschel), has established in both New Zealand and some of its offshore islands, causing significant economic damage. The opportunity was therefore taken to compare both the species' morphology and genetics of populations collected from the New Zealand mainland, Stewart Island (30 km offshore) and Chatham Island (860 km offshore). The L. bonariensis individuals from both of the offshore populations were found to be significantly smaller than those of the mainland populations. However, based on classical and molecular taxonomy, no associated species‐level differences were found and it was concluded that the island's smaller populations were the result of relatively poor habitat quality. Further, no significant genetic differences were detected between Stewart Island and mainland populations, indicating a close connection. Conversely, at the genomic level, the Chatham Island population was significantly different from the two other populations and this was attributed to probable founder effects. The evidence points to a small subset of what was still a recently‐established New Zealand L. bonariensis population early in the 20th century being inadvertently transported to the Chatham Islands. Thereafter, this founding subset expanded such that more recent introductions have had little effect on the founding genetics of weevils on the island. This study investigates whether irregular, unintended human transportation of species to isolated islands can lead to the occupation of previously uninhabited niches, with founder effects leading to genetic divergence from conspecific source populations elsewhere.

articles.title: Linking Morphological and Genetic Differentiation Among Populations in Seagrass Species With Contrasting Dispersal Strategies
articles.abstract: Long-distance dispersal sustains genetic diversity across populations and facilitates recovery from disturbance, and dispersal also may shape how ecologically important morphological traits shift in response to environmental change. We examined links among morphology, genetic differentiation, and dispersal through surveys of traits and genetics for Thalassia testudinum and Halodule wrightii distributed across a naturally occurring gradient in concentrations of total phosphorus in the water column along Florida's Gulf Coast (USA). We expected the contrasting dispersal strategies of the two seagrasses would drive patterns in genetic differentiation: T. testudinum produces floating fruits that can disperse over longer distances than the negatively buoyant seeds of H. wrightii. Genetic differentiation among populations was higher for H. wrightii (G' ST = 0.02–0.15) than for T. testudinum (G' ST = 0.00–0.07), supporting the expectation that limited dispersal leads to more genetic structure. Morphology for both species varied along the phosphorus gradient, where leaves were generally shorter in the estuarine system with the lowest phosphorus concentrations, with more pronounced differences in leaf length observed for T. testudinum. The role of the environment in driving leaf length was tested in a common garden experiment with plants of both species collected from three estuarine systems along the phosphorus gradient. Initially, leaf lengths of both species differed across plants originating from different systems. Leaf lengths became more similar throughout the experiment, with leaves of H. wrightii from the northernmost system beginning to lengthen after 11 months. Together, our results suggest that responses to environmental change can differ across seagrass species, where the species capable of long-distance dispersal exhibited greater variability in a morphological trait along an environmental gradient despite less genetic differentiation than the species with more limited dispersal.

articles.title: Shifting Dietary Ecologies of Early Ungulates Across the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum in the Bighorn Basin, Wyoming
articles.abstract: Understanding the interplay between climate change and ecology is crucial when attempting to reconstruct the evolutionary history of species, as well as predicting how modern species may fare in light of current anthropogenic climate change and habitat destruction. Here we use dental microwear texture analysis (DMTA) to infer the foraging ecologies of three lineages of early ungulates (the phenacodontids Copecion and Ectocion and the early perissodactyl Sifrhippus) across the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum (PETM) in the Bighorn Basin of western North America. The PETM was a period of rapid warming and aridification 56 million years ago that resulted in considerable evolutionary changes within these lineages, including phylogenetic dwarfing. Our results interpret both lineages of phenacodontid as frugivorous “mixed feeders” that likely incorporated a large diversity of plant species and tissues, while Sifrhippus shows strong evidence of frugivory. This is further supported by greater complexity and lesser scale of maximum complexity in both species of Sifrhippus compared to the co‐occurring species of phenacodontids. Notably, only minor changes in dental microwear across the PETM were recovered, limited to textural fill volume in Ectocion. These data show that dietary ecology was mostly unchanged within these lineages during the PETM, despite considerable floral turnover and competition from immigrant species. The results of our study detail how herbivorous mammals adapt to intensive climatic and environmental disruptions, hinting at possible responses of modern fauna to present and future anthropogenic climatic and environmental breakdown.

A comprehensive “past-future” framework for restoration priority areas identification in a coastal city: a case study of Tianjin
articles.abstract: Coastal cities, endowed with abundant ecological resources and convenient transportation, are epicenters where the tension between ecological protection and economic development is most pronounced. Precise identification of restoration priority areas (RPAs) is crucial for improving ecosystem service management and advancing sustainable development in coastal cities. However, how to integrate historical evolution and future trends into RPAs management remains insufficiently addressed. In this study, we selected Tianjin as a case study site, and developed a comprehensive analytical framework for identifying RPAs. This framework centers on the spatiotemporal evolution characteristics and interrelationships of four ESs, identifies ecological restoration areas (ERAs) through full-cycle dynamic assessment and simulation, and proposes multi-type optimization recommendations. The results indicated that the water yield (WY), soil conservation (SC), carbon storage (CS) and habitat quality (HQ) exhibited divergent temporal trajectories from 2000 to 2020, although localized improvements were observed in the peripheral zones of ring-shaped built-up areas and in coastal wetland regions. WY–HQ exhibited a robust and gradually strengthening trade-off from 2000 to 2020, while CS–SC maintained a relatively stable synergistic relationship. Based on the Ecological Restoration Priority Index (ERPI), this study delineated ecological ERAs and further classified them into three progressively differentiated zones: Core Protection Zones (defined as RPAs), Synergistic Optimization Zones, and Ecological Improvement Zones. Based on the analysis of land use composition and spatial distribution in RPAs, we proposed specific ecological restoration strategies and spatial planning recommendations. This “past-future” framework overcomes the constraints of traditional RPAs and provides a novel perspective on the evidence-based land management in coastal city.

articles.title: Waterfowl habitat conservation in the U.S. Prairie Pothole Region benefits more than ducks: evaluating overlaps and gaps across geographies and bird species
articles.abstract: The Prairie Pothole Region (PPR) is a working landscape of grasslands, cropland, and wetlands that supports some of the highest numbers of breeding waterfowl, waterbirds, shorebirds, and grassland birds in North America. Consequently, the PPR was identified as a high priority for waterfowl conservation by the North American Waterfowl Management Plan. Partners in the Prairie Pothole Joint Venture (PPJV) have used spatial decision-support tools to guide extensive land conservation efforts, primarily acquisition of wetland easements, grassland easements, and fee-title lands, to conserve waterfowl populations. However, effects of waterfowl conservation actions on waterfowl and non-waterfowl species groups across geographies are poorly understood. We used spatial predictions from models developed by eBird along with land protection data to assess effects of conservation on 77 species of birds across the PPJV. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service fee-title and easement lands covered <5% of the landscape, but have generally protected much larger percentages of species’ populations, thus demonstrating the value of spatial targeting tools and how conservationists can disproportionately move the needle for priority species through strategic protection. Proportions of PPJV populations supported by lands protected through waterfowl conservation varied within and among waterfowl (range 0.07 to 0.39), wetland-dependent (0.02 to 0.42), and grassland bird groups (0.01 to 0.28), as well as among geographies. Proportions of populations supported by waterfowl conservation lands were generally lower in the eastern and western portions of the PPJV, where less habitat protection has occurred than in the central PPJV. Protected lands not acquired for waterfowl conservation added to proportions of populations protected, particularly in the western PPJV, which has large amounts of public agency land relative to other portions of the PPJV. Fee-title lands and grassland easements protected through waterfowl conservation were estimated to support more than three times as many individuals of non-waterfowl species as waterfowl; wetland easements were estimated to support more than twice as many individuals of non-waterfowl species as waterfowl. Our results demonstrate that waterfowl conservation in the PPJV benefits many species of birds; variation in benefits can be used to guide future conservation efforts to address gaps in protection.

articles.title: Beyond observed diversity: Community completeness negatively affects ecosystem invasibility across scales
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Charles Elton proposed that species‐rich communities are more resistant to invasion, yet a well‐known paradox persists: native diversity suppresses invasion at small scales while correlating positively with non‐native species diversity at broad scales. Moving beyond native observed diversity alone to community completeness, defined as the ratio of native observed diversity to its specific species pool, may offer a potential framework to address this scale dependency. This is because the completeness index reflects the degree to which a habitat saturates its available niche space, shaped jointly by abiotic and biotic filtering in an origin‐blind manner. At small spatial scales, native observed diversity and dark diversity (suitable yet absent native species) are negatively correlated. This implies that high native observed diversity indicates high community completeness, leaving limited vacant niche opportunities for both un‐arrived native and non‐native species and thus reducing invasibility. In contrast, at large spatial scales, greater environmental heterogeneity can yield a vastly expanded regional species pool where dark diversity also accumulates more, potentially resulting in lower community completeness and heightened susceptibility. It should be noted that native community completeness, based on the extant species pool, fails to capture the niche spaces left by historical species losses—a gap tracked by temporal dark diversity dynamics—yet these hypervolume holes can instead be successfully exploited and predicted by non‐native community completeness. Following on this logic, I propose a Completeness‐Based Invasion Theory, which hypothesizes that community invasibility is inversely related to community completeness across spatial scales. While further empirical testing across diverse systems is required, measuring completeness alongside observed diversity may provide a novel, scale‐independent perspective to advance our understanding and management of biological invasions. Combining both native community completeness and non‐native community completeness to predict non‐native species invasions may currently represent the optimal approach. articles.title: Community assembly on inland cliffs is context‐dependent
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Under harsh environmental conditions, community assembly processes are expected to drive pronounced functional convergence, with communities dominated by stress‐tolerant species. Integrating local communities with their regional species pools enables evaluating environmental filtering and disentangling habitat‐specific assembly processes. To assess whether the strength and direction of environmental filtering in extreme habitats depends on regional climate and topography, we adopted a trait‐based approach on a relatively underexplored habitat such as inland limestone cliffs. To test whether limestone inland cliffs function as extreme habitats that filter regional species pools towards stress‐tolerant trait syndromes or alternative habitat‐specific assembly processes, we sampled vegetation on inland limestone cliffs along an aridity gradient in three study areas spanning different European biogeographic regions, namely Alpine, Continental and Mediterranean. We compiled regional species pools from the Global Biodiversity Information Facility and integrated them into trait‐based null models to compare observed community structure against expectations under stochastic assembly, using a combination of functional traits compiled from field measurements and from databases. Additionally, to assess whether community assembly rules are shared across regions or shaped by regional context and topography, we quantify trait‐based non‐random assembly and functional convergence across biogeographic regions and different cliff aspects. The results show that in inland limestone cliffs, extremeness is context‐dependent. It varies with the selected traits, intensifies in humid regions and weakens on pole‐facing slopes in dry regions. Cliff plants showed reduced plant height across all regions and aspects, whereas leaf dry matter content was higher and seed mass was lower under specific conditions. These patterns indicate non‐random trait distributions towards conservative leaf strategies and reduced plant size, while the prevalence of small propagules may facilitate colonization of suitable microsites for establishment, often scarce and spatially scattered. Functional convergence occurred in the Alpine region and on equator‐facing cliffs in the Mediterranean region, with slope and microtopographic heterogeneity showing limited effects. Overall, inland limestone cliffs showed evidence of non‐random trait assembly and localized abiotic filtering, suggesting that these patterns are context‐dependent. Riassunto In condizioni ambientali severe ci si aspetta che i processi di assemblaggio delle comunità determinino una marcata convergenza funzionale, con comunità dominate da specie tolleranti allo stress. Integrare le comunità locali con i rispettivi pool regionali di specie permette di valutare il filtro ambientale e di distinguere i processi di assemblaggio delle comunità specifici di un habitat. Per valutare se la forza e la direzione del filtro ambientale in habitat estremi dipendono dal clima regionale e dalla topografia, abbiamo adottato un approccio basato sui tratti funzionali in un habitat relativamente poco studiato, quale quello delle falesie calcaree dell’entroterra. Per verificare se le falesie calcaree dell’entroterra funzionino come habitat estremi in grado di filtrare i pool regionali di specie verso sindromi funzionali associate alla tolleranza allo stress o, alternativamente, verso processi di assemblaggio specifici dell’habitat, abbiamo campionato la vegetazione su falesie calcaree dell’entroterra lungo un gradiente di aridità in tre aree di studio appartenenti a diverse regioni biogeografiche europee, ossia Alpina, Continentale e Mediterranea.…

articles.title: Context‐dependent joint buffering of abiotic stress by parental care and sibling interactions
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Climate change represents one of the most complex challenges of the 21st century, increasing global temperatures and the occurrence of extreme events, such as heatwaves, cold snaps, floods or droughts. These changes exert significant pressure on biological systems, often resulting in altered behavioural patterns and impairments in fecundity, reproductive success and offspring survival. The evolution of parental care is hypothesized to represent an adaptive response to environmental challenges, with the potential to buffer offspring performance against stressors such as thermal extremes. While parental care is long regarded as the major evolutionary driver for family groups, an increasing number of studies highlight the beneficial effects of sibling interactions on offspring development, raising interest in sibling cooperation as an early driver of social life. Here, we tested whether the fitness consequences of sibling interactions depend on abiotic environmental conditions and whether sibling interactions buffer offspring against environmental stress, act synergistically with parental care or lose their beneficial effects under harsh conditions. To this end, we examined larval performance in the subsocial burying beetle Nicrophorus vespilloides. In two separate experiments, we manipulated the presence or absence of parents and siblings and exposed offspring to either temperature or soil moisture extremes. The capacity of cooperative behaviours to mitigate the effects of environmental stress depended strongly on environmental context, social constellation and the trait considered. Under low temperatures, parental care and sibling cooperation acted synergistically to buffer larval mass, whereas the benefits of sibling interactions disappeared in the absence of parents. In contrast, high temperatures reduced offspring performance when parents and siblings were present simultaneously but did not diminish the benefits associated with sibling interactions in the absence of parental care. Our findings demonstrate that the effects of social interactions under environmental stress are highly context dependent. Rather than consistently promoting or disrupting cooperation, abiotic stress modified the strength and expression of social effects across environmental conditions and social constellations. These results highlight the importance of sociality for resilience to environmental change, while showing that its buffering capacity is conditional rather than universal. articles.title: Functional variation in butterfly egg pore traits: The potential role of climate
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Immobile eggs of terrestrial animals are exposed to variable environmental conditions. Insect egg pores, critical for gas exchange (aeropyles) and fertilisation (micropyles), are ecologically important yet understudied. While aeropyles likely adapt to climatic respiratory demands, and micropyles may respond to environmental pressures, their inter‐ and intraspecific variation remains poorly studied. Here, we compared egg pore morphology of three closely related Pieris butterflies sampled in the Netherlands. In addition, we compared egg traits of different P. napi populations sampled along a 4000‐km latitudinal gradient from northern to southern Europe and linked these traits with available climatic data. After several generations under identical greenhouse conditions, egg pore traits remained highly variable within and between species and groups. Remarkably, P. napi populations from divergent climates differed more in pore number and size than did co‐occurring Pieris species. Aeropyle number and width were strongly associated with climatic variables such as summer temperature and precipitation, independent of egg size. Additionally, we observed the micropyles of older eggs to be covered by a substance more often than fresh eggs. Our findings indicate that insect egg pores are highly dynamic traits, which may be shaped by ecological, behavioural and climatic factors and an under‐recognised role of egg adaptation. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract De eitjes van landorganismen zijn statisch en daardoor direct blootgesteld aan wisselende omgevingsfactoren. Insecteneitjes hebben poriën die verantwoordelijk zijn voor gasuitwisseling (aeropyles) en bevruchting (micropyles). Deze poriën zijn ecologisch belangrijk maar desondanks weinig onderzocht. Terwijl aeropyles waarschijnlijk belangrijk zijn voor de door het klimaat beïnvloedde gasuitwisseling, en micropyles zich wellicht aanpassen aan de omgeving, is hun natuurlijke variatie maar weinig onderzocht zowel tussen als binnen insectensoorten. In deze studie hebben we de variatie van ei‐poriën vergeleken tussen drie zeer verwante Pieris vlindersoorten uit Nederland. Daarbuiten hebben we gekeken hoe ei‐eigenschappen van Pieris napi populaties verzameld over een Europese noord‐zuid‐as van 4000 km gelinkt zijn aan het lokale klimaat. Na enkele generaties onder identieke kascondities bleek dat ei‐poriën sterk variabel bleven tussen zowel soorten als populaties. De verschillen waren zelfs groter tussen populaties van P. napi, dan tussen de drie Pieris soorten. Het aantal en de groote van aeropyles was sterk geassocieerd met temperatuur en regenval, onafhankelijk van ei‐grootte. Tot slot bleken eitjes van enkele uren oud vaker een nog onbekende substantie te bevatten die de micropyles afdekt dan vers gelegde eitjes. Deze studie laat zien dat de poriën van insecteneitjes zeer variabel zijn, die wellicht beïnvloed worden door ecologische‐, gedrags‐, en klimaatfactoren, en zo een grotere rol kunnen spelen in de evolutie van insecteneitjes dan eerder gedacht.

articles.title: Fungal Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis infections proliferate during amphibian terrestrial dormancy
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract The spread and impact of wildlife pathogens is often seasonal, and identifying the season(s) of highest impact can be critical to biodiversity and public health management. We report new evidence that winter host dormancy, a period generally neglected in terms of pathogen seasonal dynamics, strongly promotes the proliferation of the globally threatening amphibian fungal pathogen, Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) in an endangered high‐elevation anuran host species. Surveillance of Bd in Yosemite toads (Anaxyrus canorus) during their first year of life showed that Bd prevalence and intensity increased fourfold during their first terrestrial winter dormancy. High prevalence and intensity of Bd infections following winter dormancy were observed in terrestrial first‐year juveniles across multiple sites and three consecutive years, and their Bd prevalence was much higher than that observed in aquatically breeding adults during the same time frame. The infections persisted into the active season. We integrated these results into a framework summarizing possible mechanisms of overwinter Bd maintenance. We recommend a reconsideration of seasons promoting Bd proliferation (i.e. increases in prevalence and/or intensity) and highlight a mechanism of interannual Bd maintenance in dormant terrestrial juveniles. The importance of host dormancy to pathogen persistence and seasonal infection spread may be far greater than previously thought. articles.title: High‐dimensional elementomes outperform CNP models in explaining photosynthetic traits
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Links between plant elementomes (i.e. the concentration of chemical elements in plant tissue) and functional traits have the potential to improve predictions of plant physiological performance and ecosystem processes, and their response to environmental change. High-dimensional plant elementomes, which encompass not only macronutrients but also micronutrients and trace elements, have been associated with various morphological and physiological plant traits, but not with photosynthetic traits. We determined elementomes, comprising 21 elements and isotopic ratios of C and N, of 26 hygrophytic bryophyte species (16 mosses and 10 liverworts) in Mediterranean springs, and examined their relationship with four photosynthetic light response traits: maximum photosynthetic rates, apparent quantum yield, light compensation point and dark respiration rates. Results from linear mixed effects models showed that high-dimensional elementomes are strongly associated with photosynthetic traits, explaining substantially more variance (R 2 = 38%–61%; 72%–85% when also including taxonomic information) than models based solely on C, N and P (R 2 = 6%–45% and 35%–72%, respectively). Model selection and averaging revealed that each photosynthetic light response trait was optimally modelled by a set of 8–13 elemental variables, including various macronutrients (e.g. N, S, K), micronutrients (e.g. Zn, Cu), trace elements (e.g. Ni, Co) and isotopic ratios (δ13C and δ15N). We demonstrate that plant elementomes capture key drivers of photosynthetic variation, which adds to growing evidence of strong links between elementomes and various functional traits that underpin organismal and ecosystem functioning. Our results suggest that characterising plant elementomes could contribute to improved predictions of ecosystem-scale processes such as CO2 uptake. Resum Els vincles entre els elementomes de les plantes (és a dir, la concentració d'elements químics en els teixits vegetals) i els trets funcionals poden millorar les prediccions sobre el rendiment fisiològic de les plantes i els processos ecosistèmics, i com aquests responen als canvis ambientals. Els elementomes d'alta dimensionalitat, que inclouen no només macronutrients, sinó també micronutrients i elements traça, s'han associat amb diversos trets morfològics i fisiològics vegetals, però no amb trets fotosintètics. Hem determinat els elementomes (incloent 21 elements i les proporcions isotòpiques de C i N) de 26 espècies de briòfits higròfits (16 molses i 10 hepàtiques) presents a fonts mediterrànies, i n'hem analitzat la relació amb quatre trets de resposta fotosintètica a la llum: taxes fotosintètiques màximes, rendiment quàntic aparent, punt de compensació de la llum i taxes de respiració. Els resultats dels models lineals d'efectes mixtos mostren que els elementomes d'alta dimensionalitat estan fortament associats amb els trets fotosintètics i expliquen una proporció substancialment més gran de la variància (R 2 = 38%–61%; 72%–85% quan també s'hi inclou la informació taxonòmica) que els models basats únicament en C, N i P (R 2 = 6%–45% i 35%–72%, respectivament). La selecció de models i la mitjana ponderada de les estimacions revelen que cada tret fotosintètic es pot modelitzar de manera òptima mitjançant un conjunt de 8–13 variables elementals, que inclouen diversos macronutrients (p. ex., N, S, K), micronutrients (p. ex., Zn, Cu), elements traça (p. ex., Ni, Co) i proporcions isotòpiques (δ13C i δ15N). Demostrem que els elementomes vegetals permeten identificar factors clau de variació fotosintètica, la qual cosa se suma a l'evidència creixent de l'existència de vincles estrets entre els elementomes i diversos trets funcionals que sustenten el funcionament dels organismes i dels ecosistemes.…

articles.title: Invasive insects outperform their native counterparts
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Invasive alien species cause substantial ecological damage worldwide, driving biodiversity loss and negatively impacting human livelihoods. Although invasive insects have some of the most severe impacts, the traits associated with their invasiveness remain unclear. We conducted a meta‐analysis comparing phenotypic traits of matched, co‐occurring invasive and native insect pairs (sympatric congeners or confamilials) in the invaded range. In total, we compared 922 invasive‐native pairs using 1327 effect sizes from 182 studies. These pairs comprised 144 unique invasive insect species and 403 unique native species. We found that invasive insects generally have greater fecundity, shorter development times, faster population growth rates and enhanced foraging and competitive capabilities compared with their native counterparts. However, some of these patterns changed after excluding the two most data‐rich families (i.e. Coccinellidae and Formicidae), likely due to divergent evolutionary histories, life history strategies and selection pressures. This study represents the most comprehensive systematic comparison of trait differences between co‐occurring native and invasive insect species and highlights that a diverse array of traits can contribute to invasiveness. Moreover, our open‐access database of insect trait data will facilitate further research into the causes and consequences of insect invasions. articles.title: Out of the fire and into the frying pan: Hostile post‐fire thermal conditions reduce activity windows for reptiles
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Climate change and intensified fire regimes are reshaping ecosystems globally. Reptiles, as ectotherms, rely on microhabitat shelters to buffer against thermal extremes, yet the capacity of these shelters to persist or function following fire remains poorly understood. As heatwaves and fire regimes intensify under climate change, effective thermal buffering will become increasingly vital for reptile persistence. This study quantifies how fire alters the structure and thermal offset of key reptile refugia: spinifex (Triodia) tussocks, chenopod shrubs, and leaf‐litter mats, in the dune and swale habitats of South Australia's Murray Mallee. Using iButton data loggers deployed across four fire histories, we measured hourly microhabitat and adjacent ground temperatures, modelling thermal offset (Toffset) via mixed‐effects models. More recent fire histories were associated with less spinifex and leaf‐litter cover and more bare ground, although evidence for changes in individual shelter dimensions was mixed. Thermal buffering declined markedly in recently burnt sites, with long‐unburnt spinifex providing the greatest daytime protection from extreme ground temperatures. Structural properties such as tussock height and litter depth were associated with Toffset, supporting a relationship between shelter structure and thermal‐refuge quality. Comparisons with the thermal tolerance of spinifex‐obligate reptiles indicate that burnt habitats often exceed critical thermal limits, effectively eliminating usable refugia during heatwaves. These results demonstrate that fire‐driven structural simplification translates to weakened thermal refugia, with implications for species persistence under increasing heat extremes. Effective fire management in arid systems should, therefore, prioritise the protection and regeneration of long‐unburnt spinifex and litter habitats as critical microclimatic refuges. articles.title: Plant‐derived compounds to improve soil inoculation for restoration
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Restoring the soil microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important requirement for the success of ecosystem restoration. Soil inoculation can reintroduce the missing taxa, but its application is limited by the large amount of donor soil that is needed and by the poor persistence of the inoculants, because of habitat filtering, priority effects and the loss of plant–microbe feedbacks. Here we propose the metabolite‐inoculum approach, a framework that combines the chemical diversity of plants with soil inoculation, in order to improve the establishment, persistence and effectiveness of introduced microbial communities. In this framework, the chemical input is delivered as fresh and dead plant material, as extracts of this material or as purified compounds that are applied together with the inoculum, and not by adding or manipulating the living plant community. We first synthesize the evidence that plant metabolites, from both above‐ and below‐ground tissues, act as selective regulators of soil microbial composition and diversity. Building on this, we propose a framework for the selection of plant materials and metabolites at the species, tissue and compound levels, and we introduce the parallel concepts of core and keystone metabolites that are matched to their corresponding microbial groups. We then identify the main challenges of the approach, the mismatch in timescale, the non‐target effects and the feasibility, and we translate them into testable hypotheses. Finally, we discuss the contexts in which the approach is likely to work and the contexts in which it is not. In this way, we frame the metabolite‐inoculum approach as a research agenda through bridging chemical ecology and microbial ecology, offering a potential solution to reduce dependency on donor soil, improve inoculant effectiveness and accelerate the recovery of degraded soils toward desired ecosystem states. articles.title: Precipitation‐mediated asymmetric fitness consequences of nectar robbing in distylous Primula florindae
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Flowers with deep corollas are frequently associated with nectar robbing, a behaviour that often reduces pollen transfer and seed production. Robbing scars, however, may further affect plant reproductive success through rainwater entry into corolla tubes. In distylous species, the reciprocal positioning of stigmas and anthers in long‐ and short‐styled morphs may create unequal exposure to incoming water and thereby impose morph‐specific precipitation‐mediated fitness costs. We used 2‐year field manipulations in one focal population of distylous Primula florindae, manipulating nectar robbing in both years and additionally manipulating pollination success in a full‐factorial design in 2024, to investigate how robbing associated with rainwater affects female fitness and interacts with legitimate visitation to shape phenotypic selection on floral traits. We further combined precipitation data, floral trait measurements and behavioural observations of the dominant visitor Bombus kashmirensis to explore the ecological context associated with the observed shift from legitimate visitation to nectar robbing. Our manipulations revealed that robbing significantly reduced seed production independently of pollen limitation. This reduction was stronger in long‐styled plants, and the contrast between morphs was more pronounced in the wetter year, consistent with differential water exposure in pendant flowers: the long‐styled stigma lies below upward‐facing robbing holes, where water may accumulate and submerge it, whereas the short‐styled stigma lies deeper within the corolla tube but spatially above this accumulation zone. Furthermore, legitimate visitation and nectar robbing exerted complex, interactive selective pressures across floral traits, with illegitimate visitation driving accentuated, morph‐specific divergent selection on corolla length. However, neither type of visitation alone, nor both types combined, fully explained the net selection on this trait, suggesting additional selective agents. Observational evidence indicated that robbing onset was associated with elevated pre‐onset rainfall, unusually long corollas and greater foraging efficiency during secondary robbing, although these relationships remain inferential. In summary, our study provides experimental evidence that nectar robbing can turn floral damage into a precipitation‐mediated fitness cost, offering new insights into how nectar robbing affects plant fitness. More broadly, our results suggest that climatic factors can mediate plant–visitor interactions along the mutualism–antagonism continuum and contribute to context‐dependent adaptive trajectories. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 花冠筒较长的花往往更易发生盗蜜，而盗蜜通常会降低花粉转移效率和种子产量。然而，盗蜜留下的伤痕还可能通过使雨水进入花冠筒，进一步影响植物的繁殖成功。在二型花柱植物中，长、短花柱型的柱头和花药呈交互式雌雄异位排列，这种繁殖器官位置差异可能导致两种花型不同程度地暴露于进入花内的雨水中，进而产生花型特异性的降水介导适合度代价。 本研究以一个二型花柱巨伞钟报春(Primula florindae)群体为对象，开展了连续两年的野外操控实验:两年均操控盗蜜，2024年进一步采用全因子设计同时操控盗蜜和授粉成功，以检验与雨水进入相关的盗蜜如何影响雌性适合度，以及盗蜜如何与合法访花相互作用，共同塑造对花部性状的表型选择。我们还结合降水数据、花部性状测量以及优势访花者克什米尔熊蜂(Bombus kashmirensis)的行为观察，探讨所观察到的合法访花向盗蜜转变的生态背景。 操控实验表明，盗蜜显著降低了种子产量，且这一效应独立于花粉限制。种子产量的下降在长花柱型中更为显著，而且两种花型之间的差异在较湿年份更加明显，这与下垂花朵中两种花型对雨水的暴露差异一致:长花柱型的柱头位于朝上的盗蜜孔下方，雨水可能在此积聚并淹没柱头；短花柱型的柱头虽然位于花冠筒更深处，但在空间位置上高于这一积水区域。 此外，合法访花和盗蜜对多个花部性状施加了复杂且相互作用的选择压力，其中盗蜜进一步强化了针对花冠长度的花型特异性分化选择。然而，无论合法访花或盗蜜单独作用，还是二者共同作用，都不能完全解释该性状的净选择格局，表明可能还存在其他选择因子。 观察性证据表明，盗蜜的开始与盗蜜发生前较高的降雨量、异常偏长的花冠以及次级盗蜜过程中较高的觅食效率相关，但这些关系仍属于推断性证据。 总之，本研究提供了实验证据，表明盗蜜可将花部损伤转化为降水介导的适合度代价，从而为理解盗蜜如何影响植物适合度提供了新的视角。更广泛地说，我们的结果表明，气候因子能够介导植物—访花者相互作用在互利—拮抗连续谱上的表现，并可能影响情境依赖的适应性演化轨迹。

articles.title: Scaling temperature‐dependent dispersal rates to metacommunity dynamics: An experimental test
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Changes in community structure under shifting thermal regimes depend on how both local population dynamics and regional dispersal respond to temperature. Processes underlying dispersal, such as movement speed and demographic density dependence, are constrained by temperature‐dependent metabolic rates; however, the temperature dependence of population dispersal rate, and effects of this relationship on local and regional diversity patterns, have received little attention in the metabolic scaling literature. Here, we propose and experimentally test a framework that relates temperature effects on individual dispersal probability, to thermal performance curves (TPCs) for population dispersal rates, to colonization dynamics in metacommunities. Using multi‐patch well plate microcosms, we measured TPCs for dispersal rate in several naturally co‐occurring ciliate species at different monoculture densities and in polyculture metacommunities. In monoculture metapopulations, the functional form of dispersal thermal responses differed at low (a few individuals) versus high (carrying capacity) population densities, and the strength of density‐dependent effects on dispersal rates varied unimodally with temperature. This may suggest distinct temperature effects on the density‐independent (individual movement speed and dispersal probability) and density‐dependent (quorum‐sensing and resource competition) components of population dispersal rate. In polyculture metacommunities, interspecific variation in dispersal TPCs explained differences in colonization dynamics and diversity patterns across temperature treatments. Species' dispersal rate TPCs differed from their growth rate TPCs; as a result, species with higher dispersal thermal optima had higher‐than‐expected per capita population growth at the regional scale compared with predictions from standard growth TPCs measured in single‐patch monoculture. Together, these results suggest that ignoring temperature‐dependent dispersal can yield an incomplete understanding of biodiversity change in spatially structured systems exposed to warming. articles.title: The oxygen uptake capacity of freshwater fish evolves to favour hypoxia tolerance in lentic species but locomotion capacity in lotic species
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Oxygen supply capacity (α) is a physiological trait hypothesized to shape the metabolic niche and biogeography of aquatic breathers, yet how natural selection targets α remains unclear. Two key fitness‐related traits—locomotor ability and hypoxia tolerance—both depend on α, yet whether this shared physiological basis leads to a functional coupling between these traits, or instead allows them to evolve independently under habitat‐specific selection, remains an open question. We therefore hypothesized that divergent selection pressures across flow regimes decouple these two traits, leading to habitat‐specific associations between α and each trait. To test this hypothesis, we measured α, hypoxia tolerance and swimming performance in 32 freshwater fish species from lentic and lotic habitats. Our results showed that the relationship between α and each trait varied with habitat type: in lotic species, α was strongly associated with enhanced swimming performance, reflecting selection for supporting the high metabolic demands of prolonged locomotion; in lentic species, α was linked to improved hypoxia tolerance, driven by adaptations to function effectively under low oxygen tensions. Overall, these findings provide insights into the evolutionary lability of α and validate it as a highly flexible, fitness‐related trait shaped by habitat‐specific selection. This highlights the role of interactions between shared physiological foundations and habitat‐specific selection in driving trait divergence, thereby offering a broader framework for understanding how physiological flexibility promotes biodiversity across heterogeneous environments. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 供氧能力(α)被认为是塑造水生生物代谢生态位与生物地理格局的核心生理指标，但自然选择如何作用于该性状尚不明确。运动能力和低氧耐受能力作为两类关键的适应性功能性状，均依赖于α这一共同的生理基础。然而，这一共同生理基础究竟是促成两性状的功能耦合，还是在生境特异性选择压力下各自独立演化，目前仍缺乏清晰的认识。 本研究基于不同水流条件所施加的分异选择压力，提出假说:运动能力与低氧耐受能力可发生功能解耦，并预测α与两性状之间将呈现出生境依赖性的关联模式。为验证该假说，我们选取静水与流水生境中32种淡水鱼类为研究对象，系统测定了其运动能力、低氧耐受能力及供氧能力。 结果显示，α与两性状的关联模式具有明确的生境依赖性。在流水物种中，α与运动能力紧密关联，表现为支持其持续运动所需的高代谢输出；而在静水物种中，α则与提升低氧耐受能力密切关联，表现为其在低氧分压环境下仍维持生理稳态。 本研究揭示了α作为生理性状的进化可塑性，证明α是一高度灵活、受生境特异性选择所塑造的适应性性状。研究进一步阐明α与环境选择压力之间的交互作用驱动功能性状分化的演化机制，并为理解生理灵活性在异质环境背景下促进生物多样性的机制提供了理论框架。

articles.title: Threat level and sound production mode modulate acoustic warnings and defensive biting in snakes
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Accurately assessing predation risk is important because it enables prey to match their defensive behaviours to the level of threat and avoid unnecessary investment in costly responses. According to the threat sensitivity hypothesis, prey should optimize the trade‐off between the costs of active defence and mortality risk by escalating their responses as danger increases. Yet, the transition from warning signals to physical confrontation remains largely understudied, particularly in relation to different acoustic signalling modes. We studied 220 individuals from 73 snake species representing four modes of acoustic warning production: two simple modes (hissing and tail vibration) and two highly specialized modes (rattling and scale rubbing). Individuals were exposed to three phases of escalating threat: a low‐threat phase without directed predator‐like stimulation, a medium‐threat phase involving visual stimulation and a high‐threat phase combining visual and tactile stimulation. Accounting for phylogeny, our findings supported the threat sensitivity hypothesis: both acoustic signalling investment and biting increased with perceived risk. Warning signals became longer and generally more intense as threat increased, while biting occurred primarily at the highest threat level. However, escalation patterns differed among sound production modes. Rattling and scale rubbing showed steeper increases in signal duration with threat than hissing, while tail vibration showed an intermediate pattern. Sound intensity also varied among modes: hissing increased throughout the escalation sequence, rattling increased overall but plateaued between the medium‐ and high‐threat phases, scale rubbing increased during the initial escalation before plateauing and tail vibration showed no significant modulation. Body mass also predicted physical defence, with larger individuals being less likely to engage in confrontation. Our results demonstrate that defensive responses in snakes are dynamic sequences in which acoustic warnings escalate with perceived risk and biting serves as a last‐resort tactic. They further show that the way acoustic signals escalate is shaped by their mode of production, highlighting the importance of considering signal‐production mechanisms when investigating threat‐sensitive defensive behaviour. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Tree species identity is associated with rhizosphere microbiome assembly via root metabolite‐mediated feedbacks in subtropical forests
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract The rhizosphere microbiome is critical for forest ecological functions, yet the mechanisms through which tree species identity and neighbour tree interactions are associated with its assembly remain poorly understood. Using Illumina MiSeq and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS), we investigated how tree species (pine vs. liquidambar) and forest composition (pure vs. mixed) shape rhizosphere microbial communities and root metabolites in subtropical forests. Rhizosphere fungal community structure differed significantly across rhizosphere types, whereas bacterial community and metabolite profiles differed primarily between the pure pine forest and other forest types. Predicted functional shifts included a decline in cellulolytic bacteria (−27%) and an increase in denitrifying groups (+54%), with ectomycorrhizal fungi enriched in mixed than pure forests (p < 0.05). Metabolite profiling revealed that lipids, organic acids and sugars were the most abundant compound classes, with 55 metabolites differentially abundant between pure pine and mixed forest rhizospheres. Rhizosphere metabolite profiles were significantly correlated with microbial community structure (p < 0.05). Specific microbe–metabolite associations were identified; fatty acids positively correlated with oligotrophic bacteria (WPS‐2), sugars with denitrifiers (Reyranella) and dipeptides with the beneficial fungus Penicillium. These results demonstrate that tree species identity is associated with rhizosphere microbiome assembly via root metabolite‐associated feedbacks, which correlate with soil nutrient cycling. This provides a mechanistic, function‐oriented framework for understanding plant–microbiome interaction and harnessing them to enhance ecosystem resilience. articles.title: When is the bait worth the risk? A mechanistic model of a compensatory ecological trap in seabirds
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Ecological traps occur when organisms preferentially select habitats that reduce fitness. In seabird–fishery systems, fishery‐derived trophic subsidies can increase foraging success, reinforce habitat preference and indirectly enhance reproductive output or recruitment, while bycatch simultaneously reduces survival. This subsidy–mortality coupling can generate a compensatory ecological trap when short‐term demographic benefits partly offset survival costs and obscure negative long‐term population consequences. We developed a spatially explicit, individual‐based model to evaluate how compensatory ecological traps emerge from the interplay among trophic subsidies, bycatch mortality and life‐history strategy. The model represented three seabird life‐history strategies—slow, intermediate and fast—and a trade‐off in which trophic subsidies increased energy intake and indirectly enhanced reproductive performance, whereas repeated use of subsidised risky cells increased mortality. Population responses were non‐linear and reflected the joint effects of subsidy level, mortality risk and life history. When mortality risk in subsidised cells was low, trophic subsidies increased population size, particularly in faster life‐history strategies. However, once mortality exceeded life‐history‐specific thresholds, subsidies continued to promote the use of risky areas, increasing exposure to trap mortality and shifting population responses from growth to decline or extinction. Short‐term improvements in reproductive performance sometimes produced transient population growth. Under equivalent behavioural, energetic and subsidy–mortality conditions, slow, albatross‐like life‐history strategies were most vulnerable in terms of long‐term persistence, whereas faster strategies were more resilient and better able to translate additional food intake into positive demographic responses. Trap configuration further modulated these outcomes: negative responses intensified when subsidised risky areas were larger or located in high‐energy habitat. Our results extend ecological‐trap theory by showing how immediate habitat benefits, such as enhanced foraging success, can generate trade‐offs among fitness components and alter trap outcomes across the slow–fast life‐history continuum. They also highlight the need to manage bycatch and trophic subsidies jointly, because their combined effects can reinforce maladaptive habitat selection, increase exposure to mortality and elevate extinction risk. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Resumen Las trampas ecológicas ocurren cuando los organismos seleccionan preferentemente hábitats que reducen su adecuación biológica. En los sistemas de interacción entre aves marinas y pesquerías, los subsidios tróficos derivados de la pesca pueden aumentar el éxito de forrajeo, reforzar la preferencia por determinados hábitats y mejorar indirectamente el rendimiento reproductivo o el reclutamiento, mientras que la captura incidental reduce simultáneamente la supervivencia. Este acoplamiento entre subsidios y mortalidad puede generar una trampa ecológica compensatoria cuando los beneficios demográficos a corto plazo compensan parcialmente los costos en supervivencia y enmascaran consecuencias poblacionales negativas a largo plazo. Desarrollamos un modelo individual espacialmente explícito para evaluar cómo emergen las trampas ecológicas compensatorias a partir de la interacción entre los subsidios tróficos, la mortalidad por captura incidental y la estrategia de historia de vida. El modelo representó tres estrategias de historia de vida de aves marinas —lenta, intermedia y rápida— y un compromiso en el que los subsidios tróficos aumentaron la ingesta energética y mejoraron indirectamente el rendimiento reproductivo, mientras que el uso repetido de celdas riesgosas subsidiadas incrementó la mortalidad.…

articles.title: Abundance Redistribution Increases Predator‐Prey Interaction Potentials Among North American Birds
articles.abstract: Species are shifting their geographical ranges, yet the consequences of these spatial redistributions for species interactions have not been examined at broad spatial and temporal scales. Here, we characterize shifts in the potential for predator‐prey interactions among North American birds over the past 50 years. We first predict potential predator‐prey interactions based on existing data, then construct a novel, abundance‐weighted metric of interaction potential for each pair of predator and prey species in local communities. We found nearly universal increases in predator‐prey interaction potentials across North America that are mostly driven by increases in predator abundances. The spatial redistributions of predators and prey lead to turnover of interactions within local communities that are less associated with changes in climate than with human‐induced land use changes. Our results highlight the importance of considering traits, abundances, and species interactions—including known and potential interactions—when studying the ecological consequences of range shifts.

articles.title: Divergent Patterns of Interactions Between Dissolved Organic Matter and Microbial Communities in Mangroves and Salt Marshes
articles.abstract: Mangroves and salt marshes are major blue carbon reservoirs, where dissolved organic matter (DOM) dynamics are co‐regulated by primary production, microbial transformation, and environmental conditions. Understanding whether these two coastal wetlands exhibit fundamentally different DOM–microbe interaction patterns is critical for assessing blue carbon functioning. However, such interactions and their environmental determinants remain unclear. Here, we conduct a continental‐scale comparison between mangroves and salt marshes spanning ~5000 km of China's coastline to elucidate the linkages between DOM molecules and microbial communities. DOM and bacterial β‐diversity are positively correlated in both wetlands, but their respective distance–decay relationships are significant only in salt marshes. DOM–microbe co‐occurrence networks are bacteria‐dominated in both wetlands, but are more complex and positively linked in mangroves, whereas negatively linked in salt marshes. DOM‐gene networks show that carbon fixation and methanogenesis genes are primarily associated with recalcitrant DOM in mangroves, but with labile DOM in salt marshes. Soil pH, together with mean annual temperature, dissolved organic carbon, soil organic carbon, total nitrogen, and amorphous calcium, collectively influence the divergences in DOM composition, microbial community structure, and carbon metabolic functions. These findings offer key insights into DOM–microbe interaction mechanisms and their divergent patterns across “blue carbon” ecosystems.

articles.title: Adoption of Adjunctive Azithromycin for Unscheduled Cesarean Delivery and Postpartum Infections

articles.abstract: This Medical News article discusses the increase in routine cannabis use among younger adults, which corresponds with a decrease in regular alcohol use.

articles.title: Azithromycin for Cesarean Delivery
articles.abstract: Preventing maternal morbidity and mortality remains an urgent global priority, yet progress has been unsatisfactory. Although maternal mortality has declined globally, the rates have increased in the US and infections are among the top causes of preventable deaths. Among women undergoing cesarean delivery (the most common major surgical procedure in the US), the risk of infection is many times higher than after vaginal delivery, underscoring the importance of effective prophylaxis.

articles.title: BORG Trend May Promote Alcohol-Related Harms Among College Students
articles.abstract: A recent college drinking trend known as the “blackout rage gallon” (BORG) may promote high-intensity drinking and alcohol-related harm, a study suggests.

articles.title: Beyond the Trial—What Do Extension Studies Add to Randomized Clinical Trials?
articles.abstract: One critical shortcoming of many clinical therapeutic trials is their focus on short-term effects, leaving unanswered questions about how participants fare in the longer term. Trial extension studies are conducted to address this gap, allowing assessment of both durability of treatment benefit (eg, whether disease remission or improvements in function are maintained or diminished over time) and long-term safety (such as incidence of delayed adverse events). In therapeutic trials, extension studies can mitigate the ethical burden associated with discontinuation of potentially effective treatments or long-term administration of placebo or inferior interventions among those initially assigned to the control group. The prospect of an extension study may also give participants greater incentive to enroll in trials, despite concerns about being assigned to the control group in the initial phase of the research. Because extension studies build on existing trial infrastructure, they also allow additional and potentially valuable information to be derived from trials that already require significant up-front investment.

articles.title: Catching Up With the Propaganda for Health
articles.abstract: Any one who reads popular periodicals or follows the current trends in folk psychology and national habits of thought can readily discover the growing popular enthusiasm for the conservation of health. Obviously, all matters of health and disease are of foremost concern to the physician; in him rests the largest public obligation as well as personal necessity of keeping abreast not only of the discoveries that bear on diagnosis and treatment but also of the features somewhat indefinitely described as preventive medicine. Every professional organization to which he belongs is in some way identified with the program of modern public hygiene.

articles.title: Communicating With Families About Brain Death
articles.abstract: This JAMA Insights discusses suggested language for clinicians to use when communicating with families about brain death evaluation and determination.

articles.title: Conversational Consent
articles.abstract: In this narrative medicine essay, a pediatrician reflects back on difficult conversations with parents of patients and stresses the importance of conversational consent as a way to initiate and advance medical conversations with empathy and respect.

articles.title: Digital Outreach to Improve Statin Refills in Patients With Low Statin Adherence

articles.title: Error in Results
articles.abstract: The Original Investigation titled “Adjuvant Nivolumab vs Observation in Resected Non–Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial,” published on June 1, 2026, was corrected to fix typographical errors in the text, including indicating that the trial was stopped for futility at 75% information, rather than 78%, and the number of participants lost to follow-up in the nivolumab group in Figure 1. This article was corrected online.

articles.title: Eternal life
articles.abstract: I spent the afternoon Checking RIP.ie To see if people my father had known had died As he sat in the armchair across from me. We found three people And Dad looked into their photos On my phone to see if they Were the people he remembered. It didn’t feel morbid But sad; It’s bad enough being the last of Your group alive, But not to know if they were alive or dead, Even 20 years after you had stood at their graveside was probably worse, Or maybe not— Maybe if you couldn’t remember if anyone had died You were already living beyond the Realm of death, You were in a kind of everlasting life Where no one really ever died to you, They could be dead one minute But then the next they would be there with you, You saw them in some last untouched memory— Offering you the jar of sugar across the table, Smiling at you from the porch as you returned a key— A last untouched memory That kept giving them back to you Eternally

articles.title: FDA Authorizes First Continuous Ketone Monitor for Diabetes

articles.title: Gastric Residual Volume Assessment in Critically Ill Children
articles.abstract: To the Editor The GASTRIC-PICU landmark trial addressed a long-standing, weakly evidenced practice in pediatric intensive care. The case for deimplementing routine gastric residual volume (GRV) assessment will likely change bedside care. We raise 2 points that may further strengthen the interpretation of this study.

articles.title: Health Care’s Identity Crisis—Is Medicine Still a Profession?
articles.abstract: This Perspective discusses the misalignment physicians face between their professionalism-based values and the conditions of practice that are influenced by pressures from market, managerial, and platform logics, and offers suggestions to align practice conditions and professional identity.
