articles.abstract: In this work, we have presented S-I-S Josephson junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ barrier. We grew base and top $α$-Ta electrodes using seed layer engineering, showing both Nb and ${\rm TaN}_x$ are viable seed layer choices, and particularly emphasize that at room temperature a re-seed layer is required to nucleate $\rmα$-Ta for the top electrode. However, we note that the choice of seed layer can have subtle implications on the electrical tunneling behavior of the junctions. We used room-temperature probing of variable junction areas, combined with Ambegaokar-Baratoff physics, to characterize the wafer scale critical current densities. For 0.4 $μ$m$^2$ junctions, we found junction spreads as low as 2.0% across the 20 x 20 mm chip relevant for device performance. The entire process was carried out using standard industry foundry processing using 150 mm wafer tooling, which is an important step towards proving that Ta-based junctions can be implemented at scale. We have successfully fabricated and tested junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ insulating tunnel barrier, demonstrating that this is a material platform which merits further investigation and studies for potential application in classical and quantum superconducting technologies.

articles.title: Thermally enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3
articles.abstract: Strong coupling between collective excitations provides a route to controlling quantum states of matter, yet its evolution under thermal fluctuations remains poorly understood. In the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3, strong magnon-phonon coupling is established at low temperatures. At the same time, recent terahertz experiments revealed the counterintuitive stabilization of a long-lived metastable magnetic state with an exceedingly long lifetime of 5 msec at the antiferromagnetic transition, not at the base temperature. This was attributed to a strongly coupled spin-lattice scenario, challenging the conventional wisdom that increased magnetic and thermal fluctuations near TN should be detrimental to the coherent control of a metastable phase. Thus it requires an independent examination for correct understanding. Using high-field Raman spectroscopy, we systematically investigate the temperature evolution of magnon-phonon coupling in FePS3. We observe a pronounced avoided crossing between magnon and phonon modes across a wide range of temperatures and find that the coupling strength remains remarkably robust with increasing temperatures. The zero-field magnon-phonon detuning decreases progressively with warming, driving the system toward resonance and thereby enhancing their hybridization near the transition temperature. This anomalous thermal evolution provides the crucial key to understanding the unusual terahertz-driven states recently reported in FePS3. More broadly, our results highlight van der Waals magnets as a promising platform for strong coupling among collective excitations and for controlling magnetic states through light-matter interactions.

articles.title: Torsion, valley holonomy, and Berry phases of quasiparticles encircling dislocations and defect complexes in graphene
articles.abstract: We investigate the geometric phase acquired by low-energy quasiparticles encircling defects in graphene. Following Anandan, this phase is the holonomy of the Poincare connection; its translational part couples momentum to torsion, giving $P_a\int T^a$. In the Katanaev-Volovich theory, dislocation torsion is confined to the defect core. For graphene, the relevant momentum is $\hbar(τ_3\KK+\mathbf q)$. We show that an isolated dislocation yields a topological valley factor $e^{\mp2πi/3}$ when its Burgers vector $\bb$ lies outside the $\sqrt3\times\sqrt3$ superlattice, together with a dispersive factor $e^{-i\mathbf q\cdot\bb}$ for every nonzero $\bb$. The topological factor recovers the lattice result of Mesaros et al. as a torsion-flux phase; 4-8 dislocations retain only the dispersive contribution. Composing Volterra elements gives the holonomy of defect complexes. At zero net Frank angle, it depends only on the net Burgers vector. The valley flux obeys a three-coloring rule: pentagons and heptagons contribute according to their Kekule site color, whereas squares and octagons do not. Atomic models confirm that ring content alone does not fix the phase: a 5-8-5 core is invisible as a divacancy or as a dislocation with $|\bb|=\sqrt3a$, but carries flux $\pm1/3$ for $\bb=2\mathbf a_1$. The torsion trace produces no geometric phase: its vector coupling violates time-reversal symmetry, while the allowed axial coupling causes only anisotropic short-range scattering.

articles.title: Toward a Quantum Information Foundation for Neutron Scattering
articles.abstract: Neutron scattering is a central probe of quantum materials, yet what quantum information can, in principle, be extracted from a scattering experiment remains unclear. Here we formulate neutron scattering as a quantum measurement, with the scattering amplitudes acting as Kraus operators on the material state. This provides a unified description of conventional intensity, coherent scattering, interferometric measurements, and entanglement witnesses, including those based on quantum Fisher information. We then ask how far this connection can be extended to nonlinear properties of a quantum state. For two independently prepared samples, we derive the general structure of probe-mediated measurement probabilities and show that, for spin-projection-conserving dynamics, low-order scattering cannot resolve certain many-body coherences required to determine purity. Conversely, an idealized single-spin protocol shows how probe-mediated exchange can access purity when the appropriate two-copy operation is realized. Our results establish a quantum-information description of neutron scattering and delineate the information accessible through conventional and interferometric measurements.

articles.title: Why strong spin-orbit coupling does not destabilize the Dirac spin liquid in the Yb delafossites
articles.abstract: The Yb delafossites NaYbSe$_2$, KYbSe$_2$, CsYbSe$_2$ and NaYbO$_2$ are candidates for the U(1) Dirac spin liquid (DSL) of the triangular lattice. Strong spin-orbit coupling gives their exchange an XXZ anisotropy $Δ$ and bond-dependent couplings $J_{\pm\pm}$, $J_{z\pm}$ that lock the spin frame to the lattice. We show that, within a single layer of a stable Heisenberg DSL, these couplings generate no relevant Lorentz-scalar operator of their own. Inversion at the bond centers removes the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya channel that gaps the kagome DSL, so the locked symmetry forbids a mass, density or current at any order and, assuming continuity, any new monopole term through charge three. Every Lorentz-scalar four-fermion operator induced by spin-orbit coupling shares an SU(4) multiplet, and hence its scaling dimension, with a Heisenberg-allowed one, and the nine non-scalar quartics without such a partner arise only at second order and are irrelevant at large $N$. The Heisenberg DSL itself allows a Lorentz-vector quartic of large-$N$ dimension 2.92, which a stable phase must also render irrelevant. Beyond a single layer, spin-orbit coupling opens an interlayer monopole channel in rhombohedral stacking. If the Heisenberg DSL is instead multicritical, an anisotropy as small as that of KYbSe$_2$ matters only below tens of mK. At the transition to 120$^\circ$ order the anisotropy is relevant, and exact diagonalization indicates that easy-plane anisotropy selects the chiral-Ising class. Existing KYbSe$_2$ neutron data below $J$ do not yet fix the K-point exponent, and gapless out-of-plane spin fluctuations at the K point would test the chiral-Ising selection.

articles.title: greenWTE: Frequency-domain solver for the phonon Wigner Transport Equation with arbitrary heating using Green's functions
articles.abstract: Heat transport in solids is usually described in a phenomenological way via Fourier's law. However, at small time and length scales in low thermal conductivity materials, a microscopic description is needed. This is traditionally done by invoking the phonon Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE), which has been successful in describing transport in high thermal conductivity materials. Recently, a generalization of the BTE, the Wigner Transport Equation, was developed to be able to microscopically describe transport in low thermal conductivity materials by taking into account not only phonon scattering processes but also phonon tunneling processes, so-called coherences. We present a Python package that solves the Wigner Transport Equation (WTE) in spatial and temporal Fourier space for arbitrary source terms, thereby enabling the study of heat transport at small space and time scales. This allows one to compute both static and dynamic thermal conductivities from bulk to nanoscale. Beyond that, it can be used to study the response of phonon systems in materials to arbitrary heat sources.

articles.title: Analog signal processing, storage, and demultiplexing via in-materia wave-based computing
articles.abstract: The ability of mechanical systems to perform basic computations has gained traction in recent years, providing a robust supplement to digital computing in off-grid, low-power, and extreme environments where electronics are inaccessible or risk failure. However, prior work has focused on Boolean logic applied via bistable structures, snap-through mechanisms, or origami lattices. Digital signal processing (DSP) underpins a wide range of computational tasks, providing the foundation for information encoding, manipulation, and analysis. In contrast to conventional DSP approaches, we present a new paradigm for analog information processing, where an elastic substrate houses a spatial wave-based platform for mechanical signal manipulation in the temporal domain. The proposed metasurface-based system exploits temperature-dependent phase transitions of shape memory alloys (SMAs) to realize key signal-processing functionalities, including gating, retention, and programmable delay of impinging mechanical loads. In doing so, we address a new set of challenges by manipulating transient mechanical waves through dispersive and lossy media. Building on this capability, we introduce the concept of mechanical wave-based memory, in which a locally resonant metamaterial's dispersion characteristics are actively reconfigured to achieve programmable delays while preserving spatial waveform integrity, and demonstrate its utility in the context of input shaping and frequency demultiplexing of superimposed waves. More broadly, the modular and scalable nature of the demonstrated framework paves the way for advanced mechanical computing architectures, enabling higher-order operations such as signal classification, parallel processing, and reservoir computing through the controlled sequencing and temporal alignment of mechanical signals.

articles.title: Autonomous cooling of Kerr-cat qubits to minutes-long bit-flip times
articles.abstract: Quantum error correction becomes more hardware efficient when physical noise is strongly biased towards one error channel. Cat qubits realize such a bias by encoding information in two opposite coherent states of a superconducting oscillator, so that bit flips are exponentially suppressed with photon number while phase-flip rates increase only linearly. In Kerr-cat qubits, a driven double-well potential confines these states and enables fast coherent control, but excitations can induce interwell switching, limiting bit-flip times to milliseconds. Here we show that the nonlinear interaction generating the confinement can also cool these excitations. When an intra-well transition becomes resonant with a lossy readout mode, excitations are transferred out of the qubit and dissipated, as established by spectroscopy and relaxation measurements. We observe the predicted exponential scaling of Kerr-cat bit-flip times with photon number, reaching 450 s, over five orders of magnitude beyond previous demonstrations. Phase-flip rates remain consistent with intrinsic photon loss at operating points with seconds-long bit-flip times. We further demonstrate fast Z gates without measurable degradation of bit-flip protection and single-shot readout with a bit-flip probability below $10^{-6}$ per measurement. Autonomous cooling thus brings minutes-long bit-flip protection to Kerr-cat qubits while retaining fast coherent control, without additional cooling drives or circuit elements.

articles.title: Bayesian optimization enhanced magnetic field gradient detection based on spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates
articles.abstract: Magnetic field detection is of great significance in modern fields such as medical diagnostics, geological exploration, inertial navigation, and space physics. We have previously investigated the expansion dynamics of a spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensate. Building on these results, here we propose a scheme for magnetic-field-gradient detection by establishing a quantitative relationship between the condensate's rotational deflection angle and the magnetic-field gradient. In this work, we present the parameter dependence of this scheme and perform a systematic optimization. We introduce a Bayesian optimization algorithm to automatically and efficiently search for the optimal combination of key parameters, thereby significantly enhancing the sensitivity of the magnetic field gradient measurement. The results show that the optimized gradiometer improves the sensitivity by a factor of five. This work not only provides a new approach for magnetic field gradient measurement but also serves as a reference for machine learning-empowered quantum precision measurement.

articles.title: Breakdown of Linearized Dispersion in Waveguide QED
articles.abstract: Exploring interactions between quantum emitters and guided photons, waveguide quantum electrodynamics (wQED) offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation and quantum interconnect. To simplify the quantized light-matter interactions, a linearized dispersion approximation (LDA) was widely used in wQED under the conditions of weak coupling and narrow photonic bandwidth. However, a growing number of strong-coupling wQED experiments have called the validity of LDA into question. Here, by investigating giant atoms coupled to a semi-infinite waveguide, we propose a principle to judge the validity of LDA. We find that the decoherence of the atoms exhibits rich dynamical behaviors determined by different numbers of bound states in and out of the continuum (BICs and BOCs) formed in the energy spectrum of the total atom-photon system. Based on this, we show that despite the LDA can partially preserve some of BICs, it completely erases BOCs. This causes the dominant role of LDA in the atomic dynamics to break down. Providing a physical insight into the validity of LDA, our results lay a firm foundation for exploring fundamental physics and its application frontier in strong-coupling wQED platforms.

articles.title: Breaking the quantum barriers for Graph Collision
articles.abstract: In the graph collision problem, the task is to decide whether a known graph on $n$ vertices contains an edge with both endpoints marked, given query access to the input bits specifying the marked vertices. We first refute the conjectured $Ω(n^{2/3})$ query lower bound with a bounded error quantum algorithm using $\widetilde O(n^{92/139})$ queries. We then refine this approach to obtain a $\widetilde O(n^{11/17})$ query algorithm. We also obtain a $\widetilde O((nq)^{11/17})$ query bound for all (partial) Boolean output functions with positive certificate complexity at most 2 and alphabet size $q$, contrasting a known $Ω(n^{2/3})$ lower bound for such problems with large alphabet sizes. We complement these algorithms with an $Ω(\sqrt{n\log n})$ quantum query lower bound for graph collision, exceeding the $O(\sqrt n)$ certificate complexity barrier for the positive adversary method.

articles.title: Bulk and edge states in Fibonacci-Bose-Hubbard clusters
articles.abstract: We study the one- and two-boson energy subspaces of finite open Bose--Hubbard chains with Fibonacci-modulated hopping and zero on-site potential. Their spectra exhibit a hierarchy of bands and gaps, and a critical zero-energy mode for odd lengths, in agreement with prior research. For the singe-excitation subspace we find two families of length-invariant finite-energy states localized at the left cluster boundary. For the two-boson subspace, we report both doublon and separated-pair excitations in the form of Tamm/Shockley states localized near either end. In particular, the right-edge doublon states occur across all Fibonacci generations whereas the left-side states appear every second generation. We check numerically that the second-order perturbation theory accounts well for the structure of the spectrum and the edge states in the doublon subspace in the strong-coupling regime. The results are useful for future explorations of many-body physics beyond numerical tractability, specifically using near-term Josephson quantum simulators.

articles.title: Comment on "Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings" (arXiv:2610.26833)
articles.abstract: We discuss the relationship between quantum Hamiltonian embeddings (arXiv:2610.26833) and prior developments in Quantum Cognition Machine Learning (QCML), including QCML's earlier implementation on IBM quantum hardware. We consider the novelty claims and the computational role of encoding an entire dataset in a single ground state.

articles.title: A validated antibody toolbox for ALS research
articles.abstract: A substantial fraction of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)-associated proteins remains poorly characterized, in part because of the limited availability of validated research antibodies. We established knockout (KO)-based antibody characterization workflows and demonstrated that widely used antibodies against the major ALS-associated protein C9orf72 lacked specificity (Laflamme et al., 2019). We subsequently scaled this framework to systematically benchmark research antibodies, revealing that up to 61% fail to perform as recommended by manufacturers (Ayoubi et al., 2023b). Here, we extend this approach by establishing the ALS-Reproducible Antibody Platform (ALS-RAP), a comprehensive effort to generate a publicly available dataset of KO-validated antibodies targeting proteins encoded by ALS risk genes. In total, we characterized 303 antibodies against 33 ALS-associated proteins to identify high-quality reagents for use in western blot, immunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence. Using these antibodies, we profiled protein levels across human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived and primary neurological cell types. These analyses revealed diverse cellular distributions and higher levels of several ALS-associated proteins in glial populations, consistent with emerging evidence for immune contributions to ALS. Together, ALS-RAP provides a validated antibody toolbox and protein expression resource to support the study of ALS-associated proteins.

articles.title: Class-wide sequence, structural, and docking-profile diversity of insect odorant receptors and structural specialization of Orco
articles.abstract: Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor–odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. Here, we integrated sequence similarity, structural similarity, and molecular docking to analyze ORs from 115 insect species. OR repertoire size was associated with adult diet, larval diet, and habitat, but not with circadian rhythm. We developed a ‘trunk–branch’ network framework to classify ORs according to sequence and structural similarity and used large-scale molecular docking to derive comparative docking profiles. Despite marked differences in sequence- and structural-community composition, almost all sampled orders contained ORs assigned to all six docking-profile communities. Holometabolous insects showed higher OR sequence-community diversity than non-holometabolous insects, and docking-profile composition differed between extant lineages whose order-level origins predate or postdate the end-Permian mass extinction. Most notably, we identified a highly conserved extracellular β-sheet in Orco that restricts ligand access to the binding pocket and may contribute to its reduced capacity to bind natural odorants. The emergence of Orco represents a key evolutionary transition from homomeric receptors to heteromeric OR–Orco complexes, and our results suggest that this transition may have been accompanied by pronounced specialization of the extracellular domain and binding pocket. Together, these analyses provide a class-wide framework for comparing insect OR diversity and generate testable hypotheses for future experimental and evolutionary studies.

articles.title: Impacts of mutation accumulation and order on tumor initiation revealed by engineered murine colorectal cancer organoids
articles.abstract: Tumorigenesis typically follows a multi-hit trajectory, driven by accumulating oncogenic mutations. Colorectal cancer (CRC) has long served as a paradigmatic model of multi-hit tumorigenesis, characterized by adenoma-carcinoma transition accompanied by acquisition of specific oncogene and tumor suppressor mutations. However, how the temporal order of early mutations influences CRC initiation remains poorly understood. To address this, we established a CRC tumorigenesis model using murine intestinal organoids. By introducing defined combinations of key CRC driver mutations (Kras, Apc, and Trp53) in distinct orders, we systematically investigated how the order of mutation accumulation affects tumor initiation. Our results reveal that the mutation accumulation confers growth advantages in both in vitro and in vivo models. Strikingly, mutation order also influenced the tumorigenic properties of the organoids. Whereas organoids with Trp53 loss before or after Apc loss similarly affected organoid phenotypes in vitro or tumorigenicity in immunodeficient mice, organoids with Trp53 loss preceding Apc inactivation exhibited reduced tumor-forming potential in immunocompetent mice, likely due to their distinct immunological features. Collectively, our study reveals a critical role of ordered mutation accumulation in CRC initiation, an insight that may hold clinical relevance.

articles.title: Spyglass is a framework for reproducible and shareable neuroscience research
articles.abstract: Scientific progress depends on reliable and reproducible results. Progress can be accelerated when data are shared and re-analyzed to address new questions. Current approaches to storing and analyzing neural data involve bespoke formats and software that make replication and reuse of data difficult. To address these challenges, we created Spyglass, an open-source data management and analysis framework written in Python. Spyglass provides reproducible pipelines for common neuroscience analyses and sharing of raw data, intermediate analyses, and final results within and across labs. Spyglass uses the Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) standard and includes pipelines for spectral filtering, spike sorting, pose tracking, and neural decoding. Spyglass can be extended to apply existing and newly developed pipelines to datasets from multiple sources. We demonstrate these features in the context of a cross-laboratory replication by applying advanced state space decoding algorithms to publicly available data. New users can try out Spyglass on a Jupyter Hub hosted by HHMI and 2i2c: https://spyglass.hhmi.2i2c.cloud/.

articles.title: Deciphering Complex Interfacial Dynamics via Operando Microbalance during Potential-Modulated Alkyne Hydrogenation
articles.abstract: Applied potentials can alter heterogeneous catalysis, but the roles of ions, solvent, and reactants at the polarized catalyst-electrolyte interface remain unclear. Here, we track potential-driven interfacial mass redistribution during aqueous Pd-catalyzed alkynol semi-hydrogenation using an operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance (EQCM). By combining gravimetric measurements with a volumetric occupancy model, we quantify the competitive redistribution of ions, reactants, and hydrogen at the solid-liquid interface. The results show that hydrated Na+ promotes cathodic interfacial mass accumulation, forming a cation-bridged microenvironment that enriches alkynol and limits H2 availability. Positive polarization disrupts this microenvironment, promotes product removal, and restores surface hydrogen. Based on these results, we developed an oscillating potential program (100 s at –0.9 V, 20 s at +0.5 V) to control reactant enrichment, product removal, and hydrogen availability, increasing alkenol selectivity from ∼50% to 97% while enhancing activity by 173%.

articles.title: Divergent Reactivity toward Decarboxylative Protonation or Oxidation via Single-Component Organocatalysis
articles.abstract: Decarboxylative protonation/deuteration provides a powerful strategy for removing carboxylic acid handles and installing C–H/D bonds. However, existing catalytic methods typically rely on separate components to conduct the necessary proton-transfer, electron-transfer, and hydrogen-atom-transfer steps, restricting substrate scope and scalability. Herein we report a single-catalyst platform for decarboxylative protonation/deuteration that is broadly tolerant of carboxylic acids and readily scalable to 100 mmol in flow. Diarylquinoline organocatalysts function simultaneously as the base, photo-oxidant, and hydrogen-atom donor, demonstrating an underexplored reactivity mode for photocatalysts in which reductive quenching occurs by facilitating C–H bond formation rather than conventional electron transfer processes. Mechanistic studies indicate that oxidation is achieved through proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), resulting in high chemoselectivity for carboxylic acid activation. Hammett analysis reveals that catalyst electronics strongly influence the reaction rate, and an uncommon inverse kinetic isotope effect provides evidence for a turnover-limiting, hydrogen-bonded transition state. Finally, reactivity can be diverted toward decarboxylative oxidation to form carbonyl compounds simply by changing the reaction atmosphere, offering versatile synthetic control.

articles.title: Exploring Liquid Metals as Dynamic Reaction Media
articles.abstract: Liquid metals often exhibit enhanced catalytic performance owing to their inherent characteristics, including the facile preparation of liquid alloys, atomic dispersion of dissolved elements, high-entropy surface structures, adaptive atomic configurations, and resistance to coking. These features fundamentally distinguish liquid metals from their solid counterparts, which possess fixed atomic arrangements. The transient geometries and electronic properties of liquid atoms within a dynamic matrix increase the possibility to align with various reactants, enabling energy-favorable adsorption patterns and reaction pathways. The catalytic properties of liquid media can be tuned by regulating the dissolved components and/or combining with other functional species. To date, a variety of bond dissociation and formation reactions, centering on C–C, C–H, C–O, C=C, C–N, and C–Cl, have been achieved using liquid metal media. The distinctive catalytic phenomena and the underlying mechanisms associated with liquid metals challenge the conventional understanding of catalysis based on solid-state catalysts. The use of liquid metal media for chemical reactions remains at an early stage, offering great opportunities for future exploration.

articles.title: Hydroxyl-Directed Anchoring and Electronic Structure of Pt–Sn on γ-Al2O3 for Propane Dehydrogenation
articles.abstract: Although γ-Al2O3-supported Pt–Sn catalysts are central to industrial propane dehydrogenation (PDH), conventional support design has primarily focused on structural properties, largely overlooking the role of surface hydroxyl chemistry in governing metal–support interactions. Here, we show that the distribution of surface hydroxyl types strongly affects Pt–Sn anchoring, particle growth, and performance of the catalyst supported on γ-Al2O3. By hydrothermally tailoring AlOOH precursors and exploiting a topotactic phase transition, three γ-Al2O3 supports (Al2O3-AIP, Al2O3-NP, and Al2O3-NF) with distinct distributions of terminal μ1-OH and doubly bridged μ2-OH sites were prepared. Systematic characterization showed that the hydroxyl-rich Al2O3-NP and Al2O3-NF supports produced substantially smaller Pt–Sn particles than Al2O3-AIP. Spectroscopic trends suggest preferential involvement of acidic μ1-OH sites at lower precursor loadings and progressively greater involvement of μ2-OH sites as the μ1-OH sites approached saturation. The μ2-OH-enriched surfaces favored precursor anchoring associated with highly dispersed Pt–Sn clusters (∼0.6 nm) after reduction. In propane dehydrogenation at 580 °C, the μ2-OH-enriched 0.5Pt–1.3Sn/Al2O3-NF catalyst achieved an initial propane conversion of 60% while maintaining a propylene selectivity above 97%. Site-occupancy experiments and C3H6-DRIFTS further suggest that precursor anchoring involving μ2-OH sites is associated with improved Pt–Sn dispersion and weaker propylene adsorption. These results show that controlling surface hydroxyl types can regulate metal anchoring and particle growth in Al2O3-supported dehydrogenation catalysts.

articles.title: Kinetic Multi-reaction Model of Platinum Nanoparticle Oxidation and Cathodic Dissolution in a Wide Potential Window
articles.abstract: Mathematical modeling provides a powerful framework for understanding and mitigating degradation in catalyst materials such as platinum nanoparticles. A hallmark of platinum degradation during voltage cycling is the appearance of two distinct maxima in the dissolved Pt concentration: a smaller peak upon increasing potential and a larger peak upon decreasing potential. To explain this observation, we propose a kinetic multi-reaction model of Pt nanoparticle oxidation and dissolution, which describes dissolution as an interplay between direct electrochemical dissolution, passivation of the Pt surface, and the electrochemical dissolution of Pt oxides. The model is calibrated using cyclic voltammograms and time traces of Pt ion concentrations measured for two Pt catalyst samples with different nanoparticle sizes and different supports (carbon-supported 3 nm and unsupported 30 nm particles). The model results show very good agreement with the experimental data and indicate that the dissolution dynamics are indeed governed by oxide surface passivation and dissolution. Furthermore, comparison of results for different catalysts shows that the observed differences in Pt dissolution arise not only from variations in reaction rates on particles of different sizes but also from differences in the catalysts’ microscopic structure, which significantly influence Pt loss through diffusion.

articles.title: Mechanistic Insights into Cobalt-Catalyzed Kumada C(sp2)–C(sp2) Cross-Coupling Enabled by High-Denticity Cobalt(I) Intermediates
articles.abstract: Understanding the role of low-valent cobalt species in cross-coupling catalysis remains a central challenge, particularly in distinguishing two-electron organometallic pathways from radical-based mechanisms. Herein, we report the isolation and comprehensive characterization of cobalt(II) and cobalt(I) intermediates supported by a tetradentate diazapyridinophane (tBuN4) ligand and elucidate their roles in Kumada cross-coupling reactions. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal partial ligand-centered reduction in the “Co(I)” species, which function as single-electron initiators for halogen atom transfer from aryl bromides. Mechanistic investigations suggest that the resulting aryl radicals follow two distinct pathways: solvent-mediated hydrogen atom transfer leading to protodehalogenation, or interception by Grignard reagents to form C(sp2)–C(sp2) bonds through an SRN1-type mechanism (radical-nucleophilic aromatic substitution). Overall, these findings establish a radical-mediated framework for Co-catalyzed Kumada coupling and highlight ligand denticity as a key factor in governing reaction pathways.

articles.title: Spatial Coupling of Metal and Acid Sites via Amorphous Nb–O–Al Interfaces for Selective Polyolefin Hydrocracking
articles.abstract: Hydrocracking of polyolefin waste into liquid fuels over bifunctional catalysts requires efficient synergy between metal sites for H2 activation and acid sites for C–C bond cleavage. However, on nonzeolitic, oxide-based supports, these two functionalities are typically distributed in a random manner, limiting their spatial proximity and, consequently, the overall catalytic efficiency. Herein, we report an interface-design strategy that enforces nanoscale spatial coupling between metal and acid sites within a single structural unit, specifically tailored for polyolefin hydrocracking. The catalyst comprises highly dispersed rhodium (Rh) species anchored on an amorphous NbOx-doped γ-Al2O3 support. The amorphous Nb–O–Al interfaces generate electron-deficient Nb centers that function as medium-strong Lewis acid sites, while simultaneously modulating the electronic and coordination environment of the adjacent Rh species responsible for H2 activation. The nanoscale proximity of these complementary sites facilitates the coupling of acid-mediated C–C bond transformation with the subsequent hydrogenation of reactive intermediates. When applied to the hydrocracking of low-density polyethylene under mild conditions (240 °C, 2 MPa H2), the optimized Rh/10Nb–Al catalyst achieves a liquid product space-time yield of 283 gliquid·gmetal–1·h–1 with a methane selectivity of only 0.77%. Quantitative analysis reveals a linear correlation between the density of these interfacial strong Lewis acid sites and the hydrocracking activity, thereby directly linking the catalytic performance to the interfacial structure. This study establishes interfacial engineering as a rational strategy to encode metal–acid intimacy into the catalyst architecture, thereby offering a general design principle for selective plastic-to-fuel conversion.

articles.title: Synergistic Catalysis of Single-Site Rhenium and Ruthenium Nanoclusters for Ammonia Synthesis under Mild Conditions
articles.abstract: The development of high-efficiency NH3 synthesis catalysts under mild conditions is urgently required to alleviate the excessive energy consumption and carbon emissions in traditional Haber–Bosch processes. Although Ru-based catalysts show considerable potential, their catalytic activity is often severely constrained by hydrogen poisoning caused by strong H2 adsorption. Herein, we report the fabrication of a Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst through the strategic integration of single-atom Re species into a conventional Ba/Ru/AC framework. Notably, the Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst exhibits a high NH3 synthesis rate of 65.1 mmol g–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 1 MPa. Mechanistic investigations reveal that single-atom Re species function as a supplementary active site for H2 adsorption and activation. The incorporation of Re also facilitates H-spillover over the catalyst surface, which effectively alleviates the competitive adsorption between H2 and N2 on Ru sites and consequently mitigates hydrogen poisoning on Ru nanoclusters. Concurrently, the incorporation of single-atom Re modulates the defect density of the support and promotes the creation of additional strong Lewis basic sites. These structural changes induce a strong electronic metal–support interaction (EMSI) effect, which specifically tunes the electronic structure of the Ru nanoclusters. This synergistic interplay between single-atom Re sites and Ru nanoclusters establishes a compelling paradigm for the rational design of highly efficient NH3 synthesis catalysts.

articles.title: Diagnosis of Mechanisms of Kinetics in Lithium-Rich Manganese-Based Cathode Materials
articles.abstract: The rate-determining step (RDS), which determines rate capability in lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials, remains unclear. In this work, we establish a quantitative diagnostic method for the RDS in LRMOs using in-situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) at different states of charge (SOC) and C-rates. From our results, the SOC determines the intrinsic bottleneck of the RDS, while the C-rate drives the transition from single-step to mixed control. Upon discharging to 4.4 V, the RDS is dominated by electron transfer at the interface accompanied by layered-to-spinel phase transition, whereas it is strongly influenced by solid-state diffusion in the bulk with depletion of Li vacancies arising from Jahn–Teller distortion when discharging to 3.0 V. Furthermore, Li+ diffusion, instead of charge transfer, plays a major part in the RDS of LRMOs when the C-rates are increased. These findings establish quantitative criteria for designing future cathode materials.

articles.title: UV Exposure and Durability of Emerging Photovoltaics: Quantifying and Reporting Outdoor UV Doses
articles.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation in sunlight is well known to harm components of solar modules, especially those of emerging photovoltaic technologies. Current accelerated UV tests, however, differ in spectral range and by orders of magnitude in intensity and dose. Their usual anchors, IEC 61215-2 preconditioning at 15 kW h m–2 and a fixed UV fraction of AM1.5G, do not represent long-term outdoor exposure. Here, we quantify annual outdoor UV doses (280–400 nm) across the contiguous United States from the National Solar Radiation Database for horizontal, fixed-tilt, and tracked mounting. Spectroradiometer measurements at two sites validate the model. Annual horizontal-plane doses span 72–133 kW h m–2, with a median of nearly 100 kW h m–2, so IEC 61215-2 preconditioning simulates only 1.4–2.5 months of outdoor exposure. Single-axis and dual-axis tracking typically add 10 and 18 kW h m–2, respectively. Finally, we propose reporting the source spectrum and expressing the test dose as a multiple of the annual outdoor dose for a stated location and mounting.

articles.title: Air-Stable Nickel Oxide Nanosheets as a Model Platform for Decoupling Structure–Activity Relation in Oxygen Evolving Electrocatalysts
articles.abstract: Nickel oxides are among the most active electrocatalysts for the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a key process in green hydrogen production. However, the fundamental reaction mechanism remains unclear, limiting the rational design of electrocatalysts capable of reducing the cost of sustainable hydrogen generation. Herein, we develop an air-stable model electrocatalyst system of submonolayer nickel oxide (NiO) nanosheets with controlled coverages and morphologies on atomically flat Au(111), enabling atomic-scale investigation of structure–activity relationships under ambient conditions. Atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and electrochemical measurements were combined to correlate nanosheet structure and composition with electrocatalytic performance. We reveal OER activity scales with nanosheet edge density, identifying edge sites as the dominant active sites of the reaction. XPS measurements demonstrate the formation of nickel hydroxide on the nanosheet surfaces and edges following OER testing, consistent with the generation of a catalytically active nickel oxyhydroxide phase during operation. These findings provide insight into the structure–activity relationships governing NiO electrocatalysts and demonstrate a strategy for resolving atomic-scale structure–activity relationships without the need to maintain samples under UHV. We propose that future NiO-based OER electrocatalysts are designed to maximize the number density of accessible edge sites, hence maximizing the electrocatalytic activity.

articles.title: Bipolar Redox Molecule-Assembled Freestanding Film Cathodes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries with Excellent Thermal Adaptivity and Ultralong Life
articles.abstract: Organic molecules with high redox potentials and large theoretical capacities are promising cathode materials for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs). However, their practical application is hindered by issues of dissolution, low electrical conductivity, and insufficient utilization of active sites. We report herein freestanding film cathodes for high-performance ZIBs with superior charge storage and heat management, wherein a meticulously designed bipolar redox molecule is assembled into a continuous three-dimensional conductive framework of MXene-bonded single-walled carbon nanotubes. The optimal cathode-based coin cells deliver the highest specific capacity of 406.6 mAh g–1 at 0.05 A g–1 and an initial capacity of 219.61 mAh g–1 at 10 A g–1 with extraordinary cycling stability over 60,000 cycles with an average capacity decay of only 2.5 × 10–4% per cycle. Further cycling test at 55 °C and 3 A g–1 reveals an initial capacity of 252.15 mAh g–1 with over 82.75% retention after 3000 cycles and ∼100% coulombic efficiency. Importantly, thermal conductivity and infrared thermal imaging were employed for clear elaboration of temperature evolution dynamics and thermal distribution under different electrode structures. Our work correlating the structure design and thermal management of electrodes provides insights for the rational design of high-performance ZIBs.

articles.title: Cation-Intercalated Mott Insulator α-RuCl3 Superlattice for Actively Tuned Optoelectronics
articles.abstract: Active tuning of the spectral response within sensing materials is critical for application-specific optoelectronics. However, current approaches typically suffer from limited tunability, complex architectures, or sacrificed stability. Here we report an on-chip cation intercalation strategy that transforms the Kitaev-candidate Mott insulator α-ruthenium chloride (α-RuCl3) into a tetramethylammonium (TMA+)-intercalated RuCl3 layered superlattice. The intercalation-induced reconstruction of the Mott-derived electronic states substantially narrows the optical gap from ∼1.1 eV to ∼0.6 eV, extending the spectral response into the short-wave infrared (SWIR) regime. The introduction of an in situ van der Waals tunneling barrier suppresses dark current by >3 orders of magnitude and enhances specific detectivity by 4–6 orders of magnitude. By employing machine learning models, we demonstrate device-response-guided image processing for intelligent recognition under degraded environments. This work establishes a connection between correlated-electron systems and intelligent sensing, stimulating research directions at the intersection of quantum materials, optoelectronics, and intelligent sensing systems.

articles.title: Controlling Redox Interplay in the Formation of Anisotropic Multimetallic Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Controlling the interplay between reduction and galvanic processes is critical for tailoring the structure and composition of multimetallic nanocrystals. Here, we report a synthetic strategy to produce anisotropic Au–Pd–Pt nanocrystals with tunable morphologies and elemental distributions. Platinum deposition on single-crystal Au@Pd nanorods (NRs) was modulated by varying the concentration of ascorbic acid, enabling control over the balance between reduction and galvanic-like processes. This approach yields distinct nanostructures, including nanoframes, cloud-like morphologies, and core–shell–shell architectures. Advanced electron microscopy, including high-resolution HAADF STEM imaging, EDX elemental mapping, and electron tomography, reveals intricate elemental distributions, the formation of cavities and tunnels, the apparent preservation of single-crystal characteristics in Au@Pd NRs under the explored conditions, and gold etching induced by the platinum precursor. A preliminary evaluation of catalytic activity suggests enhanced ethanol oxidation performance for nanoframe structures. These findings establish a versatile strategy for engineering anisotropic multimetallic nanocrystals through controlled redox interplay.

articles.title: Design of Water-Resistant, Food-Grade Microneedles for Fish Injection and Underwater Cargo Delivery
articles.abstract: Aquatic foods provide around 15% of consumed animal-derived protein worldwide and aquaculture now supplies most of it. But the industry faces significant challenges in disease prevention and excessive use of antimicrobials. Vaccination, particularly for juvenile fish, can mitigate these risks, but manual and automated needle-based vaccination methods are costly, stressful, and labor-intensive. Here, a water-resistant, food-grade microneedle platform is designed to deliver cargos underwater. Silk fibroin-based microneedles are engineered to remain water resistant from minutes to hours in order to penetrate fish skin in wet conditions. To meet the requirements of different underwater applications, three microneedle morphologies─shell, solid-tip, and hollow─are developed, and their different combinations of mechanical integrity, water-resistance performance, cargo compatibility, and release kinetics are studied. The microneedles also preserve the supercoiled conformation of ⩾50% of the loaded pIHNVw-G plasmids─developed to protect fish against infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus─outside the cold chain for 4 weeks under dry conditions. In pilot animal studies, injected microneedles remain attached to zebrafish and juvenile rainbow trout while swimming. Using this food-based microneedle platform, we envision the development of tools for underwater vaccination of juvenile fish that increase aquaculture efficiencies and reduce environmental impact.

articles.title: Early Pathway Selection Precedes Conformational Locking in Protein Self-Assembly
articles.abstract: When early intermediates begin to bias subsequent pathways during protein self-assembly remains difficult to resolve experimentally because early-stage processes are transient and poorly accessible. Here, using regenerated silk fibroin as a model system, we experimentally capture and analyze an early nucleation window in which assembly pathways begin to diverge before conformational locking occurs. By combining controlled electric-field perturbation with multiscale structural characterization and coarse-grained simulations, we identify reproducible nanoscale intermediates that mediate pathway selection. Within this window, electric fields bias early assembly kinetics in a nonmonotonic manner, modulating the formation, elongation, and competition of intermediates rather than directly enforcing structure or orientation. Time-resolved measurements show that subsequent growth proceeds primarily through elongation and fusion of existing intermediates, while β-sheet formation and crystallization emerge only at later stages and serve to stabilize pathways that were biased at earlier stages. Together, we locate the emergence of detectable pathway biasing within the nucleation stage and provide a framework for understanding and guiding protein self-assembly under nonequilibrium conditions.

articles.title: Human Urine–Derived Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell Membranes Enable Personalized Transdermal Nanotherapy for Melanoma
articles.abstract: Melanoma treatment remains limited by drug resistance, immune-related adverse effects, and inadequate tumor-specific drug delivery. Nanoparticle (NP)-based delivery platforms have shown promise, but their clinical translation is hindered by rapid immune clearance and suboptimal biocompatibility. Current membrane-coating strategies often depend on invasive cell sources and lack patient-specific applicability. This study introduces a personalized melanoma therapy platform that integrates MnO2 NPs (MNPs) coated with urine-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) membranes into a hydrogel-based transdermal patch. The patient-derived iPSC membrane enhances tumor targeting and immune evasion through the CXCR4/CXCL12 axis, while the MNPs facilitate pH-responsive release of cytotoxic drugs within the tumor microenvironment, maximizing therapeutic efficacy. The hydrogel transdermal patch enables direct, noninvasive delivery to skin lesions, promoting sustained drug exposure and potentially improving patient compliance. By combining autologous cell membrane coating, pH-responsive nanocarriers, and transdermal administration, this platform addresses key limitations of current melanoma therapies and supports the potential for clinical translation of personalized nanomedicine.

articles.title: Intracellular Polymerization-Induced Self-Assembly of Peptide Nanosheets for Inflammatory Breast Cancer Therapy
articles.abstract: Inflammatory breast cancer (IBC) is a highly aggressive breast cancer subtype characterized by diffuse, biologically invasive growth and poorly defined tissue boundaries, resulting in a high mortality rate even after multimodal treatment. Here, we report an intracellular polymerization-induced self-assembly (PISA) strategy that constructs mechanically active peptide nanosheets. Upon 365 nm UV irradiation, the photoinitiator Irgacure 2959 (I2959) initiates intracellular PISA of HisMAm in IBC cells. The corresponding nanosheets prepared in vitro exhibit a thickness of ∼30 nm and a wet-state apparent Young’s modulus of 8.02 ± 0.43 MPa. These nanosheets act through two coordinated materials-cell interactions: (i) increasing cellular viscosity and spatially associating with the actin cytoskeleton, suppressing cell migration and invasion; and (ii) accumulating in the endoplasmic reticulum and eliciting paraptosis-like cell death. In a subcutaneous IBC xenograft model, localized fiber-assisted light activation achieves 72.2% tumor growth inhibition without overt systemic toxicity. Overall, this work establishes intracellular PISA as a spatiotemporally controlled materials strategy for localized IBC treatment.

articles.title: Nanotechnology-Integrated Diagnostic Platforms toward Decentralized Infectious Disease Management
articles.abstract: Nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms are increasingly being developed across infectious disease management, from screening and diagnosis to potentially treatment-guiding assessment and monitoring. Yet current progress has rarely been synthesized from a clinical management perspective, making it difficult to determine which technologies are ready for decentralized use, where progress remains fragmented, and which clinical needs remain unmet. This review examines nanotechnology-enabled strategies according to how they enable the sample-to-answer workflow, rather than classifying them by material type. Major diagnostic platform architectures are then assessed in terms of practical implementation, with emphasis on platform-specific limitations and emerging solutions. Current applications are further mapped across the infectious disease management continuum to identify established capabilities, missing links, and disconnects from clinical workflows. The broader changes needed to close these gaps are also discussed. This review aims to clarify how nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms can be better developed toward decentralized, reliable, and clinically actionable infectious disease management.

articles.title: Photodoping-Driven Lattice Expansion Enables Polarization Enhancement in Sliding Ferroelectric MoS2
articles.abstract: Light-matter interactions provide a powerful route to dynamically control ferroelectricity in low-dimensional materials, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing light-induced polarization remain elusive in sliding ferroelectrics. However, the influence of photodoped carriers on the macroscopic polarization and lattice responses remains largely unexplored. In this work, we employ first-principles calculations to demonstrate the microscopic origin of the photostrictive response in rhombohedral bilayer MoS2 under carrier photodoping. The system exhibits a characteristic lattice deformation, including in-plane expansion with the magnitude of 2% under a moderate photodoping density, collectively enhancing electronic hybridization. The coupling gives rise to a substantial interlayer contraction and an increase in out-of-plane spontaneous polarization, accompanied by a softening of the interlayer vibrational mode. These results demonstrate a microscopic, nonthermal pathway for modulating ferroelectric properties and underscore the potential of lattice-engineered polarization control in two-dimensional sliding ferroelectrics for advanced optoelectronic and information storage technologies.

articles.title: Recent Advances in De Novo Synthesis of Interfacial Two-Dimensional Polymers
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional polymers (2DPs) integrate the molecular programmability of synthetic polymers with the reduced dimensionality and surface accessibility of atomically thin materials. Realizing their functional potential and establishing reliable structure–property relationships, however, require precise control over lattice topology, crystallinity, orientation, thickness, and defect structure. Interfacial polymerization is particularly suited to this objective because interfaces confine network formation while regulating molecular organization, reactant transport, bond-formation kinetics, nucleation, crystal growth, and defect evolution. This Review summarizes the molecular design principles underlying interfacial 2DP synthesis and compares four major environments according to whether polymerization occurs at a liquid or solid surface: air–liquid, liquid–liquid, solid–liquid, and vapor–solid interfaces. We contrast liquid surfaces, which couple dynamic confinement with transport-regulated molecular reorganization and scalable film growth, with solid surfaces, which provide adsorption, templating, and catalytic control while enabling direct mechanistic investigation at the molecular scale. We further examine how precursor organization, mass transport, crystallization pathways, stacking, and defect evolution collectively determine the structural quality of 2DPs. Particular attention is given to mechanistic insights from advanced characterization methods that directly track nucleation and domain-growth dynamics and resolve grain-boundary and defect structures from molecular to atomic resolution. Emerging electronic and stimuli-responsive devices are discussed to illustrate how framework design, structural quality, and interfacial organization translate into functional performance. Finally, we identify opportunities to advance interfacial polymerization from empirical optimization toward predictive synthesis that bridges local atomic precision with macroscopic structural uniformity.

articles.title: Spatially Decoupled Donor and Acceptor Gradient Brush Particle Blends for Mechanically Robust, Fatigue-Resistant, and Recyclable Elastomers
articles.abstract: Combining high mechanical strength, fatigue resistance, and reprocessability in a single soft material remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a strategy based on spatially decoupled interparticle hydrogen bonding in architecturally controlled brush particle blends. Complementary hydrogen-bonding motifs, namely poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) as donor and poly(dimethylaminoethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) as acceptor, were incorporated into poly(n-butyl acrylate) (PnBA)-based gradient brush particles via surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP). Upon blending, reversible interparticle hydrogen bonds were formed, functioning as dynamic physical cross-links. The resulting materials exhibited tensile strengths up to 18 MPa, Young’s modulus of 95 MPa, and fracture strains exceeding 150–200%, a combination rarely achieved in physically cross-linked polymer networks. Hierarchical viscoelastic analysis revealed that the synergy between reversible interparticle bonding and architectural heterogeneity generates broad relaxation spectra and multiscale energy dissipation pathways. These features collectively underpin outstanding fatigue resistance, crack-propagation suppression, reprocessability, and thermally assisted self-healing, with annealing at 50 °C restoring approximately 90% of the original modulus and near-complete tensile strength. This work establishes spatial decoupling of hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors as a transferable design principle for durable, recyclable structural soft materials.

articles.title: Turning Insulators into Accelerators: Deciphering the Interfacial Ionic Conductivity Boost in Composite Solid-State Electrolytes through Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics Simulations
articles.abstract: Halide solid-state electrolytes have emerged as promising candidates for all-solid-state lithium batteries due to their high oxidative stability and deformability, yet their moderate ionic conductivity remains a bottleneck. While incorporating ionically insulating ZrO2 nanoparticles has been experimentally shown to enhance the ionic conductivity of Li2ZrCl6, the atomistic origin governing this interfacial phenomenon remains unclear. Here, we bridge the spatiotemporal gap in modeling complex heterostructures by developing an accurate machine-learned force field based on the neuroevolution potential, enabling large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of ZrO2/Li2ZrCl6 heterostructures. By systematically investigating four representative low-lattice-mismatch ZrO2/Li2ZrCl6 interfaces, we identify spontaneous interfacial amorphization driven by space-charge effects upon surface cleavage, trapping Li+ and leading to under-coordinated Li+ polyhedra with pronounced geometric distortion. These distorted amorphous interfacial regions exhibit markedly enhanced Li+ hopping activity, significantly outperforming the bulk lattice, provided that the local mobile Li+ density is not depleted by surface charge redistribution. This work establishes a computational framework for training validated machine-learned force fields for interfaces and provides one plausible origin for the experimentally observed conductivity boost in the insulator-conductor composites, guiding the rational design of electrolytes toward next-generation solid-state batteries.

articles.title: Visualizing Kinetic Control and Thermodynamic Selection in Nanocluster Structural Evolution
articles.abstract: It is extremely challenging to clarify the precise atomic-level evolution of nanoclusters from a dynamically trapped state to a thermodynamically selected product. Various factors play distinctly different roles in the thermodynamic and kinetic control of structural transformation reactions. In this study, we used the system Ag14(SPh)12(DPPH)4 → Ag23(SPh)18(DPPH)4 as a homologous model system, and combined single-crystal structural analysis, time-resolved electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS), ultraviolet–visible absorption spectroscopy, and photoluminescence measurements for correlation analysis. Crystallographic studies revealed that the Ag23 framework could be geometrically decomposed into two substructures related to Ag14, both sharing the metal and thioimine groups, providing a structural basis for the bimolecular fusion hypothesis. Time-dependent spectroscopic techniques revealed the consumption process of Ag14 and the growth process of Ag23, while temperature-dependent experiments showed a kinetic window within which the conversion rate accelerated, but higher thermal input would promote breakage/decomposition and form Ag10. Due to the ability of ESI-MS to generate gas-phase fragments, ions containing Ag5- and Ag9 were regarded as candidate species detected by ESI, rather than confirmed solution intermediates. Therefore, the core breakthrough was not the isolated Ag14 or Ag23 nuclear numbers, but the mechanistic connection of the two structurally similar cluster states in a single reaction network and the identification of thermal activation as the key factor guiding the evolution of the cluster states.

articles.title: Competing deformation mechanisms controlled by oxygen content lead to a strength-failure turnover in CuO-doped NiTi shape memory alloys
Critical role of austenite in yielding behavior of ultrahigh-strength maraging steels fabricated via laser powder bed fusion
Direct observation of chemical short-range ordering in multicomponent alloys by resonant and non-resonant X-ray diffraction
Asymmetric Cooperative Solvation Structure Enables Entropy‐Enthalpy Compensation for Ultralow Temperature Sodium‐Metal and Sodium–Ion Pouch Cells
articles.abstract: Sodium-metal batteries are promising for low-temperature energy storage, yet conventional electrolytes suffer from an intrinsic trade-off between thermodynamic stability and kinetic transport, causing salt precipitation and solvation collapse. Herein, an asymmetric cooperative solvation structure (ACSS) is introduced to spatially decouple these conflicting requirements via coordination competition between a strong solvating solvent (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether, DME) and a weak solvating (diethylene glycol diethyl ether, DEE). The DME-rich inner core forms compact ternary coordination clusters with Na+ and anions (PF6 −/BF4 −), ensuring enthalpic stability and high salt solubility via geometric ion confinement, while the DEE-rich outer shell sustains entropic mobility through rapid ligand exchange, facilitating hopping transport and lowering desolvation barriers. This enthalpy–entropy compensation preserves ionic conductivity and structural integrity below −40°C. High anion occupancy within the stable clusters promotes preferential anion reduction, yielding an inorganic-rich SEI with high mechanical modulus and low Na+ migration energy, effectively suppressing dendrite growth and interfacial polarization. Consequently, Na||Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 94% at −40°C. Scaled-up 1.2 Ah hard carbon||Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 and 1.2 Ah hard carbon||NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 pouch cells sustain 400 and 550 cycles at −30°C and −20°C, respectively, demonstrating the promising practical applicability of this electrolyte design.

articles.title: Chemical Coordination and Pore Confinement Enabling a Bifunctional Interface for Accelerated Desolvation and Oriented Deposition Toward Stable Zinc Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries show great potential for large‐scale energy storage; however, dendrites formation and corrosion on zinc anodes significantly hinder their practical applications. Uneven Zn deposition leads to dendrite growth, while H2O molecules in solvated Zn2+ ions exacerbate surface corrosion and the hydrogen evolution reaction. Herein, we propose a Schiff‐base‐covalently‐grafted UiO‐66‐NH2 metal‐organic framework to construct a bifunctional interface for stable zinc metal anodes. Specifically, the chemical chelation between Schiff base and Zn2+ accelerates desolvation and suppresses side reactions. Meanwhile, the uniformly distributed Zn2+‐chelated sites and the well‐defined confined pore channels of UiO‐66‐NH2 scaffold guide a homogeneous Zn2+ flux and promote Zn(002)‐oriented deposition. As a result, this bifunctional interface enables Zn plating/stripping with a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.8% over 2000 cycles at 5 mA cm−2/1 mAh cm−2. Furthermore, it achieves a capacity retention of over 90% after 4000 charge–discharge cycles in a Zn||MnO2 full cell. This work is expected to open a new avenue for interfacial chemical regulation toward stabilizing zinc metal anodes.

articles.title: Decoupled Dual‐Stream Seawater Electrolysis Toward Cost‐Effective Green Hydrogen Production
articles.abstract: Ocean, as a vast natural reservoir of ionic minerals, provides a promising approach to offset the high cost of hydrogen production from electrocatalytic water splitting. However, the complex ionic environment of seawater compels us to separate out scaling-prone ions via cost-effective membrane separation technology, and further separately electrolyze diluted and concentrated seawater to produce H2 and high value-added marine chemical products. We herein apply electrodialysis to separate out divalent cations and produce twofold concentrated seawater and fresh seawater. A decoupled dual-stream seawater electrolysis (DDSE) strategy is designed. The fresh seawater is routed into an alkaline/AEM water electrolyzer to sustain stable H2 evolution. The concentrated seawater is fed into a home-made electrolyzer to produce NaClO and high-purity Mg(OH)2. A scalable non-noble metal-based electrode (50 cm × 50 cm) was designed and fabricated with high activity and stability when applied in the chlorine evolution reaction. System-level evaluation validates the feasibility of the DDSE strategy. Through rigorous techno-economic analysis, the unit price of H2 production is reduced to $0.39 kgH2 −1 (DOE 2030 target: $1 kgH2 −1), and the Global Warming Potential can be reduced up to 6.83%. This proposed DDSE strategy offers a new approach for cost-effective green hydrogen production with comprehensive seawater valorization.

articles.title: Light‐Induced Ce–Ov–Ni Motifs Enable Hydrogen‐Poisoning‐Resistant Photothermal NH3 Decomposition
articles.abstract: NH3 is an attractive hydrogen carrier, but efficient H2 release is hindered by N–H bond cleavage and hydrogen poisoning. Herein, we develop Ni nanoparticle‐supported CeO2 (Ni/CeO2) for low‐temperature photothermal NH3 decomposition. Light irradiation is accompanied by the dynamic generation of oxygen vacancies on CeO2, which couple with adjacent Ni sites to form Ce–Ov–Ni motifs, indicating that illumination can regulate the catalyst surface state beyond its thermal contribution. Experiments and DFT calculations indicate that these interfaces create differentiated local environments for NH3 activation and product evolution. Oxygen‐vacancy‐associated sites favor NH3 adsorption, N–H bond activation, and N‐containing intermediates, whereas adjacent Ni sites accommodate H migration and recombination. Moreover, vacancy‐induced electronic modulation weakens H2 adsorption on Ni, thereby facilitating H2 release. Such site differentiation and facilitated hydrogen removal reduce the competitive occupation of active sites by N‐ and H‐containing species and contribute to the resistance to hydrogen poisoning. Under photothermal conditions, 10 wt.% Ni/CeO2 achieves 96.3% NH3 conversion at 450°C, versus 42.5% under thermal catalysis, and maintains >95% conversion at a GHSV of 18,000 mL·gcat−1·h−1. It delivers 20.09 mmol·gcat−1·min−1 H2 with 50 h stability. This work demonstrates light‐induced oxygen‐vacancy–metal interfaces for efficient, hydrogen‐poisoning‐resistant NH3‐to‐H2 conversion.

articles.title: N‐Heterocyclic Molecular Additives Enable Solvation and Interfacial Chemistry Regulation for High‐Stability, High‐Rate, and High‐Capacity Lithium Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: Most electrolyte additives enable long-term Li plating/stripping at <3 mA cm− 2, non-applicable to practical Li-metal batteries (LMBs) operating at ≥5 mA cm− 2 and ≥ 5 mAh cm− 2. Here, we report an interaction chemistry that enables simultaneous solvation and interfacial regulation by exploring a novel N-heterocyclic molecule (i.e., TPTC)—comprising an N-heterocyclic core and four pyridine units–as an efficient additive for achieving ultra-stable Li-metal anodes under practical conditions. Electron-rich N atoms in TPTC serve as ion-dipole interaction sites, inducing competitive coordination that weakens Li+ solvation and enhances Li+ migration in the bulk electrolyte, which homogenizes Li+ concentration near the interface, favoring high-rate Li deposition. TPTC also adsorbs on Li surface to construct a protective layer with a low interfacial de-solvation barrier, which–together with low-barrier Li+ transport through heterocyclic cavities–facilitates uniform Li deposition. Meanwhile, electron-deficient C–H sites in pyridine weakly interact with TFSI−, forming an anion-rich interfacial region that in situ decomposes into an inorganic-rich interphase, affording high-flux Li+ transport. This synergy allows stable Li plating/stripping at 10 mA cm−2/10 mAh cm−2 for 3000 h. Paired with a high-loading LiFePO4 cathode (∼15 mg cm−2) and thin Li (∼100 µm), the cell maintains 87.8% capacity after 400 cycles.

articles.title: Strengthening TMP‐Derived Phosphate SEI via Sn Scaffold and BF4− Interphase Chemistry for Ultra‐Stable, High‐Rate Zn Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: While dynamic solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) construction and solvation engineering have transformed aqueous zinc-ion batteries, translating these approaches to Organic electrolytes (OE) remains a challenging endeavor due to fundamentally different interfacial environments, solvation thermodynamics, and anion decomposition pathways. Despite providing superior thermodynamic stabilization to Zn anode, OE exhibits low ionic conductivity, thereby limiting operational current densities. Herein, we report the first demonstration of Sn(BF4)2/H2O (SFB) additive integration in a non-flammable trimethyl phosphate (TMP)-ethanol (EtOH) (2:1 v/v) OE to architect a gradient SEI interphase on Zn anodes. The multifunctional integration of SFB facilitates the formation of a Sn-coated Zn surface, a BF4 1−-derived SEI@Zn, and H2O molecules as a proton source, collectively contributing to enhanced capacity. This strategic solvent-salt-metal synergy enables bi-layered interfacial engineering within a single electrolyte system, significantly improving the reversibility and stability of the Zn anode. Consequently, SFB enables a robust SEI, achieving exceptional Zn anode durability (7000 h), high-rate capability (10 mA cm−2), and a high Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 99.8%. Full cells with SFB outperform controls in coin and pouch configurations. Given the rarity of additive(s) in OEs, this study offers a new path to boost stability and lifespan of non-aqueous Zn batteries.

articles.title: Surpassing Metal‐Centric E‐Waste Recycling: Unveiling Graphite in Spent Lithium‐Ion Batteries Towards Electrocatalytic Upcycling
articles.abstract: With tonnes of battery shredded globally, tracing down pathways in upcycling black mass (BM) as catalysts would be a game changer. Existing unwavering synergic combination of inherent metals and graphite in BM drives this novel objective. Herein, we report the critical role of spent graphite for electrocatalytic water splitting applications by systematic evaluation of diverse NMC, LFP, and LCO BM. The study revealed an interesting pattern, wherein the graphite in BM complemented their impurity flaws by delivering an excellent oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. Defects, surface activation, structural variation, and metal‐graphite synergism arising from prolonged cycle life served as a serendipitous finding of upcycling BM for OER, despite being loaded with impurities and/or degradation byproducts. Further, among these BM sets, direct upcycling of select graphite‐containing BM via mechanochemical functionalisation aided downsized derivatives delivering an overpotential of 260 mV at 10 mA cm−2, while functionalized graphite via bioleaching BM recorded an overpotential of 249 mV, an epoch‐making record in graphite upcycling. By correlating the overall insights using advanced material, electrochemical characterisation studies, and life cycle analysis, the current study unlocks spent graphite benefits for achieving sustainable energy solutions and beyond.

articles.title: Versatile Acetyl‐Functionalized Phenothiazine Self‐Assembled Monolayers for Efficient Perovskite and Organic Solar Cells
articles.abstract: The development of versatile, stable, and cost-effective hole-transport layers (HTLs) is essential for advancing next-generation photovoltaic technologies. Herein, we report a series of phenothiazine-based self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) as HTLs for perovskite and organic solar cells. By systematically tuning the substituents, including unsubstituted phenothiazine (PTZ), dibromo-PTZ (PTZ-diBr), and diacetyl-PTZ (PTZ-diACE), we achieve control over interfacial energetics and surface properties. The dual coordination sites of carbonyl groups and sulfur in PTZ-diACE provide Lewis basic sites that coordinate undercoordinated Pb2 + ions, facilitating passivation at the buried HTL/perovskite interface. Additionally, polar acetyl groups induce interfacial dipoles that reinforce the built-in electric field, promoting efficient hole extraction. Among the series, PTZ-diACE exhibits superior film formation, a deeper HOMO level, and stronger interfacial interactions, resulting in enhanced charge extraction and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Consequently, inverted perovskite solar cells employing PTZ-diACE achieve a power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.5% with excellent operational stability, retaining 93% of its initial efficiency after 500 h under the ISOS-D-2I protocol. These advantages extend to organic solar cells, where PTZ-diACE delivers a PCE of 20.4% in D18:L8BO devices and demonstrates compatibility across multiple active layers. This study demonstrates phenothiazine-based SAMs as HTLs and provides design guidelines for efficient, stable interfacial materials.

articles.title: Zwitterionic Thermoplastic Polyurethane‐Based Quasi‐Solid Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium Metal Batteries With Machine‐Learning‐Assisted Mechanistic Insights
articles.abstract: This study presents a quasi‐solid‐state electrolyte based on zwitterionic thermoplastic polyurethane (QS‐Z‐TPU) for lithium metal batteries. Unlike conventional quasi‐solid polymer electrolytes that mainly serve as passive liquid‐electrolyte reservoirs, QS‐Z‐TPU is designed as an active ion‐regulating matrix via phosphorylcholine‐derived zwitterionic groups in the TPU framework. The resulting electrolyte combines the elasticity and film‐forming capability of TPU with dual‐site ion regulation, where phosphate sites coordinate Li+ while quaternary ammonium and urethane N‐H groups immobilize TFSI− anions. This design enhances electrolyte affinity while suppressing destructive swelling due to ionic crosslinking. QS‐Z‐TPU exhibits high ionic conductivity, a wide electrochemical stability window, and an enhanced Li+ transference number. Machine‐learning‐assisted molecular modeling further reveals that the zwitterionic oligomer stabilizes separated LiTFSI configurations through cooperative Li+ coordination and TFSI− association, substantially reducing the energetic penalty for ion‐pair separation. This regulated ion environment promotes uniform Li+ flux at the lithium metal interface and facilitates the formation of a stable inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase. Consequently, QS‐Z‐TPU enables stable Li plating/stripping and improves the cycling stability and rate capability of LFP|Li full cells, further validated in flexible pouch‐cell demonstrations. These findings highlight zwitterionic molecular engineering as an effective strategy for interface‐stabilizing quasi‐solid electrolytes.

articles.title: A Defect‐Engineered Sono‐Piezocatalytic In Situ Hydrogel for Preventing Hepatocellular Carcinoma Recurrence After Incomplete Radiofrequency Ablation
articles.abstract: Residual tumor cells and the immunosuppressive microenvironment caused by incomplete radiofrequency ablation (iRFA) lead to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence. In this study, HA-V-MTO/LMP@Gel, an injectable sono-piezocatalytic hydrogel, is developed for local treatment of HCC after iRFA. It combines hyaluronic acid-modified, oxygen vacancy-engineered Mn–Ti metal–organic framework nanosheets (HA-V-MTO) with reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive liposomes co-loaded with STING agonist MSA-2 and an anti-PD-1 antibody (LMP) within a thermosensitive chitosan/β-glycerophosphate (CS/β-GP) hydrogel. Oxygen-vacancy engineering lowers the O2 adsorption energy from 0.187 to −2.559 eV and raises the piezoelectric coefficient d 33 from 35.36 to 108.73 pm V−1. Under ultrasound, HA-V-MTO generates ROS through sono-piezocatalysis, with an additional Fenton-like reaction from the Mn-containing framework. The resulting oxidative stress induces mitochondrial injury and promotes cytosolic mtDNA release, thereby facilitating cGAS-mediated STING activation. ROS-mediated LMP destabilization releases MSA-2, which further enhances STING signaling. The hydrogel undergoes temperature-triggered gelation for sustained local release. In a post-iRFA model, HA-V-MTO/LMP@Gel + US raises intratumoral IFN-β 7.9-fold, increases the proportion of mature dendritic cells to 50.8% and that of intratumoral CD8+ T cells to 26.5%, suppresses residual regrowth, prolongs survival, and protects against tumor rechallenge. This work presents a locally retained sono-piezocatalytic system that couples tumor killing with STING-driven immune activation after iRFA.

articles.title: A Microphase Engineering Strategy for Spider Silk‐Inspired Fibers With Exceptional Strength, Toughness, and Damping Capacity
articles.abstract: Spider silk exhibits exceptional mechanical properties, inspiring the development of diverse biomimetic fibers. However, spider silk‐inspired fibers typically introduce β‐sheet‐like domains while neglecting microphase structure regulation, failing to overcome inherent strength‐toughness conflict. Herein, a spider silk‐inspired fiber is fabricated through a microphase engineering strategy by mimicking spidroin assembly process and microphase structure evolution during natural spider silk spinning. Polyurethane (PU) serves as raw material because its molecular structure closely resembles that of nature spidroin's architecture. Through a solvent exchange‐induced phase separation process, the long‐range oriented microphase structures are constructed. The as‐spun fiber achieves a high toughness of 626.14 ± 38.01 MJ m−3, surpassing that of the strongest natural spider silk. Subsequently, post‐treatment is applied to induce crystallization, further increasing the tensile strength to 418.21 ± 9.56 MPa while maintaining a high toughness of 333.09 ± 20.64 MJ m−3. Notably, the spider silk‐inspired fiber can be used as an energy‐absorbing layer in a ballistic board due to its excellent energy dissipation capabilities, reducing deformation by 36.5% compared with a ceramic‐aramid control upon impact with a ∼730 m s−1 bullet. This work highlights the microphase engineering strategy in enhancing mechanical properties of fibers, offering a simple pathway to fabricate high‐performance spider silk‐inspired fibers.

articles.title: A Retinal Matrix Stiffening Model Reveals FAK‐Dependent Mechanotransduction in Pericytes Underlies Vascular Destabilization
articles.abstract: Pericyte loss, an early hallmark of diabetic retinopathy (DR), is linked to hyperglycemia and inflammation, whereas the contribution of mechanical changes in the retina remains unclear.
