Balancing Fast Li-Ion Transport Kinetics and Mechanical Strength in PEO-Based Composite Solid Electrolytes through Minimal Dinitrile Incorporation
articles.abstract: Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based composite solid electrolytes (CSEs) suffer from poor ionic conductivity because strong Li+–ether oxygen coordination restricts Li+ transport. Herein, we develop a competitive coordination strategy by introducing a minimal amount of hexanedinitrile (HDN; 2.30 wt %) into PEO CSEs. Its flexible tetramethylene spacer allows nitrile groups to compete with PEO for Li+, forming mobile Li(HDN)x+ species while largely preserving the polymer backbone. This design accelerates local Li+ migration and promotes interfacial Li+ exchange, mitigating the trade-off between ionic conductivity and mechanical strength. The optimized CSE-HDN achieves an ionic conductivity of 4.87 × 10–4 S cm–1 (60 °C) and a tensile strength of 1.08 MPa. Li||Li symmetric cells cycle stably for 1000 h at 0.2 mA cm–2, while Li||LiFePO4 cells retain 94.8% capacity after 250 cycles at 3C. These results identify competitive Li+–nitrile coordination as a strategy for designing high-performance PEO-based CSEs.

articles.title: Band-Engineering W18O49 with Cu Single Atoms Enables Efficient Photo-Induction of Oxygen Radicals for Highly Sensitive Room-Temperature NO2 Detection
articles.abstract: Metal oxide semiconductor gas sensors suffer from insufficient sensitivity and slow response/recovery due to inefficient charge separation and sluggish surface reaction kinetics at room temperature. Herein, we demonstrated that single-atom Cu doping enabled precise band structure engineering of W18O49, thereby enabling photoassisted room-temperature NO2 detection with high sensitivity and selectivity. Single-atom Cu induced abundant oxygen vacancies and regulated the electronic configuration, facilitating oxygen radical generation and interfacial charge transfer. Consequently, the Cu1–W18O49 sensor exhibited a high response (RNO2/Rair = 572.3) toward 10 ppm of NO2 and excellent selectivity under light. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed the formation of multiple nitrogen oxide species on the Cu1–W18O49 surface and revealed that the Cu doping induces a transformation of the NO3 adsorption configuration from a weak monodentate to a bidentate binding mode, highlighting the enhanced surface reactivity by Cu doping. This work provides fundamental insights into the rational design of high-performance photoactivated gas sensors.

articles.title: Direct Optical Lithography of Intrinsically Stretchable Colloidal Emissive Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Realizing high-resolution stretchable displays requires emissive materials that combine photopatternability with intrinsic stretchability. In colloidal nanocrystal films, however, the network formation needed for precise patterning often restricts molecular mobility, creating a fundamental trade-off with mechanical compliance. Here, we address this challenge using a benzophenone-based dual-crosslinker strategy that forms an elastomeric nanocrystal network. The tetrafunctional small-molecule crosslinker promotes efficient photopatterning, whereas the benzophenone-terminated polybutadiene crosslinker provides mechanical compliance. By tuning the crosslinker composition, the dual-crosslinking system enables direct optical patterning with line widths down to 2 μm and crack-free deformation up to 36% uniaxial strain. Both perovskite and InP-based nanocrystals largely retain their photoluminescence after processing, while the dual-crosslinking platform enables multicolor patterning and transfer to elastomeric substrates. QLEDs incorporating strained emissive layers maintain more than 90% of the maximum luminance of their unstretched counterparts. This dual-crosslinker design offers a general route to intrinsically stretchable, directly photopatternable colloidal nanocrystal emission layers.

articles.title: Efficient Carrier Multiplication Beyond Mo- and W-Based Transition Metal Dichalcogenides: Multilayer HfSe2 and ReSe2
articles.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) are layered van der Waals semiconductors that can convert a single high-energy photon into multiple electron–hole pairs through carrier multiplication (CM). However, the factors governing CM efficiency within the TMDC family remain unclear, with studies limited to Mo- and W-based compositions. Here, we address this question by investigating HfSe2 and ReSe2, two less-explored TMDCs with markedly different electronic densities of states. Combining first-principles calculations with ultrafast optical spectroscopy, we establish the occurrence of efficient CM in both materials, with quantum yields 20–30% higher than those of previously studied multilayer TMDCs. Our analysis reveals that CM outcompetes phonon-mediated cooling. Furthermore, we observe similarly high CM efficiencies in HfSe2 and ReSe2 despite their vastly different number of possible CM pathways. This comparison reveals that the CM efficiency is mainly determined by the presence of at least a single CM decay pathway rather than the total number.

articles.title: High Refractive Index Silver Nanoparticle Metamaterials Approaching Fundamental Bounds
articles.abstract: Dense assemblies of metal nanoparticles offer a scalable route to high-index optical metamaterials, yet their collective response and loss mechanisms remain poorly understood. We synthesize quasi-spherical Ag nanoparticles with diameters ranging from 17 to 66 nm and assemble them into closely-packed monolayers. These films exhibit size-dependent refractive indices reaching a maximum of 10.3 with a low loss region emerging on the red shoulder of the resonance. We introduce a compact analytical model that quantitatively reproduces the measured optical constants and identifies the interparticle gap as the lever controlling the achievable index and loss. We compute Bergman-Milton fundamental limits, finding that our best assemblies reach two-thirds of the high-index–low-loss Pareto frontier for silver/polystyrene composites of arbitrary microstructure with the remaining samples approaching within a factor of 1.7–4. Together, experiment and theory establish silver nanoparticle assemblies as a tunable platform approaching fundamental bounds and define pathways for further performance gains.

articles.title: Mesoporosity Regulates Microbubble Emergence and Interfacial Bubble Accumulation during Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Gas bubbles generated during water electrolysis alter electrolyte access, ionic conduction, and local mass transport, thereby influencing electrochemical performance. Directly resolving this process is often challenging because numerous bubbles evolve and interact simultaneously on conventional gas-evolving electrodes. Here, we establish mesoporous Pt microelectrodes as a simplified model system to examine how the nanoscale porous architecture affects H2 bubble evolution relative to nonporous Pt electrodes with the same macroscopic disk geometry at matched nominal H2 generation rates. The mesoporous Pt electrode exhibited smaller detachment diameters and shorter detachment periods during single H2 bubble evolution in H2SO4. During multiple H2 bubble evolution in HClO4, the mesoporous electrode concentrated microbubble emergence into fewer locations and developed a less crowded near interface bubble population, with a smaller current-induced resistance increment. These results show how the nanoscale porous architecture can reorganize collective bubble evolution and thereby modify the associated ohmic penalty during electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution.

articles.title: Molecularly Addressable Nanoparticle-on-Mirror Cavity Arrays via DNA Origami-Mediated Template Assembly
articles.abstract: Nanoparticle-on-mirror (NPoM) cavities confine light within molecular gaps, but conventional drop casting does not register cavities at predefined coordinates. We integrate electron-beam lithography, face-selective DNA origami placement, and DNA-mediated gold-nanosphere docking to position molecularly programmable NPoMs on flat gold mirrors. Across six patches containing 2538 sites in total, the estimated mean single-particle occupation was approximately 84.7%. Dark-field spectra of cavities programmed with cyanine 5 (Cy5) show a split response centered near the Cy5 transition. Comparison with bare-cavity sweeps of facet width, gap thickness, and spacer index supports a molecularly anchored, Rabi-like interpretation of this response within a damped coupled-oscillator model. Photoluminescence controls reveal substantial gold luminescence, so dark-field scattering is used as the primary coupling observable. The platform therefore combines deterministic cavity registration with sequence-programmable molecular optical functionality.

articles.title: ROS-Responsive Selenocysteine-Releasing Nanozyme for Targeted Ferroptosis Suppression and Pancreatic β-Cell Protection in Type 2 Diabetes
articles.abstract: Pancreatic β-cell ferroptosis, driven by oxidative stress and impaired glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) activity, has emerged as an important contributor to the progression of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, persistent reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and insufficient selenocysteine (Sec) availability limit GPX4-dependent antioxidant defense, making effective ferroptosis intervention challenging. Here, we engineered a ROS-responsive Sec-loaded copper-based single-atom nanozyme (Se@CuSAzyme) that combines catalytic ROS scavenging with Sec supplementation. Benefiting from its intrinsic superoxide dismutase- and catalase-like activities, Se@CuSAzyme efficiently eliminated excessive ROS, while oxidative stress-triggered Sec release enhanced GPX4 expression. As a result, Se@CuSAzyme markedly suppressed high glucose and erastin-induced ferroptosis, reduced lipid peroxidation, and preserved mitochondrial integrity in pancreatic β-cells. In high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, Se@CuSAzyme demonstrated therapeutic efficacy comparable to that of metformin in ameliorating hyperglycemia, alleviating insulin resistance, and increasing energy expenditure. Importantly, Se@CuSAzyme outperformed metformin in protecting against hepatic steatosis and glycolipid metabolic dysfunction.

articles.title: Single-Layer Diverse Chiral Metasurfaces Driven by Generative AI
articles.abstract: Optical chirality has been extensively explored in chiral molecules, helical structures, and metasurfaces with bound states in the continuum. Attempts to attain chirality have mainly relied on human intuition and ideas. Here, we show various types of single-layer silicon-nanostructured metasurfaces exhibiting prominent circular dichroism (CD) containing perfect, broadband, and opposite CD responses at short near-infrared wavelengths. The designs were obtained based on a generative AI-assisted structural search for chiral metasurfaces, enabling a series of nonempirical structural searches beyond the boundary of human knowledge and experience. The physical mechanisms yielding the outstanding CD responses are elucidated from detailed insights into subwavelength electromagnetic dynamics in the single-layer metasurfaces. Furthermore, we experimentally demonstrate several metasurfaces. This type of single-layer thin CD metasurface serves as a key element in the development of compact optical-wave-manipulating devices at telecommunication bands.

articles.title: Stereochemical Optimization Boosts the Chemotherapeutic Efficacy of Isomeric Bile Salt-Aquated Cisplatin Nanocomplexes
articles.abstract: Cisplatin (CDDP) requires a rate-limiting intracellular aquation to generate aquated cisplatin (aqCDDP) for DNA binding and exertion of oncostatic effects. On this basis, three isomeric bile salt-aqCDDP nanocomplexes (12α-SDC@CDDP, 7α-SCDC@CDDP, and 7β-SUDC@CDDP) were constructed to directly deliver aqCDDP. Although 7β-SUDC@CDDP exhibited the optimal pharmacokinetics, poor cellular uptake resulted in limited tumor accumulation and insufficient antitumor activity. For 7α-SCDC@CDDP, the nonspecific distribution in the liver and lung resulted in suboptimal antitumor activity. Notably, 12α-SDC@CDDP demonstrated 3-fold higher tumor accumulation than CDDP solution and the best antitumor activity owing to its highest cellular uptake. These results revealed that the stereochemical configuration of the hydroxyl group on bile salts regulated the trade-off between systemic circulation and cellular internalization, with 12α-hydroxylation favoring uptake and 7β-hydroxylation favoring circulation. These findings provided guiding implications for future bile salt–platinum nanomedicine design, particularly through stereochemical regulation to improve therapeutic performance.

articles.title: Super-Toughness Self-Healing MOF-Based Composite Solid Electrolyte with Reaction-Transport Coupling Regulates Transportation of Ions and Polysulfides in High-Performance Solid-State Li–S Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium–sulfur batteries have emerged as a promising candidate for next-generation energy storage systems due to high theoretical energy density and low cost. However, the practical application is severely hindered by issues such as the polysulfide shuttle effect, sluggish ion transport, and lithium dendrite growth. Here, we proposed a synergistic strategy based on nanoconfinement polymerization and self-healing dynamic cross-linking to successfully fabricate a self-healing composite solid electrolyte, composed of PVDF-HFP, graphene oxide, UiO-66, linear polydopamine chains, and a boronic ester cross-linked network. The electrolyte demonstrates high ionic conductivity (1.7 × 10–4 S cm–1), good puncture resistance (9.7 N), high elongation at break (335%), and superior capacity retention (a capacity decay rate of 0.0276% per cycle over 500 cycles). Even under a high sulfur loading of 4 mg cm–2, the capacity retention remained as high as 94.8%, which exceeds previously reported electrolytes. This strategy offers a new pathway to designing advanced solid electrolytes for high-energy batteries.

articles.title: A genome‑wide screen in E. coli reveals metabolic adaptations that enhance intratumoral fitness and bacterial cancer therapy efficacy
articles.abstract: Despite decades of investigation, the fundamental molecular and cellular principles that enable bacteria to thrive within the tumor microenvironment have yet to be defined. Here, through a genome‑wide functional screen, we identify the bacterial genes and pathways that govern intratumoral fitness. Targeted deletion of nonglucose phosphotransferase systems to align bacterial metabolic preference with tumor metabolite availability promotes bacterial intratumoral fitness. Integrating multiple metabolic adaptations into a single tumor‑avid Escherichia coli strain (Ec‑TA) results in increased tumor colonization, not only after intratumoral delivery but also after intravenous delivery, leading to increased anti‑tumor efficacy when using Ec‑TA engineered to deliver an encoded immunostimulatory payload. Furthermore, Ec‑TA displaces wild‑type bacteria from pre‑colonized tumors when administered systemically, underscoring its potential for locally delivering therapeutics in the presence of resident tumor microbes. These data demonstrate that adapting bacteria to the unique characteristics of the tumor metabolic microenvironment can drive the development of safer and more effective chassis for next‑generation bacterial cancer therapies.

articles.title: AI for detection of adverse events in the real world
articles.abstract: Immune-related adverse events are common in cancer immunotherapy and can be difficult to recognize in clinical routine. Work now shows that an agentic AI system built around a large language model can identify such events in prospectively collected clinical notes and can make human review of such notes faster and more consistent.

articles.title: An agentic AI system enhances clinical detection of immune-related adverse events in a multi-phase validation study
articles.abstract: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) affect up to 40% of patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, yet identification requires laborious, inconsistent manual chart review. Here we show that agentic artificial intelligence coupled with human verification could enhance efficiency, performance and consistency for irAE assessment. We developed and evaluated an agentic large language model system to extract the presence, temporality, severity grade, attribution and certainty of six irAE types from clinical notes. Retrospectively, the system achieved a macro-averaged F 1 of 0.92 for current-event detection and 0.66 for multi-class severity grading; self-consistency improved F 1 by 0.14. The best-performing configuration cost approximately US$0.02 per note. In prospective silent deployment over 3 months, the binary F 1 was 0.72–0.79. In a randomized crossover study of clinical trial staff, agentic assistance reduced annotation time by 2.71 min ( P < 0.001), increased complete-match accuracy (odds ratio 1.45; 95% confidence interval 1.01–2.08; P = 0.045) and improved interannotator agreement (Krippendorff’s α from 0.22–0.51 to 0.82–0.85).

articles.title: Chemical-linkage-regulated single-phase crystallization and uniform gallium alloying for efficient solution-processed chalcopyrite solar cells
articles.abstract: Controlling phase evolution and composition homogeneity are challenging for chalcopyrites. Ma, Wu, Liu, Yan et al. use acetate anions to build complex networks in precursor solution, achieving single-phase crystallization and an 18.53% efficient Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cell.

articles.title: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics
articles.abstract: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells are promising for high area-normalized power output, but factors governing the photothermal stability of perovskite absorbers remains unclear. Xu et al. identify lattice compliance as a descriptor when screening stable perovskites.

articles.title: Translating sulfur flow batteries into deployable systems
articles.abstract: Sulfur-based redox flow batteries promise low-cost, long-duration energy storage using abundant active materials, but commercial success depends on much more than low-cost materials. Yi-Chun Lu and her team explore how deployment reshapes research priorities and reveals the scientific and engineering bottlenecks that determine technology translation.

articles.title: Autophagy in macrophages curtails IL-1α-mediated immune priming against lung infections
articles.abstract: Wang and colleagues show that autophagy deficiency in alveolar macrophages upregulates the expression of IL-1α and increases resistance to respiratory infections.

articles.title: Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
articles.abstract: The electron-beam-assisted subtraction method enables the controllable fabrication of free-standing metal oxide monolayers, along with lateral heterostructures and twisted bilayers, expanding the material space of 2D quantum systems.

articles.title: Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces
articles.abstract: Photonic metasurfaces patterned in anisotropic ReS2 create robust, spectrally scalable directional photonic flatbands, enabling the topological control of polarization-resolved exciton–polaritons and enhanced light–matter coupling.

articles.title: Writing monolayer oxides with electrons
articles.abstract: Layered metal oxyhalides can be selectively dehalogenated inside a scanning transmission electron microscope, yielding free-standing monolayer oxide sheets and coupling synthesis with atomic-resolution observation.

articles.title: 5-year outcomes of chemotherapy de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and exploratory circulating tumor DNA analyses from the randomized phase 2 PHERGain trial
articles.abstract: A 5-year secondary analysis of the phase 2 PHERGain trial supports the clinical utility of a PET-guided adaptive strategy for treatment de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and provides circulating tumor DNA insights that could inform further treatment approaches.

articles.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability
articles.abstract: A multimodal vision language foundation model, EVLF-FM, integrates extensive clinical data and advanced training techniques, achieving superior diagnostic accuracy and explainability across diverse imaging modalities, enhancing clinical decision-making through robust reasoning and interpretability.

articles.title: A small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer’s disease
articles.abstract: Preclinical analysis and a phase 1 trial support VG-3927 as a promising drug candidate for Alzheimer’s disease, demonstrating successful penetration of the central nervous system, target engagement and tolerability.

articles.title: Applying digital twins to prevent preterm births
articles.abstract: Researchers developed a digital twin framework to safely evaluate the effects of drugs on the immune system and time to labor, which could enable personalized interventions to prevent preterm births.

articles.title: Insights into early-onset colorectal cancer from a single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas of colorectal cancer across the age continuum
articles.abstract: A high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas of 189 colorectal tumors from patients aged 20–90+ years uncovers age-associated features of colorectal cancer.

articles.title: Advancing morphological profiling with self-supervised learning through comparative insights into representation learning of cellular perturbations
articles.abstract: This Article presents a large-scale analysis of self-supervised learning methods for high-content morphological profiling.

articles.title: Enhanced cfDNA methylation profiling by detection and correction of jagged ends
articles.abstract: The computational tool JEEPERS detects and corrects jagged-end-induced errors in cell-free DNA methylation analysis, demonstrating improved performance in multiple applications, such as cancer detection and monitoring.

articles.title: Imaging hot-electron Thomson cooling beyond the Boltzmann–Onsager framework
articles.abstract: Classical Thomson cooling is inefficient. Now non-equilibrium energy dissipation with a breakdown of the Boltzmann–Onsager limit is demonstrated by imaging hot electrons in HgTe and HgCdTe quantum wells.

articles.title: Priming systemic immunity against glioblastoma
articles.abstract: A preprint by Wisdom et al. shows that combining radiotherapy with intramuscular mRNA vaccination supports better T cell priming and produces complete responses in glioblastoma transplant models in mice.

articles.title: Design principles for porous liquid synthesis
articles.abstract: Porous liquids combine permanent porosity with fluidity, extending the design of porous materials beyond conventional solid frameworks. This Perspective outlines universal design principles, emerging synthetic strategies and theory-guided methodologies that enable rational control of permanent porosity, fluidity and functionality, accelerating the predictive development of next-generation porous liquids.

articles.title: Liquid-phase growth of dense ceramic films
articles.abstract: By decoupling ceramic-film densification from high-temperature sintering, molten-salt-mediated liquid-phase growth enables a dense, compositionally uniform proton-conducting thin film to form at 800 °C, despite its melting point exceeding 2,700 °C. This strategy opens opportunities for low-temperature ceramic fabrication and on-demand materials design.

articles.title: Christoph Bachofen
articles.abstract: Christoph Bachofen, Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research (WSL) Site de Lausanne (Switzerland).

articles.title: Correction to ‘The underappreciated roles of fog and dew on vegetation and biocrusts’
Jenn Brophy
Light‐induced phyB‐NPR1 interaction activates systemic acquired resistance
articles.abstract: Model showing phyB‐mediated fine‐tuning of defence responses via NPR1. Summary Light perception by phytochromes controls different aspects of plant–environment interactions including plant immunity; however, the underpinning molecular mechanisms are less well‐understood. Upon localized attack on leaves by avirulent pathogens, the systemic accumulation of salicylic acid (SA) is required for the establishment of systemic acquired resistance (SAR) throughout the plant to curtail pathogen spread. We demonstrate that light‐mediated Small Ubiquitin‐like Modifier 1 (SUMO) conjugation to phytochrome B (phyB) is critical for increasing cellular SA levels to orchestrate SAR upon avirulent bacterial infection. SA promotes SUMOylation of phyB, which enables it to interact with the SA receptor, Nonexpressor of Pathogenesis‐Related 1 (NPR1) via its SUMO1‐interacting motif. SUMOylation of phyB is enhanced by the accumulation of SUMO‐Conjugating Enzyme (E2) (SCE1) and the degradation of SUMO protease Overly Tolerant to Salt 1 (OTS1) in SAR‐induced systemic tissues. Using confocal imaging, we show that SUMOylated phyB undergoes liquid–liquid phase separation together with NPR1 in nuclear bodies. We further validated through immunoprecipitation, ChIP and RNA‐seq analysis that SUMOylated phyB associates with NPR1 and TGA transcription factors in nuclear photobodies to induce the expression of PR1 gene. We reveal a post‐translational modification mechanism in which light‐induced SUMOylation of photoreceptors promotes SAR by regulating NPR1 function.

articles.title: Trait‐based plant ecology: some history and some future
articles.abstract: Schematic of plant species range boundaries, some mechanisms that might set them, and some traits that might explain them. Summary Since around the year 2000, trait‐based ecology has become self‐aware as a strand of research within ecology. How did this happen? What is trait‐based ecology now? And where might it go in future? This paper offers selective answers to those questions. We first outline the history leading up to the emergence of trait‐based plant ecology during the 1990s. Second, we assess briefly what has been achieved up to mid‐2020s. Third, we discuss two challenges (among many) for trait‐based plant ecology over the next 25 yr. One is about the boundaries of species ranges along temperature gradients. Some of these boundaries may be decided by thermal tolerance, others by biotic interactions such as competition or pathogens. How can we identify which applies to which species? Which traits, feasible to measure across many species, might help with this? A second major challenge is about the global zonation of vegetation physiognomy or biome types. How well can we explain this in terms of traits, and from first principles, meaning via eco‐evolutionary models for why different trait values should be competent and competitive in different settings? First‐principle rules for how ecosystems are constructed should be central to ecology as a discipline. Resumen Desde aproximadamente el año 2000, la ecología basada en caracteres funcionales se consolidó como una línea de investigación autoconsciente y distintiva. ¿Cómo surgió, qué representa actualmente y hacia dónde avanzaría? Este artículo ofrece algunas respuestas selectivas. Primero, resumimos los antecedentes históricos que condujeron al desarrollo de la ecología vegetal basada en caracteres funcionales en los años 1990. Segundo, evaluamos los logros en la década de 2020. Tercero, examinamos dos desafíos (entre los muchos que existen) para los próximos 25 años. El primer desafío se refiere a los límites de distribución de las especies a lo largo de gradientes térmicos. Algunos pueden estar determinados por la tolerancia térmica y otros por interacciones bióticas, como la competencia o los patógenos. ¿Cómo podrían distinguirse estos mecanismos y qué caracteres, factibles de ser medidos en muchas especies, podrían ayudar? El segundo desafío involucra la zonación global de las fisonomías de vegetación y los biomas. ¿Hasta qué punto pueden explicarse mediante caracteres funcionales y primeros principios, es decir modelos eco‐evolutivos, cuáles valores de caracteres deberían ser competentes y competitivos en diferentes ambientes? Las reglas fundamentales que explican a partir de primeros principios cómo se construyen los ecosistemas deberían ocupar un lugar central en la ecología.

articles.title: Tree and neighborhood damage have distinct effects on delayed mortality after a severe hurricane
articles.abstract: Directed acyclic diagram (DAG) illustrating causal relationships between variables to estimate the effects of individual and neighborhood damage on delayed mortality. Summary Tropical forest resilience, biodiversity, and carbon sequestration depend on tree survival. Disturbance events, such as hurricanes, generate distinct forms of damage at the individual‐tree and neighborhood scale, providing a unique setting to disentangle the causal contributions of mortality drivers. Leveraging post‐hurricane census data for nearly 4000 trees in the Luquillo Forest Dynamics Plot, Puerto Rico, we used a causal inference framework combined with Bayesian multilevel models to estimate the effect of individual‐ and neighborhood‐scale damage on delayed tree mortality following Hurricane Maria (2017). Individual damage effects depended on species identity and tree size. Stem break emerged as the most lethal form of damage across the community. Neighborhood damage was associated with elevated mortality following Hurricane Maria, independent of focal tree damage. This effect was strongest among large trees, consistent with disproportionately high physiological stress resulting from greater inherent metabolic demands, refoliation energy costs, and evapotranspiration following canopy recovery. Severe biomass loss (> 75% crown loss) buffered large trees from negative neighborhood effects, revealing a positive pruning effect on survival. Our study advances mechanistic understanding of delayed tree mortality, while also suggesting how mortality patterns may shift with expected increases in disturbance severity under a warming climate. Resumen La resiliencia, la biodiversidad y el secuestro de carbono de los bosques tropicales dependen de la supervivencia de los árboles. Las perturbaciones, como los huracanes, generan distintos tipos de daño tanto a escala del árbol individual como de su vecindario, proporcionando un escenario único para desentrañar las contribuciones causales de los factores determinantes de la mortalidad. Utilizando censos de aproximadamente 4000 árboles en la Parcela de Dinámica del Bosque de Luquillo, Puerto Rico, usamos un método de inferencia causal combinado con modelos multinivel bayesianos para estimar el efecto del daño a escala individual y de vecindario sobre la mortalidad diferida de los árboles tras el huracán María (2017). Los efectos del daño individual dependieron de la identidad de la especie y del tamaño del árbol. La rotura del tronco resultó ser el tipo de daño más letal en toda la comunidad. El daño en el vecindario se asoció con un aumento de la mortalidad tras el huracán María, independientemente del daño sufrido por el árbol focal. Este efecto fue más fuerte entre los árboles grandes, lo cual concuerda con un estrés fisiológico desproporcionadamente alto debido a mayores demandas metabólicas inherentes, costos energéticos de refoliación y evapotranspiración tras la recuperación del dosel. La pérdida severa de biomasa (> 75 % de pérdida de copa) amortiguó los efectos negativos del vecindario sobre los árboles grandes, revelando un ‘efecto poda’ positivo sobre la supervivencia. Nuestro estudio avanza en la comprensión mecanística de la mortalidad diferida de los árboles y, además, sugiere cómo los patrones de mortalidad pueden cambiar con los aumentos esperados en la severidad de las perturbaciones bajo un clima en calentamiento.

articles.title: When wounds cool: a physical cue for plant repair
A chemomechanical bifurcation landscape unifies sustained growth, length homeostasis, and regenerative collapse in axons
articles.abstract: Axonal growth machinery is largely shared across neurons, but axons exhibit strikingly different fates depending on developmental and environmental context: sustained elongation in peripheral neurons under permissive conditions, length homeostasis in cortical neurons after target innervation, and pathological collapse into dystrophic endbulbs in injured adult central nervous system (CNS) axons. These divergent outcomes have resisted explanation by length-sensing and biomechanical models that treat long-range transport and local force generation as separate problems. We unify these phenomena through a mechanochemical model that couples bidirectional motor transport and intracellular signaling to growth-cone balance of axonal tension, actomyosin contraction, and adhesion within a single feedback loop: The lengthening axon uses its own growing transport delay to establish self-limiting mechanical feedback, as the accumulating delay reshapes signaling waveforms to progressively elevate myosin contractility against actin-driven protrusion. Two physical parameters, the transport delay and the signaling feedback strength, organize axon fate into a unified state-space landscape spanning sustained growth, length homeostasis, and pathological collapse. Reduced feedback strength weakens this self-limiting mechanical feedback by simultaneously enhancing protrusion and suppressing contractility, providing a mechanistic interpretation of axon lengthening under partial reduction of retrograde transport. Bistability in the inhibitory regime explains why mature CNS tracts persist where nascent sprouts collapse, recasting regenerative failure as a state-dependent gate rather than a capacity limit. The framework predicts that partial rather than complete inhibition of retrograde transport could shift collapsed axons across the bifurcation into a growth-permissive regime, identifying a class of interventions complementary to existing capacity-restoration strategies for nerve injury.

articles.title: A sulfotyrosine motif in the human TrkB extracellular domain is required for activation by the agonist antibody ZEB85
articles.abstract: The brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) signaling axis is a key effector of synaptic plasticity and neuroprotection. While TrkB activation is a major target to prevent neural dysfunction, stimulation with exogenous BDNF administration has not proven tractable given the unfavorable physiochemical properties of BDNF. In addition, BDNF also activates a cell death pathway by binding to the neurotrophin receptor p75. The TrkB agonist antibody ZEB85 provides an alternative route to the selective activation of TrkB. To understand the ZEB85 mechanism of action, we mapped the binding site for ZEB85 to the TrkB extracellular juxtamembrane domain and found a sulfotyrosine modification at residue 400 crucial for ZEB85 interaction and activation of TrkB signaling. We determined the structures of ZEB85 and BDNF bound to their respective binding sites on human TrkB suggesting independent sites for each ligand, despite prior evidence of direct competition. Using structure-guided BDNF- and ZEB85-binding deficient TrkB mutants, we assessed their ability to sequester ligands from full-length TrkB in cultured human neurons. We found that the BDNF binding site extends into the juxtamembrane domain of TrkB but does not require the sulfotyrosine 400 to activate TrkB. Together with biophysical analysis and AlphaFold modeling, these results explain how BDNF can displace ZEB85 from TrkB through an overlapping epitope. Our findings reveal unique features of TrkB, not present in the related neurotrophin receptors TrkA and TrkC and suggest future directions to explore the role of sulfotyrosine in TrkB signaling.

articles.title: A symbiogenic merger enabled by oxygen initiated the evolution of eukaryotes
articles.abstract: Recently, extensive genetic information about archaeal hosts at the basis of eukaryogenesis has come to light. Characterization of these first eukaryotic common ancestor (FECA) related organisms allows improved understanding of the enigmatic FECA to last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA) transition. However, these gene-centered discoveries have the unfortunate side effect of entrenching erroneous ideas about early eukaryotic evolution. This is apparent in the two-Domain vision of life, with eukaryotes seen as specialized Asgard archaea, while underestimating the contribution of the endosymbiont to eukaryogenesis. Establishment of the alpha-proteobacterium as the future mitochondrion is treated as one of many such endosymbiotic occurrences, ignoring its unique evolutionary position. I will marshal evidence for symbiogenic mechanisms involved in the FECA to LECA transition, with a key role for the endosymbiont’s electron transport chain and its acceptor molecular oxygen, especially in the incarnation of reactive oxygen species occurring in the host cytoplasm. We should overcome overestimating gene determinism, while not sufficiently allowing for effects of biological hierarchies, emergent properties, and chance. Many eukaryotic properties are best understood by envisaging the crucial uptake of the future mitochondrion as a merger instead of an acquisition. This merger is characterized by a new kind of elaborate cellular entity emerging as a result of rapid coevolution, replacing a scenario in which already complex pre-eukaryotes acquired endosymbionts, accompanied by important, but limited, changes. Successful mergers are rare because they are intrinsically more difficult, but synergistically open up completely new areas of possibilities, as illustrated by incredible eukaryotic success.

articles.title: Complexity functions of infinite sequences
articles.abstract: We address the inverse problem for complexity functions of infinite words, which asks which functions can occur as complexity functions of infinite words. We survey our recent advances on this problem and several of its ramifications. We describe an asymptotic solution to the inverse problem, realizing every function satisfying two necessary conditions as the complexity function of an infinite word up to asymptotic equivalence. We then turn to phenomena beyond asymptotic equivalence, presenting constructions of infinite words with seemingly contradictory behavior of the discrete derivatives of their complexity functions. These lead to a solution of a 1995 problem of Cassaigne and to applications in symbolic dynamics, including the question of convergence of Rauzy graphs, as well as to the growth and asymptotic invariants of algebraic structures.

articles.title: Computation and sampling for Schubert specializations
articles.abstract: We study a problem at the interface of enumerative algebraic geometry, algebraic combinatorics, and the statistical mechanics of vertex models with long-range interactions. We develop methods to explore the values S w ( 1 , … , 1 ) of Schubert polynomials (called principal specializations), which count reduced bumpless pipe dreams (RBPDs) with boundary permutation w ∈ S n . We exhibit counterexamples to the conjecture of Merzon and Smirnov that S w ( 1 n ) is maximized on layered permutations; the smallest such example we find is at n = 17. Despite the counterexamples, we present bounds that support a refined conjecture that the maximum of S w ( 1 n ) over all w ∈ S n grows at the same asymptotic rate as the maximum over layered permutations (found by Morales, Pak, and Panova). We implement and benchmark four recurrences for Schubert specializations: the descent formula of Macdonald, the transition formula of Lascoux–Schützenberger, the cotransition formula of Knutson, and the formula of Billey, Jockusch, and Stanley. We also explore typical random permutations drawn with probability proportional to S w ( 1 n ) , equivalently from uniformly random RBPDs. Our simulations reveal a permuton-like limit analogous to the Grothendieck setting studied by Morales, Panova, Petrov, and Yeliussizov. For sampling, we show that the standard monotone Coupling From The Past framework does not apply to RBPDs, leaving exact uniform sampling open. To bypass this, we develop an efficient Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler augmented with macroscopic “droop” updates that preserve connectivity and accelerate mixing. Our publicly available fast implementations reach n = 20 for exact computation of S w ( 1 n ) and n = 100 for Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling using a chain whose stationary distribution is uniform on RBPDs (run on a cluster).

articles.title: Correction for Bernabé-Rubio and Watt, Caspase-8-dependent autophagy regulates neutrophil infiltration in oral squamous cell carcinoma
Crowding limits relative bacterial surface accumulation with density-induced effective heating
articles.abstract: The accumulation of microswimmers near walls has been studied for decades. While hydrodynamics and single-cell kinematics are well-explored, the role of cell-cell interactions remains understudied. However, in realistic, crowded environments such as the human gut, these interactions can be just as crucial. Here, we demonstrate that they actively weaken bacterial surface accumulation. Analysis of entrapped cell tracks reveals that crowding enhances orientational fluctuations, which increase the effective rotational diffusion and facilitate wall escape. A minimal model shows that this collective effect is equivalent to raising the system’s effective temperature with density.

articles.title: Ddx3x deficiency in mice impairs corticofugal motor circuits and causes motor deficits that are attenuated by early-life exercise
articles.abstract: The X-linked RNA helicase DDX3X is a high-risk gene for autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability primarily in females. Individuals with pathogenic variants in DDX3X have pervasive and often severe motor manifestations. Using mouse models, we studied the circuits underlying the motor phenotypes associated with Ddx3x deficiency and examined the feasibility of an early intervention to ameliorate motor trajectories. We show that Ddx3x controls both the development and later plasticity of motor circuits connecting the motor cortex with the pontine nuclei. Ddx3x haploinsufficiency during development affects the dendritic arborization of corticopontine neurons. Juvenile-onset Ddx3x loss in corticopontine neurons is sufficient to induce adult motor impairments overlapping with those caused by chemogenetic disruption of corticopontine circuits. Further, Ddx3x mutant mice engage corticopontine circuits in skilled motor tasks in a sex-dependent manner. Last, Ddx3x haploinsufficient female mice undergoing a juvenile motor intervention show long-lasting specific benefits in their adult motor function. Together, these findings establish Ddx3x as an essential regulator of corticopontine neuron development and function and provide an early motor intervention to ameliorate motor outcomes in a mouse model of DDX3X haploinsufficiency.

articles.title: Direct atomic-scale observation reveals rare earth element fractionation at mineral–water interfaces
articles.abstract: Clay minerals, ubiquitous across diverse geological systems, exert fundamental controls on critical geochemical processes, particularly through their adsorptive interactions with economically vital elements such as heavy rare earth elements (HREEs). The adsorption of HREEs onto clay surfaces is not only the key process that enriches these critical resources but also a potential archive for dating significant weathering events. However, the atomic-scale mechanisms governing the preferential adsorption and fractionation of rare earth elements (REEs) at mineral–water interfaces have remained poorly constrained. Here, employing in situ atomic-scale imaging via high-resolution atomic force microscopy, we systematically investigate the adsorption behaviors of light and heavy REEs (La, Y, Yb) onto key crystallographic planes—Si-basal, Al-basal, and edge terminations—of representative clay minerals (kaolinite, illite, mica) under environmentally relevant conditions (pH 4.8 to 6.4). We directly visualize and quantitatively reveal that Si-basal planes selectively enrich HREEs with pH-enhanced adsorption capacity, whereas Al-basal planes exhibit negligible REE adsorption below pH 5.8 but preferential HREE adsorption at pH 6.4. Integrating synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we identify the adsorption mechanism of REE on Si-basal and Al-basal/edge planes as outer-sphere complexation and inner-sphere binding, respectively. Furthermore, we quantify the contributions of distinct planes via surface complexation modeling, revealing Si-dominated to Al- and edge-controlled adsorption with elevating pH. These atomic-scale findings not only resolve long-standing debates about clay mineral-mediated REE fractionation but also redefine fundamental paradigms of surface reactivity at silicate mineral–water interfaces, offering insights into the cycling and metallogeny of other critical metals in aqueous and sedimentary environments.

articles.title: Elucidating molecular regulatory rules of nanoparticle biological identity via standardized deep proteomics
articles.abstract: The biological identity of nanoparticles is often redefined upon exposure to physiological fluids through the formation of a protein corona (PC), However, the molecular rules linking synthetic design to biological fate remain elusive owing to the fragmented and inconsistent proteomics data. Here, leveraging a standardized deep proteomic database of 42 diverse nanomaterials, we reveal the general molecular selection rules that govern the PC formation. We demonstrate that the PC is not a product of random adsorption but is shaped by strict property-dependent recruitment. First, surface charge regulates cellular uptake, with anionic nanoparticles specifically recruiting adhesion proteins to promote Itgav-mediated endocytosis, thus forming a causal charge-corona-receptor chain. Second, PEGylation engineers immune evasion by selectively depleting specific complement and coagulation factors, rather than merely preventing protein adsorption. Third, nanoparticle geometry imposes structural constraints and selects proteins based on specific physicochemical features such as lysine content. Beyond mechanistic insights, we show that material-specific PCs can rebalance the serum proteome and enable the detection of low-abundance disease biomarkers. This work shifts the paradigm from empirical description toward rule-based prediction and provides a foundational framework for rationally engineering nanomedicines with predictable and programmable biological identities.

articles.title: Global bee bioregions mirror those of other taxa despite a uniquely bimodal latitudinal diversity gradient
articles.abstract: Bioregionalization, the partitioning of the globe into areas of biotic similarity, is one of nature’s most striking patterns, and highly congruent boundaries have been identified across plants, tetrapods, ants, and butterflies. However, these taxa also share a unimodal latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG), raising the question of whether bioregionalization and the LDG are mechanistically coupled or instead arise from largely independent processes acting on different timescales. Bees (Hymenoptera: Anthophila) provide a natural test, their diversity peaking at mid-latitudes rather than in the tropics. Using range estimates for 3,370 species and a phylogenetic beta-diversity framework, we recover 21 bee bioregions nested within at least six major realms (Australasia, Indomalaya-Oceania, Nearctic, Neotropics, Palearctic, and Sub-Sahara) that closely align with those of other taxa despite bees’ atypical diversity gradient. We propose that bioregionalization and species richness are decoupled because they arise from distinct processes: the former reflects historical dispersal and evolutionary history, the latter local diversification, extinction, and environmental filtering. Our analysis provides a global biogeographic framework for future bee research and highlights the processes shaping the world‘s major biogeographic boundaries.

articles.title: Hydration at the base of the mantle transition zone by ancient subductions in Asia
articles.abstract: Whether and how the subduction processes result in water enrichment at the base of the mantle transition zone (MTZ) remain elusive. The major orogenic belts of the Asian continent, including the Central Asian, Tethyan, and Alpine–Himalayan belts, which record extensive subduction processes, offer an ideal target to address the hydration of the MTZ and its relationship with subduction. Here, we map water content at the MTZ base by combining mineral physics constraints on hydrous pyrolite and global seismic observations of velocity structure and 660-km discontinuity topography. Our results indicate an average global water content of approximately 0.14 wt%, with pronounced hydration anomalies in parts of Asia. Linking these anomalies with reconstructions of past subduction events since 410 Ma reveals extensive water delivery to the MTZ, particularly beneath parts of the Mongol–Okhotsk suture zone, the Central Asian Orogenic Belt, and the Tethyan orogenic domain, where water content exceeds 0.5 wt%. These results connect ancient subduction history to present-day mantle hydration, offering insights into Earth’s deep water cycle.

articles.title: Intrinsic function of leptin receptor–regulated endothelial PD-L1
articles.abstract: Programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD-L1) is an immune checkpoint protein expressed in vascular endothelial cells (ECs). In contrast to cancer, our understanding of endothelial PD-L1 in relation to metabolic syndromes and its vascular complications is less studied. For example, its regulation and intrinsic function remain unclear. Here, we showed that endothelial PD-L1 is regulated by leptin receptor signaling in male mice. In particular, endothelial PD-L1 expression is affected by leptin resistance. A lack of leptin receptors leads to PD-L1 downregulation in vascular ECs via posttranslational degradation. To understand the fundamental roles of endothelial PD-L1, RNA interference and selective knockout are employed in human endothelium and animals, respectively. Silencing or deleting endothelial PD-L1 expression delays cell cycle progression and proliferation due to rat sarcoma (RAS)/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) inactivation. In obesity, endothelial PD-L1 deficiency impairs the EC turnover and worsens the vascular function. Overall, we provide an insight into how endothelial PD-L1 contributes to vascular homeostasis, suggesting its pathophysiological importance in maintaining cellular turnover.

articles.title: Potential energy landscape networks of confined vortex matter
articles.abstract: Advances in nanoscale patterning of superconducting films [Y. L. Wang et al ., Nat. Nanotechnol. 13 , 560–565 (2018)] and the availability of submicron-sized superconducting single crystals with controlled geometry allow for the investigation of superconducting vortex matter under extreme confinement [A. K. Geim et al ., Nature 390 , 259–262 (1997)]. It has been observed in these systems that the interplay between sample geometry and vortex number results in the emergence of so-called “magic number” configurations which show unusually high stability against thermal fluctuations. However, a detailed, comprehensive theoretical study of the ground state and metastable states of confined vortex matter has not yet been developed. Here we show that the intricate properties of a system of vortices under extreme confinement can be characterized in detail by mapping the potential energy landscape of the system onto a network [J. P. K. Doye, Phys. Rev. Lett. 88 , 238701 (2002)] with nodes corresponding to local potential energy minima and edges to transition states between local minima. We apply these techniques to systems featuring repelling particles/vortices confined in small containers of various geometric shapes. We demonstrate that the ground state almost always belongs to a subset of system states within the deepest network core. We find that the emergence of magic number configurations in the ground state results in a drastic decrease in the complexity of the entire network. We use large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to study the size dependence of melting in different configurations. We find that as confinement effects increase, magic number configurations transition to states with lower symmetry.

articles.title: The ABCD hypothesis
articles.abstract: If α and β are cardinals, then the cardinal exponentiation α β is the set of all functions from α into β . The ABCD hypothesis is the statement that for all infinite cardinals α ≤ β and γ ≤ δ , | α β | ≤ | γ δ | if and only if α ≤ γ and β ≤ δ . The Axiom of Determinacy, AD, states that every two-player infinite game on ω has a winning strategy for one of the two players. Let Θ be the supremum of the ordinals onto which R surjects. This paper will show that if AD holds and V = L ( R ) , then the ABCD hypothesis holds below Θ .

articles.title: The efficiency of information gain by natural selection
articles.abstract: Natural selection enriches populations for genotypes that are well adapted to their environments, accumulating information about the selective conditions in the process. Therefore, selection can be viewed as a learning process through which populations acquire information about the environment. Motoo Kimura derived a relationship between the amount of information gained by selection and a measure of the inefficiency of the selective process, known as substitution load [M. Kimura, Genet. Res. 2, 127–140 (1961)]. Due to the gradual nature of selection and the ongoing mismatch of types to the environment, a lineage that is still acquiring information has lower mean fitness than a lineage that already has it. While this has been an influential insight, we find that Kimura’s model is inconsistent with selection experiments involving Escherichia coli . To address limitations in this model and develop a more robust measure for the efficiency of selection, we turn to computational learning theory. We show that the learning-theoretic concept of regret quantifies the inefficiency of selection as a learning process in terms of relative lineage fitness. We establish bounds on the efficiency of information gain in general settings, including frequency-dependent selection and arbitrary environmental change. We experimentally validate these bounds and demonstrate that our extended theory recovers Kimura’s fundamental insight. Finally, we show that selection is an asymptotically optimal algorithm for the basic problem faced by evolving populations and that it acquires information more efficiently than comparable processes in complex environments.

articles.title: Consistent Time Reversal and Reliable and Accurate Inference in the Presence of Memory
articles.abstract: Thermodynamic inference from coarse observations remains a key challenge. Memory, in particular correlations between consecutively observed mesostates, blur signatures of irreversibility and must be accounted for in defining physical time reversal, which remains an open problem. We derive an experim…

articles.title: Curvature Potential Formulation for Thin Elastic Sheets
articles.abstract: Thin sheets, from graphene to biological membranes, exhibit wrinkling, folding, and thermal deformations driven by geometric nonlinearities. They are treated using weakly nonlinear theories such as the Föppl–von Kármán equations, whose reliance on small slopes and a single-valued height field exclud…

articles.title: Odd-Even Parity of Nonlinear Hall Effects in Bilayer Graphene
articles.abstract: Experiments reveal a potentially useful odd–even dichotomy in the nonlinear Hall response of bilayer graphene.

articles.title: Quantum Monte Carlo Studies of U(1) Lattice Gauge Models of Kondo Breakdown
articles.abstract: In the local-moment regime, heavy fermions are most economically described by a compact U(1) gauge theory. Motivated by this perspective, we study a minimal compact U(1) lattice gauge model describing a spin chain coupled to two-dimensional Dirac conduction electrons. The spin chain is described by …

articles.title: Reduced Gravitational Wave Signal Reopens the Ultralight Primordial Black Hole Window
articles.abstract: The hot big bang may have emerged from evaporation of primordial black holes (PBHs) lighter than ${10}^{9}\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{g}$. Standard monochromatic treatments predict nearly simultaneous evaporation, abrupt reheating, and a large poltergeist scalar-induced gravitational wave signal. We con…

articles.title: Making information engines do useful work
articles.abstract: The thermodynamic and quantum mechanical properties of topological insulators provide a path toward scalable energy storage in information-based batteries.

articles.title: Corrigendum to “Proton-coupled charge storage in aqueous batteries: mechanisms, interfaces, and design strategies” [Prog. Mater. Sci. 165, Part A (2027) 101821]
Degradation of metallic interconnects in solid oxide electrolysis cells: mechanisms, materials challenges, and design strategies
A case study in conflicts of interest
A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness
articles.abstract: At the skin’s surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E 2 , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.
