Seed‐derived microbiota in the Medicago holobiont: Associations with host phylogeny and breeding‐associated traits
articles.abstract: Seed‐derived bacterial communities tracked host phylogeny across wild Medicago, revealing a phylosymbiotic pattern, whereas fungal communities did not. In cultivated alfalfa, bacterial composition differed between cultivars with high‐yielding and stress‐resistant traits. Trait‐associated bacterial SynComs improved plant growth under non‐stress or combined drought–salinity conditions, respectively, demonstrating the functional relevance of breeding‐associated microbiota. Abstract Seed microbiota occupy unique ecological niches within plants and can form intimate associations with their hosts. However, how seed‐derived microbial communities are related to host phylogeny and breeding‐associated traits across natural and agricultural contexts, and whether trait‐associated microorganisms influence plant performance, remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized endophytic communities in sterile‐grown seedlings from surface‐sterilized seeds of 10 wild Medicago genotypes representing 8 species and 20 domesticated alfalfa cultivars spanning multiple breeding decades. We assessed phylosymbiosis in wild hosts, examined associations between microbial community composition and breeding‐related cultivar characteristics in domesticated alfalfa, and constructed trait‐associated bacterial synthetic communities (SynComs) for functional evaluation. In wild Medicago, bacterial, but not fungal, community composition exhibited significant congruence with host phylogeny, consistent with phylosymbiosis. In domesticated alfalfa, bacterial community composition was associated with cultivar trait category (high‐yielding vs. stress‐resistant), whereas fungal communities were not. Six cultivable candidate bacterial strains associated with the two trait categories were assembled into two SynComs, SynComY (high‐yielding associated) and SynComR (stress‐resistance‐associated). In vitro assays revealed multiple plant growth‐promoting and stress‐tolerance capacities among the constituent strains, while greenhouse experiments showed that SynComY promoted plant growth and SynComR enhanced plant performance under combined drought–salinity stress. Synthesis. Together, these findings show that seed‐derived bacterial community structure is associated with host phylogeny in wild Medicago and breeding‐related trait differentiation in cultivated alfalfa, and further establish that selected bacteria associated with the latter can influence plant performance. Viewed within a holobiont framework, this combined evidence broadens our understanding of seed‐derived microbiota across natural and agricultural contexts and highlights their potential value for microbiome‐informed crop improvement.

articles.title: How the TREX-2 complex associates with the nuclear pore
articles.abstract: Obarska-Kosinska et al. combine cryo-electron tomography, AI-assisted modeling, and crosslinking mass spectrometry to build an extended model of the human nuclear pore. They identify five additional nucleoporins and show how the nuclear basket and TREX-2 complex are attached to the nuclear ring, revealing the spatial organization of mRNP export.

articles.title: Genomic Signatures of Endemic Pathogen Exposure in a Declining Amphibian
articles.abstract: Endemic wildlife diseases can impose strong selection on threatened populations, yet whether persistence is associated with adaptive genomic responses remains poorly understood. We tested whether long‐term exposure to Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) following population declines has left detectable selection signatures in the genome of the alpine tree frog, Litoria verreauxii alpina. Because prior work suggests limited immunity to Bd within the species, we did not expect persistence to be explained primarily by repeated shifts at canonical immune genes. Instead, we expected pathogen‐associated differentiation, if present, to be diffuse and weakly shared across contrasts, potentially involving regulatory, signalling or reproduction pathways consistent with tolerance, compensatory recruitment or demographic turnover. Using genome‐wide SNP data, we compared Bd‐naïve and Bd‐endemic populations and two 11‐year temporal resampling contrasts. Candidate SNPs were annotated to identify genomic context, nearby genes, putative functions and overlap with previously reported Bd‐associated transcriptomic responses. Using an empirical 99th‐percentile XtX threshold, scans identified high‐differentiation candidate SNPs in all contrasts. Most occurred in noncoding and putatively regulatory regions, with relatively few canonical immune genes. Candidate‐associated genes were more often linked to signalling, transcriptional regulation and cell‐cycle processes. A descriptive comparison with previous work in the species identified 64 candidate‐associated genes matching Bd‐associated transcriptomic annotations, supporting several immune‐adjacent, regulatory, cellular and reproduction candidates. Persistence under endemic Bd might reflect pathogen‐associated selection, compensatory recruitment and demographic change following recurrent adult mortality rather than uniform adaptive rescue through immune resistance.

articles.title: Divarasib as Compared with Sotorasib or Adagrasib in KRAS G12C–Mutated NSCLC
articles.abstract: BackgroundDivarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib.MethodsIn this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety.ResultsA total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. The median progression-free survival was 9.8 months with divarasib and 5.7 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.76; PConclusionsAmong patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC, divarasib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than control treatment. (Supported by F. Hoffmann-La Roche; Krascendo 1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06497556.).

articles.title: Osimertinib–Savolitinib in Advanced NSCLC after Progression during EGFR-TKI Therapy
articles.abstract: BackgroundSavolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy.MethodsIn this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety.ResultsOf the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; PConclusionsOsimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

articles.title: Sacituzumab Tirumotecan plus Pembrolizumab in PD-L1–Negative Advanced NSCLC
articles.abstract: BackgroundPembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal.MethodsIn this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis.ResultsA total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; PConclusionsAmong patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. (Funded by Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical; OptiTROP-Lung06 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06711900.).

articles.title: A license to disperse: climatic niche lability and geographic expansion shape the diversification of Oleaceae
articles.abstract: SEM for seven variables (rPC1, rPC2, rPC3, rFRic, FRic, dispersal, and speciation) in Oleaceae and that in Jasmineae and Oleeae, respectively. Summary Patterns of species diversity reflect interactions among ecological, biogeographic, and lineage‐specific evolutionary processes. Oleaceae provides a useful comparative system because its five tribes differ markedly in species richness, geographic extent, dispersal history, and genomic background. Using distribution data for 476 species and a time‐calibrated phylogeny of 283 Oleaceae species spanning all five tribes, we integrated ecological niche modelling, ancestral‐range and climatic‐niche reconstruction, diversification‐rate analyses, and phylogenetic comparative methods while accounting for uneven tribal sampling. Climatic niche position and breadth evolved heterogeneously across Oleaceae, while major range expansions beyond the reconstructed ancestral Asian region were concentrated in Jasmineae and Oleeae. Climatic niche evolution and speciation rates were not consistently coupled; rather, their relationships with dispersal and diversification were lineage‐ and climatic‐axis‐specific. Oleeae showed more coordinated associations among niche evolution, dispersal, and speciation, whereas Jasmineae exhibited a more restricted, axis‐specific pattern. The ancient whole‐genome duplication (WGD) in Oleeae may have contributed to its distinctive evolutionary trajectory. Overall, our results support a conditional ‘license to disperse’ framework in which climatic niche lability facilitates geographic expansion, thereby indirectly increasing opportunities for diversification.

articles.title: A single‐nucleus multiome profiling reveals the regulatory programs driving plant nematode–induced syncytium
articles.abstract: Single‐nucleus transcriptome profiles of Heterodera schachtii–induced syncytium on Arabidopsis roots. Summary Plant‐parasitic cyst nematodes induce the formation of specialized feeding structures, known as syncytia, within host roots by orchestrating extensive transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming. Here, we generated parallel single‐nucleus RNA‐seq and ATAC‐seq libraries from fully developed Heterodera schachtii–induced syncytia on Arabidopsis roots. We analyzed high‐quality transcriptome and chromatin profiles independently and in an integrated framework. We identified multiple transcriptomic cell states, several of which were highly syncytium‐enriched and spanned vascular and cortical identities. Differential expression analysis identified hundreds of syncytium‐enriched genes, and pseudotime trajectory inference points to potential compartmentalization or functional heterogeneity of syncytium nuclei, consistent with the possibility of distinct transcriptional programs within or between mature syncytia. Joint clustering of snATAC‐seq with snRNA‐seq delineated syncytium‐unique chromatin accessibility landscapes, with several cell states exhibiting extensive open chromatin linked to upregulated genes. Motif enrichment across these accessible regions highlighted cis‐regulatory elements mainly for AP2, bZIP, bHLH, MYB, and TCP transcription factors and identified functionally validated members of these families as candidate regulators of syncytium identity. Our study establishes a multiome atlas of syncytial cells and uncovers the regulatory programs driving nematode feeding site maintenance, as well as transcriptionally distinct nuclear states that may reflect functional specialization within or between the syncytia.

articles.title: Frenemies forever: when parasitic fungi become an insect's secret weapon
articles.abstract: Insect symbiotic yeast and fungi shape host–plant interactions. Summary Plant‐feeding insects pose a major threat to global food production, and finding sustainable pest control strategies is challenging. Insect‐associated symbiotic microorganisms fulfill important beneficial functions for their host insects, enabling them to adapt and thrive in a changing environment. Understanding how these interactions evolve and what they mean for insect–plant interactions is key to the development of novel targets and potential tools for pest control. Since yeast and fungal insect symbionts are understudied in comparison to bacterial symbionts, this Tansley Insight explores their role in insect–plant interactions.

articles.title: High‐light adaptation via ferredoxin‐mediated tuning of the photosynthesis–photoprotection trade‐off
articles.abstract: Proposed model of the alternative regulation of the photosynthesis in Fd1‐OE Nicotiana tabacum plants. Summary Plants continuously adjust photosynthesis to balance growth and photoprotection under changing environmental conditions. Environmental fluctuations frequently impose a mismatch between energy production and CO2 assimilation. How photochemical reactions are regulated to maintain performance under these conditions remains a central question in plant biology. We previously developed transplastomic tobacco (Fd1‐OE plants) overexpressing ferredoxin displaying enhanced photoprotection and growth penalties with a variegated leaf phenotype under glasshouse conditions. Here, we investigate how these plants respond to different growth irradiances using physiological, ultrastructural, and photosynthetic analyses, including Pulse‐Amplitude Modulation (PAM), gas exchange, and P700 absorbance measurements, and dynamic‐light assays. Fd1‐OE plants progressively recovered growth, leaf phenotype, and photosynthetic performance as growth irradiance increased, reaching near wild‐type performance at 1400 μmol m−2 s−1. This enhanced adaptation to ‘high‐light’ was associated with a larger fraction of open Photosystem II reaction centers and enhanced nonphotochemical quenching. Dynamic‐light analyses further revealed faster plastoquinone (PQ) turnover, a more oxidized (PQ) pool and enhanced electron withdrawal downstream of Photosystem I. Our results indicate that ferredoxin overexpression redefines the balance between photochemistry and photoprotection. This adjustment shifts adaptation toward higher irradiance and enhances photosynthetic performance under changing light environments. Electron partitioning downstream of Photosystem I emerges as a promising target to improve photosynthetic resilience. Resumen Las plantas regulan continuamente la fotosíntesis para equilibrar el crecimiento y la fotoprotección frente a condiciones ambientales cambiantes. Las fluctuaciones ambientales imponen con frecuencia un desajuste entre la producción de energía y la asimilación de CO2. La forma en que se regulan las reacciones fotoquímicas para mantener el rendimiento bajo estas condiciones continúa siendo una cuestión central en la biología vegetal. Previamente desarrollamos plantas de tabaco transplastómicas (Fd1‐OE) que sobreexpresan ferredoxina y presentan una fotoprotección mejorada, junto con penalizaciones en el crecimiento y un fenotipo foliar variegado bajo condiciones de invernadero. En este trabajo, investigamos cómo estas plantas responden a diferentes irradiancias de crecimiento mediante análisis fisiológicos, ultraestructurales y fotosintéticos, incluyendo mediciones con PAM, intercambio gaseoso y absorbancia de P700, así como ensayos bajo luz dinámica. Las plantas Fd1‐OE recuperaron progresivamente el crecimiento, el fenotipo foliar y el rendimiento fotosintético a medida que aumentó la irradiancia de crecimiento, alcanzando un rendimiento cercano al del tipo silvestre a 1400 μmol m−2 s−1. Esta mayor adaptación a condiciones de ‘alta luz’ se asocia con una mayor fracción de centros de reacción del fotosistema II abiertos y un mayor NPQ. Los análisis bajo luz dinámica revelaron además una mayor velocidad de recambio de las plastoquinonas, un pool de plastoquinonas más oxidado y una mayor extracción de electrones cadena abajo del fotosistema I. Nuestros resultados indican que la sobreexpresión de ferredoxina redefine el equilibrio entre la fotoquímica y la fotoprotección. Este ajuste desplaza la adaptación hacia irradiancias más altas y mejora el rendimiento fotosintético frente a entornos lumínicos cambiantes. La partición de electrones cadena abajo del fotosistema I emerge como un blanco prometedor para mejorar la resiliencia fotosintética.

articles.title: Pathogen nutrient acquisition strategy mediates the strength of diversity–disease relationships in natural grasslands
articles.abstract: Overview of the study sites. Summary The relationship between biodiversity and disease risk is a cornerstone of disease ecology, yet predicting its direction and strength remains challenging. Pathogen nutrient acquisition strategies may be key to resolving this context dependency, but their roles in mediating diversity–disease relationships are poorly understood. Here, we combine a large‐scale survey spanning 2000 km in natural grasslands with advanced statistical modeling to demonstrate that pathogen nutrient acquisition strategy is a critical mediator. We show that diseases caused by biotrophic pathogens (e.g. rusts and powdery mildews), which depend on living host tissues, exhibit a significantly negative diversity–disease relationship, whereas diseases caused by necrotrophic pathogens (e.g. leaf spots and blights) show no significant relationship. Furthermore, the strength of this negative relationship for biotrophic pathogens is amplified in regions with higher disease severity. Bayesian structural equation modeling reveals that plant species richness directly reduces biotrophic disease severity, while for necrotrophic pathogens, precipitation is the primary driver of severity, with no direct effect of richness. Our findings provide a trait‐based framework linking climatic drivers, pathogen nutrient acquisition strategies, and the strength of diversity–disease relationships. These results enhance our ability to predict disease dynamics under biodiversity loss and inform biodiversity‐based disease management strategies.

articles.title: Phosphatidylcholine acyl turnover facilitates thylakoid lipid remodeling and promotes plant survival under heat stress
articles.abstract: Coordinated galactolipid–TAG conversion during heat stress–induced thylakoid lipid remodeling. Summary Heat stress destabilizes chloroplast membranes, requiring rapid lipid remodeling to maintain photosynthetic function. Although thylakoid lipid remodeling and triacylglycerol (TAG) accumulation are established heat responses, the role of phosphatidylcholine (PC) acyl turnover remains unclear. We investigated lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase 1 and 2 (LPCAT1/2), REDUCED OLEATE DESATURATION1 (ROD1), phospholipid:diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (PDAT1), and lipins in heat‐induced lipid remodeling and thermotolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana. Using genetic, lipidomic, physiological, and photosynthetic analyses, we examined mutants defective in PC acyl editing, PC–diacylglycerol (DAG) interconversion, TAG synthesis, and phosphatidic acid dephosphorylation during heat stress. Loss of LPCAT1/2 severely impaired basal and acquired thermotolerance, caused irreversible photosystem II damage, and disrupted thylakoid lipid remodeling. rod1 showed minor defects, whereas rod1 lpcat1/2 exhibited enhanced thermosensitivity. In mature vegetative plants, pdat1‐2 showed thermotolerance and photosystem II defects comparable to lpcat1/2. Lipin‐mediated phosphatidic acid dephosphorylation provided the major DAG source for heat‐induced TAG synthesis. Defective PC acyl turnover also increased free fatty acids and lipid peroxidation. These findings establish LPCAT1/2‐mediated PC acyl turnover as a central regulator of heat‐induced membrane remodeling and thermotolerance and link lipin‐dependent DAG production and TAG synthesis with chloroplast membrane homeostasis.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: BackgroundTo our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival.MethodsThis open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting.FindingsBetween July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group.InterpretationIn this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX.…

articles.title: Robust Full-Spectrum-Responsive Multi-junction Tandem Solar Cells via Enhanced Near-Infrared Photon Harvesting
articles.abstract: Developing robust multi-junction tandem photovoltaics remains constrained by the instability of mixed-halide perovskite subcells, given their dominating contribution to overall power output. Integrating near-infrared (NIR) PbS quantum dots (QDs) with FAPbBr3 and crystalline silicon (c-Si) broadens spectrum utilization while improving overall operational stability by reducing the perovskite power contribution. However, enlarged (100) facets and the trade-off between film thickness and quality limit efficient NIR photon harvesting. Herein, a Lewis-basic dihydrazide molecule achieves universal passivation across diverse PbS QD facets via synergistic lead chelation and hydrogen-bonding interactions. Consequently, 0.8 eV PbS QD solar cells with a 685 nm-thick active layer achieve a short-circuit current density of 41.31 mA cm–2 and a 1100-nm-filtered efficiency of 1.80%. The resulting FAPbBr3/c-Si/PbS triple-junction tandems achieve a promising efficiency of 31.04%, with the perovskite subcell contributing 30.4% of the total power output, demonstrating a well-matched operational lifetime. This work offers a strategic framework for efficient multi-junction tandem photovoltaics.

HOST MATTER: Parasite infection drives chemical reconfiguration of decomposing host and shapes insect behavioural responses
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Host–parasite interactions shape ecosystems by driving species dynamics, yet their influence is typically considered in terms of host mortality rather than the chemical environments generated during infection and decomposition. Here, we show that parasitic infection actively reconfigures the chemical phenotype of decomposing hosts, reshaping ecological interactions through volatile‐mediated signalling. Using soil‐dwelling parasites‐entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) and their symbiotic bacteria‐as a model system, we integrate behavioural assays, comprehensive volatolomic characterization and CO2 quantification across three insect orders and two EPN species over four post‐mortem intervals. We demonstrate that EPN‐infection generates a distinct and conserved volatile signature dominated by carboxylic acids, sulphur‐containing compounds and unsaturated hydrocarbons, accompanied by elevated CO2 emissions. These infection‐derived blends elicit contrasting behavioural responses: they repel non‐natural hosts while consistently attracting natural hosts, indicating that infected cadavers function as chemically structured information hubs. In contrast, frozen‐killed insects exhibit fermentation‐type profiles, and bacteria‐only infection produce simplified alkane‐dominated blends, demonstrating that the full chemical phenotype emerges from the nematode–bacteria complex. Our findings reveal parasitic infection as a process that reorganizes decomposition chemistry with measurable behavioural consequences, uncovering a previously underappreciated mechanism by which parasites structure soil food webs and influence multitrophic interactions. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Local adaptation to host plants in herbivorous insects: A meta‐analysis
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Local adaptation, wherein populations are well‐adapted to local biotic and abiotic conditions, is a common outcome of natural selection and a driver of diversification. Previous theory identified two criteria to detect local adaptation: (a) the home‐away criterion compares the fitness of a population in its home environment to its fitness in a different environment and (b) the local‐foreign criterion examines differences in fitness between a local and a foreign population when experiencing the local environment. We conducted a meta‐analysis synthesizing empirical evidence of insect herbivores' local adaptation to their host plants using both criteria to assess how diet breadth, geographic distance among populations, herbivore taxonomic affiliation, herbivore clonality, the herbivore response variable measured, taxonomic distance among host plants and features of the study design impact the likelihood of detecting local adaptation. Overall, we found patterns consistent with herbivore local adaptation using both the home‐away and local‐foreign criteria. Herbivore diet breadth, taxonomic affiliation and geographic distance between herbivore populations did not affect the likelihood of finding local adaptation. In contrast, the detection of local adaptation varied with herbivore clonality, the specific response variables measured, taxonomic distance among host plants and elements of the experimental design. These findings clarify the conditions under which local adaptation emerges in the world's most diverse group of multicellular organisms. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Resumen La adaptación local consiste en el desarrollo de características que permiten un mejor desempeño de las poblaciones en las condiciones bióticas y abióticas de su entorno. Este fenómeno es una consecuencia común de la selección natural y uno de los mecanismos de diversificación biológica. Se han identificado dos criterios para detectar adaptación local: (a) el criterio ‘en casa‐fuera de casa’ que compara la adecuación de una población en su propio ambiente contra la adecuación de esa misma población en un ambiente foráneo; y (b) el criterio ‘local‐forastero’, que compara la adecuación de dos poblaciones, una local y otra foránea, cuando habitan el ambiente natal de cada una de ellas. Utilizamos un meta‐análisis para sintetizar evidencia empírica de la adaptación local de insectos herbívoros a sus plantas hospederas de acuerdo con cada uno de los criterios anteriores. Este análisis nos permitió evaluar el efecto de la amplitud de la dieta, distancia geográfica, afiliación taxonómica del herbívoro, clonalidad, variable de respuesta, distancia taxonómica entre la planta local y la foránea, y características del diseño experimental, en la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local. Encontramos patrones consistentes con la noción de que los insectos herbívoros exhiben adaptación local a sus plantas hospederas de acuerdo con ambos criterios. Adicionalmente, encontramos que la amplitud de la dieta, afiliación taxonómica y la distancia geográfica entre las poblaciones de herbívoros no afectaron la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local. Por el contrario, variables que sí afectaron la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local incluyen la clonalidad del herbívoro, la variable de respuesta que se utilizó para evaluar el desempeño del herbívoro, la distancia taxonómica entre las plantas local y foránea, y algunos elementos del diseño experimental. Nuestros resultados contribuyen al esclarecimiento de las condiciones que determinan la ocurrencia de adaptación local en el grupo más diverso de organismos multicelulares.

articles.title: Biodegradable and Non‐Biodegradable Microplastics Drive Divergent Microbial Carbon and Nitrogen Metabolism Regimes in Soil–Plant Systems
articles.abstract: The accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in soils worldwide has raised concerns about their potential impacts on microbially mediated carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling. However, whether biodegradable and non‐biodegradable MPs differently affect microbial C and N metabolism and coupling, and whether these responses are modulated by co‐occurring plant identity remain uncertain. We combined a meta‐analysis with a controlled pot experiment comparing soil responses under two congeneric plant species exposed to two biodegradable and two non‐biodegradable MPs at doses ranging from 0% to 2% (w/w). In the meta‐analysis, MPs generally increased CO2 emission and microbial biomass N (MBN), but had no significant overall effect on microbial biomass C (MBC). In the pot experiment, MPs likewise increased CO2 emission, whereas overall effect sizes of MBC and MBN were nonsignificant. Nevertheless, these overall responses did not capture the distinct patterns of microbial C–N metabolic coordination between MP types. Under biodegradable MPs, tighter MBC–MBN coupling with a dose‐dependent shift toward greater respiratory C loss relative to MBC collectively indicated a maintenance‐associated metabolic pattern. In contrast, MBC–MBN decoupling and stronger MBC–CO2 coupling under non‐biodegradable MPs indicated a biomass‐linked metabolic pattern. In addition, plant identity modulated these microbial metabolisms in an MP‐type manner, particularly in N‐related processes. These metabolic responses were accompanied with changes in soil property conditions and substrate availability, weakened DOC–DON coupling, and shifts in microbial community structure and life history strategy. RDA‐based hierarchical and variation partitioning and SEM further indicated that modeled soil property pathways were more prominent under non‐biodegradable MPs, while substrate‐related pathways were prominent under biodegradable MPs. Together, the meta‐analysis reveals the general microbial metabolic patterns under MP type, and the pot experiment further reveals how MP type and plant identity jointly influence microbial C–N metabolism through contrasting associations with soil substrates and property conditions.

articles.title: Conservative Spruce Outperforms Acquisitive Larch Under Warming and CO2
articles.abstract: Predicting boreal forest growth is hindered by limited experimental tests on the compounding effects of climate change and atmospheric CO2. We integrated regional tree‐ring data with a peatland warming and CO2 manipulation experiment, including 45 trait measurements, to assess growth responses of two widespread boreal conifers, Larix laricina and Picea mariana, to temperature, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), soil moisture, and elevated CO2. L. laricina growth was consistently more climate‐sensitive than P. mariana, increasing strongly with soil moisture and declining slightly with VPD at the regional scale, but responding positively to VPD and temperature—not soil moisture or CO2—at the experimental peatland. L. laricina's acquisitive strategy enhanced water and nutrient uptake, sustaining growth but reducing hydraulic safety. By contrast, P. mariana's conservative strategy maintained water‐use efficiency and hydraulic resilience without compromising growth. Our results challenge projections of widespread CO2 fertilization in boreal forests and highlight conservative conifers as potential winners under warming and drying, sustaining growth while maintaining low mortality risk. This dynamic could reshape projections of the boreal carbon sink and its role in global climate feedback.

Canopy spectral variability is a weak proxy for plant alpha diversity
articles.abstract: Canopy spectral variability is a context‐dependent and incomplete proxy for plant alpha diversity in herbaceous communities. Explicit consideration of community composition is therefore important when canopy spectral variability is used to infer plant alpha diversity across plant communities. Abstract Canopy spectral variability is widely used as a proxy for plant alpha diversity, yet this relationship often varies among plant communities and spatial scales. This instability may partly arise because canopy spectral variability responds not only to species richness and evenness but also to community composition, including differences in species identity and dominance structure. We examined the influence of community composition on canopy spectral variability using two herbaceous datasets: airborne hyperspectral imagery from 706 National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) grassland plots across the United States and UAV multispectral imagery from 330 quadrats in the Northeast China marshes (NECM). For each dataset, we quantified canopy spectral variability using the coefficient of variation of reflectance (ReflCV), and calculated alpha diversity indices and Bray–Curtis‐based community‐composition gradients. We then assessed how canopy spectral variability varied along community‐composition gradients, compared the variance contributions of community‐composition gradients and alpha diversity, and evaluated how relationships between ReflCV and alpha diversity changed after accounting for community composition. Canopy spectral variability changed significantly along community‐composition gradients, and community composition accounted for more variance in ReflCV than alpha diversity in both datasets. Accounting for community composition also altered the estimated relationships between ReflCV and alpha diversity, but in contrasting directions: these relationships generally weakened in NECM but strengthened in NEON. These contrasting responses indicate that community composition can either enhance or obscure apparent associations between canopy spectral variability and alpha diversity, depending on the underlying compositional context. Synthesis. Canopy spectral variability is a context‐dependent and incomplete proxy for plant alpha diversity in herbaceous communities. Explicit consideration of community composition is therefore important when canopy spectral variability is used to infer plant alpha diversity across plant communities.

articles.title: Vendi information gain for active learning and its application to ecology
articles.abstract: While monitoring biodiversity through camera traps has become an important endeavour for ecological research, identifying species in the captured image data remains a major bottleneck due to limited labelling resources. Active learning—a machine learning paradigm that selects the most informative data to label and train a predictive model—offers a promising solution, but typically focuses on uncertainty in the individual predictions without considering uncertainty across the entire dataset. We study Vendi information gain (VIG) as an active learning policy that selects images based on their impact on dataset‐wide prediction uncertainty, capturing both informativeness and diversity. We applied VIG to two representative datasets in ecological image classification, the Kenya Camera Trap Dataset and the Missouri Camera Trap dataset, and compared VIG against common active learning methods. On both datasets, VIG achieves higher accuracy with fewer labelled examples. We further conducted extensive ablation studies to investigate the effects of the predictive model, batch sizes and other hyperparameters to find relatively robust performance from VIG. VIG has broad applicability beyond ecology, and our results highlight its value for biodiversity monitoring in data‐limited environments.

articles.title: Interspecific Gene Flow and Potential Hybrid Breakdown in South Atlantic Sea Turtles
articles.abstract: Interspecific hybridisation can play an important evolutionary role, generating new taxa or outbreeding depression, which can also lead to behavioural reproductive isolation through reinforcement. Still, there are few studies investigating how divergence time relates to hybridisation rates and its impact on introgression. Sea turtles are known to hybridise, despite their long divergence times and behavioural, ecological and morphological differences. Several genetic studies have attempted to determine the extent of hybridisation between four of the seven extant sea turtle species (Caretta caretta, Eretmochelys imbricata, Lepidochelys olivacea and Chelonia mydas) in the South Atlantic coast of Brazil, an area known to include nesting and feeding sites for all these species. In this work, we combined new and published genomic data of all four sea turtle species and their hybrids in a detailed population genomics study. Although hybridisation does occur in Brazilian nesting sites between three of the four species, it appears to be limited to first‐generation hybrids and few backcrosses, which points to some postzygotic barriers between species and hybrid breakdown. Moreover, our evidence suggests a moderately high level of relatedness among hybrids, indicating a reduced number of independent hybridisation events. Despite this fact, we found evidence of backcrosses involving different species, and an F2 progeny between Ca. caretta x E. imbricata F1 hybrids, which suggests hybrid male fertility. Limited interspecific gene flow appears to be part of the long history of divergence of sea turtles, as low levels of deep time introgression were inferred. In summary, this work contributes important evidence regarding the rate and success of hybridisation at large scales of divergence, and how this seemingly equates to low rates of introgression, pointing to temporal limits to gene flow.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab with or without visugromab in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: the phase 2a GDFATHER-NEO trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In this exploratory, nonrandomized phase 2a trial, treatment of patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-naive muscle-invasive bladder cancer with the GDF-15-neutralizing antibody visugromab and nivolumab produced encouraging pathological complete response and radiographic response rates with no new safety signals, supporting further evaluation in larger randomized studies.

articles.title: Relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab for advanced melanoma: 5-year survival and biomarker analyses of the phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial
articles.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In a 5 year follow-up of survival and correlative data from the pivotal phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial comparing relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab alone in patients with metastatic or unresectable melanoma, statistically significant differences in progression-free survival, overall survival and melanoma-specific survival were seen with high baseline levels of LAG3 high CD8+ T cells associated with improved response in the combination arm.

articles.title: Abortion Care in Puerto Rico — A Fragile Legal Landscape
Anbenitamab plus HB1801 for HER2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe combination of docetaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) is an established first-line treatment for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive advanced breast cancer. The efficacy and safety of anbenitamab, a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody, plus albumin-bound docetaxel (HB1801) in this context are unknown.MethodsIn this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in China, we randomly assigned patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer in a 1:1 ratio to receive either anbenitamab plus HB1801 or THP. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Objective response was a secondary end point.ResultsA total of 885 patients were enrolled (445 were assigned to receive anbenitamab plus HB1801 and 440 to receive THP). At this prespecified interim analysis (with 401 events [disease progression or death] and a median follow-up of 21.0 months), the estimated 24-month progression-free survival was significantly higher with anbenitamab plus HB1801 than with THP (58.5% vs. 34.4%; hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.46; 95% confidence interval, 0.37 to 0.56; PConclusionsAnbenitamab plus HB1801 led to significantly higher progression-free survival than THP among patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. (Funded by Shanghai JMT-Bio Technology and others; HEALER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05838066.).

articles.title: Durvalumab, Tremelimumab, and Enfortumab Vedotin in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe standard of care for patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer continues to evolve. Whether perioperative durvalumab, with or without tremelimumab, plus neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin is effective in such patients is unknown.MethodsIn this phase 3 open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1:1 ratio, patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based chemotherapy to receive neoadjuvant durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin every 3 weeks for three cycles, followed by radical cystectomy and then adjuvant durvalumab every 4 weeks for nine cycles; neoadjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (tremelimumab for two cycles only), radical cystectomy, and adjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab (tremelimumab for one cycle only); or radical cystectomy alone (control). The dual primary end points were event-free survival in each of the two durvalumab groups as compared with that in the control group. The two durvalumab groups were not compared with each other. The key secondary end point was overall survival.ResultsIn total, 233 patients were assigned to the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group, 233 to the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group, and 229 to the control group. Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 63.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 56.5 to 69.7) with durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin and 45.1% (95% CI, 38.2 to 51.8) with control (hazard ratio for an event or death, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.38 to 0.67; PConclusionsPerioperative durvalumab with or without tremelimumab plus three cycles of neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin resulted in significantly better event-free survival outcomes than surgery alone. Perioperative durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin led to significantly better overall survival outcomes than surgery alone. Grade 3 or higher adverse events of any cause were noted in more than half the patients in the durvalumab groups. (Funded by AstraZeneca; VOLGA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04960709; EudraCT number, 2020-005452-38.).

articles.title: Expanding the Evidence and Indications for Thrombectomy in Ischemic Stroke
Mechanical Thrombectomy 24 to 72 Hours after Large-Vessel Ischemic Stroke
articles.abstract: BackgroundEndovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain.MethodsWe conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety.ResultsA total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively.ConclusionsAmong patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. (Funded by the National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and others; LATE-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05326932.).

articles.title: My Father’s Code
Targeting HER2 — A Triumph of Science
Tarlatamab–Durvalumab Maintenance for Extensive-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer
articles.abstract: BackgroundPatients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer have poor outcomes, with a median overall survival of approximately 12 to 13 months. Tarlatamab (a bispecific T-cell engager targeting delta-like ligand 3 [DLL3] and CD3) was previously shown to improve survival as second-line therapy. Whether adding tarlatamab to durvalumab (an anti-programmed death ligand 1 agent) after initial chemoimmunotherapy could significantly improve survival in the context of maintenance therapy after first remission has been unclear.MethodsIn this phase 3, international, open-label, randomized trial, we compared tarlatamab-durvalumab with durvalumab as first-line maintenance therapy in patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer without progression after initial chemoimmunotherapy. Overall survival and progression-free survival were assessed from randomization at the start of maintenance therapy as the primary and key secondary end points, respectively. Results of the prespecified interim analysis (data-cutoff date, July 7, 2026) are reported here.ResultsA total of 563 patients were randomly assigned to receive tarlatamab-durvalumab (282 patients) or durvalumab (281 patients). At a median follow-up of 15.9 months in the tarlatamab-durvalumab group and 16.1 months in the durvalumab group, the estimated median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 20.8 to could not be estimated) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 12.7 months (95% CI, 11.2 to 14.8) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for death, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.54; PConclusionsTarlatamab-durvalumab maintenance therapy resulted in significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival than durvalumab alone among patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. (Funded by Amgen and AstraZeneca; DeLLphi-305 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06211036.).

articles.title: The Future of Health Agency Enforcement Fines
Thelaziasis
Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion
articles.abstract: BackgroundWhether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain.MethodsWe conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of ResultsA total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; PConclusionsIn this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. (Funded by Fujian Medical University Union Hospital and others; MILD-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06179017.).

articles.title: [Articles] 14-day versus 28-day trifluridine–tipiracil plus bevacizumab for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (PRABITAS): a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial in Japan
articles.abstract: A 14-day schedule of FTD–TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD–TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.

articles.title: [Comment] Optimising late-line treatment administration in metastatic colorectal cancer: an even brighter SUNLIGHT
articles.abstract: Offering late-line systemic therapy to patients with chemo-refractory metastatic colorectal cancer demands a careful estimation of the balance between the expected treatment benefit and its potential impact on quality of life, including adverse events, hospital visits, and psychosocial consequences.1 In such a comprehensive and individualised assessment of patients’ general conditions, usually summarised by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, the cumulative burden of disease-related symptoms and previous treatment-related adverse events, together with the potential decay of organ functional reserve, cannot be neglected.

articles.title: High-Performance LiNiO2 Cathodes through Microstructural Engineering
articles.abstract: LiNiO2 (LNO) is a promising high-capacity cathode, but its practical application is hindered by severe structural and microstructural instability. Herein, we develop a two-step calcination strategy that decouples lithiation from Ta introduction. This approach promotes the segregation of a Ta-rich phase at grain boundaries, producing nanosized, radially aligned primary particles that mitigate strain and suppress microcracking. It also preserves a layered–rocksalt nanostructured multiphase that reversibly transforms into a layered–spinel-like state during charging, which may contribute to structural stability and Li-ion transport. The optimized TS-Ta-LNO delivers 252.7 mAh g–1 and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a TS-Ta-LNO/Li-metal pouch cell maintains stable voltage profiles under an electric vertical take-off and landing dynamic-load protocol, demonstrating its potential for high-energy, high-power batteries.

articles.title: Hot Carrier Cooling Dynamics in Tin Tri-Iodide Perovskites Thin Films
articles.abstract: Hot carriers (HC) offer a potential route to surpass conventional efficiency limits in solar cells. Generated after light absorption, these high-energy carriers can significantly boost device performance if extracted before dissipating energy as heat. Although HC cooling has been studied in tin-based perovskites, interpreting these dynamics is challenging because high-energy, high-fluence pump pulses required to generate HCs have shallow penetration depths, confining excitation near the surface. In tin-based perovskites, surface properties differ from the bulk, and surface defects may strongly contribute to the optical response. Here, by using pump-push-probe ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, we photo-excite the semiconductor thin film with a low-energy pump, in a photon density range typical for solar cell operation, making relevant the bulk electronic properties, and selectively re-excite the photo-carriers only once they cool down, enabling direct tracking of HC relaxation in the relevant spectral region while minimizing surface contributions. We track the cooling process in FA0.85Cs0.15SnI3 (FA = Formamidinium) as a benchmark sample and extend the analysis to single-cation FA+, MA+ (MA = methylammonium), and Cs+ tin perovskites. Across all compositions, and at different doping densities, we find cooling timescales in the 150–600 fs time range. These results highlight the central role of phonon-mediated interactions and show that ultrafast cooling fundamentally limits hot carrier extraction in tin halide perovskites.

articles.title: Quantifying Sodium Metal SEI Dissolution and Relation to Corrosion Using Quartz Crystal Microbalance
articles.abstract: Sodium-metal batteries present a more abundant alternative to lithium-based batteries, with high theoretical capacity and comparable reduction potential. Ether electrolytes perform well in sodium-metal batteries under continuous cycling and are presumed to have a stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI). However, the solubility of sodium SEI components is a cause for concern, and SEI evolution during calendar aging is not commonly studied for the ether sodium-metal system. In this work, SEI mass formation and dissolution are quantitatively measured for NaPF6 in diglyme. For varying potential hold levels, significant SEI dissolution is observed, from 55 to 76% of the originally formed SEI. Characterization shows that in addition to organic component dissolution, inorganic salts such as NaF and NaxPOyFz are unstable in SEI during open circuit rest. This instability results in continuous corrosion of sodium metal during calendar aging, highlighting an important understanding and concern of SEI stability in sodium-metal batteries.

articles.title: Weak-Solvating Carboxylate Ester Electrolyte Enables Hybrid Interphase via Cooperative Additives toward Wide-Temperature Sodium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Fast Na+ transport and durable interfacial stability remain challenging for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries. To address these issues, we developed a synergistic solvation-interphase regulation strategy by integrating methyl propanoate (MP) with a combined VC/NaDFOB additive pair. MP modifies the Na+ solvation sheath and facilitates Na+ desolvation, while VC and NaDFOB cooperatively generate a mechanically robust hybrid organicinorganic interphase. This coupled regulation enables enhanced ion transport and interfacial stability over a broad temperature range. The EC/EMC/MP + VC/NaDFOB electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.52 mS cm–1 at –40 ̊C and an increased Na+ transference number. Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells retain 96.5% of their initial capacity after 1000 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% at room temperature. At –20 ̊C, the cells deliver 69.4 mAh g–1 for over 900 cycles, corresponding to 82% of their room-temperature capacity. This work establishes a practical solvation-interphase regulation approach for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries.

articles.title: Concentric tubular lattice metamaterials: Decoupling load-bearing capacity and finite-strain zero Poisson’s ratio
Coupling proton-conducting and layered oxygen-ion-conducting perovskites for accelerated oxygen reduction kinetics
From migration barriers to diffusion networks: Materials design principles for fast ion transport
Quantification of the atomic-level structures and motifs of short-range order in Cr-Co-Ni alloys
Revisiting the role of chemical short-range and long-range order in the mechanical behavior of Ni–Cr binary solid solution alloy
The effects of short-range order and secondary phases on the thermal properties of a CoCrFeNi multiprincipal element alloy
Ideal Quantum Geometry for Fractional Chern Insulators
articles.journal: Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics
articles.abstract: Quantum geometry plays a fundamental role in many aspects of condensed matter physics. Among its central objects are the Berry curvature and the quantum metric—quantities that, while distinct, are intertwined through geometric constraints. In this article, we survey recent progress in understanding when and how this bound is saturated, with particular emphasis on the emergence of momentum-space holomorphicity of Bloch states. These developments highlight a profound connection between certain ideal Bloch bands and the Hilbert space structure of the lowest Landau level. We elucidate this relationship through a review of quantum Hall physics in both homogeneous and spatially varying magnetic fields and conclude by exploring its implications for the search for fractionalized phases in emerging platforms, including moiré materials.

articles.title: From Optimization to the Pontryagin Maximum Principle
articles.journal: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems
articles.abstract: This article is a gentle stroll through the field of optimization and optimal control, aiming to acquaint the reader with the evolution of developments leading up to the Pontryagin maximum principle. The exposition adheres to simplicity without sacrificing integrity. The continuous versions of results are derived as limits of discrete versions, thus adopting a unified approach to finite-dimensional and function spaces, and wherever permissible, an intuitive connection to physics is established. Complete proofs are not provided; instead, the key geometric ideas in the proofs are presented.

articles.title: Proactive Biological Control of Invasive Exotic Arthropod Pests and Weeds
articles.abstract: Invasive exotic arthropods and weeds pose a growing threat to biodiversity, food security, and the functioning of whole ecosystems, resulting in significant socioeconomic and ecological impacts. Classical biological control—the importation of specialist natural enemies from the native range—can lead to long-term, sustainable pest suppression, but it is typically implemented reactively after the invasive species is established and is causing significant negative impacts. Proactive biological control offers an anticipatory approach, developing biological control agents before or shortly after establishment and enabling rapid response to new incursions. This review examines current applications, opportunities, and challenges of proactive strategies and proposes steps to advance proactive management of invasive arthropod pests and weeds.

articles.title: T Cell Receptor–Engineered T Cell Therapy in Solid Tumors: Where We Stand and What's to Come
articles.abstract: T cell receptor–engineered T (TCR-T) cell therapy has emerged as a promising adoptive cellular therapy for solid tumors by enabling recognition of intracellular antigens presented via human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules. Unlike chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy, TCR-T cell therapy targets a broader antigen repertoire, including cancer-testis antigens, neoantigens, and viral antigens. Recent clinical advances, highlighted by the approval of afamitresgene autoleucel in synovial sarcoma, demonstrate meaningful antitumor activity. However, several limitations remain, including HLA restriction, antigen heterogeneity, toxicity related to on-target/off-tumor effects, and mechanisms of resistance such as antigen loss and T cell exhaustion. Advances in antigen selection, gene editing, and synthetic biology are improving both safety and efficacy. Combination strategies and next-generation engineered constructs are expected to overcome current barriers. This review summarizes the biological rationale, clinical evidence, safety considerations, and resistance mechanisms of TCR-T cell therapy in solid tumors and discusses future directions to optimize their therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Biomolecular Condensates in Bacteria
articles.abstract: Bacteria use membraneless compartments, or biomolecular condensates, to organize cellular processes in space and time. These condensates assemble and function within a highly constrained physical landscape shaped by a crowded cytoplasm, structured nucleoid, membrane surfaces, and distinct polar zones. In this review, we examine condensates involved in genome maintenance, RNA metabolism, cell division, signaling, and metabolic regulation, focusing on how cellular microenvironments and physiological state shape when and where these condensates form, which molecules they recruit, and the material states they adopt. In turn, condensates can concentrate molecules for biochemical reactions, sequester them for storage or protection, release or redistribute them as conditions change, and position them at specific cellular sites. Disentangling the contribution of the condensed state from that of the underlying molecular interactions will be essential for determining how condensates regulate bacterial physiology.

articles.title: Biophysics of Microbial Locomotion
articles.abstract: Eppur si muove —the work of Galileo Galilei marked the beginning of the quantitative study of motion for scope-observable entities. Extending this physics-based perspective to the microscope-observable microbial world has uncovered principles of motion that diverge sharply from our everyday intuition, revealing physics as being essential to understanding microbial motility. In this review, we explore the fundamental physical principles that enable and constrain the motility strategies evolved by diverse microorganisms, with a focus on prokaryotes, to enable propulsion in fluids and along surfaces. We examine how microbial motility functions in complex, heterogeneous environments, and we provide a brief evolutionary perspective on microbial motility by highlighting its costs and benefits. In summary, we show how including a physical approach in the study of microbial motility both unveils general solutions and specific adaptations and enables a better understanding of a world for which our intuition is not trained.

articles.title: Computational Peptide Design: Emerging Concepts in Antibiotics, Immunity, and Evolution
articles.abstract: Peptides are among the smallest functional biomolecules. Learning to systematically design their activity would revolutionize biology and medicine. Yet achieving this goal remains an open challenge. Recent advances in machine learning enable the discovery and design of peptides at scale, not only yielding new antibiotic agents effective against priority pathogens but also revealing unexpected roles for peptides in host immunity. In this review, we survey how artificial intelligence (AI) methods can be used to mine genomes, proteomes, and even ancient sequence data to uncover “encrypted” peptide antibiotics across the tree of life and over evolutionary time. We highlight emerging approaches for activity prediction, structure–activity modeling, sequence optimization, and de novo peptide generation, and we discuss workflows that tightly couple in silico design with high-throughput experimental validation. We further introduce the concept of “encrypted immunity,” in which ordinary proteins encode latent antimicrobial fragments, and we outline translational opportunities as well as remaining challenges on the path to bringing AI-designed peptides to the clinic.

articles.title: Ecological Kinetics and Evolutionary Dynamics of Antibiotic Resistance in Complex Environments
articles.abstract: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria are common in natural environments, including the microbiota of animal and human hosts. The local physical, chemical, and biological conditions of environmental patches and matrices vary both qualitatively and quantitatively. Often, these conditions are found as gradients, creating intersections that can either facilitate or inhibit the spread and evolution of antibiotic resistance (AbR). Ecological kinetics (EcoK) describes how combinations of these conditions influence the abundance and transmission of antibiotic-resistant populations, as well as the mobile genetic elements that carry resistance genes. Evolutionary dynamics (EvoD) concerns the effects of environmental conditions on genetic variation, the expression of resistance traits, and the evolvability of host bacteria, ultimately contributing to the emergence and selection of AbR. This review examines the influence of numerous environmental conditions on EcoK and EvoD. This field remains poorly understood, and further research is essential to identify high-risk areas where surveillance for the emergence and spread of AbR should be implemented.

articles.title: Mg2+, ATP, and the Control of Bacterial Metabolism
articles.abstract: In all living cells, chemical reactions known as metabolism generate energy and building blocks for cellular structures. Metabolism produces and consumes ATP, the major currency of cellular energy. Because approximately 85% of ATP is bound to Mg 2+ , bacteria reduce their ATP concentration when cytoplasmic Mg 2+ availability drops below a certain threshold. This reduction in ATP concentration reshapes metabolism and gene transcription as well as protein synthesis, solubility, and turnover. This article reviews how ATP acts both directly and via ATP-derived signaling molecules, such as 3′,5′-cyclic AMP (cAMP), bis-(3′,5′)-cyclic dimeric-AMP (c-di-AMP), diadenosine tetraphosphate (Ap 4 A), and guanosine-3′,5′-tetra- and pentaphosphate [(p)ppGpp], which direct adaptations to stresses bacteria experience in their natural environments. It also discusses how Mg 2+ -responsive regulatory systems supersede canonical control of metabolism and protein homeostasis by governing ATP amounts and how this bacterial response slows growth, modifies cell envelope structures, and favors survival.

articles.title: Cell-state-specific metabolic networks govern ferroptosis versus apoptosis in small cell lung cancer
articles.abstract: SCLC cell states dictate how cancer cells respond to metabolic stress, revealing how metabolic plasticity determines whether the cells undergo ferroptosis or apoptosis.

articles.title: Perforin triggers iron-induced mitochondrial damage to drive ferroptosis and anti-tumor immunity
articles.abstract: Perforin is best known for delivering granzymes into tumor cells, but this study shows it has a second, independent killing function: it drives iron uptake and mitochondrial iron overload that trigger ferroptosis. This granzyme-independent pathway links cytotoxic immunity to iron metabolism, predicts patient response to checkpoint blockade, and points to iron supplementation as a possible lever for boosting anti-tumor immunity.

articles.title: Taurine lowers inflammaging by regulating the NLRP3 inflammasome in macrophages
articles.abstract: Taurine levels increase with age in mice and humans. Boosting taurine levels even further in aged mice increases health span and dampens inflammation through its regulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome.

articles.title: Secretory bile salt hydrolases regulate niche displacement and gut colonization of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus
articles.abstract: Hasegawa et al. show that a class of bile salt hydrolases (BSHs) harbored by Bacteroidales species promote elimination of vancomycin-resistant enterococcus (VRE) in the presence of Lachnospiraceae bai+ bacteria. In the gut, bacteria producing this subclass of BSH eliminate and displace VRE through deoxycholic acid (DCA) production.

articles.title: Heterogeneity propagation and surface homogenization for pouch-cell-sized Li metal anodes
Using NMR to predict molecular reactivity
articles.abstract: NMR chemical shifts are plainly transformed into machine learning features that have rational and intuitive chemical meaning. A small number of these features are used to predict molecular reactivity (via the HOMO-LUMO energy gap), resulting in a model that is not reliant on a priori knowledge of chemical structure or charge.

articles.title: Mechanochemical crystallization of covalent organic frameworks: from the linkage up
articles.abstract: This review discusses transferrable lessons and parameters from solution-based COF syntheses and small molecule mechanochemistry for the mechanochemical syntheses of imine and imine-derived COFs.

articles.title: Ferroelectricity in Single-Layer Ruddlesden−Popper Oxyfluorides Enabled by Low-Temperature Fluorination of Amorphous Precursors
articles.abstract: The development of ferroelectric materials relies on cation engineering of pure oxide systems. However, the discovery of new polar frameworks in pure oxides has become increasingly difficult because of their chemical and structural limitations. We report an approach to realize ferroelectricity in the n = 1 Ruddlesden−Popper (RP) family (A2BX4), a structure that is typically nonpolar in the oxide form because of its high crystalline symmetry. To stabilize the polar order in this rigid framework, we utilized anion engineering, specifically the partial substitution of O2− with F−. Although traditional topochemical fluorination requires a stable crystalline parent oxide, the parent n = 1 oxide Pb2MO4 (M = Fe, Co, Ni) is thermodynamically unstable and cannot be synthesized as a crystalline template. A low-temperature fluorination method using amorphous oxide film precursors was used to overcome this challenge. c-Axis-oriented epitaxial thin films of metastable Pb2M(O,F)4 were obtained, because a stable parent crystal was not required. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and electrical measurements (P−E) hysteresis and positive-up-negative-down (PUND) measurements confirmed that these layered oxyfluorides exhibited clear and switchable ferroelectricity. This behavior probably originates from the strong O/F anisotropy, which forces significant off-center cation displacements within the single perovskite layers. Thus, amorphous-based low-temperature fluorination provides a universal route for exploring novel functional materials across various mixed-anion systems.

articles.title: High Defect Formation Energies Limit Ionic Conductivity in Na3Ga2Li3F12 and Na3Al2Li3F12
articles.abstract: Lithium-conducting fluoride garnets exhibit ionic conductivities of ∼10–10 S cm–1, far below those of their oxide counterparts. Here, we investigate the origin of this poor transport in Na3Ga2Li3F12 and Na3Al2Li3F12 through a combination of structural characterization and first-principles calculations. Both compounds are highly ordered, with no significant antisite disorder, and exhibit intrinsic ionic conductivities of ∼2 × 10–11 S cm–1 at 100 °C. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal low Li-ion migration barriers (0.16 to 0.29 eV), indicating that the fluoride garnet framework does not inherently restrict Li-ion diffusion. However, the formation energies for lithium Frenkel and Schottky defect pairs are high (1.9 to 2.4 eV), indicating that the intrinsic concentrations of mobile Li-ion defects are negligibly small. These results establish that the low conductivity of stoichiometric fluoride garnets arises from high defect-formation energies, rather than high migration barriers.

articles.title: Revisiting 2-Isopropylthioxanthone: Direct and Reactivable Photopolymerization of Acrylates from Near-UV to Blue Light. Efficient 3D Printing and Surface Modification
articles.abstract: Reversible-deactivation radical photopolymerization (photoRDRP) enables precise spatiotemporal control of polymer architectures. Because of embedded active chain ends, photoRDRP offers straightforward reactivation and chain extension, providing unmatched flexibility for fine-tuning structural, mechanical, and physicochemical properties for targeted applications. Nevertheless, its application to 3D printing remains limited by the cost and synthetic effort of the control agent, as well as by a limited reactivity under common near-UV and blue light sources, which requires printers working in the visible range and results in usually low printing rates. Herein, we show the unexpected ability of 2-isopropylthioxanthone (ITX) to promote both a direct acrylate photopolymerization, (with no need for any conventional co-initiator and a printing rate close to those of conventional photoinitiators) and a subsequent surface-initiated (SI) photopolymerization via reactivable surface-bound species, yielding postfunctionalization results that are equivalent to, or surpass, those of RAFT systems. Compared to benzyldithiocarbamate (BDC) and N-(tert-butyl)-N-(2-methyl-1-(4-benzoylphenyl)propyl)-O-(1-phenylethyl) hydroxylamine (MBA), two model photoinitiators for photoRDRP in the near-UV range, ITX enabled controlled SI photopolymerization of neat acrylate monomers over thicknesses of several hundred micrometers, with higher molar reactivity and a broader spectral response. This allowed for direct photopolymerization and photostructuring using wavelengths from 365 to 405 nm. This straightforward and scalable approach opens promising avenues for the on-demand functionalization and assembly of complex 3D-printed architectures and is expected to bridge the gap between academic precision and industrial accessibility.

articles.title: Decoupling Mass Transport in Wood‑Based Separators Enables Ion Selectivity for Highly Stable Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
