articles.abstract: The widespread use of the term ‘battery’ has caused misunderstandings about what truly defines a battery. In this Comment, we critically examine the terminology and fundamental concepts of batteries to favour reliable interdisciplinary advancement of energy storage technology and research.

articles.title: 5-HT2A receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediate the neuroplastic but not the hallucinogenic effects of psilocybin
articles.abstract: Psilocybin promotes and stabilizes new connections between neurons in the mouse cerebral cortex, especially after stress. Baker et al. show that 5-HT2A receptor signaling in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediates this effect but is not required for a mouse behavioral proxy of hallucinations.

articles.title: A half-center oscillator regulates sleep pressure
articles.abstract: Changes in oscillatory neural dynamics reflect—but may not necessarily determine—transitions between sleep stages and variations in sleep pressure. Here we show that sleep-control neurons innervating the dorsal fan-shaped body of Drosophila (dFBNs) produce slow-wave activity (SWA) that is causally linked to sleep. The dFBN ensemble contains bistable cells whose membrane voltages oscillate between hyperpolarized DOWN and depolarized UP states. The oscillations rely on interhemispheric competition of two half-centers connected by inhibitory glutamatergic synapses. dFBN-restricted interference with glutamate release disrupts SWA and baseline as well as rebound sleep, whereas the optogenetic replay of SWA induces sleep. dFBNs generate SWA throughout the sleep–wake cycle (despite mutual antagonism with arousing dopaminergic neurons) and adjust its power to sleep need via sleep history-dependent increases in excitability and homeostatic synaptic depression. The oscillatory format permits a continuous encoding of sleep pressure but requires mechanisms that convert the amplitude-modulated signal into binary sleep–wake states.

articles.title: An aging-sensitive secreted phospholipase confers neuroprotection and cognitive resilience
articles.abstract: This study identifies a secreted phospholipase in the hippocampal dentate gyrus that mediates an aging-sensitive compensatory mechanism promoting cognitive resilience and neuroprotection.

articles.title: Periventricular gradient pathology is linked to ependymal reactivity and cell adhesion disruption in multiple sclerosis
articles.abstract: This study identifies ependymal dysfunction as a mechanism linking inflammatory cerebrospinal fluid to increased ventricular permeability and periventricular pathology in multiple sclerosis.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal AI-based modeling of gene regulation and variant effects in the developing human brain using Seal
articles.abstract: Seal is an artificial intelligence framework that predicts the effects of regulatory variants in 802 brain cell states, revealing spatiotemporal gene regulation and pinpointing cell types and developmental stages associated with neuropsychiatric conditions.

articles.title: Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics
articles.abstract: The experimental realization of intrinsic 2D kagome materials with controllable flat bands has remained challenging. Now a van der Waals kagome material family is shown to host an isolated, gate-tunable flat band down to the monolayer limit.

articles.title: Reaction–diffusion competition drives anomalous relaxation of vitrimers
articles.abstract: Vitrimers—polymers that form covalent networks—show glassy behaviour with viscosity decoupled from structural relaxation. This decoupling is now found to originate from a competition between chemical exchange reactions and diffusion processes.

articles.title: Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates in a spin qubit array
articles.abstract: Silicon spin qubits offer a promising path to scalable quantum computing due to their compatibility with industrial semiconductor manufacturing. A key requirement for scaling quantum processors is the ability to perform high-fidelity operations in parallel across many qubits. However, simultaneous control remains a major challenge in silicon devices, as fidelities typically degrade under parallel operation. Here we identify microwave-drive-induced a.c.-Stark shifts as the dominant source of this degradation in a five-qubit silicon spin array. We address this by introducing a scalable mitigation protocol based solely on pairwise phase calibrations. Using tailored control pulses on a shared control line, we achieve primitive X and Y gate fidelities well above 99.99% for each qubit individually, with some approaching 99.999%. Furthermore, these fidelities are preserved above 99.99% during simultaneous operation of up to three qubits. During parallel five-qubit operation, fidelities remain above the widely targeted fault-tolerant threshold of 99.9%. By maintaining high-fidelity control during simultaneous operation, shared qubit-control lines can support the development of large-scale semiconductor quantum processors.

articles.title: One year of Commissioner’s National Priority Vouchers
Non-Abelian Quantum Signal Processing: A Composite Pulse for Fast Analytic Control of Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Processors
articles.abstract: Researchers extend quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables, enabling analytical control of hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processors.

articles.title: Nonsymmorphic Time-Reversal-Doubled Axion Insulators
articles.abstract: Extension of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals establishes a spin-resolved classification scheme and identifies mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.

articles.title: Alan M. Title
articles.abstract: (10 February 1938 – 24 March 2026) The solar physicist was a driving force behind many of the most influential scientific instruments for studying the Sun.

articles.title: Oscar Edgardo Vilches
articles.abstract: (20 February 1936 – 29 June 2026) The longtime University of Washington professor advanced ultralow-temperature techniques and performed groundbreaking experiments on adsorbed films.

articles.title: Deep eutectic solvent–assisted biorefineries: Mechanistic biomass deconstruction, hierarchical materials assembly, and AI-driven process feasibility
From embrittlement to enhancement: pathway toward using hydrogen as a beneficial interstitial solute element in austenitic steels
[Perspectives] Richard Dadd's beguiling art
articles.abstract: The Victorian painter Richard Dadd was born in 1817. By the time of his death in 1886 he had been detained in psychiatric hospitals for 42 years. Dadd's life trajectory once promised to be very different. He began to draw seriously at the age of 13 years and was admitted to London's prestigious Royal Academy Schools when he was 19 years old. There he excelled, winning prizes in drawing and painting. But any possibility of a distinguished career evaporated in 1843 when, experiencing delusions, he tragically murdered his father and was later admitted to London's Bethlem Hospital.

articles.title: Europe has fallen behind in number of oncology trials
Russia slashes federal cancer funding to spend on defence
You can’t see what you don’t look for: why glycan function remains in the dark
articles.abstract: A weakness in glycobiology research is the insufficient integration of approaches used to connect glycan structure to function. From glycogene knockouts to understanding glycan structures, dynamics, and interactions, to determining whether a single glycan structure underlies a specific cellular function, no single approach provides sufficient information to establish these relationships. We argue that resolving glycan structure–function relationships requires the integration of complementary approaches spanning genetics, analytical glycomics, glycoengineering, structural biology, and computational modelling. The field stands at a transition point: from cataloguing glycan structures to understanding their diverse roles in regulating the biology of health and disease. Such an integrated approach will be critical for translating structural glycan information into mechanistic insights and, ultimately, informed glycoengineering and therapeutic design.

articles.title: Back to seedlings: rethinking the slow–fast continuum across tree life stages
articles.abstract: Forest dynamics have traditionally been interpreted through the lens of adult trees, yet most mortality occurs during the seedling stage, shaping future forests. A central assumption in ecology is that demographic trade-offs, such as the slow–fast continuum, operate consistently across ontogeny. However, increasing evidence challenges this view. Seedlings experience high pest-driven mortality, strong environmental filtering, and stochastic variation in dispersal and microsite conditions, which can decouple early-life performance from adult demography. We synthesize recent developments suggesting that seedling trade-offs may either reflect a scaled-down version of adult dynamics or diverge into alternative axes, such as the recruitment–stature axis. Recognizing these shifts is important, as climate change is likely to further reshape the regeneration process and alter community assembly in future forests.

articles.title: Socioeconomics and biodiversity in cities: moving beyond patterns to mechanisms
articles.abstract: Socioeconomic status–biodiversity associations are widely reported in cities. However, most studies remain correlational and cannot distinguish whether socioeconomic status drives biodiversity change, biodiversity shapes socioeconomic outcomes, or whether observed patterns reflect biodiversity gains versus losses. We propose a unifying framework organizing established mechanisms from diverse urban research into four hypothesized causal pathways: (A) investment-driven biodiversity enhancement, (B) disinvestment-driven biodiversity degradation, (C) biodiversity-driven socioeconomic improvement, and (D) biodiversity loss reinforcing socioeconomic decline. This framework supports pathway-specific study designs and helps practitioners anticipate whether biodiversity interventions will reduce or exacerbate inequality. Shifting from pattern description to mechanism identification is essential for credible inference and for informing urban planning and governance interventions aimed at reducing environmental inequality.

articles.title: Trees alone do not make forests
articles.abstract: Forest restoration is often evaluated based on tree cover, while other dimensions of ecosystem recovery remain depleted, simplified, or incompletely reassembled. We define this mismatch as hollow forest syndrome and propose deficit profiles and an adaptive framework to diagnose recovery gaps, identify limiting processes, and guide restoration toward whole-forest recovery.

articles.title: Cu/Fe mineralized film recovered from Cu 2+ /Fe 2+ -containing wastewater by carbide slag and bentonite composite particles: heterogeneous Fenton-like catalytic performance and degradation mechanism of Congo red
articles.abstract: In this study, a Cu/Fe bimetallic mineralized film (Cu/Fe-MF) was recovered from Cu 2+ /Fe 2+ -containing acidic wastewater as a heterogeneous Fenton catalyst for degradation of CR.

articles.title: A pseudoenzyme sensor of trehalose-6-phosphate directly represses the metabolic integrator SnRK1 in plants
articles.abstract: In Arabidopsis, pseudoenzyme class II T6P synthase functions as a T6P sensor that directly represses the master metabolic regulator SnRK1, highlighting a conserved switch that couples carbon availability to metabolic homeostasis in plants.

articles.title: Sensing endoplasmic reticulum redox state by ethylene receptors
Choice of phenotype scale is critical in biobank-based G × E tests
articles.abstract: Phenotype measurement scale has long been known to impact genetic inference, yet it is often ignored in modern studies. Costantino et al. characterize how the choice of phenotype scale affects the results of common analyses. They find that it can change GWAS hits and PGS × E interactions and influence PGS performance in specific subgroups.

articles.title: Lignin depolymerization and carbohydrate preservation by linking selective fractionation to radical mechanisms
Electric rectification by a redox-conductive metal-organic framework bilayer electrode
articles.abstract: Redox-conductive metal-organic frameworks (RC-MOFs) combine molecularly tunable redox chemistry with crystalline, porous architectures. Stacking two RC-MOFs with different redox potentials creates a bilayer in which the direction of electron flow is governed by thermodynamically allowed interfacial redox reactions. This chemical rectification establishes RC-MOF bilayers as electrochemical diodes and provides a molecular strategy for programming directional charge transport.

articles.title: Introduction: Insertion and Folding of Membrane Proteins and Peptides
Two-Dimensional IR Spectroscopy as a Window into the Molecular Structure and Dynamics of Electrolytes and Ionic Liquids: A Review
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional infrared (2DIR) spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for probing the structure and picosecond dynamics of complex, condensed-phase systems at the molecular level. In electrolytes and ionic liquids, where physicochemical properties arise from the interplay between solvation and ionic interactions, 2DIR spectroscopy provides unique insights into intermolecular interactions and dynamical processes that are often inaccessible to conventional spectroscopies. This review highlights seminal and recent advances in understanding the behavior of these systems using 2DIR spectroscopy, with particular emphasis on spectral diffusion, vibrational relaxation, and chemical exchange dynamics. The review also describes how complementary information from the vibrational modes of solvents, salts, and external probes enables detailed characterization of ion–ion interactions, hydrogen-bonding networks, and solvation environments, providing a molecular framework of the structure and time evolution of these charged systems. Moreover, particular attention is given to the dynamics of distinct molecular moieties and to the role of specific anions, cations, and solvent environments in governing behavior on femtosecond to picosecond time scales. Finally, the review describes current challenges, including the limited availability of intrinsic vibrational reporters and experimental constraints, and key open questions in electrochemical and energy-relevant systems that remain despite an extensive number of studies in the area.

articles.title: Large-scale first-principles electronic structure methods
articles.abstract: This review offers a unified view of large-scale first-principles electronic-structure algorithms through the tension between locality and global quantum constraints. It also highlights stochastic methods, AI, and advanced-computing paradigms.

articles.title: Magnetic induction heating: where will the field go next?
articles.abstract: This review explores the diverse emerging uses of magnetic induction heating across a broad range of fields, highlighting recent developments and potential future directions.

articles.title: Metal–organic frameworks based on macrocycles: from design to function
articles.abstract: This review traces how the host–guest precision of macrocycles, merged with the periodic order of reticular lattices, is replicated into material function, and charts the remaining path toward practical implementation.

articles.title: A new place for stories in conservation
articles.abstract: Michael Soule writes in his foundational article “What is Conservation Biology?” that “in crisis disciplines, one must act before knowing all the facts; crisis disciplines are thus a mixture of science and art, and their pursuit requires intuition as well as information.” Since this article was published three decades ago, conservation biology has largely focused its energies on formalizing and memorializing its scientific findings. There is no doubt this empirical turn has developed vital methods and tools, enabled links between science and policy, and fortified the discipline's credibility within the broader biological sciences. Nevertheless, Soule's intuition that conservation biology requires a kinship with art, and particularly with storytelling, remains essential to the discipline—particularly in an information environment saturated by generative artificial intelligence—in at least three important ways. First, as a crisis discipline, conservation biology remains firmly attached to questions of not only valuation but also value, which have always relied on stories and myth for expression and enrichment. Second, conservationists continue to find that stories are at least as effective as logic in communicating results and precipitating action. Fortunately, conservation science lends itself to narrative arcs by demonstrating evidence of change. Revelations of the degradation and restoration of biological diversity rhyme with myths of loss and redemption and create important roles for storytelling in conservation projects. Third, as the conservation tent continues to expand beyond understanding what humans have done to understanding why, there is an increasingly pressing need to listen to the stories that accompany human behavior. Conservation continues to thrive as an empirical discipline. Embracing the opportunities and obligations of storytelling will allow conservation to engage even more deeply with a complex world. Un nuevo lugar para la narrativa en la conservación Resumen Michael Soule escribe en su artículo fundacional «¿Qué es la biología de la conservación?»: en las disciplinas de crisis, hay que actuar antes de conocer todos los hechos; las disciplinas de crisis son, por tanto, una mezcla de ciencia y arte, y su estudio requiere tanto intuición como información. Desde que se publicó este artículo hace tres décadas, la biología de la conservación ha centrado muchos de sus esfuerzos en formalizar y dejar constancia de sus hallazgos científicos. No cabe duda de que este giro empírico ha desarrollado métodos y herramientas fundamentales, ha facilitado los vínculos entre la ciencia y la política y ha reforzado la credibilidad de la disciplina dentro del ámbito más amplio de las ciencias biológicas. No obstante, la intuición de Soule de que la biología de la conservación requiere una afinidad con el arte —y, en particular, con la narración de historias— todavía es esencial para la disciplina —especialmente en un entorno informativo saturado por la inteligencia artificial generativa— al menos en tres aspectos importantes. En primer lugar, como disciplina surgida en tiempos de crisis, la biología de la conservación todavía está firmemente ligada a cuestiones no solo de valoración, sino también de valor, que siempre han recurrido a las historias y los mitos para expresarse y enriquecerse. En segundo lugar, los conservacionistas todavía constatan que las historias son al menos tan eficaces como la lógica a la hora de comunicar resultados y propiciar la acción. Afortunadamente, la ciencia de la conservación se presta a los arcos narrativos al demostrar la evidencia del cambio. Las revelaciones sobre la degradación y la restauración de la diversidad biológica concuerdan con los mitos de la pérdida y la redención, y otorgan un papel importante a la narración de historias en los proyectos de conservación.…

articles.title: Ecosystem service gradients at protected area borders reveal multiple patterns and prevalent management conflicts
articles.abstract: Protected areas cannot halt biodiversity loss in isolation; integrating them with surrounding human‐dominated landscapes is critical. However, this integration is challenged by substantial landscape heterogeneity at protected area borders, making it difficult to determine cross‐border changes in ecosystem service provision. To address this knowledge gap, we developed a novel framework for characterizing these dynamics by analyzing ecosystem service gradients along protected area borders. For 16 protected areas in the French Alps, we used a mix of established biophysical models and novel connectivity‐based models for mobile species to assess 12 ecosystem services. These services were aggregated into three stakeholder‐driven domains reflecting rural, cultural, and urban management priorities. Automated polynomial regression analysis classified borders into five gradient types. The most common types were decreasing gradients, representing a decline in ecosystem services outside the protected area, and increasing gradients with the opposite pattern. Our analysis revealed that these patterns are driven by specific landscape configurations and uncovered frequent trade‐offs between the three management priorities; for example, landscapes supporting rural priorities often degrade cultural and urban ones. We also identified key opportunities for synergies by identifying areas where ecosystem services for all three priority domains increased simultaneously outside the protected area. This spatially explicit typology provides a powerful diagnostic tool for designing targeted interventions, such as prioritizing habitat restoration where ecosystem services decline or managing agricultural landscapes to mitigate conflicts across management priorities, supporting a more effective integration of protected areas into the wider landscape. Los gradientes de los servicios ecosistémicos en los límites de las áreas protegidas revelan múltiples patrones y conflictos de gestión frecuentes Resumen Las áreas protegidas no pueden detener la pérdida de biodiversidad por sí solas; es fundamental integrarlas con los paisajes circundantes dominados por el ser humano. Sin embargo, esta integración se ve obstaculizada por la considerable heterogeneidad del paisaje en los límites de las áreas protegidas, lo que dificulta determinar los cambios transfronterizos en la provisión de servicios ecosistémicos. Para abordar esta brecha de conocimiento, desarrollamos un marco novedoso para caracterizar estas dinámicas mediante el análisis de los gradientes de servicios ecosistémicos a lo largo de los límites de las áreas protegidas. Para 16 áreas protegidas en los Alpes franceses, utilizamos una combinación de modelos biofísicos establecidos y modelos novedosos basados en la conectividad para especies móviles, con el fin de evaluar 12 servicios ecosistémicos. Estos servicios se agruparon en tres ámbitos impulsados por las partes interesadas, que reflejan las prioridades de gestión rural, cultural y urbana. El análisis automatizado de regresión polinómica clasificó los límites en cinco tipos de gradientes. Los tipos más comunes fueron los gradientes decrecientes, que representan una disminución de los servicios ecosistémicos fuera del área protegida, y los gradientes crecientes, con un patrón opuesto. Nuestro análisis reveló que estos patrones están determinados por configuraciones específicas del paisaje y puso de manifiesto frecuentes compensaciones entre las tres prioridades de manejo; por ejemplo, los paisajes que apoyan las prioridades rurales a menudo degradan las culturales y las urbanas. También identificamos oportunidades clave para generar sinergias al detectar áreas donde los servicios ecosistémicos para los tres ámbitos prioritarios aumentaban simultáneamente fuera del área protegida.…

articles.title: Effects of climate change on marine biodiversity on the western Atlantic coast
articles.abstract: The current climate crisis, driven by greenhouse gas emissions, threatens global biodiversity, including that in marine ecosystems. However, projections for the western Atlantic Ocean that jointly quantify species richness and endemism while accounting for spatially biased and incomplete occurrence data remain limited. We addressed this gap across the western Atlantic from 57°S to 40°N, within 1500 km of the coast and on the continental shelf in waters shallower than 150 m. Using broad taxonomic coverage across vertebrates, invertebrates, and algae, we modeled biodiversity metrics directly as species richness and the corrected weighted endemism index (WEIc), applied uniform sampling from sampling effort (USSE) to minimize the effects of spatially biased and incomplete occurrence records on predictions, and tested multiple algorithms to project these metrics under Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) scenarios SSP2‐4.5 and SSP5‐8.5 for 2050 and 2100. The results indicated a significant reduction in species richness and endemism, with up to 69% of the study area projected to experience a reduction of more than 5% in species richness under the high‐emissions scenarios. The most affected areas included the coast of Florida, the Gulf of Mexico, the Caribbean, the northern region of South America, and southern Brazil. The decrease in endemism was equally concerning, with significant reductions predicted in areas of high diversity, threatening species adapted to specific ecological niches and increasing the risk of local extinctions. Vertebrates and invertebrates showed the greatest reductions in richness in the Gulf of Mexico, the Caribbean, northeastern Brazil, and northern Argentina. For algae, the most significant decreases were predicted for Florida and southern Brazil. This loss of biodiversity could compromise the resilience of marine ecosystems and the availability of fishery resources, highlighting the urgent need for coordinated global actions. Efectos del cambio climático en la biodiversidad marina de la costa atlántica occidental Resumen La actual crisis climática, impulsada por las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero, amenaza la biodiversidad global, incluida la de los ecosistemas marinos. Sin embargo, las proyecciones para el Océano Atlántico occidental que cuantifican conjuntamente la riqueza de especies y el endemismo, al tiempo que toman en cuenta datos de presencia incompletos y con sesgos espaciales, siguen siendo limitadas. Abordamos esta brecha en todo el Atlántico occidental, desde los 57°S hasta los 40°N, a menos de 1,500 km de la costa y en la plataforma continental, en aguas con una profundidad inferior a 150 m. Utilizando una amplia cobertura taxonómica que abarca vertebrados, invertebrados y algas, modelamos los indicadores de biodiversidad directamente como riqueza de especies y el índice de endemismo ponderado corregido (IEPc), aplicamos el muestreo uniforme basado en el esfuerzo de muestreo (MUBEM) para minimizar los efectos de los registros de presencia con sesgo espacial e incompletos en las predicciones, y probamos múltiples algoritmos para proyectar estos indicadores bajo los escenarios de la Trayectoria Socioeconómica Compartida (TSC) TSC2‐4.5 y TSC5‐8.5 para los años 2050 y 2100. Los resultados indicaron una reducción significativa en la riqueza de especies y el endemismo; se prevé que hasta el 69 % del área de estudio experimente una reducción de más del 5 % en la riqueza de especies bajo los escenarios de altas emisiones. Las zonas más afectadas incluyeron la costa de Florida, el Golfo de México, el Caribe, la región norte de Sudamérica y el sur de Brasil. La disminución del endemismo fue igualmente preocupante, ya que se predijeron reducciones significativas en áreas de alta diversidad, lo que pone en peligro a especies adaptadas a nichos ecológicos específicos y aumenta el riesgo de extinciones locales.…

articles.title: Coinfections Dampen the Effects of Temperature on Host–Parasite Interactions
articles.abstract: Coinfections by multiple parasite species are widespread and often modify disease outcomes. To what degree other forms of ecological complexity, such as environmental change, influence the impacts of coinfecting parasites on disease remains unclear. We exposed nematodes (Caenorhabditis elegans) to naturally coinfecting parasites (Leucobacter celer and Leucobacter musarum) at temperatures across the host's thermal range. While we found that host mortality varied widely with temperature during single infections, coinfections buffered hosts against temperature‐mediated variation via ongoing parasite competition. We extended our experiments with mathematical models indicating that changing virulence, rather than transmission, most plausibly underpins temperature‐dependent host mortality. At moderate, but not extreme temperatures, we found coinfection continued to dampen mortality outcomes due to another source of host variation, genotypic susceptibility. Coinfection may provide a stabilizing effect on disease in a warming world—but this effect can falter when hosts are faced with multiple stressors.

articles.title: Cross-interface diffusion-driven exsolution of praseodymium oxide nanoparticles for enabling electrolysis at industrially relevant temperatures in protonic ceramic cells
articles.abstract: Ce-containing BZCYYb protonic ceramics trigger Pr 6 O 11 nanoparticle exsolution from PrNiCo-based positrodes, which, combined with acid treatment and Ca doping, enable efficient and stable H 2 O electrolysis at industrially relevant temperatures.

articles.title: Design rules for bifunctional molecules as perovskite/C 60 interfacial passivation: linking mechanisms, efficiency, and stability
articles.abstract: Mitigating non-radiative recombination at the perovskite/C 60 interface is critical for achieving high-efficiency perovskite solar cells. A common strategy relies on small organic, mostly amino- or ammonium-functionalized molecules as interfacial layers....

articles.title: Electrolyte design toward stable layered oxide cathodes of sodium-ion batteries
articles.abstract: This review analyzes layered oxide cathode degradation in sodium-ion batteries from an electrolyte perspective, proposes electrolyte design principles, summarizes traditional and emerging electrolyte systems, and outlines future perspectives.

articles.title: From active site dynamics to durable Ir-based aerogels: operando insights and a flash calcination strategy for the oxygen evolution reaction in proton exchange membrane water electrolysers
articles.abstract: Operando X-ray techniques reveal the instability of the IrCu aerogel arising from reversible oxide formation. A flash-calcination strategy enables successive surface passivation of the IrCu aerogel, resulting in an active and stable catalyst.

articles.title: Multifunctional π–π conjugated molecular bridges for perovskite solar cells
articles.abstract: A π–π co-assembled SAM formed by Me-4PACz and CDA optimizes NiO x /perovskite heterojunction. Interfacial dipole tunes band alignment, suppresses non-radiative recombination, accelerates hole extraction, yielding PSCs with 26.94% PCE.

articles.title: Suppressing carbonate formation in alkaline CO 2 electrolysis
articles.abstract: A dual-function porous layer suppresses carbonate formation by restricting electrolyte convection, enabling alkaline CO 2 electrolysis for 500 h with 80% C 2 -product selectivity at 2.30 V and the lowest energy cost reported to date.

articles.title: Stepwise delithiation and interfacial electric field engineering enabling stable cycling of LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2/LiFePO4 hybrid cathode under harsh conditions
Environmental DNA metabarcoding performance for biodiversity monitoring at livestock–wildlife interfaces
articles.abstract: Open-air farming systems represent critical landscapes for integrated wildlife monitoring, enhancing biosecurity and reducing the risk of pathogen transmission at the wildlife-livestock interface. Therefore, there is a need for comparative studies to improve non-invasive methodologies for monitoring wild animal populations in these livestock-dominated environments. This study aims to conduct comparative monitoring of the biodiversity and detectability of wild species using methods based on morphological identification and environmental DNA (eDNA) sampling. Research was conducted on 13 farms distributed across the Iberian Peninsula, where 27 to 30 camera traps were deployed, and water samples were collected by filtration at one lentic water body per study site. Our results showed that camera traps detected higher taxa richness than eDNA under the sampling design used in this study, and ecological characteristics of the species, including their classification as gregarious or non-gregarious, were associated with differences in eDNA detection rates. Nevertheless, the complementary use of both approaches is recommended for wildlife population assessments. Livestock density was associated with variation in some molecular parameters of water samples under the conditions evaluated in this study. This study provides preliminary insights into the most suitable non-invasive approaches for assessing wildlife populations in livestock-dominated landscapes, within an integrated wildlife monitoring framework.

articles.title: Novel grazing strategies increase milkweed (Asclepias spp.) availability and monarch (Danaus plexippus) abundance in rangelands
articles.abstract: IntroductionMonarch butterfly (Danaus plexippus) populations are declining, emphasizing the need for conservation throughout their range. An understudied and underutilized area for conservation includes rangelands managed with livestock grazing. Although this region is on the edge of the eastern monarch population range, rangelands can provide billions of milkweed (Asclepias spp.) stems, the host plant for monarch butterflies. A better understanding of the dynamics between milkweed, monarchs, and grazing strategies are necessary, especially since previous research has shown how milkweed stem abundance changes based on grazing management. Our objectives were to 1) quantify the influence of three livestock grazing strategies on milkweed and flowering forbs and 2) determine how adult and juvenile monarch abundance is influenced by milkweed and flowering forbs.MethodsOur study was conducted at the Central Grasslands Research Extension Center in North Dakota from 2021-2022. We examined three grazing strategies that varied in their spatial and temporal disturbance patterns (modified twice-over rest-rotation [MTORG], patch-burn grazing [PBG], and season-long grazing [SLG]).ResultsWe found higher milkweed abundance in MTORG compared to PBG and SLG, and milkweed abundance was not impacted by drought during the study. Floral resources were generally more abundant in MTORG, but we detected a significant interaction between year and grazing regime. Floral resources declined dramatically in PBG in 2021 because of the drought but recovered quickly the following year and matched floral resource availability in the MTORG strategy in 2022. Both adult and juvenile monarch abundance were positively correlated with milkweed abundance.DiscussionDespite adult monarchs needing both milkweed for reproduction and nectar resources for fueling adult flight, the best explanation for changes in adult monarch abundance was milkweed abundance. Overall, we found rangelands can benefit monarchs, both during juvenile and adult life stages, by providing vital plant resources. However, the magnitude of benefit will depend on the spatial and temporal influence of grazing disturbance on host plant availability.

articles.title: Complementary root and mycorrhizal foraging strategies for phosphorus acquisition among arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal trees in a subtropical forest
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Phosphorus (P) availability is widely recognized as an important constraint on plant growth in many subtropical forest ecosystems, yet how contrasting mycorrhizal strategies mediate the use of inorganic and organic P forms remains unclear. In a subtropical forest, we integrated a 50‐ha survey of adult tree dominance, a seedling growth survey across six 1‐ha plots and a shade‐house experiment to examine how arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) and ectomycorrhizal (ECM) trees adjust root‐fungal foraging strategies across gradients of inorganic and organic P availability. In the field, quadrats with higher inorganic P availability were dominated by AM trees, whereas ECM trees were dominant in soils with greater organic P availability. In both the field survey and the shade‐house experiment, the growth of AM seedlings increased with inorganic P availability, whereas that of ECM seedlings increased with organic P availability. The results of structural equation modelling showed that, in AM seedlings, inorganic P enhanced specific root area and mycorrhizal colonization, thereby increasing root P concentration and biomass. In ECM seedlings, organic P increased mycorrhizal colonization and acid phosphatase activity, elevating root P concentration and biomass. Our findings reveal functional complementarity between AM and ECM tree species in nutrient acquisition strategies. By providing a trait‐based framework, we offer mechanistic insight into variation in seedling performance and community assembly along soil P gradients in subtropical forests. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Charcoal as a Fire Reconstruction Proxy
One Proxy to Rule Them All? The Use of Charcoal in Estimating Tropical Peatland Burning History
Electrochemical energy conversion beyond Earth
articles.abstract: Terrestrial electrochemical design implicitly relies on Earth-bound physics, such as gravity and natural convection. Beyond Earth, where these conditions no longer apply, we argue that designing with architecture, co-integrating electrochemical, thermal, and mechanical functions into a single structure, emerges as a primary physical variable rather than a downstream choice. Furthermore, additive manufacturing enables rapid structural iteration, allowing electrochemical energy conversion devices to be tailored to the strict operational demands of both space environments and resource-limited terrestrial applications.

articles.title: Burned habitats facilitate predation and lead to long‐term reductions in prey success
articles.abstract: By evaluating the effects of burned habitats on the habitat selection and movement responses of cougars and mule deer, cougar kill sites, and mule deer reproduction, the authors find that increasingly large, severe burns are diminishing herbivore reproductive success, potentially due to advantages for predators created by burned landscapes. Abstract Intensifying wildfire regimes under global change are expected to shift species interactions through changes in habitat structure and composition, vegetation productivity, and sensory cues. Yet there is little evidence of how burn‐induced changes in habitat composition and structure modify predator–prey relationships. We investigated how wildfires influence relationships between mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus) and cougars (Puma concolor) in the US Intermountain West using high‐resolution telemetry data, kill site locations, and annual measures of mule deer fawn production. Burned habitats experienced a wide range of fire severities, and most fires occurred between 5 and 20 years prior to animal data collection. We found that cougars were located closer to deer and their kill sites were nearly 2× more likely to occur in burned areas compared to unburned sites, suggesting that burns confer advantages to predators. In addition, fawn production declined by up to 14% at sites with histories of more recent, higher severity burns. Our findings suggest that increasingly frequent, severe burns are diminishing herbivore reproductive success, potentially due to increasing predation risks that outweigh improved foraging opportunities for prey. Ultimately, we reveal a possible pathway through which changing fire regimes could threaten herbivore prey populations in Western US ecosystems.

articles.title: Hydrodynamic gradients affect facilitation in soft sediment communities
articles.abstract: This study extends ecological theory on facilitation to marine soft-sediment systems and offers insight into the functional role of habitat-forming infauna. Abstract Positive species interactions, or facilitation, are fundamental drivers of ecological community assembly and stability. In terrestrial plant-dominated systems, the effects of facilitation on biodiversity have been shown to intensify along environmental stress gradients; however, comparable examples are absent for marine soft-sediment ecosystems (particularly those with animal facilitators), hindering progress in expanding ecological theory. Using a multi-site field experiment, we investigated the role of an intertidal infaunal clam (Austrovenus stutchburyi) as a community-level facilitator of macrofaunal species diversity across gradients of hydrodynamic forces acting on the seabed (wind waves and tidal currents). Strong density-dependent influences of the clam on seabed stability were expected to be central to facilitation. At 21 intertidal sites across 4 estuaries in Aotearoa New Zealand, we removed adult clams from 9 m2 plots (removal plots) and then, after 12 months, measured the difference in macrofaunal community composition, richness and abundance between removal and adjacent non-removal plots. After 12 months, differences in macrofauna biodiversity between removal and non-removal plots were observed, and at some sites, these differences were associated with non-removal plots supporting up to 9× higher macrofauna abundance and up to 4× higher species richness than removal plots, indicating facilitation by Austrovenus as important for community composition. Facilitation was strongest at sites with high adult Austrovenus density (linear model R 2 = 0.52) but also proximity to strong tidal currents (polynomial model R 2 = 0.52), indicating that Austrovenus may extend macrofaunal communities into locations where they would otherwise be excluded by hydrodynamic forces. Synthesis: Our results provide evidence that the strength of facilitation in intertidal soft-sediments changes across hydrodynamic stress gradients; however, there are likely to be interactions between indirect and direct effects that we discuss in the context of our study system. Our study extends ecological theory on facilitation to marine soft-sediment systems and offers insight into the functional role of habitat-forming infauna.

articles.title: Activity-stability differences in fenton catalysis: distinct roles of Fe-N4 and Fe-N4O2 sites
Temporal evolution of potential oscillations during ethanol electro-oxidation driven by CHx accumulation: insights from microkinetic modeling
Local conspecific density affects the relationship between species abundance and plant–soil feedback in a subtropical forest
articles.abstract: The relationship between species abundance and plant–soil feedback depends on the local density of each species. Our shade‐house experiment detected a negative abundance–feedback relationship only under high local density, with soil fungal pathogens potentially contributing to this pattern. These findings highlight local density as an important spatial context for interpreting contrasting feedback patterns in forest communities. Abstract Increasing evidence suggests that plant–soil feedback (PSF) is essential in shaping species abundance and promoting the coexistence of common and rare species. Yet, empirical studies have yielded inconsistent results regarding the relationship between species abundance and PSF strength. To reconcile the debate on the species abundance–PSF relationship (SAPR), we propose a conceptual framework that decomposes PSF into two components: PSF1 caused by the focal tree and PSF2 caused by the conspecific neighbours. These two components drive community assembly and diversity maintenance processes, respectively. Moreover, our framework emphasizes that local conspecific density is critical for measuring species PSF in natural communities. We then conducted a shade‐house experiment involving 14 subtropical tree species to test the SAPR in a subtropical forest. We found a significant negative relationship between species abundance and PSF only when inoculum soils were collected from areas with high local conspecific density. The fungal pathogens in the soil and roots were identified as the key drivers of this pattern. Our study provides direct experimental evidence that local conspecific density affects the SAPR, which may clarify discrepancies across studies and advance our understanding of how PSF contributes to species coexistence in forest ecosystems. Synthesis. Integrating a conceptual framework with a multi‐species soil inoculation PSF experiment, we reveal intensifying negative PSF from rare to common species in a subtropical forest community, with local conspecific density influencing this pattern. Consequently, our study suggests that the intricate relationship between species abundance and PSF is closely implicated in the dynamics of local species coexistence. We propose that previous controversies regarding the SAPR primarily stemmed from the neglect of local species density and the confusion of distinct ecological processes across studies.

articles.title: Can weakly interlayer-coupled transition metal dichalcogenides open up a new prospect of two-dimensional family?
articles.abstract: Weak interlayer coupling, originating from electron interactions of adjacent layers, can provide promising prospects for two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), which can be respectively evaluated by energy criteria qualitatively and by band-gap transformation and band-shifting ratios quantitatively. Weakly interlayer-coupled TMDCs will promote the development of all-2D processing-in-memory devices together with strongly interlayer-coupled ones.

articles.title: Metal-organic pulsed laser deposition for complex oxide heterostructures
articles.abstract: Point defects govern the properties of complex oxides, yet they are hard to control precisely. Lee et al. introduce metal-organic pulsed laser deposition (MOPLD), which tunes the cation stoichiometry of SrTiO3 films to within a 0.1% solubility limit. By selectively adjusting antisite and vacancy populations, MOPLD suppresses oxygen vacancies and boosts the low-temperature mobility of the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 electron gas, offering a general route to defect engineering in oxide heterostructures for quantum materials research.

articles.title: Thermodynamic decoupling of polymer pre-aggregation in sustainable solvents enables high-detectivity flexible organic photodiodes
articles.abstract: Precise control of solution aggregation enables flexible organic photodiodes processed from sustainable solvents to combine high detectivity with strong mechanical durability. By slowing rapid nucleation and improving film formation, this approach reduces trap formation and structural defects, offering a practical route toward sustainably manufactured wearable optoelectronics.

articles.title: STING engages PKR to drive lysosomal cell death in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury
articles.abstract: Gao et al. identify protein kinase (PKR) as a non-canonical stimulator of interferon genes (STING) effector in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury. STING oligomerization at the endoplasmic reticulum drives PKR-S33 autophosphorylation and TBK1-independent IKK-NF-κB activation. This pathway induces LAMP3-dependent lysosomal cell death, and its inhibition attenuates epithelial injury.

articles.title: Acidogenic Bacteria Dominate Brood Pollen Provisions Across Diverse Bee Taxa
articles.abstract: Bacteria and fungi play vital roles in bee health and development, yet microbial communities associated with pollen provisions remain largely uncharacterized for most bee species, particularly ground‐nesting taxa. Microbial communities may prevent pollen provision spoilage, liberate nutrients from pollen, supply direct nutrition and/or suppress pathogens, though these functions appear context‐dependent and variable among hosts. To determine whether bee evolutionary history and ecological traits structure pollen provision microbiomes, we analyzed 345 ‘live’ brood cell pollen provisions representing 39 species, 18 tribes and six bee families spanning diverse life histories, diet breadths, floral resource use and nesting substrates. Microbial composition was determined by amplicon sequencing of bacterial 16S rRNA (V5–V7) and fungal ITS (1 and 2) regions. Bacterial richness and community composition were strongly structured by bee taxonomy and were also associated with several ecological traits, while community composition was significantly associated with host phylogeny. Fungal richness also varied among bee taxa and ecological groups, whereas fungal community composition showed greater variability and weaker, though detectable, taxonomic structure, with comparatively small ecological‐trait effects. Across phylogenetically distant bee tribes, pollen provisions were often dominated by lactic‐ or acetic acid‐producing bacteria, indicating a strategy of microbial fermentation that reduces bacterial richness and may enhance food preservation. Together, these results reveal broad evolutionary and ecological patterns underlying the microbiome of solitary bee brood cells and suggest that acid‐producing bacteria play a stabilizing role in the preservation and function of pollen provisions.

articles.title: Overcoming Detection Lag in a Cryptic Panzootic: Chytrid Invasion Linked to Historically Enigmatic Amphibian Declines in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
articles.abstract: As human activity accelerates the spread of pathogens and other invasive species, reconstructing the cryptic early dynamics of undetected invasions has become a central challenge in disease ecology and invasion biology. Here, we leverage museum specimens to reconstruct the invasion of Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd), a fungal panzootic driving global amphibian biodiversity loss, across historically enigmatic declines in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest. Two hypotheses have been proposed to explain Bd's historical dynamics in this region: long‐term enzootic persistence versus recent epizootic invasion coinciding with declines. Using molecular screening, histopathology, and genotyping of museum and modern specimens, we find no evidence of Bd infection prior to the decline, followed by widespread infection immediately thereafter. Only the global panzootic lineage (Bd‐GPL) was detected during the first year of post‐decline sampling, implicating its invasion in driving regional losses. Infection prevalence varied among species following the decline, likely reflecting species‐specific interactions between baseline susceptibility and ecological exposure risk. Contemporary host populations exhibit more uniform prevalence regardless of decline history, consistent with the evolution of pathogen tolerance under enzootic conditions. Together, these results provide the first site‐specific evidence linking Bd‐GPL invasion to enigmatic amphibian declines in Brazil and demonstrate the power of museum collections for resolving detection lag dynamics in emerging infectious diseases.

articles.title: Rhizosphere Fungal Community Responses to Nitrogen Addition Reflect Genotypic Versus Trait Variation in the Marsh Sedge Schoenoplectus americanus Over Time
articles.abstract: There is growing recognition that shifting environmental conditions can alter the nature and potential benefits of plant‐microbe interactions. While it is well established that interactions with fungi can benefit plants under environmental stress, little is known about how plant exposure responses correspond to different factors that might shape fungal communities, particularly over time. Using a resurrection ecology approach, we examined the relative influence of contrasting environmental conditions and intraspecific variation in the foundational marsh sedge Schoenoplectus americanus on rhizosphere fungal communities. Cohorts of ancestral plants germinated from 100+ year old seeds and modern plants were grown under low and high nitrogen (N) concentration in a common‐garden experiment. Fungal communities were characterized according to plant presence as well as genotypic and associated trait variation. The study revealed that the influence of S. americanus on fungal communities differed between the nitrogen regimes. Under low N, fungal taxonomic, but not guild, diversity was higher in rhizosphere soils than unplanted controls. Plant effects were, however, diminished under high N conditions. We also found that heritable traits had limited influence on fungal communities, whereas both taxonomic and guild diversity and composition reflected genotypic variation and G × E interactions. Cohorts of ancestral and modern plants also recruited distinct fungal communities depending on N conditions. These results indicate that shifts in plant‐fungal associations over time are contingent on prevailing environmental conditions. Our findings also indicate that N‐driven changes in plant–fungal interactions likely alter ecosystem processes that are central to saltmarsh resilience to shifting environmental conditions.

articles.title: A spatial map of the atmospheric limb of a hot Jupiter
articles.abstract: Planets are inherently three-dimensional objects shaped by their thermal structure and dynamics. Observations of transiting exoplanets have begun to uncover this three-dimensional nature, with JWST measuring their dayside atmosphere structure with eclipse mapping and exploring spectroscopic asymmetries in the limbs of planets during transit. Here we apply the novel transmission strings mapping method to the hot Jupiter WASP-17 b. With this method, we are not only able to extract hemispheric limb asymmetries from east-to-west, but can also map equator-to-pole variations around the transmitting atmosphere as a function of angle, spanning 0.6–12 μm. We find a clear transition in the thermal scale height around the limb of the atmosphere, with an approximately 650 K temperature difference between the morning ( $$85{8}_{-233}^{+434}\,{\mathrm{K}}$$ 85 8 − 233 + 434 K ) and evening $$1{,}52{2}_{-114}^{+116}\,{\mathrm{K}}$$ 1 , 52 2 − 114 + 116 K ). These results are consistent with both nightside emission and dayside eclipse mapping measurements, and represent a fully comprehensive set of observations for a transiting exoplanet. We are also able to constrain the abundances of H 2 O and CO 2 to constant values around the limb, providing observational constraints for results from global circulation models. The transmission string technique, combined with the outstanding observability of WASP-17 b, pushes the study of exoplanet atmospheres further into a three-dimensional understanding of hot Jupiter dynamics and chemistry.

articles.title: Reframing cancer therapy through tumor plasticity
articles.abstract: de Sauvage and colleagues discuss the latest advances in therapy-driven cancer plasticity processes and how this knowledge might be applied to clinical strategies.

articles.title: Stroke-induced astrocyte memories promote glioma progression
articles.abstract: The impact of earlier brain insults on the glioblastoma microenvironment is poorly understood. A study now shows that prior stroke alters astrocytes to promote glioblastoma growth and invasion via downregulation of calcium signaling.

articles.title: Compartment-specific PPARδ activity controls the outcome of cancer–immune cell competition and immunotherapy efficacy
articles.abstract: Cancer cells and immune cells compete for metabolic fitness within the tumor microenvironment. Here the authors show that PPARδ is instrumental in this battle and that activating it in immune cells can boost immunotherapy in resistant mouse tumors and improve human chimeric antigen receptor T cells.

articles.title: Evidence for maternal autoantibodies in the pathogenesis of preterm birth
articles.abstract: Preterm birth is associated with breakdown of maternal–fetal tolerance and remains the leading cause of global mortality in young children. However, the role of self-reactive antibodies has been limited to a handful of pathogenic allo- and autoantibodies linked to pregnancy complications. Here we identify a shared autoreactive signature of pregnancy in pregnant sera (n = 2,719) relative to never-pregnant controls (n = 130), using proteome-wide autoantibody profiling. Across eight human pregnancy cohorts, we define autoreactivities associated with preterm birth by comparing preterm (n = 688) and term (n = 1,505) pregnancies. Within the signature, antibodies to IL1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) induce resorption, inflammation and vascular malperfusion in pregnant mice. IL1RA localizes to placental endothelial adherens junctions, suggesting a role in vascular integrity. These findings identify a term pregnancy humoral immune program and shared changes preceding preterm delivery, including anti-IL1RA, which may have direct pathogenic consequences. Preterm labor is linked to breakdown of maternal–fetal tolerance. Rackaityte et al. report that some pregnant mothers harbor maternal autoantibodies, including those against IL-1 receptor antagonist, that may contribute to preterm delivery.

articles.title: Integrating sex as a biological variable into one’s science
articles.abstract: Addressing sex-related variation might seem like an experimental or data analysis time-sink. It’s not.

articles.title: LoL-align: sensitive and fast probabilistic protein structure alignment
articles.abstract: The ubiquitous availability of protein structures permits replacing sequence alignment with more accurate and sensitive structure alignment algorithms. LoL-align maximizes a local log-odds score for proteins to be homologous, given their intra-protein C α − C α distances. Here we show that LoL-align is markedly more sensitive in detecting remote homologs than TM-align and Dali on single- and multidomain benchmarks and achieves better alignment quality at 5–20 × their speed. LoL-align is fully integrated into Foldseek.

articles.title: MassNet: billion-scale AI-ready mass spectral corpus empowering scalable deep learning in proteomics
articles.abstract: This Article presents MassNet, a large-scale AI-ready corpus of 1.5 billion MS/MS spectra spanning 35 species, paired with a standardized storage format called Mass Spectrometry DDA Tensor (MSDT). Built on this resource, XuanjiNovo is a nonautoregressive transformer for de novo peptide sequencing that substantially outperforms previous methods.

articles.title: Cryogenic shock exfoliation for ultrahigh mobility rhombohedral graphite nanoelectronics
articles.abstract: A scalable cryogenic shock exfoliation method for the fabrication of large and uniform rhombohedral graphene flakes is demonstrated.

articles.title: Evidence for an excitonic insulator
articles.abstract: Using local probes and impurities on Ta2Pd3Te5 two experimental groups prove and characterize the presence of an excitonic gap via the impurity-induced breaking of excitonic pairing.

articles.title: Gate-induced layer sliding drives non-volatile switching of magnetism in tetralayer graphene
articles.abstract: Gate-voltage sweeps drive a first-order sliding transition between Bernal-dominant and rhombohedral–Bernal mixed stacking in marginally twisted double-bilayer graphene, which allows for non-volatile on/off switching of the low-temperature ferromagnetic phase.

articles.title: Sliding ferroelectricity scales up
articles.abstract: Wafer-scale growth of a metastable rhombohedral boron nitride polytype takes sliding ferroelectricity from handcrafted structures in the laboratory towards integrated devices.

articles.title: Ring attractor networks go full circle
articles.abstract: Clark et al. demonstrate that heterogeneous data-driven models implement head-direction selectivity through the same dynamical principles as classical ring networks. In doing so, the authors reconcile biological realism with theoretical simplicity, unifying existing frameworks and broadening the space of connectivity structures to be searched in data.

articles.title: Symmetries and continuous attractors in disordered neural circuits
articles.abstract: Head-direction cells are far more disorderly than classical continuous-attractor models allow. Clark et al. show that this disorder is nevertheless compatible with these models and that the underlying connectivity matrix hides a circular symmetry.

articles.title: A dynamic ruler for positional memory in regeneration
articles.abstract: Zebrafish can determine the amount of tissue to regrow after appendage amputation. Now, a study shows that a signal gradient that scales with the amount of tissue left to regenerate ensures that an amputated tailfin regrows to the correct length.

articles.title: Fusion digital twins from imperfect models
articles.abstract: Digital twins could transform how fusion plasmas are predicted, designed and controlled. We argue that realizing this promise requires multi-fidelity frameworks that systematically combine imperfect models and data while quantifying uncertainty.

articles.title: FDA new drug approvals in Q3 2026
Atomically ordered dual atomic pairs in CuAuZn2 intermetallics for efficient urea electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Atomically ordered CuAuZn2 intermetallics with high-density Cu–Zn and Au–Zn dual atomic pairs are developed for urea electrosynthesis. The Cu–Zn sites facilitate nitrate reduction to *NH2, while neighbouring Au–Zn sites enhance CO2 reduction to *COOH and urea formation. This overcomes the kinetic mismatches between carbon and nitrogen intermediates, enabling the selective production of urea.

articles.title: Enantioselective synthesis of π-extended carbo[17]helicene via sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions
articles.abstract: Sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions, followed by onward Scholl reactions, enable the enantioselective synthesis of a giant π-extended carbo[17]helicene from a dodecayne substrate. This Ni-catalysed process forms a chiral nanocarbon that exhibits strong circularly polarized luminescence.

articles.title: Mechanoradical-chain C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling with unactivated arenes
articles.abstract: Mechanically generated radicals are often considered detrimental in materials. Now, a method for mechanically generating reactive carbon-based radicals and applying them in selective C(sp3)–C(sp2) bond formation is reported. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and polymers are compatible with the process, forming benzylated arene products without the need for a solvent.

articles.title: Electric-Field-Induced X-Ray Nonreciprocal Dichroism in Hematite
articles.abstract: X-ray absorption spectroscopy under an applied electric field uncovers signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles in hematite (Fe2O3), supported by theoretical calculations.

articles.title: Topological Phase Transitions and Their Thermodynamic Fate in Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
articles.abstract: A theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin pyrochlore spin ice reveals that S = 3/2 magnets alone switch abruptly between two distinct spin-liquid states, a transition that survives the thermal fluctuations that wash all the other transitions into crossovers.

articles.title: Synergistic metal halide perovskite–metal-organic framework heterostructures: interfacial engineering for stable and multifunctional next-generation devices
Fast Feature Field (F3): A general predictive representation of events for robot perception
articles.abstract: This paper develops a mathematical argument and algorithms for building representations of data from event-based cameras that we call Fast Feature Field (F 3 ). We learned this representation by predicting future events from past events and show that it preserves scene structure and motion information. F 3 exploits the sparsity of event data and is robust to noise and variations in event rates. It can be computed efficiently using ideas from multiresolution hash encoding and deep sets, achieving 120 hertz at high-definition (HD) resolution and 440 hertz at video graphics array (VGA) resolution. F 3 represents events in a contiguous spatiotemporal volume as a multichannel image, enabling a range of downstream tasks. We obtained state-of-the-art performance on optical flow estimation, semantic segmentation, and monocular metric depth estimation, on data from three robotic platforms (a car, a quadruped robot, and a flying platform) and across different lighting conditions (daytime and nighttime), environments (indoors, outdoors, urban, and off-road), and dynamic vision sensors (resolutions and event rates). Our implementations can predict these tasks at 25 to 75 hertz at HD resolution.

articles.title: MonoRace: Robust monocular AI for champion-level drone racing
articles.abstract: Autonomous drone racing represents a major frontier in robotics research. It requires an artificial intelligence (AI) that can run onboard lightweight flying robots under tight resource and time constraints while pushing the physical system to its limits. The state of the art in this area consists of a system with a stereo camera and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) that beat human drone-racing champions in a controlled indoor environment. Here, we present MonoRace, an onboard drone-racing approach that generalizes to a competition environment without any external motion tracking system, using only a monocular rolling-shutter camera and an IMU. The approach features robust state estimation that combines neural network–based gate segmentation with a drone model. Moreover, it includes an offline optimization procedure that leverages the known geometry of gates to refine any state estimation parameter. This offline optimization is based purely on onboard flight data and is important for fine-tuning the extrinsic camera calibration parameters. Furthermore, the guidance and control are performed by a neural network that forgoes inner-loop controllers by directly sending motor commands. This small network runs on the flight controller at 500 hertz. The proposed approach won the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Drone Racing Competition 2025, outperforming all competing autonomous drone race teams and three world champion human pilots in a direct knockout tournament. It reached speeds up to 100 kilometers per hour on the competition track and successfully coped with problems such as camera interference and IMU saturation.

articles.title: System design of the Ultra Mobility Vehicle: A driving, balancing, and jumping bicycle robot
articles.abstract: Trials cyclists and mountain bike riders can hop, jump, balance, and drive on one or both wheels. This versatility allows them to achieve speed and energy efficiency on smooth terrain and agility over rough terrain. Inspired by these athletes, we present the design and control of a robotic platform, Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV), that combines a bicycle and a reaction mass to move dynamically with minimal actuated degrees of freedom. We used a simulation-driven design optimization process to synthesize a spatial linkage topology with a focus on vertical jump height and momentum-based balancing on a single wheel contact. Using a deep reinforcement learning (RL) framework, we demonstrate zero-shot transfer of diverse athletic behaviors, including track stands, jumps, wheelies, rear-wheel hopping, and front flips. This 23.5-kilogram robot is capable of high speeds ( v max = 8 meters per second) and jumping on and over large obstacles (1-meter tall or 130% of the robot’s nominal height).

articles.title: Editorial Expression of Concern for the Research Article “In vivo CRISPR activation screen identifies acyl-CoA–binding protein as a driver of bone metastasis”
From code to cure: Harnessing AI for antibiotic discovery and design
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) now enables the exploration of vast chemical and sequence spaces, the design of synthesizable antibiotics, and the prioritization of safe, mechanism-diverse candidates through integrated modeling and accelerated testing. Here, we survey recent advances in AI for both small-molecule and peptide antimicrobial drugs, highlight emerging data and reporting standards, and outline translational pathways and regulatory hurdles needed to bring these agents to patients.

articles.title: Innovative roadmaps for sustainable antimicrobial resistance interventions
articles.abstract: Integrated strategies to combat antibiotic-resistant bacteria and fungi require innovative commercial models, new discovery platforms, standardized genomic surveillance, and streamlined clinical trials. Machine learning and other new technologies will accelerate the development of diagnostics and therapeutics (small molecules, antibodies, and vaccines) to combat antimicrobial resistance. Next-generation approaches should align societal impact with investment to ensure rapid global public health gains.

articles.title: Metabolomic aging and mortality clocks based on ensemble learning identify systemic aging risk across the human life span in 18,476 individuals
articles.abstract: Aging is characterized by progressive functional decline, yet metabolomic signatures across the human life span remain incompletely defined. Here, we profiled plasma metabolomes from 18,476 participants aged 1 to 96 years across six centers in China using nano-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) and identified 56 representative age-associated metabolites. In a healthy cohort, we developed a stacking ensemble model to estimate metabolomic age and quantified metabolomic age acceleration (mAA) as each individual’s deviation from chronological age. Higher mAA was associated with health deterioration and unfavorable lifestyles. During follow-up from 2019 to 2025, individuals with accelerated mAA showed increased risk of incident chronic diseases, such as fatty liver disease, hypertension, and diabetes, as well as increased all-cause mortality. In a disease cohort, we further developed a mortality-linked metabolomic metric (age deviation) that quantified individualized departures from age-expected mortality risk inferred from plasma metabolites. Age deviation was associated with established composite health measures and increased with multisystem disease involvement and higher multimorbidity burden. Together, these findings support the potential of plasma metabolomic profiling as a scalable, life span–wide approach for deriving clinically interpretable metabolomic aging metrics associated with health status, chronic disease risk, and mortality.

articles.title: Orthogonal Fc engineering enables multiplexed delivery of mRNA-encoded bispecific antibodies that constrain viral escape
articles.abstract: The continuous antigenic evolution of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has repeatedly undermined the effectiveness of monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapies, underscoring the need for innovative approaches that improve therapeutic mAb breadth and durability of protection. Here, we engineered messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA)–encoded bispecific antibodies (bsAbs) that, upon intravenous administration in lipid nanoparticles, achieved high serum concentrations, extended half-life, and serum neutralizing titers exceeding 1:10,000 in human neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)–expressing mice. To enhance resilience to viral escape, we used structure-guided computational design to introduce Fc modifications that promoted selective homodimerization, thereby enabling codelivery of multiple mRNA-encoded bsAbs with cognate heavy chain pairing. In vivo expression of a triple bsAb combination resulted in broad serum neutralization of historical and contemporary SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the highly mutated BA.3.2.2 lineage. Preexposure prophylaxis with the mRNA-delivered bsAb combination conferred protection against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 challenge, preventing weight loss and decreasing viral burden in the lungs compared with vehicle control treatment. Together, the results provide proof of principle for mRNA-based delivery of Fc-engineered bsAb combinations to combat SARS-CoV-2 and potentially other rapidly evolving pathogens.

articles.title: Preclinical and first-in-human evaluation of VG-3927/SAR448851, an oral small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer’s disease
articles.abstract: Microglial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathogenesis, with loss-of-function variants in the microglial receptor TREM2 as major risk factors for late-onset AD. We report VG-3927, an oral, CNS-penetrant small-molecule TREM2 agonist that engages the transmembrane domains of TREM2 and its adaptor DAP12 to promote higher-order receptor complex formation and downstream signaling. VG-3927 and tool compound VG-3909 exhibited (sub)nanomolar potency, cooperated with endogenous ligands including amyloid-β (Aβ), and restored signaling in disease-associated TREM2 variants. In human iPSC-derived neuron-microglia-astrocyte cultures, VG-3927 reduced inflammatory cytokines and markers of neuronal damage. In 5xFAD amyloidosis mice expressing the common variant of hTREM2 (5xFAD;hTREM2 CV ), VG-3909 induced neuroprotective transcriptional reprogramming of microglia, particularly in the plaque niche; enhanced Aβ phagocytosis; and boosted brain glucose metabolism. By contrast, a TREM2 agonist antibody, which may be sequestered by soluble TREM2 (sTREM2), failed to engage plaque microglia. In a first-in-human, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1 trial (NCT06343636, n = 115), VG-3927 was well tolerated across single and multiple ascending doses of up to 140 milligrams. Pharmacokinetics supported once-daily dosing with high CNS penetration (CSF-to-unbound plasma ratio of 0.91). VG-3927 induced dose-dependent reductions in CSF sTREM2, a biomarker of target engagement, consistent across healthy and elderly participants and participants with AD, supporting further clinical development in AD under the new designation SAR448851.

articles.title: Prevention is better than cure
articles.abstract: Wider access to clean water and sanitation is needed in the battle to combat bacterial diseases.

articles.title: Quinolinic acid contributes to maladaptive kidney injury and acute kidney injury–to–chronic kidney disease transition
articles.abstract: The transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains a major clinical problem with unclear underlying mechanisms. Emerging evidence suggests that alterations in tryptophan metabolism, particularly in the production of downstream metabolites such as quinolinic acid (QA), play a role in renal pathophysiology. QA, an intermediate in de novo nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide biosynthesis, is metabolized by quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase (QPRT). We investigated whether QA contributes to kidney injury using models of folic acid–induced AKI-to-CKD transition and cisplatin-induced AKI, genetic and exogenous approaches to alter QA, and clinical observations. Untargeted kidney metabolomics identified QA as one of the most elevated metabolites after folic acid injury. After folic acid injury, Qprt haploinsufficiency exacerbated kidney injury and fibrosis-related gene expression; aged Qprt -haploinsufficient mice exhibited increased fibrosis-associated gene expression without overt renal dysfunction. Exogenous QA administration increased serum creatinine in uninjured mice and worsened renal dysfunction and fibrosis-related gene expression in the folic acid AKI-to-CKD model. Conversely, mice deficient in either 3-hydroxyanthranilate 3,4-dioxygenase (HAAO) or kynurenine 3-monooxygenase (KMO), which reduce flux toward QA, showed improved renal outcomes after folic acid injury and cisplatin-induced AKI. Multimodal spatial metabolomics analysis of kidney biopsies from patients with AKI revealed QA accumulation in regions of inflammatory infiltration. Last, children with CKD exhibited higher urinary QA compared with healthy individuals. These findings underscore QA as a potential mediator of kidney injury and a therapeutic target for preventing the progression from AKI to CKD.

articles.title: Restoration of PP2A AαB56αC trimer formation by RPT04402 molecular glue in high-grade uterine cancer
articles.abstract: The incidence and mortality of high-grade endometrial cancers are increasing, and heterozygous hotspot mutations in PPP2R1A are drivers of the most aggressive forms of uterine cancer. PPP2R1A encodes the Aα scaffolding subunit of the heterotrimeric phosphatase PP2A. These recurrent mutations, specifically at the Pro 179 and Ser 256 residues, disrupt the binding of tumor-suppressive substrate-directing B56 and B55 subunits to the PP2A scaffolding subunit while maintaining binding to other regulatory subunits. Here, we identified a series of molecular glues that correct PP2A trimer formation in the context of the P179R (Pro 179 →Arg) and S256F (Ser 256 →Phe) mutants. A small-molecule library was designed to fit into the pocket at the binding interface of the Aα/B56α/C heterotrimer. The lead molecule, RPT04402, promoted B56α heterotrimerization to the Aα P179R and Aα S256F mutant scaffolds. In mice, RPT04402 treatment drove tumor regressions and extended median survival in multiple independent mutant cell lines and patient-derived xenografts, proving a robust single-agent activity. This activity was abrogated upon knockout of B56α. Combined, these data demonstrate that PP2A molecular glues are a promising first-in-class therapy that might benefit patients with PPP2R1A mutant uterine cancer by targeting a driver of this aggressive disease.

articles.title: Retraction of the Research Article “SARS-CoV-2 S2–targeted vaccination elicits broadly neutralizing antibodies”
Rifampicin-resistant TB: An inflection point in antimicrobial resistance
articles.abstract: Rifampicin-resistant TB should be integrated into the global AMR response through diagnostics, surveillance, and optimized treatment regimens.

articles.title: A Ferrier sesquicentenary
APOE, p-tau217, and cognitive impairment in diverse cohorts
Antibody-mediated encephalitides: distinct diseases with transdisciplinary implications
articles.abstract: The discovery of antibody-mediated glial and neuronal disorders has transformed the diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases previously considered idiopathic or not recognised as immune-mediated. Antibody-mediated disorders targeting glial aquaporin-4 and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein are distinct nosological entities, defined by specific targets, mechanisms, syndromes, and therapeutic implications. By contrast, antibody-mediated disorders targeting neuronal antigens (ie, autoimmune encephalitides) are still frequently analysed collectively, with data from different disorders pooled as if they represent a single disease rather than distinct entities. Evidence from anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, anti-LGI1 encephalitis, and anti-IgLON5 disease (used here as exemplars of autoimmune encephalitides) indicates that individual autoimmune encephalitides differ in demographics, triggers, mechanisms, clinical manifestations, post-acute trajectories, and treatment requirements. The broad, heterogeneous presentations of autoimmune encephalitides require coordinated multidisciplinary care within and beyond neurology, involving specialists in paediatrics, infectious diseases, epilepsy, movement disorders, sleep medicine, intensive care, cognitive rehabilitation, and other relevant disciplines.
